Fast-sale options for a Houston owner

Listing with a broker, selling privately and taking cash are the Houston owner's three options. The city is a market unto itself, with 2,397,315 people at the 2025 estimate, and prices can differ sharply between neighboring blocks.

Owners occupy only 42.1% of Houston homes, so landlords, investors and first-time buyers all bid for houses. Cash tends to suit a house with postponed upkeep, storm damage, a tenant or a cloudy title. A listing works best for a house that shows well.

  • Find your deed and survey, and check whether restrictions cover your street.
  • Confirm the appraisal district and taxing units for the address.
  • Collect two written offers, each naming a closing date.

No zoning, but deed restrictions and plats

Houston has no citywide zoning. Voters rejected it, and subdivision deed restrictions steer most construction. Such private restrictions can limit what gets built and how a lot is used. Read yours, then hand the buyer a copy.

The city's planning department requires a plat, a surveyed map of the lot, before building permits. Single-family classification can include a duplex or a garage apartment under 900 square feet unless the deed restrictions forbid it. Houston also reviews plats in an area about five miles beyond its limits, where its permit and inspection rules do not apply.

Plats are filed with the Harris County Clerk's records office after approval. The city's planning site has a map viewer and a Plat Tracker for searching by address.

Houston home values

Houston's midpoint home value was $277,800 over 2020 to 2024, and owners with a mortgage spent $2,240 a month at the median. Because that midpoint spans the whole city, treat it as background and let written offers price your own house.

Houston housing, 2020 to 2024 survey

Median home value$277,800

With rent at $1,361 and owners in a minority of homes, the rental market runs deep. That helps a landlord who is selling, but any seller with a tenant should read the lease and notice rules before saying yes to an offer.

Harris Central Appraisal District and exemptions

Most Houston property is valued for tax by the Harris Central Appraisal District. Owners can file protests, renditions and homestead exemptions on its site, which also has an Exemption Wizard. A deed protection feature lets you register your home with the Harris County Clerk as a guard against deed fraud.

The valuation date is January 1. Homestead notices start near April 1. Your protest is due by May 15, or 30 days after the notice if that is later. A ruling you dislike can be challenged in district court or binding arbitration. Above a board value of $1,000,000, the State Office of Administrative Hearings is another option. Throughout, pay the part of the tax nobody disputes.

  • After the exemption is approved, a homestead's appraised value may grow by 10% at most in any year.
  • Anyone who inherited but is not named on the recorded deed must file an ownership affidavit with the death certificate and a current utility bill to claim it.
  • If the seller never filed, a buyer closing after January 1 can still apply for what is left of that year.

Look at your tax bill to see which district and taxing units cover the parcel.

Flood history and storm damage

Buyers and lenders will want answers. Paving and fast runoff have long fed flooding here, and severe floods in 1929 and 1935 led to the Harris County Flood Control District and later the Addicks and Barker reservoirs.

The city says flood mitigation, drainage, water and sewer are outside the Planning Commission's plat review, so a plat does not settle a house's flood risk. Ask the city and the county for flood records on your address, and keep repair records and insurance claims ready for buyers.

Heat, humidity and heavy rain are hard on roofs, siding and air conditioning. A cash buyer will accept storm damage as is, and a documented history helps both sides agree on price.

City limits and neighborhood names

Many buyers search by neighborhood name. Houston Heights and Pasadena grew as developer-built suburbs in 1892, Bellaire in 1911, West University Place in 1919 and River Oaks in the mid-1920s, and those names still anchor listing descriptions. Several of them are separate municipalities, so check whether your address sits inside Houston or in another city, because that decides who issues permits and which rules apply.

Mention the drive time to downtown, the Texas Medical Center or the ship channel, because the average commute of 27.2 minutes is something buyers weigh. Verify your school district before you print it in a listing; your tax bill or the district itself can confirm it.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Houston houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Preparing the paperwork

Build a single folder before you list or accept anything. It should hold the deed, any survey, your subdivision's deed restrictions, the newest tax statement and a payoff letter for each loan, plus flood records, repair receipts and insurance claims.

In a market this large buyers compare many houses, and a seller who answers with documents closes faster. Have each bidder state price, closing date, closing-charge split and what happens if the deal collapses, then compare the net after payoffs.

Tenants in the house

The first step is a written notice to vacate, three days long unless the lease sets a different period. Next the landlord files in justice court and a hearing follows in 10 to 21 days. Either side has five days after judgment to appeal to county court, and the writ of possession waits six days after the final judgment.

Notify each buyer in writing that someone rents the house, and attach the lease. Investors may keep the tenant; a buyer moving in needs the house vacant at closing.

Inherited houses and probate

Texas repealed its inheritance tax effective September 1, 2015, so heirs owe none. A probate case should open within four years of a death. The small estate affidavit is available only to estates of $75,000 or less apart from the homestead.

County clerks record deeds. Heirs should bring the death certificate, any will and a recent tax statement to the first buyer meeting, since the title company will ask who has legal power to sign.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Selling with tax debt

Unpaid taxes leave the January 1 lien on the house, and penalty plus interest start on February 1. If nothing is paid, a taxing unit may sue and have the property auctioned.

Closing a sale first sidesteps all of that. The title company deducts the balance from your proceeds, so request a payoff figure early and compare offers by what remains afterward.

From accepted offer to keys

Once you accept, a title company takes over the paperwork. Expect it to search the record, ask each lender for a payoff figure and look at your parcel's tax standing. It then drafts a deed and a settlement statement. Read both before closing day and ask about any line you cannot explain.

At the table a notary witnesses your signature. After the deed is recorded, payoffs and charges are subtracted and the balance goes to you. Cash purchases skip a lender appraisal, so the date holds more easily. Disclose repairs, storm damage or a tenant early, schedule your move so the house is empty at handover, and keep your own copy of every signed page.

Frequently asked questions

How big is Houston?

Houston covers 640.44 square miles of land and counts 2,397,315 residents at the 2025 estimate. Verify the county and appraisal district for your own address before you rely on any tax figure.

Does Houston zone land?

Not citywide. Voters turned it down, but private deed restrictions and the city's plat and permit rules still apply, so read your restrictions.

Can I protest my Houston property value?

Yes. File with the appraisal review board by May 15, or within 30 days of receiving your notice if that is later. The Harris Central Appraisal District site accepts online filing.

Where do I find the plat for my lot?

After approval, plats are filed with the Harris County Clerk's records office. The city's planning site offers a map viewer and a Plat Tracker that search by address.

Does $277,800 predict my sale price?

That is a citywide midpoint from the 2020 to 2024 survey. Your own house needs written offers or an appraisal.

Sell Your San Antonio House for Cash

Selling in San Antonio?
We buy San Antonio houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

Selling in a big city market

San Antonio sits at the head of the San Antonio River in Bexar County. Interstate 10, Interstates 35 and 37, Loop 410 and State Loop 1604 cut the city into very different pockets, and blocks inside and outside the loops can vary a lot in age, price and commute. A citywide average tells you little, so anchor your asking price to what sold close by.

  • Compare recent sales within a mile or two of your address.
  • Note whether the house is inside Loop 410, between the loops or beyond 1604.
  • Pull up the flood map when your lot backs onto the river or a creek.

Choosing how to sell

Going through a broker rewards patience and a house in good repair. Investors fit better when the house needs work or your deadline is fixed.

San Antonio draws a wide range of buyers, so bids vary. A retail sale often produces the highest number, but it comes with inspections, showings and lender conditions. Skipping the agent saves the commission, but then the photos, the ads and the contracts are yours. Investors buy as-is on the date you pick, and they subtract repair and resale costs from what they offer. Line the bids up by what lands in your pocket once every cost is out.

  • Listing: the house is updated and the date can move.
  • Investor sale: a lien, an empty inherited house or tenant trouble.
  • Before signing, read who pays title, recording and repair credits.

Who sets value and who collects

Two offices touch your bill. BCAD puts the value on your property, and the Bexar County Tax Assessor-Collector is where the money goes. BCAD does not accept tax payments, so send payment questions to the assessor-collector.

For 2026, notices went to new owners and to owners whose value rose $1,000 or more, and a protest does not require a notice. Values are fixed as of January 1 across the state. Bills show up in October, and January 31 is the last day to pay without penalty. Every taxing unit on your lot sets its own rate, so your bill is the sum of several.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your San Antonio house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Property tax dates

Six dates shape the year for a Bexar County owner.

Texas property tax schedule for Bexar County owners
DateWhat it means
January 1Valuation date and lien date
April 30Common exemption filing cutoff
May 15Usual protest deadline
July 20Review board approves appraisal records
September 29Deadline for most units to adopt rates
February 1Delinquency begins on unpaid taxes

The full list is on the Comptroller calendar.

Back taxes before you sell

Get the balance from the Bexar County Tax Assessor-Collector, then plan to clear it before closing day. Selling the house does not erase the lien.

An account that slips past January starts February with a 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest. Come July the penalty is 12 percent, while interest continues to accrue. If collection lawyers get involved, up to a fifth more may be added. A homestead owner may ask for an installment plan, and some offices stretch it to 36 months. If the account goes to suit, a tax sale can follow, and the former owner can claim surplus proceeds for two years.

  • If you are appealing a value, pay at least the part nobody disputes.
  • Save each receipt.
  • Tell the closer about any plan in place, since the payoff figure depends on it.

Homestead exemptions

Your main tool is the residence homestead exemption. Extra relief exists for age, for disability and for service-connected disability.

A school district takes $140,000 off a homestead's value, and another $60,000 comes off for owners who are seniors or disabled. Individual taxing units may add an exemption of their own, up to 20 percent of value but never under $5,000. A yearly 10 percent cap limits how fast a homestead's appraised value can grow. Depending on rating, a service-disabled owner gets $5,000 to $12,000 off, and at 100 percent the entire homestead is exempt. An heir missing from the recorded deed brings an affidavit, a death certificate and a recent utility bill.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy San Antonio houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Occupants who will not leave

You can remove someone who stays after being told to go through a justice court case. Property Code chapter 24B also lets you ask the sheriff or constable to act, but only in narrow cases.

The shortcut applies only when the person refused to leave, the property was closed to the public at entry, no suit is pending between the two of you, and the occupant is no relative and no past or present tenant. An owner who removes someone wrongly can be sued. Tenants normally receive three days' notice. The writ of possession cannot go out until six days after judgment. Some investors will buy with the occupant still inside and deal with it themselves, which spares you the wait.

Recording the deed

Your deed gets recorded with the Bexar County clerk, after a notary or comparable officer witnesses the signature. Recording costs $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for each page after, with other records fees on top. In most sales the title company handles the filing.

Selling an inherited house

Heirs have several routes to clear title. The right one depends on what the owner left and what the house owes.

With a will, the executor or an heir files it for probate, which Texas permits for four years after death. When no administration is needed, the muniment of title order and the will get recorded with the county clerk. No will? A small estate affidavit can serve for modest estates. A deed naming a beneficiary and recorded before the owner's death moves the house outside probate, and a Lady Bird deed lets the owner keep selling rights while alive. Expect the closer to ask for whichever paper applies.

  • Order certified copies of the death certificate.
  • Find the last recorded deed for the parcel.
  • Ask the appraisal district about the homestead exemption before the next tax year.
You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Foreclosure timeline

Most Texas mortgages allow a sale without a court case, so the clock runs fast.

Under federal rules a servicer generally cannot begin until the home loan is over 120 days past due. A default notice then opens a 20 day period to bring the loan current. At least 21 days before the auction, the sale notice has to be mailed, posted at the courthouse and filed with the clerk. The auction falls on a first Tuesday. If that Tuesday lands on January 1 or July 4, it moves to the Wednesday. Selling before the date can preserve equity and spare you a foreclosure on your record.

Reading your Bexar County bill

Your bill is a stack of separate rates, one for each taxing unit that touches your lot, so two houses a mile apart can owe quite different amounts. Pull the BCAD record for your parcel and read it line by line: the value, the exemptions on file and the units listed. A buyer from out of town may not know that Bexar County values are fixed on January 1 while bills do not arrive until October. Explain that gap, and give the figure from the assessor-collector rather than a guess. Where a protest is pending, say so, because a lower value would change what the buyer carries.

Neighborhood differences to explain

Inside Loop 410 you may be selling a house of real age, with older wiring and plumbing that an inspector will flag. Between the loops and out toward 1604, buyers expect newer systems and will compare lots and commutes. Say plainly which kind of block you are on, and match your bid requests to it. An investor who knows the area will price the roof and the foundation within minutes, so a seller who has already priced them avoids a long haggle. Photos of recent work and any warranty papers speak louder than adjectives.

Cash sale checklist

If you go with a cash buyer, line up a few things early. Carry your photo ID, your deed or inheritance papers and the newest tax statement. Have the title company quote you a payoff on every lien. Get the closing date in writing. Read the settlement statement ahead of time so each fee has a name beside it.

Frequently asked questions

Which office collects San Antonio property tax?

Payments go to the Bexar County Tax Assessor-Collector. The Bexar Central Appraisal District does not take them.

Do I need a notice to protest my value in San Antonio?

No. You can file a protest without a notice. Check any notice you get for the cutoff, which most years falls in mid May.

What homestead exemption do school districts give?

School districts deduct $140,000 from the value, plus $60,000 more when the owner is a senior or disabled.

What happens to the lien when a San Antonio house sells?

The lien stays attached, so the title company pays any old tax from your proceeds at closing.

When do foreclosure auctions occur near San Antonio?

On a first Tuesday, during daytime hours, after a sale notice at least three weeks earlier.

Sell My House Fast in Dallas, TX: Options, Costs and Cash Offers

Selling in Dallas?

Getting a Dallas house sold in a hurry

In Dallas you may hand the house to an agent, sell it yourself or deal directly with a cash buyer. An agent reaches the widest audience, selling yourself saves commission, and a cash buyer shortens the clock.

Whichever path you take, start by collecting the vesting deed, each lender's latest statement, tax bills for every taxing unit and any city notices. Then you can rank offers by the money you actually receive.

  • Check whose name is on the deed.
  • Request payoff letters for every lien.
  • Photograph each room before showings.
  • Keep receipts for repairs you made.

Describing your house by era

The city expanded outward for over a century, taking in East Dallas in 1890 and Oak Cliff in 1904, with later subdivisions built mostly to the north and east. A house from the 1920s near Swiss Avenue and a 1990s suburban home raise very different inspection questions, so describe yours by its era and say what has been updated.

Historic districts and landmark rules

Some streets carry landmark rules. The Landmark Commission has designated buildings and neighborhoods including Swiss Avenue, Munger Place, South Boulevard-Park Row and State-Thomas.

A house inside a designated area may face city review of exterior changes, so find out what applies before a buyer makes plans. Preservation Dallas, which began in the 1970s as the Historic Preservation League, is another place owners go for guidance.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Dallas house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Dallas County recording office

Most of Dallas sits in Dallas County, where the County Clerk's Recording Division handles deeds and liens. The office works out of the Records Building and handles about 400,000 recordings a year.

Dallas County recording office
TopicRequirement
LocationRecords Building, 500 Elm Street, Suite 2100
HoursWeekdays, closed on court-approved holidays
Court documentsA certified copy, authenticated by the court or clerk
ID rulePhoto ID required for documents conveying property, effective July 1, 2023
Online copiesElectronic certified copies can be bought on the clerk's website

Part of the city extends into Collin, Denton, Kaufman and Rockwall counties, so confirm which clerk holds your parcel.

Dallas property taxes at a sale

Dallas bills come from the county, the city, the school system and other local units. Value is set each January 1, which is also when the lien attaches, and protests generally close in mid-May.

Mailings begin near October 1, and unpaid bills are delinquent after January 31. The January 1 owner stays liable, so ask the title company how closing treats each unit's bill. On the relief side, a school district exempts $140,000 of a homestead, and seniors and disabled owners get another $60,000 and a school tax ceiling. The appraisal district can tell you which units add a local exemption.

Schools, roads and parks

Commute and schools top most buyers' lists. Interstate highways 20, 30, 35 and 45 cross the city, and the Dallas Independent School District has more than 155,000 students. Parks cover about 50,000 acres, anchored by White Rock Lake, Bachman Lake and Lake Cliff. Confirm school boundaries for a specific address with the district, not by neighborhood name.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Dallas houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

If a Dallas house is behind on its mortgage

Foreclosure on a home loan normally cannot begin until the payment is 120 days late. After the default notice you have 20 days, and the sale notice goes out three or more weeks before the first-Tuesday auction, held where the commissioners court designates.

Anything left over after the debt goes to junior lienholders and then to you, while a deficiency claim must come within two years. A sale ahead of the auction keeps price and closing date in your control. Your servicer can give you the payoff and the scheduled sale date.

Code concerns and city services

The city runs a 311 service, and its Planning and Development site lists code concerns, missed garbage, street repair, loose animals and water line locates among frequently requested items. Code Compliance and permitting pages sit on the same site.

Check for open code complaints or unpermitted work at the address, then fix or disclose them before listing. Parks, libraries and the zoo are quality-of-life points buyers like to see in a description.

Renting instead of selling

That is possible, but short-term rentals come with city registration and hotel occupancy tax. Short-Term Rentals (HOT) registration appears among the city's licenses, so confirm what is required before advertising.

A long-term tenant leaves only through a justice court eviction suit, and no writ of possession can issue until six days after judgment. Selling during an active lease means buyers will ask for the lease and the payment history.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Pricing in a city this large

Dallas values vary block by block. Two houses a mile apart can sit under different school boundaries, different taxing units and even different counties. Anchor your price to recent sales near your address, and be ready to say what makes the house stand out: its era, updates, lot or landmark district.

When a cash offer competes with a listing, ask the buyer to show how the number was reached. Repair estimates, holding costs and resale risk should all be visible. A fair offer can withstand questions.

Documents for the title search

Title will want the vesting deed, a payoff letter per lender, tax bills for every taxing unit, any lease and the name of each person who must sign. A house held through an estate also needs the probate papers or the recorded instrument giving someone authority to sell.

Send these early. In a city with several taxing units and sometimes more than one county involved, the title search is where timelines stretch, and a complete file moves it along.

Disclosing what you know

A buyer's inspector will find many defects anyway, so be upfront. Write down roof leaks, past foundation work, drainage problems and any open permit. Fixing everything is not required, but a clear list reduces the chance of a late-stage fight over the price.

How a Dallas cash sale proceeds

The buyer tours the house and submits an offer. When you say yes, the title company checks the records of the right county, requests payoffs and pulls a tax certificate for each taxing unit. You name the closing date and sign, and funds arrive once liens and any tax balance are cleared.

You skip open houses, loan approval and the risk of a short appraisal. You give up some price, because the buyer discounts for repairs. Set the written offer beside a listing's net after commission, fixes and months of holding costs.

Frequently asked questions

How long does a Dallas closing usually take?

Plan on a few weeks for a cash sale and longer when a buyer needs financing and an appraisal. Payoff letters and a title search set the minimum, and a lien or probate issue can stretch it.

Which clerk records a deed for a Dallas house?

Whichever county holds the parcel, which is Dallas County for most addresses. A few Dallas parcels lie in Collin, Denton, Kaufman or Rockwall counties. Bring photo ID if you file a conveyance in person.

Are taxes split at a Dallas closing?

A closing usually apportions the year's bill between seller and buyer. Because the January 1 lien stays with the house, the title company checks each taxing unit and holds back funds for anything unpaid.

Can I protest my Dallas appraisal before selling?

Yes, until mid-May or 30 days after your notice arrives, whichever comes later. A lower value trims the bill the buyer inherits, though it does not by itself change the sale price.

What if a Dallas house has a lien or back taxes?

Sale funds pay it off, or it is cleared before closing. Delinquent taxes cannot be skipped, since the lien follows the property. Have the title company list every payoff so you know your true net.

Fast-sale routes in Fort Worth

Owners in Fort Worth have three ordinary choices: an all-cash bid, an agent listing, or a sale to an investor who will renovate. Paying cash buys you speed and certainty at some cost in price. Listing buys a larger audience at a cost in time.

The city is large and varied. It has 334,230 households, 56.7 percent of them owner occupied, and single-family homes cover 24.1 percent of the land. A bungalow near downtown, a ranch house on the far north side and a newer subdivision near Alliance are three different sales with three different buyer pools, so ask any buyer how they priced your specific house, not just the area.

  • Cash offer: often as-is, with no lender appraisal and a date you negotiate.
  • Agent listing: staging, photos, showings, and repair negotiation after the inspection.
  • Investor purchase: common for dated homes, rentals with tenants, or houses with code or foundation concerns.

Whichever you choose, ask for an itemized estimate of your take-home.

Fort Worth's size and your price

Fort Worth is home to over one million people and was the fastest-growing large city in the nation, gaining 170,237 residents between 2010 and 2020. Projections reach 1,306,400 by 2050. Steady demand helps a seller. Vacant land makes up 37.6 percent of the city's land use, though, and new construction on it gives buyers alternatives to your house.

The city is served by 13 independent school districts, so the district name on a house matters as much as the city name. Check the district for your exact address before you advertise.

Property tax owed at closing

An unpaid balance for the year stays with the house regardless of who holds title when the bill comes. The county tax office can print a statement that shows each unit's share, which matters because school, county, city and special district bills vary by address. Penalties begin in February and keep climbing into summer.

ChargeRule
First penaltySix percent, added the first day of February
InterestOne percent a month with no cap

Collection lawyerUp to 20 percent extra if the unit has a contract

Any balance is paid by the closing agent, so get the payoff figure early.

Exemptions when you move

For the most part, no. A homestead exemption stops when you stop owning. The one carry-over is the school tax ceiling for older or disabled owners, which can follow you in proportion to a new Texas homestead.

  • After the exemption is first claimed, a homestead's appraised value can rise by no more than 10 percent a year.
  • Any local taxing unit may adopt an exemption of up to 20 percent of value.
  • Owners with a disability rating may get partial or full relief on the home.

Let the appraisal district know about the sale so your account closes properly, and keep your final tax statement for your records in case a question comes up later.

Inherited, in default or rented

All three have a workable path. Heirs can use a muniment of title to pass a house when no administration is needed. A lender generally waits until a loan is more than 120 days late, and the default notice includes time to cure, which leaves room to sell instead of losing the house.

For a rented house, many buyers will take the property with the lease intact, which can spare you an eviction. If you need it empty, the process starts with written notice and then moves to justice court.

In all three cases, tell buyers up front. A cash buyer who knows about an heir's signature, a default date or a tenant can price the situation. A buyer who learns about it at the end tends to cut the offer or walk.

Filing the deed

The clerk of the county where the land is located records the deed. Your closing agent normally submits it, and the fee is taken from closing funds, which you can confirm on the settlement statement. A notary or similar officer has to acknowledge the signature first.

  • Ask your lender for a payoff letter.
  • Find the last recorded deed and releases of any old liens.
  • Run a lien search for judgments and tax liens.
  • Leave keys, garage openers and warranty papers for the new owner.

Local features that help a listing

Parks and open space draw buyers. The city maintains 300 parks covering 13,000 acres, and the Fort Worth Nature Center and Refuge spans 3,621 acres with more than 20 miles of trails. Mention the nearest park, trail or transit route in your listing.

Large public projects, including a $700 million convention center expansion, can shift traffic and nearby demand over several years. Ask a local agent or the city planning office what is under way near your street before you set a price, and keep records of any recent upgrades for the buyer.

What the closing table looks like

At signing you will receive a settlement statement that lists every dollar. The sale price sits at the top and the deductions follow: the lender's payoff, your share of the tax, title and recording charges, and whatever the contract assigns to you. The remainder is your net. Check each line against the contract, and ask the closing agent about any entry you cannot identify.

A rental sale may add prorated rent and the tenant's deposit to the statement. An inherited house requires everyone with signing authority over the estate to attend or send signed paperwork beforehand.

Build your move around funding. Proceeds typically arrive the same day or the next business day after recording, so hold off on any purchase that depends on that money until it is in your account.

Preparing for a quick closing

A fast sale starts with a tidy file. Before asking for bids, round up your deed, a contact at the lender who can issue the payoff, this year's tax statement and any receipts for roof, foundation or plumbing jobs. Then walk the house with a notepad and write down every defect you already know about. An inspector will uncover them regardless, and a list in your own hand makes a buyer trust the rest of what you say.

Judge each bid on four points: the amount that reaches you, the closing date, the repairs you are expected to make, and who covers title and recording costs. Insist on the bid in writing with an expiration date. Once you accept, an escrow officer orders the title search, clears any liens and sets a signing time. You sign with a notary, the loan is retired, and the remainder is wired to you.

Frequently asked questions

Can I sell in Fort Worth while a mortgage is open?

Yes. Your lender is paid first at the closing table and the remainder is yours. Request a payoff letter that stays valid through your closing date.

Which clerk records my Fort Worth deed?

The clerk for the county that holds the lot. Your tax bill names the county, so check it before you file.

Must I fix things before a cash sale in Fort Worth?

No, as-is buyers take the house in its current state. Roof, foundation and plumbing issues lower the offer, so set it beside a listing net after repairs.

Who pays unpaid Fort Worth property tax at a sale?

The closing agent clears the balance from your proceeds. Ask the county tax office for a statement before you sign.

Can a Fort Worth rental be sold with the tenant inside?

Yes. Many buyers accept the lease. If you want the house empty, written notice and a justice court case come first.

Choosing a sale route when you need to move fast

Austin owners usually pick among a standard listing, a sale they manage themselves, and a direct cash purchase. A cash buyer will close on your chosen day and accepts the property as is. A listing depends on showings, an appraisal and whatever financing the next buyer arranges.

Austin is expensive. The middle owner-occupied home is valued at $555,300, and just 43.4 percent of households own where they live. Because renters are so common, many Austin houses have been rentals or could become one, which shapes what an investor will pay and how quickly a deal can move.

  • Standard listing: the choice for an updated house priced close to nearby sales, if you can spare weeks for showings and a buyer's lender.
  • Self-managed sale: you set the price, draft the contract and negotiate, with a title company still handling the closing.
  • Cash purchase: a fit for deferred maintenance, an inherited house, a tenant who is staying or a firm deadline.

Austin household and housing costs

Austin passed one million residents: the July 2025 estimate is 1,002,632, roughly 4.6 percent over the April 2020 baseline of 958,151. In 2010 the count was 790,390.

Creeks, lakes and your lot

Austin's lakes came from dams on the Colorado River built in 1940 and 1941, which formed Lake Austin and Lake Travis and stopped the floods that had struck as late as 1935. Buyers know where the water is. A house next to a creek or on a lake invites flood questions that a house on higher ground does not.

Additions draw scrutiny as well. Since the 1970s, neighborhood groups and environmental ordinances have protected creeks, lakes and wooded hills. If you added a room without a permit, or your lot touches a creek, a buyer's inspector will ask. Pull permit records and any flood paperwork together before you list.

Short-term rental licenses

Each license is personal to the person holding it. Operating licenses are non-transferable, so anyone buying your house who wants nightly guests has to start a new application.

The council made short-term rental a secondary use on residential property in every zoning district in February 2025, for license holders. October 2025 changes extended each license to two years and removed the occupancy certificate and proof of insurance for new applicants and renewals. A tenant may hold one with the landlord's permission.

  • On single-family sites one person can run two units, and any further units must sit 1,000 feet apart.
  • For multifamily sites the limit is whichever is larger, one unit or a tenth of the units.
  • The required local contact has to be in Travis, Williamson, Hays, Bastrop or Caldwell County and able to respond within two hours.
  • Neighbors within 100 feet get written notice of the contact when a license is issued or renewed.
  • Booking platforms must display license numbers and take down unlicensed listings on the city's request.

Land in the extraterritorial jurisdiction needs neither a city license nor local hotel tax, so look at the jurisdiction map on the city's short-term rental page before you tell a buyer what is permitted.

Homestead exemptions and the appraisal cap

An owner who lives in the house probably pays tax on less than the market value a buyer sees in the listing. School districts exempt $140,000 of a homestead, and its appraised value cannot rise more than 10 percent a year apart from new improvements.

The cap belongs to the owner who claimed the exemption, so an investor begins without it. Ask the title company to estimate the buyer's first full-year bill so the contract holds no surprise. Owners over 65, or with a disability, get an extra $60,000 school exemption and a school tax ceiling that can follow them to a replacement Texas homestead.

Exemptions are granted by Travis Central Appraisal District, while bills are collected by the Travis County tax office. The latter's tax breaks page links to each one, and the Comptroller's limitations page covers the cap and the ceiling.

Steps and paperwork to close

Closing centers on the deed. The county clerk will not record it until a notary has acknowledged it or two witnesses have sworn to it.

  1. Locate your deed and tax statement, and ask lenders for payoff letters.
  2. Request payoffs for liens too. A tax lien attaches every January 1.
  3. Confirm which county records deeds for your parcel, since the city covers a lot of ground.
  4. Sign the settlement papers and the deed, then let the title company file it.

With an inherited house, title becomes the question: executor's deed, muniment of title order, or affidavit of heirship. The affidavit is only a sworn statement, and no law forces a third party to accept it, so find out early which document the title insurer will honor.

Unpaid taxes at sale

You can sell with back taxes owing, as long as they are paid first. Delinquency begins February 1, when a six percent penalty and one percent interest apply. Since the lien stays with the property, closing pays the balance from your proceeds.

Request a payoff figure from the Travis County tax office before you settle on a closing date. Any earlier year still open should be dealt with first, so the title company can issue a clean commitment. Keep the receipt.

Comparing offers on an Austin house

Look at the amount that reaches your account and the date it arrives. A higher price weighed down by repair credits, a slow financing window and a commission can net less than a lower cash bid with a firm date.

Press each buyer on tenants, unpermitted work and open code complaints, and find out whether the bid holds up through an inspection. Write down each deadline, then choose the offer that covers your payoff and matches your move. If two offers look close, the one with fewer conditions is usually the safer one to accept.

Ask for proof of funds from a cash buyer and a pre-approval letter from a financed one. Both are easy to produce for a serious buyer, and they tell you quickly which offers can actually close.

Frequently asked questions

Can an Austin short-term rental license be handed to the new owner?

No, licenses stay with the holder. The buyer applies for a new one, and handing over your license history can smooth that application.

Is Austin in Travis County?

Yes, it is the county seat. Still, your tax bill names the county of record for your parcel, and that decides which clerk files the deed.

Does my homestead tax cap pass to the person who buys my Austin house?

No. Each owner's cap starts the January after that owner first qualifies, so a buyer who moves in and applies begins a fresh one. A buyer who rents the house out cannot claim it at all.

What if my Austin house has unpaid property taxes?

It comes out of your proceeds at closing, as the lien follows the house. A bill left unpaid is delinquent from February 1 and picks up a six percent penalty and one percent interest.

How big is Austin?

About 1,002,632 people in 2025, 4.6 percent more than the 2020 base, spread over 319.94 square miles of land.

Small landlords and renovators do. They subtract the work from their offer and bring their own crews, so you avoid estimates and a lender's repair demands.

Does the size of the market slow a sale?

City rules to check before you sell

No city inspection is needed to sell, yet buyers ask about permits for earlier work. Find out whether a garage conversion, added room or porch went through the permit process, and ask the City of El Paso which office covers your address.

Foreclosure on an El Paso house

The El Paso County Clerk files the instrument once a notary has witnessed the signature. Charges are per page and shift over time, so request the clerk's current schedule before closing.

From accepted offer to the closing table

After you accept an offer, the title company opens an escrow file, searches the records and requests a payoff from your lender. Send over the folder of papers in the first few days. Missing permits, a lien nobody remembered or an unsigned lease are the usual reasons a closing date slips.

At closing you sign the deed and a settlement statement before a notary. The deed goes to the county clerk, the lender is paid, the year's tax is settled, and the balance comes to you. If a tenant lives there, agree on the move-out date in writing before you sign.

The county tax office collects, while the appraisal district sets the value. Ask for your balance and a tax certificate before the closing date.

Yes. A sale ahead of the auction date pays the lender out of the proceeds and can leave you with equity. The notice period is short, so move early.

Who buys in Arlington and how fast can they close?

Expect three kinds of buyers in Arlington: families with a mortgage, individuals paying cash, and investors who will take a house whatever its shape. How fast you close is up to them. Cash can fund as soon as title work wraps up, but a loan has to clear an appraisal and underwriting first.

A short-term rental permit does not pass to the new owner. Arlington issues each one to a single owner for a single address, with no transfer or assignment allowed, so the next owner has to file a new application.

Property tax dates

Values are set as of January 1, and whoever owns the house that day is responsible for the year's tax. Bills reach Arlington owners around October 1, and homestead value notices arrive near April 1. To dispute a value, file a protest with the appraisal review board by May 15 or 30 days after the notice, whichever comes later.

Most accounts are due January 31. Splitting the bill in two is allowed, with halves due November 30 and June 30. Small agreements like these, written into the contract, prevent last-minute friction on the day the house changes hands. Money changes hands once both sides have signed, and the deed then goes to the county clerk. Keep the settlement statement: each payoff taken from your proceeds appears on it, and you may need that record later.

Questions a buyer will ask about your Arlington house

Expect questions about the age of the roof, the state of the foundation and whether the wiring was updated. Buyers also want to know if the property was rented to guests, if any city notice is open, and what the yearly tax runs. Answer from paper where you can: receipts for repairs, the tax statement, the permit and inspection file for any rental.

An honest, organized answer sets you apart from sellers who scramble after the inspection report arrives. It also helps a cash buyer move quickly, because fewer unknowns mean fewer reasons to lower the offer.

Cash offer or listing?

Work out what each route puts in your pocket once payoffs, repairs and waiting time are counted. Listing can bring a higher price for a well-kept house. Selling for cash gets rid of the repair list, the open houses and the danger of a buyer's loan collapsing.

Insist that offers be written out with the price, closing date, settlement charges and any exit clauses. Find out if the buyer will take the house with a tenant in it or with city notices still open. Take away your payoffs and carrying costs, then pick the number and date that suit you.

For a vacant house or one needing big repairs, ask each buyer who handles utilities, insurance and access until closing. Buyers differ more on these points than on headline price, and a written answer protects you if the closing slips.

Frequently asked questions

Will a buyer pay for a house in Arlington that needs a new roof?

Yes. Investors and cash buyers routinely accept roof work and lower the offer to match. You repair nothing before closing, so weigh the bid against a repaired house's price minus your own repair bills.

Can I sell a house in Arlington that has been used as an Airbnb?

Yes. The permit does not convey, so the buyer applies fresh and must pass the city's inspection. Tell buyers plainly whether the address sits inside an eligible zone.

What happens to unpaid tax when my Arlington sale closes?

The amount owed is taken from your proceeds when you sign, because the lien remains on the house. Request a payoff figure from the tax office early to avoid a surprise on the closing statement.

Where is the deed filed after an Arlington sale?

The county clerk for the county that holds the house, which is Tarrant County for most Arlington addresses. If your lot is near a county line, check the tax bill.

How large is Arlington?

About 402,134 residents in 2025, with 142,455 households and 95.87 square miles of land.

Sell My House Fast in Corpus Christi, TX: Options, Costs and Cash Offers

Cash Home Buyers in Texas

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Corpus Christi?

What shapes a Corpus Christi sale

Two things matter most: condition and timing. A well kept house can do well on the market, but one with storm damage, an estate attached or tenants inside often sells faster to a buyer who accepts it as it is.

Corpus Christi is a seaport on the west end of Corpus Christi Bay, the county seat of Nueces County and the largest city on the South Texas coast. It sits where Interstate 37 meets U.S. highways 77 and 181, 210 miles southwest of Houston. Salt air, wind and storm history make roofs, windows and foundations the first things coastal buyers check.

  • Open listing: widest reach for a house that shows well.
  • Owner sale: no commission, more paperwork for you.
  • Cash purchase: quicker and as-is, useful after storm damage or for an estate.

Keeping storm records

A hurricane on September 14, 1919 destroyed much of the North Beach area and the central business district, and the city has lived with coastal weather ever since. Buyers, insurers and lenders often ask about past damage. Keep repair receipts, permits for storm work and insurance claim records together, since they back up every answer you give.

Short-term rental rules

Under city rules, renting any part or all of a residence for under 30 days, and for at least 12 hours, makes it a short-term rental, and every such property must be registered. Permits are valid for the calendar year and renewed each January. Hotel occupancy tax filing applies to short-term rentals, hotels and bed and breakfasts.

The ordinance approved on June 28, 2022 allows rentals with restrictions in single-family districts citywide, except in single-family districts within the Padre and Mustang Island area plan.

Short-term rental permit types

Type 1Owner or operator lives thereMoratorium on new permits while the city reviews rules
Type 2No one lives there15 percent of a block face, first come first served

The city paused new Type 1 permits while staff prepare changes for council, and permits valid through December 31, 2026 stay active. It also directed staff to apply the density limit to renewals, with at least one Type 2 rental per block face. Rules may have changed, so ask Development Services at (361) 826-3240 for the current version.

Applications ask for owner and agent contacts, a floor plan with sleeping areas, a guest maximum and exits, and a 24-hour contact person. Ask the city for the current fee. Do not tell a buyer a permit transfers with the house unless the city confirms it.

Where deeds and tax records live

City parcels in Nueces County are filed at the Nueces County clerk, and the appraisal district for that county sets values. Addresses near the city edge can lie in a neighboring county, so your latest tax bill is the quickest check.

To be accepted for filing, a deed must be acknowledged or have two witnesses. The clerk manual's price list puts page one at $5.00 and each later page at $4.00, with surcharges for names past five and for records funds. The clerk can quote today's rates, and your title company normally does the filing itself.

What happens if property taxes go unpaid

Miss January 31 and the bill is delinquent on February 1. That day interest of one percent a month begins and a six percent penalty attaches, climbing to 12 percent by July 1. An attorney for the taxing unit may tack on up to 20 percent more.

Each year's tax lien forms on January 1 and travels with the house through any sale, which means a buyer cannot get clear title while back taxes remain. The title company settles the balance from your proceeds at closing. Seniors, disabled owners and owners with a disabled veteran exemption may use installments, and some collectors offer payment plans up to 36 months on a homestead.

A land contract or an occupant in the house

Under a contract for deed, sometimes called an installment land contract, title stays with the seller until the buyer has paid everything. Texas Property Code chapter 5, subchapter D governs those for residences, and the purchaser has a statutory right to cancel, so get legal advice before selling a house under such a contract.

When someone stays after being told to go, Property Code chapter 24B lets an owner ask the sheriff or constable to remove them, but only if conditions are met. One is that the occupant is not a relative or a current or former tenant. A removal done wrongly can bring a lawsuit. Failing that, the normal path is a justice court eviction suit.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Corpus Christi houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What to gather before an offer

Pull together the deed, loan payoff, tax bill, insurance claim history and permits for any storm work. Coastal buyers raise flood and wind coverage early, so know what your policy covers and which company writes it.

Line up offers by net proceeds and by weeks to closing. A cash buyer may close sooner and will price in repairs, while a listing may net more after a longer wait. Have each buyer state in writing who pays title, recording and the tax split.

  • Does the buyer accept the house with storm damage unrepaired?
  • Can an open insurance claim be assigned, or must it be settled first?
  • How soon are funds available once the title company clears the file?

Anyone relocating or settling an estate may prize a firm closing date above a few extra dollars, so give certainty weight next to price.

Pricing a coastal house

Buyers on the coast look past paint and flooring to the envelope of the house. Expect questions about the age of the roof, whether windows are impact rated, how the foundation has held up and whether the house has ever flooded. Answer them with documents, not impressions.

If repairs are still undone, say so early. A buyer who learns about unrepaired damage at inspection will renegotiate, while one who knew from the start has already priced it in. A cash buyer will quote you for the house as it stands, which can save you from paying contractors before you sell.

Choosing between offers

Compare more than price. A buyer paying cash can often close in a few weeks, while one using a loan needs an appraisal and an inspection first. Put each offer's closing date, repair terms and title costs side by side, then pick the combination that fits your move.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

How a cash sale works here

The buyer looks at the house, usually once, and makes a written offer reflecting repairs. After you accept, the title company searches the records and orders payoffs, and you pick the closing date. With no lender, no appraisal can delay the schedule. Roof, window and foundation condition drive most of the discount on a coastal house.

Frequently asked questions

Is Corpus Christi the county seat of Nueces County?

Yes. City parcels are recorded at the Nueces County clerk's office.

May I operate a short-term rental in Corpus Christi?

Only with a registration permit. The city requires one for any rental under 30 days, and the rules are under review, so ask Development Services which permit type applies and whether new ones are issued.

What happens to a rental permit when I sell?

Do not assume it carries over. Permits are issued annually and renewals face density rules, so get the city's answer before you describe the permit to a buyer.

When do property taxes go delinquent?

On February 1 for most bills. Penalty and interest begin that day, and the penalty grows each month through July 1.

Do I need to keep hurricane repair records?

Keep them. Buyers, insurers and lenders often ask about past damage, and receipts back up your answers.

Is a quick sale realistic for a Plano house?

Often, though condition and deadline decide it. Plano sellers usually weigh an investor's cash offer against an agent listing, with a small repair project in between.

This is an expensive market: the median home value is $465,900, and most buyers need a loan. A loan means an appraisal and an inspection, two spots where deals slip, which is why hurried sellers often prefer cash.

  • Cash: no lender to wait on, and you choose the closing day.
  • Listing: more buyers see it and the price may be higher, at the cost of prep time.
  • Repairs first: sensible only when the fix is cheap and visible, like paint, flooring or a roof leak.

Plano at a glance

Plano lies in southwestern Collin County on U.S. Highway 75, roughly fifteen miles north of Dallas. It was laid out and incorporated in 1873, and for nearly a century it stayed a farm town. Then Dallas pushed north: 3,695 residents in 1960 became 17,872 in 1970 and more than 72,000 by 1980. A 1970 land reappraisal raised taxes and helped end farming around town.

Today about 293,028 people live on 71.69 square miles of land. With so little open land left, your house competes with similar homes nearby. Look up its build year in your appraisal record, because age drives how buyers weigh the roof, foundation and plumbing.

Many buyers are corporate or professional workers, and the average commute is 25.4 minutes. A plain, accurate listing that is easy to forward to relatives reaches more households, and a quiet home office is a fair selling point.

A little Plano history that buyers still ask about

Rail shaped the early town. The Houston and Texas Central reached it in 1872, and a second line crossed in 1888. An 1881 fire destroyed fifty-two buildings and briefly left a tent city. The Farrel-Wilson Farmstead Museum, on a former sheep ranch, is described as the one remaining sign of that farming past.

Every September the city hosts balloon races and carries the nickname Balloon Capital of Texas. By the mid-1980s Plano had overtaken McKinney as the commercial and financial center of Collin County, and Frito-Lay and several computer makers were based here. Houses from that boom now run several decades old, so be ready for questions about original systems.

Rental rules when you sell

Plano requires each short-term rental in the city to be approved and registered, and the city's program points to a zoning map and the short-term rental part of the zoning ordinance.

A past or present rental use raises two questions for a buyer: is the address registered, and does the zoning allow the use to continue? Ask the city's Property Standards staff how your address is classified before you promise a buyer any rental income.

  • Collect any registration or approval paperwork for the address.
  • Give the buyer tenant names, lease end dates and deposit amounts in writing.
  • Read your owners' association documents if the subdivision has one, since many add their own leasing limits.

Property taxes in Plano

At a $465,900 median home value, the tax bill is big even at a modest rate, which is why buyers scrutinize it. Value is fixed as of January 1. A bill is delinquent after January 31, with penalty and interest starting February 1. Protests of value are generally due by May 15.

  • Homestead: $140,000 school exemption, and appraised value can grow only 10% a year.
  • Owners 65 or older, or disabled: another $60,000 and a school tax ceiling.
  • Ask the county tax office for your payoff and the title company for the proration.

Where the deed gets filed

Your deed is filed with the county clerk where the parcel sits, usually Collin County. The title company prepares it and you sign in front of a notary. Recording costs combine a first-page fee, a per-page fee after that and a handful of records fees, so ask the title company for the final figure.

After an owner's death the paperwork changes: depending on the estate, you may need an affidavit of death, an executor's deed, or a court order together with the will.

Loan default or an estate to settle

Where time is short, a direct sale can move faster than a listing. Texas foreclosure auctions land on first Tuesdays, so ask the servicer for the sale date and the reinstatement amount in writing. Probate of a will generally has to happen within four years of death, and estates up to $75,000, homestead aside, may use a small estate affidavit.

  • Behind on tax: ask the collector about an installment plan.
  • Estate: have it confirmed in writing who may sign.

Paperwork and questions before you take an offer

Pull together the deed, the latest tax bill and appraisal notice, the payoff contact at your lender and any lease. A homeowners association on your street means a status letter, which can take days, so ask for it early.

With each buyer, nail down who buys the title policy, how long closing takes and whether the price can change after a walkthrough. Be wary of anyone wanting a fee before an offer, or unwilling to write terms down. Mention a tenant, lien or estate on the very first call.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Comparing a cash offer with a listing

What matters is what you keep and when you get it. Take each offer's price, subtract commissions, repairs, carrying costs, concessions and title charges, and line the totals up side by side.

When prices are this high, a small percentage is a big sum, so a sound house in a popular school zone often earns more listed. A direct sale competes when there are deferred repairs, a tenant, a lien or probate. Keep every offer in writing, check dates and contingencies, and hold on to two for comparison.

What to expect from offer to closing

Saying yes sets the process moving. The title company opens a file, checks for liens, orders tax figures and books your signing; bring photo ID and every key. Your settlement statement spells out price, payoffs, prorated taxes and fees, and the balance is released once the deed is recorded.

A cash buyer skips the lender's appraisal and underwriting, so the date is less likely to slip. Request proof of funds and the earnest money figure, and do not pay anyone merely to receive an offer.

Frequently asked questions

Does Plano require registration for short-term rentals?

Yes. Every short-term rental operating in Plano must be approved and registered. Ask Property Standards how your address is classified before you list or accept an offer.

Why were Plano's farms replaced by houses?

Dallas grew northward in the 1970s. The population more than doubled by 1975 and again by 1980, and a 1970 land reappraisal raised taxes and helped end farming.

What is Plano's median household income?

It is $112,253 for 2020 to 2024. The median owner-occupied home value is $465,900 and median gross rent is $1,841, so buyers here are mostly dual-income households.

Which office records the deed on a Plano house?

The county clerk for the county where the parcel sits, usually Collin County. The title company confirms this and files the deed at closing.

How quickly can a Plano cash sale close?

Often in a few weeks when the title is clear. Liens, probate or tenants add time, so ask the buyer for a written closing plan.

Selling in Lubbock on a short timeline

A short timeline usually points to a cash buyer, while a full listing suits an owner who can wait. The choice turns on three things: the condition of the roof, plumbing and floors, any liens on the title, and how soon you need the money.

Texas Tech University, a large medical center and the farm trade give Lubbock steady demand. Near campus or a hospital, investors and renters bid alongside families, which gives even a dated house a market. The South Plains weather is hard on roofs, and inspectors and buyers look closely at hail damage and storm protection.

  • Agent listing: widest exposure, though showings, repair requests and lender timelines stretch the calendar.
  • Owner sale: skips the commission and puts pricing and paperwork on you.
  • Cash offer: quick close, no repairs, typically priced under a polished retail sale.

Who bills Lubbock property tax

The Lubbock Central Appraisal District handles valuation and tax collection. Texas levies no state property tax, so your bill is the sum of local rates. Owners in the Lubbock Cooper ISD should ask the district office which rate their bill uses.

Under state law the year's tax lien attaches January 1, and a bill still unpaid on February 1 is delinquent. In a sale, the closing statement shows how the year's bill was divided.

The district's home page warns that some firms charge a one-time processing fee to file a homestead exemption. Filing costs nothing.

Homestead breaks for Lubbock owners

Owners can file for a residence homestead exemption online through the district's property search. Besides the general exemption, the district lists separate ones for disabled owners, seniors, a veteran rated 100 percent disabled and certain surviving spouses.

  • School districts across Texas subtract $140,000 from a homestead's value, and seniors or disabled owners get $60,000 more off the school levy base.
  • Counting from the year after the exemption starts, a homestead's appraised value may rise by at most 10 percent a year.
  • A senior or disabled owner can defer taxes while living in the house. The deferred debt, penalty and interest then come due 181 days after the property stops qualifying.

Questions go to 806-762-5000. An exemption does not travel with the seller, so the next occupant files a fresh application.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Lubbock house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How to pay or look up taxes on a Lubbock house

Search the account on the district site, mail a check to P.O. Box 10568, Lubbock, TX 79408, drop it at 2109 Avenue Q, or pay online or by phone. Processing charges on card and online payments go to Certified Payments rather than the district.

Online and phone payment charges

Credit card2.19% of the amount paid, minimum $1.00
Debit card1% of the amount paid, minimum $1.00

The district also publishes GIS maps and takes documents and address changes by email, and the office welcomes visitors. If the title company needs a tax certificate, ask the district for one. An account that reaches tax foreclosure involves a notarized written-statement request, form 50-307, with a $10.00 fee in certified funds.

If you are late on the mortgage or taxes

Options shrink with each missed month, so move early. The lender owes you a default notice with twenty days to catch up, then an auction notice three weeks before the sale. Auctions run monthly, during daytime hours, in an area the county designates.

Back taxes work differently. On a homestead, a collector can offer a payment plan running as long as 36 months, and a written request made soon after payment may win penalty relief.

  • A sale ahead of the auction protects equity and keeps a foreclosure off your record.
  • Get the lender's payoff number in writing, and raise a short sale if the balance exceeds value.
  • Search county records for liens so nothing surprises the title company.

Estates and rented houses

Both can sell fast once the paperwork is sorted. An inherited house starts with the will. Probate is possible for four years after the death, and a muniment of title can let the will and court order substitute for a full administration. If there is no will, modest estates can use a small estate affidavit. An heirship affidavit is only a sworn statement, and a buyer may refuse it.

A rented house raises timing questions. Written notice to leave is normally three days, a justice court hears the case, and possession by writ is available six days after judgment. Cash buyers often accept a tenant in place, which skips that sequence.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Lubbock houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Filing the deed

The Lubbock County Clerk keeps the official records. The signature needs a notary's acknowledgment first. State caps and county charges differ, so request the clerk's fee schedule. The closing agent files the deed and pays from your proceeds.

Preparing the house and the paperwork

Lubbock buyers examine roofs first, so find out the roof's age and any hail repair history, and gather receipts. Add plumbing and floor records, then check county records for liens. If a past owner left an old lien behind, learn about it before a buyer's title search does.

Ask the appraisal district at 806-762-5000 for your account summary and exemption status. Ask your lender for a payoff figure in writing. With that folder assembled, a cash buyer can give a firm number quickly, and an agent can price a listing with confidence.

Reading a Lubbock closing statement

The statement lists every dollar that comes out of the sale price. Expect to see the payoff on your mortgage, your share of the year's property tax, any tax certificate fee, recording charges at the county clerk and the title company's own fee. If a collector's plan or a deferral is open on the account, the amount owed shows up here too. Review it a day early and ask about anything you do not recognize.

When an offer is cash, the statement tends to be shorter, because no lender fees are included. That is one more reason a cash sale can feel simpler even when the price is a bit lower.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

From offer to closing

  1. Gather the deed, the tax account details and the payoff letter.
  2. Compare a cash offer with what an agent expects to net you after repairs and commission.
  3. Select a title company and give it the account numbers.
  4. Sign before a notary.
  5. The closing agent files the deed with the Lubbock County Clerk and pays the costs from your proceeds.

A cash buyer without a lender usually closes sooner, since the wait for an appraisal and loan approval disappears.

Frequently asked questions

Does a Lubbock house with big repair needs still sell?

Yes. A cash buyer accepts the house as it sits, so an aging roof or old plumbing can stay unrepaired. Expect the offer to reflect repair cost, and set it beside an agent's listing price before you choose.

When do Lubbock property taxes go delinquent?

Texas treats most unpaid taxes as delinquent on February 1, when penalty and interest begin. Statement dates are on the district's site, and you can confirm your own account by calling 806-762-5000.

Does filing a homestead exemption in Lubbock cost anything?

No. Filing any exemption is free, and the appraisal district tells owners to disregard anyone asking for a one-time processing fee.

Does a tax lien stop a Lubbock sale?

It slows things but does not stop them. A new lien attaches every January 1, and clear title waits until delinquent taxes are cleared, which the title company can do out of your proceeds.

Who files the deed when a Lubbock house sells?

The title company normally submits it to the Lubbock County Clerk. The signature must be acknowledged before a notary, and the clerk can quote the recording charges.

Selling fast in Laredo

Laredo owners usually weigh an as-is cash sale against a regular listing. The better fit depends on how much work the house needs and how soon you need the money. Laredo is a border city on the Rio Grande, in southwestern Webb County, and many buyers have jobs tied to freight, customs and logistics. Older homes cluster near downtown and newer subdivisions spread outward, so a house's age points to the building codes it was built under.

An investor who pays cash generally accepts the property in its present state, so you skip permit fees and contractor bids. A listing can attract more bidders but adds repairs, showings and the wait on a buyer's lender. Run both numbers against your own deadline before you sign anything.

What buyers ask about

A short list of questions comes up before most Laredo offers. Answers in hand speed up any sale.

  • Does the house sit in the floodplain? The city handles that through a separate floodplain development permit.
  • Were past additions, porches, carports or block fences built with permits?
  • How old is the roof, and was electrical, plumbing and cooling work done by registered trade contractors?
  • Is the property tax bill current, and which exemptions are on file?

Unpermitted work will not block a cash sale, but an informed buyer will lower the price for it.

Do Laredo permits matter when selling?

They can. The city requires a building permit for remodels, additions, porches, carports, block fences and demolitions. Building Development Services follows the International Residential Code and allows up to 21 days for residential review.

Electrical, mechanical, plumbing, irrigation and mobile home installation permits have to be pulled by a contractor in that trade. A homeowner may pull a general permit but is treated as the contractor on the job. When records are missing, the city offers an Amnesty Certificate of Occupancy, which requires proof that the structure has been occupied continuously since August 2, 1983.

A separate $20.00 technology fee applies. Fees get updated, so ask the city for its current schedule before you budget.

Other city permits that come up

Sellers tend to forget the small permits that inspectors look for. A few touch a typical residential lot.

  • Driveway work in the right-of-way needs a $50 residential permit, pulled by a registered contractor.
  • A garage sale permit costs $15, with a limit of five per year.
  • A solar panel permit carries a non-refundable $200 fee and must be in hand before work starts.
  • A permit lapses six months after issuance if work has not begun, and all work must finish within twelve months.

General contractors register with the city for a $60 fee. Had a contractor in? Request the registration and the final inspection record, because proof of approval is something a buyer's inspector may ask to see.

Laredo adopted the 2021 International codes in 2024 and keeps separate floodplain, fence and residential setback rules. Call Building Development Services if a porch or fence went up without a permit. A cash buyer may live with it, while a buyer using a loan often will not.

Webb County property tax

The Webb County tax office mails statements every October. The lump-sum deadline is January 31, and penalty and interest start February 1. A split into two halves, due November 30 and June 30, is also available.

Pair a homestead exemption with an over-65, disability or disabled veteran exemption and you may pay in four installments, due January 31, March 31, May 31 and July 31. For owners without a mortgage escrow, the county runs a monthly prepayment plan through September 15. To enter a plan for delinquent taxes you need your name on the account and a homestead exemption, and interest on the plan accrues monthly up to 12 percent.

Selling with taxes owed

Texas attaches the tax lien to the property each January 1, so an unpaid bill follows the house to its next owner. The owner on January 1 stays liable. Ask the Webb County tax office for the exact balance early, so the closing date works around it. The balance is settled from your proceeds, and the contract spells out how buyer and seller split the current year.

State rules that touch a Laredo closing

  • Homestead owners get $140,000 off from school districts, and seniors and disabled owners get another $60,000.
  • Appraisals use a valuation date of January 1.
  • County clerks record deeds, and the signature must be notarized.

Webb County's appraisal district posts its own exemption forms. A loan in default can be paid off by a sale that closes ahead of the auction date.

If your Laredo home is in foreclosure

A lender owes you notice of sale at least 21 days ahead, and auctions take place on a set Tuesday each month. Selling before that Tuesday can pay the loan off and halt the auction. Ask the servicer for a written payoff, pick a buyer who can close inside the window and keep the sale paperwork moving the same week you sign.

Steps to sell a Laredo house fast

  1. Round up the deed, the latest tax statement, permits and a list of known repairs.
  2. Ask the Webb County tax office what is owed so there are no surprises.
  3. Request offers from cash buyers and, if you like, a listing agent, and compare net amounts.
  4. Choose a title company and sign the deed.

Selling a house you inherited? Take an affidavit of ownership interest and the death certificate to the appraisal district so the homestead exemption can be moved.

Papers to request from city and county

Before listing, ask Building Development Services whether any open permit exists on the address, and ask the Webb County tax office and appraisal district for a printout of what is owed and which exemptions are active. Put those pages next to your deed and any survey. A short, organized stack lets an investor make a firm offer instead of a cautious one.

What a cash sale skips

A cash buyer does not need a lender's appraisal, so the sale avoids the gap between contract and loan approval. You also skip staging, repeated showings and most repair negotiation. What you give up is some of the price. Weigh that against the cost of fixing a roof, a fence or an unpermitted porch, plus the months you would pay the mortgage, taxes and utilities while the house waits for a buyer.

Get three things in writing before you accept: who covers title and recording charges, the closing date the buyer commits to, and any condition beyond clear title.

Frequently asked questions

Can I sell a Laredo house that needs repairs?

Yes. Many cash buyers take homes needing work, and the offer reflects the repairs. Two or three offers show how much condition moves the number.

Is a permit required before putting a Laredo home on the market?

No permit is needed just to sell. Permits come into play only if you plan to remodel, add a porch or carport, or build a block fence before selling. Laredo's Building Development Services can tell you which projects need one.

What is the Webb County tax deadline?

The lump-sum payment is due by January 31 each year. Statements go out in October, and a split plan divides payment between November 30 and June 30.

Who pays property tax when a Laredo house sells?

The tax lien dates from January 1, which means the unpaid year's tax travels with the property. Closing usually settles the balance, and the buyer and seller divide it as the contract says.

What happens if my Laredo home is in foreclosure?

Notice of sale has to come at least 21 days ahead, and the auction falls on a set Tuesday every month. Selling first can pay off the loan and stop the auction.

Choices for selling an Irving house

In Irving you can hire an agent, find your own buyer or accept a cash offer for the house as it stands. Which one wins depends on condition, debt and the date you need to be done.

Irving sits in western Dallas County along State Highways 183 and 114, about 12 miles west of downtown Dallas, between the Elm and West Forks of the Trinity River. The city reports 264,546 residents and a daytime population above 300,000, so many employees look for housing near work. With plenty of competing listings, price and condition decide how long yours sits.

  • Agent: best for a house in good order.
  • Own buyer: no listing fee, more forms to handle.
  • Cash: no repairs, no showings.

Irving neighborhoods and who buys in them

Irving began as a rail town. The Chicago, Rock Island and Gulf Railway founders held a lot auction on December 19, 1903, and voters incorporated the city in 1914. Farmland turned into subdivisions fast: 2,615 people in 1950, 45,895 in 1960 and 100,996 by 1970.

Today you find mid-century neighborhoods, newer Las Colinas areas and a large share of rental property, and each draws a different buyer. The economy leans corporate, with about 8,500 businesses and Dallas-Fort Worth Airport along the western edge. Many buyers are relocating employees working to a deadline. A firm closing date, clear title and move-in condition give you an edge with them.

Dallas County Tax Office

Irving's property tax goes to the Dallas County Tax Office. Visit the Records Building downtown at 500 Elm Street, Suite 3300, call customer care at 214-653-7811, or pay online.

Use the county site for figures on your own parcel, and ask for a payoff statement well before closing.
