Permits and open work on an Irving house

Permits run through city staff. After a remodel or a new deck, check that the permit was actually closed out. A permit left open is a classic reason for a closing to slip, and clearing it before you list is cheaper than scrambling mid-contract.

Deed recording fees

The Dallas County clerk records Irving deeds. The state's published schedule looks like this.

What Texas lists for filing a deed
Filing chargeAmount
First page$5.00
Each added page or attachment$4.00
Each name beyond five indexed$0.25
Records technology fee$2.00
Records management and preservationNot more than $10

Fees change, so ask the clerk for the total on your own instrument. The title company usually files for you.

Tenants in an Irving house

More Irving residents rent than own, so a seller may well be holding a house with a tenant in it. The first step is a written notice to vacate. Unless the lease says otherwise it gives a few days, and it can be handed over, mailed or e-mailed if the lease allows.

  • If the tenant stays, the landlord sues in justice court and the tenant is served before trial.
  • A hearing follows within a few weeks.
  • Anyone appealing to county court has a very short deadline after judgment.
  • After a final judgment comes a writ of possession, with warning before removal.

Certain covered properties carry a longer federal notice. Before you promise any buyer an empty house, speak with an attorney.

Using a cash sale to clear tax or lien trouble

Selling for cash helps with tax or lien trouble as long as the proceeds cover what is owed at the table. The tax lien is created in January and stays with the property, which is why the closing agent will demand that unpaid taxes be settled. Whoever owned the house that January also remains liable for that year's levy after the sale.

From February 1 penalty and interest run, an attorney's collection surcharge can be added, and some collectors allow installments on a homestead. Before you accept any offer, get a payoff figure from the Dallas County Tax Office and have the closing agent check every lien.

What if an Irving owner dies without a will?

Before an heir can sell, authority has to be shown. If there is a will, it is generally offered for probate within four years of the death. Without one, a modest estate may use a small estate affidavit when every heir agrees, though a court must approve it.

A transfer on death deed, if recorded before the owner passed, moves the house outside probate. An affidavit of heirship is another route, although a buyer is free to refuse it. A Dallas County probate lawyer can say which one fits, ideally before the house goes on the market.

Squatters and adverse possession

Adverse possession is open and visible use of land under a claim hostile to the owner. Section 16.026 of the Civil Practice and Remedies Code sets a ten-year period, and a claimant sues as a trespass to try title case.

The realistic risk at an unattended Irving house is a squatter rather than a title claim. Under Property Code chapter 24B an owner may ask the sheriff or constable for removal, within limits. Keeping a vacant house secured, visited and insured is the better protection, and a quick sale can end the exposure.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Getting an Irving house ready for a fast close

Relocation buyers value certainty. A tidy file, meaning the deed, a payoff letter and a current Dallas County tax statement, does more for you than a few extra dollars of staging. Settle early whether you will repair, sell as-is or price for a renovator, then weigh each written offer by closing date, title charges and the buyer's likely reaction to inspection.

Why corporate buyers shape Irving offers

Many Irving buyers come through an employer, so their timelines are tight and their questions concrete: when can we close, is the title clean, and does the house need work they would have to arrange from another city? Answer all three in the first conversation and you can beat a slightly higher offer.

Landlords see the other side of this. An investor may happily keep the tenant in a leased rental, but an empty house shows better to a family that plans to live in it. Pick your target buyer before setting the price.

Papers to gather before listing

The recorded deed and a current Dallas County tax statement come first. With a loan outstanding, ask for the payoff in writing so the closing agent knows the exact balance. Add permit records for any remodel or deck, plus the lease on a rented house, and a payoff for each lien. With those in hand a title company can run its search quickly, and a wary buyer sees that nothing is hidden.

Include a brief note on the roof, the foundation and the main systems. A cash buyer can price faster from honest notes, and they protect you if a dispute surfaces after closing.

The step-by-step sale from listing to keys

The sale runs in four stages. First you set a price and pick a route. Next you accept an offer and open title. Third comes inspection, where a loan buyer may ask for repairs and a cash buyer usually will not. Last is closing, where you sign before a notary and the Dallas County clerk files the deed. Between the final two stages the closing agent confirms taxes and liens, so surprises come out before you sign.

Frequently asked questions

What county is Irving in?

Dallas County, in its western part, along State Highways 183 and 114.

Where do I pay Irving property taxes?

The Dallas County Tax Office, online or at its downtown Records Building at 500 Elm Street, Suite 3300.

What does the Dallas County clerk charge?

A set fee per page plus a handful of smaller records fees. For an exact total, ask the clerk.

How long is a Texas tenant's notice to vacate?

Written notice, normally a few days unless the lease differs. Covered properties may fall under a longer federal notice.

Does unpaid tax follow the house to a buyer?

The lien stays with the property, so closing agents ask for payment at or before closing.

Cash, listing or owner sale in Garland

Cash closes quickest and a listing takes longest, with an owner sale in the middle. Whether tenants live in the house, and what shape it is in, should steer you.

Garland runs a permit program for single-family and short-term rentals through its Code Compliance Department. If your house is a rental, that program will shape a sale more than any market swing. An investor can buy as-is and sort out the permit change afterward, while a retail buyer usually expects an inspected, move-in ready home.

  • Cash sale: no showings or repair haggling, with a closing day you pick.
  • Listing: more buyers see it, and you carry prep work and inspection requests.
  • Owner sale: you manage the contract, disclosures and title work yourself.

Rental permit rules that affect a sale

Every single-family rental in Garland, duplexes included, needs a permit from Code Compliance. The permit cannot be assigned or transferred, so a buyer who keeps renting the house must apply in their own name.

Garland rental permit terms
Permit typeAnnual feeInspection and other terms
Single-family rental$65, with renewals at $250 from Oct. 1, 2026Full inspection at each change of tenancy, unless the property is certified
Short-term rental$500Floor plan and proof of insurance; annual inspection for renewal

The city council has also looked at treating short-term rentals as their own land use, generally allowed by right only in Light Commercial and Heavy Commercial districts and in planned development districts that expressly allow it. Call Code Compliance at 972-485-6400 to ask whether that rule now applies to your address.

Can code violations stop a Garland sale?

No. Violations do not block a sale, but they can cool buyer interest and you should disclose them to anyone who asks. A cash buyer is often the easier match because the house is bought as-is.

If you have a notice of violation and need more time, contact your Code Compliance Officer. The department also takes requests through its online portal and the eAssist app, and the phone line is 972-485-6400. A short extension in writing is handy to give a buyer along with the notice.

  • Keep a copy of every notice and any extension.
  • Ask the officer what a reinspection would require.
  • Tell the title company about open violations before the contract is signed.

Selling with unpaid property taxes

Delinquent tax stays with the house. Each year's lien attaches January 1, and title is not clear until the balance is paid.

October is when bills mail, and they turn delinquent after January 31. Charges then accumulate monthly until the penalty reaches 12 percent on July 1, and a collection attorney's fee may add up to 20 percent.

Help may be available. A homestead can qualify for a payment plan of up to 36 months with some collectors, and a written request may win penalty relief if you meet the printed deadlines. The office billing your Garland parcel can give a payoff figure and its plan terms. Because the title company pays the balance from your proceeds at closing, no cash is needed beforehand.

If the house is sold for taxes

Auctions are run by a constable or an agent of the taxing unit. No statewide list exists, so look for notices on county clerk and tax office websites.

A former owner of homestead, farm or mineral property can redeem it during the two years after the purchaser's deed is filed, paying the bid and costs plus a premium of 25 percent in year one or 50 percent in year two. Other property gets 180 days. Any surplus from the sale can be claimed for two years.

Closing your own sale first spares you all of that. Ask for a current payoff and find out whether a suit has been filed.

Selling a house you inherited

Start by settling who owns it on paper. An heir who is not on the recorded deed and wants the homestead exemption has to give the appraisal district an ownership affidavit, the death certificate and a utility bill.

A recorded transfer on death deed lets the property skip probate, and a Lady Bird deed let the owner sell freely during life. If there is neither, the county clerk can explain probate filings and small estate affidavits.

Heirs frequently do not want to fix up and list a house they never lived in, so a documented as-is cash sale is a common pick.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Garland houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Inspection timing and your closing date

A single-family rental gets a full inspection whenever tenancy changes, unless the property is certified. The owner must tell Code Compliance about the vacancy and book the appointment. A short-term rental needs an inspection every year to renew the permit.

Timing counts when a tenant is leaving a house you are selling. A buyer who plans to re-rent will ask whether an inspection is pending, what it could flag and who pays for fixes. A copy of each inspection report goes to the landlord or manager, so ask for the latest one and hand it to the buyer or the title company.

  • Ask Code Compliance, at 972-485-6400, about your permit status.
  • Request the most recent inspection report.
  • List any open items in the sale contract.

What a rental buyer should agree to

Settle who applies for the new permit, who pays for any inspection, and how existing tenants are treated. Those answers decide whether closing runs smoothly.

  • Whether the offer is as-is, covering anything a city inspection might flag.
  • Whether the buyer assumes the lease and security deposit or wants the house vacant.
  • Who covers the permit fee and the inspection at the change of tenancy.
  • The closing date and which title company will handle the funds.

Put every answer in the written contract. For a short-term rental, also confirm the buyer understands the annual inspection and insurance steps the city requires for renewal.

Someone is living in the house without a lease

Sometimes an owner can ask the sheriff or constable to remove an occupant without a lawsuit, if specific conditions hold. Property Code chapter 24B sets them, and the State Law Library eviction guide summarizes it.

  • The person refused to leave after a request.
  • The house was closed to the public when the person walked in.
  • You and the occupant are not in a pending suit over the property.
  • The occupant has never rented from you and is not kin.

Removing the wrong person can expose you to a lawsuit, so check every item. A former tenant goes through the regular justice court eviction instead. In both cases, tell prospective buyers about the occupant in writing. An investor may accept an occupied house where a retail buyer will not.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Closing steps and deadlines

The seller signs before a notary, and the deed is then filed with the clerk serving the parcel's county. Recording charges vary, so get the total from the clerk or the title company.

A pending foreclosure notice makes its sale date a hard deadline, since notice is due at least 21 days in advance. Aim to close well before it.

Before the closing appointment, gather your photo ID, any lease and deposit records for a tenant-occupied house, and every city notice you have received. A cash sale skips lender appraisals and buyer financing, which removes two common causes of delay.

Frequently asked questions

Can a Garland rental permit transfer to the buyer?

No. Permits cannot be assigned or transferred, so a buyer who rents the house needs a new one.

Are there new Garland short-term rental rules?

The city council has considered limiting short-term rentals to certain commercial and planned development districts. Call Garland Code Compliance at 972-485-6400 to learn whether it applies to your address.

What is the annual Garland rental permit fee?

A single-family rental permit is $65 a year, with renewals at $250 from October 1, 2026. Short-term rental permits are $500 a year.

When do Garland property taxes become delinquent?

A bill still open after January 31 is late, and charges begin the next day.

Can I sell a Garland house before a tax foreclosure auction?

Yes. Paying the taxes from closing proceeds clears the lien, and finishing ahead of an auction sidesteps redemption rules and added court costs.

Quick-sale paths for a Frisco home

A Frisco seller can take a cash purchase, list with an agent, or sell to an investor. The mean home value was near $476,000 in 2020, so a house here is a large asset and the comparison between offers deserves care.

Frisco draws many movers, which gives sellers of updated homes a ready pool of financed buyers. A cash offer suits a different seller: someone relocating, settling an estate, facing a deadline or holding a house whose repairs would cost time and money before listing.

  • Cash route: fewer contingencies and a closing date you can often set, at a price below a fully prepared listing.

Two counties, several school districts

Frisco lies in west central Collin County and east central Denton County, about 25 miles north of downtown Dallas. Your tax bill and deed show which county applies to your lot.

Frisco ISD is the main district, with 63,533 students enrolled in 2020. Parts of the city also fall in Lewisville ISD, Little Elm ISD and Prosper ISD, so check the district for your exact address before advertising. About 34 percent of residents rent among 73,633 housing units, so a Frisco seller may also be selling to an investor or landlord.

New homes compete with resale houses here. The city issued 2,373 residential building permits in fiscal 2021, so price a resale house against new builds nearby, not just against old sales. If your house backs onto a development site, ask the city planning staff what is planned before you list.

What to point out in a listing

Parks, trails and schools carry a Frisco listing. The city has 1,545 acres of developed parks, 24 baseball fields, 35 soccer fields, six tennis courts and a recreation center. DFW Airport and Love Field are within about a half hour's drive, and the average commute was about 29 minutes in 2020.

Voters approved a $345 million bond authorization in May 2019 for public safety, streets, public works, the library and parks. Street and park projects can change traffic near a house, so a buyer may ask what is planned near your lot. The city engineering staff can share the capital project list.

  • Name the nearest park or trail and the school zone.
  • Note proximity to the tollway or Highway 121 if it applies.
  • Keep records of recent updates, since buyers compare homes against newer builds.

The Frisco tax bill

A Frisco bill can carry several line items. A house in Collin County and Frisco ISD pays the city, the county, the school district and Collin College, while Denton County parcels pay that county instead.

Texas property tax dates
DateWhat happens
January 1Value and the year's lien are fixed
October 1Bills are mailed
January 31Unpaid tax turns delinquent

The closing agent settles the current year from your proceeds. Homestead exemptions on a Frisco bill have included a senior exemption of $80,000 and a 10 percent homestead exemption, but amounts change, so ask the Collin or Denton County tax office about the exemptions on your current bill.

Exemptions and caps

Exemptions stay with the property. The buyer applies for new ones, while the school tax ceiling for an older owner can follow them to another Texas homestead.

  • A homestead appraisal cap limits yearly increases after the first exemption year.
  • Owners with a disability rating receive relief from $5,000 to $12,000 by rating, and a 100 percent rating can exempt the entire homestead.

The Collin Central Appraisal District or its Denton counterpart can show the exemptions on your account.

Inherited, behind on payments or leased

Each case changes the paperwork more than the price. Heirs can compare the small estate affidavit, the affidavit of heirship and the muniment of title, and your title company will say which one it accepts.

For a loan in default, a lender may sue for a deficiency within two years after a foreclosure sale. Selling first can avoid that exposure.

For a leased house, the process runs through notice and court steps, though many buyers simply take the lease. Tell each buyer what applies before they bid, because a surprise discovered late is the usual reason an offer drops.

Moving out and handing over

Plan the physical handover as carefully as the paperwork. Decide what stays: appliances, window coverings, a shed or playset. Write the list into the contract so no one argues at the walkthrough. Remove personal items and trash, leave the garage openers and every key, and photograph each room on your last day.

Call the utility providers a few days ahead to schedule transfers, and keep the final bills with your closing papers. Cancel your homeowner policy only after the deed is recorded and funds are in your account.

Recording the deed

The Collin County or Denton County clerk files the deed, depending on the parcel. The instrument must carry an acknowledgment from an authorized officer.

Your closing agent handles the filing and the fee, so read the settlement statement the day before you sign.

  • Bring photo ID to closing.
  • Have your payoff letter and tax statements ready.
  • Confirm who signs for any trust or estate.

Reading a cash offer closely

Two bids with the same headline can leave you with very different checks. Read for the items that move money: who pays for the title policy, whether the buyer wants a credit for repairs after walking through, how many days you have to move out, and whether the earnest money is refundable. A bid that looks lower but has no strings can beat a higher one that leaves room to renegotiate.

Ask who the buyer is and how they have paid in the past. A buyer with funds ready needs no financing contingency, and that is the real value of cash. Ask for a copy of the proof of funds, and ask the title company to confirm that the earnest money has arrived once the contract is signed.

If anything is unclear, bring the contract to a real estate attorney before signing. A short review costs little compared with a sale that falls apart over a missed clause.

Preparing to take offers

Start by deciding how much work you are willing to do. Newer homes nearby set the standard buyers compare against, so fresh paint, clean floors and working fixtures help even when you sell as-is. Skip big renovations unless an agent shows you the return.

Gather the deed, a payoff letter, tax statements and any receipts for the roof, air conditioning or plumbing. Then ask each buyer for the same things in writing: price, closing date, who pays title and recording fees, and whether the price holds after their walkthrough. Compare the net amounts side by side. If you need to stay in the house after closing, ask for a short leaseback and put the dates in the contract.

Frequently asked questions

Is Frisco in Collin County or Denton County?

Both. The city lies in west central Collin County and east central Denton County, so your tax bill and deed show which applies.

How quickly can I close on a cash offer in Frisco?

A clear title closes fastest, and the buyer should give you a date in writing.

Do Frisco tax exemptions go to the buyer?

No. The buyer files fresh applications.

Can a Frisco house with a loan still be sold?

Yes. The lender is paid at the closing table and the balance is yours. Ask your servicer for a payoff letter.

Where is a Frisco deed recorded?

With the Collin or Denton County clerk, whichever county holds the lot.

What makes a McKinney sale go quickly

Three things: clear title, a price buyers believe and a house someone can move into without a long repair list. Demand in McKinney is strong, but so is the supply of competing listings, and those three points tend to separate the fast sales from the slow ones.

The city had an estimated 236,001 residents on July 1, 2025, up 20.8 percent from 195,331 in 2020. About 26.2 percent are under 18, which keeps family-sized houses in demand.

  • An agent gets you the largest audience, in exchange for commission and weeks on the market.
  • Selling without one keeps the fee and makes you the negotiator.
  • A cash buyer works on a shorter calendar and takes the house as it is.

McKinney home values and housing costs

Values here run above most of Texas. For 2020-2024 the median owner-occupied home was worth $471,800, and median household income was $124,215.

Over a third of homes are rented, so there is a sizable landlord and investor segment. If you own a rental house and the buyer wants it empty, the lease end date will matter to them.

Older and newer neighborhoods

McKinney is the Collin County seat, and the town and county are both named for Collin McKinney. The railroad arrived in 1872. By the 1980s the town had become a commuter base for people working in Plano and Dallas.

Expect older homes around the historic center and large newer subdivisions farther out. Your buyers will compare your house with whichever of those two groups it resembles, so price against the right one.

Collin County offices for McKinney sellers

McKinney sits in Collin County. The Collin Central Appraisal District values the house, and the county clerk records the deed. The district's website has a property search, a map, homestead forms and a link to the appraisal review board that hears protests.

  • Pull your property account before listing and confirm which exemptions are on file.
  • A separate tax transparency site lists details for each taxing entity.
  • A buyer's agent will likely pull the same record, so fix errors in square footage or exemption status early. That prevents surprises during the option period.

Request the total owed from the county tax office. A balance from an earlier year stays attached to the house.

Short-term rental registration

Every short-term rental inside McKinney city limits must register each year, and the program is free. The city defines one as a house, apartment, room or other dwelling rented through Airbnb, VRBO or similar platforms for thirty days or less. Long-term leases, apartment complexes renting standard units, hotels, motels and bed and breakfasts are outside the rule.

  • Each rental unit is registered separately, and every owner provides contact information.
  • A responsible person must be reachable 24 hours a day about concerns.
  • Registration does not override HOA or deed restrictions, and it does not ban short-term rentals.
  • All short-term rentals must pay Hotel Occupancy Tax.

Owners register through the city's Customer Self-Service portal or in person at Development Services on the second floor of City Hall. If the house you are selling has hosted guests, confirm the registration is current so the buyer gets a clean file.

Hotel occupancy tax on vacation rentals

McKinney charges a 7 percent city Hotel Occupancy Tax on lodging, vacation rentals included, on top of the 6 percent state rate that is remitted separately. Booking platforms that take payment for a short-term rental now collect and remit the city tax for the operator, a rule in place since September 2, 2025.

  • Reports and payments are due on the 20th of the month after each reporting month.
  • A report is required even in a month with no tax collected.
  • Late payment adds a 5 percent penalty at 1 to 30 days, 10 percent after 30 days, and 10 percent plus 10 percent annual interest at 60 days or more.

A seller who has run a rental should have these filings in order. A buyer or title company may ask whether any tax is unpaid.

Homestead and veteran exemptions

Texas has no state property tax, so exemptions come off local bills. Any taxing unit may adopt an optional homestead exemption of up to 20 percent of appraised value with a $5,000 minimum, and the Collin appraisal district's taxing entity page shows which units offer one.

A veteran rated 100 percent disabled may qualify for a total homestead exemption under Section 11.131, and lesser ratings earn smaller exemptions listed in the Comptroller's table. If you are buying a disabled veteran's former home, ask the appraisal district what carries over.

What heirs of a McKinney house should do first

An heir has several routes, and the one you choose sets the schedule. Texas allows four years from the death to offer a will for probate.

  • Muniment of title, for an estate with no debts beyond real-estate liens.
  • Small estate affidavit, used when no will exists and assets come to $75,000 or less, homestead excluded.
  • Affidavit of heirship, which buyers need not accept.
  • Transfer on death deed, recorded during the owner's life.

Ask the Collin County clerk what is filed on the property and have a title company confirm it before you accept an offer.

Who is buying in McKinney

Newcomers tend to be well paid, and per capita income is $55,643. About 85.5 percent of people lived in the same house a year earlier, so most owners stay put and listings come from a smaller pool than the population suggests.

Census counts went from 131,117 in 2010 to 195,308 in 2020, and land area grew from 62.21 to 66.96 square miles over that decade. That growth is why so many nearby listings are recent construction, which sets the bar for finishes on an older house.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Steps to sell and what to bring

Before any buyer sees the paperwork, collect the deed, the current tax statement and a payoff figure if a mortgage remains. Open your account on the appraisal district's property search to confirm the exemptions and square footage on record.

  1. Pick the route: agent, sale on your own or a cash buyer.
  2. Accept an offer and let a title company look for liens, unpaid taxes and probate gaps.
  3. Clear whatever turns up. A clean title closes sooner than one with liens or missing heirs.
  4. Sign the deed and have the county clerk record it.

A cash sale skips inspection repair requests and most showings, which can help when the house needs work or the calendar is tight.

Frequently asked questions

Which county handles McKinney property records?

Collin County. McKinney is the county seat, about thirty-two miles north of Dallas, and the Collin Central Appraisal District and county clerk handle values and deeds.

What is a typical McKinney home worth?

The 2020-2024 median for owner-occupied homes is $471,800. Individual houses vary a great deal by age, size and neighborhood.

How quickly can a McKinney sale close?

It depends on the buyer and on title. A clean title closes sooner than one with liens, probate or missing heirs, so order a title search early.

Must a McKinney house go through probate before I sell it?

Usually some court or recorded step comes first. A transfer on death deed recorded before the death is the main exception, and a Texas attorney can say which route fits.

Does the Collin appraisal district publish homestead forms?

Yes. Its site lists residential homestead exemption information and forms. Call the district for the filing deadline that applies to you.

Cash buyer, listing or private sale in Grand Prairie

Pressure on your calendar, or a house in rough shape, favors a cash buyer. A tidy house and no rush favor a listing, and a known buyer favors a private sale. Grand Prairie owners have one extra step first: the city covers pieces of three counties and six school districts, so identify which combination your parcel belongs to.

The answer names the appraisal district holding your file and the office that mails your tax bill. Find it before you speak with buyers, since their title company will ask within days of a signed contract. Set the deed's legal description next to it so the two agree.

  • Cash buyer: no loan to wait for, so the date bends to your needs.
  • Agent listing: wider exposure, slower timeline, repair requests likely.
  • Private sale: keeps the commission in your pocket, with all paperwork on your desk.

Whatever you pick, jot down your earliest and latest workable closing dates first. Then negotiations center on your real constraint instead of the sticker price.

Location, creeks and older plats

The city lies in western Dallas County and eastern Tarrant County, with a smaller piece in Ellis County. Mountain Creek Lake borders the east side, Joe Pool Lake reaches in from the south, and Kirby, Cottonwood and Fish creeks and the West Fork of the Trinity River cut through town. Lenders and inspectors often raise drainage questions about lots near that water, so hold on to any flood or elevation papers you have.

Population reached 175,396 by 2010. The city grew by absorbing neighboring communities over the decades, including Dalworth Park in 1943 and, by the 1980s, Burbank Gardens, Florence Hill, Freetown, Idlewild-Mountain Creek and Shady Grove. A title search can reveal older plats or easements that predate a merger.

Which taxing units bill a Grand Prairie house?

Dallas County with Grand Prairie ISD and Tarrant County with Arlington ISD are the usual pairings. Six school districts overlap the city, so households only blocks apart can owe different combined rates. The Dallas Central Appraisal District or the Tarrant Appraisal District can help you work out a bill. Ask for current rates, since printed ones may belong to an earlier fiscal year.

No statewide property tax exists in Texas; each local unit sets a rate of its own. The person holding title on January 1 owes that year's lien, which is why the settlement sheet divides the bill.

The city's tax rates page prints an average annual city property tax of $1,089 on a $248,000 home with a homestead exemption, labeled for fiscal year 2024-25, and a combined sales tax of 8.25 percent (6.25 percent state, 2 percent city). Take both as rough guides and read your own notice for current numbers.

Late payment is costly. From February 1 penalty and interest run, and the penalty rises each month to twelve percent on July 1, with collection attorneys free to add fees. Sellers in spring should ask the title company to order a tax certificate, so any balance gets cleared at closing.

Nightly-rental rules for Grand Prairie hosts

Grand Prairie's council adopted a short-term rental ordinance on May 17, 2022. It calls for a yearly permit, with hotel occupancy tax sent directly to the city each month. It applies to any residence advertised for stays of one to thirty consecutive days, whether the listing is on a booking site or social media.

An operator who is not the owner needs the owner's written permission. Check any HOA rules before applying, since the application fee is not refundable. If the house has a rental history, gather the permit paperwork and tax filings for the buyer, who inherits whatever the property has been doing.

  • Permits renew every year.
  • Hotel tax is paid monthly to the city.
  • Non-owner operators need an owner's statement.

Falling behind on the mortgage

Lenders in this state rarely sue first. The deed of trust gives them a power of sale, and the auction is held in public on a month's first Tuesday. A notice of default comes first and gives 20 days to catch up. A notice of sale follows at least 21 days before the auction, posted at the courthouse and filed with the county clerk.

Time is tight. Close a sale ahead of the auction and the lender is repaid from the proceeds while your equity stays yours. If foreclosure goes ahead anyway, the lender can sue for any shortfall within two years, and you may ask the court to credit fair market value. Surplus from the auction goes first to junior lien holders, then to you.

Federal rules generally bar a servicer from starting until the loan is more than 120 days late. Do not wait for that, though. Call your servicer and a housing counselor the moment payments look doubtful, because options shrink as the auction nears.

Inherited Grand Prairie houses

No one can sign a deed until the law gives them that power, and heirs are no exception. The right document varies by estate. Options include a probated will, a muniment of title, an executor's deed, a recorded transfer on death deed or an affidavit of heirship. Probate of a will generally has to happen within four years of death.

Which clerk you deal with, Dallas, Tarrant or Ellis County, follows the county where the parcel sits. Find out early what the title company will accept, so closing does not stall on a missing signature.

What happens between contract and closing

The contract goes to a title company, which opens a file, runs the title search and asks each lender for a payoff letter. It also confirms which taxing units cover your parcel and whether this year's bill has been paid.

You sign the deed in front of a notary, and your proceeds arrive once payoffs, the tax split and closing charges are deducted. Cash deals tend to move quicker, since no lender appraisal or underwriting stands in the way. Should an inspection or permit question arise, get the agreed fix or credit written down before closing day. Bring a government photo ID, the keys, and any garage or gate openers, and plan your move-out so the house is empty and swept when the buyer takes possession. Forward your mail and cancel utilities for the day after closing, not before, so nothing lapses while you still own the place.

How quickly can a cash sale close on a Grand Prairie home?

Usually a few weeks when title is clean. Delays tend to come from liens, back taxes or a probate that is still open.

Which appraisal district applies to my address?

Look at your tax bill or the city's tax rates page. A Dallas County parcel falls under the Dallas Central Appraisal District, and a Tarrant County parcel under the Tarrant Appraisal District.

Who pays the current year's taxes when I sell?

The settlement sheet normally splits them between you and the buyer. Older unpaid balances are taken from your proceeds, since a Texas tax lien stays with the property.

Is hotel occupancy tax due on a Grand Prairie rental?

Yes, if guests stay one to thirty days. The city collects it monthly from permitted short-term rental operators.

Can heirs sell a Grand Prairie house before the estate is settled?

Only if they hold proper authority, through a court-approved route or a recorded transfer on death deed. The title company can say which paper it will accept.

Fastest ways to sell in Amarillo

A house in good shape can go through an agent if you can wait for a buyer with a loan. When speed, repairs or a tenant complicate a regular listing, a cash sale is the alternative. Amarillo is the commercial hub of the Texas Panhandle, with an estimated 205,130 residents in mid-2025.

Amarillo spreads over two counties, so first find out which one holds your parcel. Most of the city is in Potter County, while a portion extends into Randall County. The tax office, clerk and appraisal records you need follow from that.

  • Look up the address with the Potter Randall Appraisal District, which covers ownership for both counties.
  • Call the tax office printed on your tax statement early.
  • Ask the City of Amarillo's Building Safety office about open permits on the property.

Amarillo housing numbers

Amarillo is one of the more affordable Texas cities. Typical home values sit under $200,000, and about four in ten households rent. The 2020 count was 200,393 people, up from 190,695 in 2010.

Amarillo city, Texas: housing and income, 2020-2024 estimates
Housing measureAmarillo

Typical monthly rent$1,092

The average commute is only 19.6 minutes across a city of 102 square miles.

Taxes on the Randall County side

Randall County sends statements on October 1 and treats them as payable immediately. Penalty and interest start only if the bill is unpaid after January 31, so February 1 is the first delinquent day. A check sent by first-class mail is treated as paid on its postmark date.

The county tax office also explains what a sale does to the bill:

  • The taxing unit never divides the year between buyer and seller. Most sales contracts do, which makes the contract and closing statement the documents to read.
  • The person who held title on the first of January of the prior year remains responsible for that year's tax, although the lien lets the unit pursue the buyer as well.
  • Four installments are open to homesteads of owners over 65, disabled owners and disabled vets. The first fourth and a signed agreement are due by January 31, and a first payment received by February 28 carries 7% penalty and interest. Skip a later installment and 6% penalty plus 1% interest accrue monthly.

On a tax certificate you will find delinquent taxes, penalties and interest, broken out by taxing unit. The fee is $10 in certified funds when you pick it up. Email your request and collect it in Canyon or Amarillo. To get a zero-balance certificate when taxes are due, pay with cash or certified funds, or wait 10 working days for a check to clear.

The Potter Randall Appraisal District is at 5701 Hollywood Road, Amarillo, phone 806-358-1601, mailing address P.O. Box 7190, Amarillo, TX 79114. For a parcel in Potter County, ask the Potter County tax assessor-collector for the same certificate.

Permits and the certificate of occupancy

The Building Safety office sits in the Simms Municipal Building, 808 S Buchanan Street, Suite 104, and keeps weekday hours of eight to five. You file permits online through MGO Connect. City ordinance Sec. 4-10-21 bars use of land until a Certificate of Occupancy and Compliance has been issued.

A new building receives its certificate as soon as the permit is completed. Anything else needs a separate one: a change of use, or a property that never got one. Alterations require a remodel or repair permit, and a registered contractor has to pull it. If the house has a converted garage, a rented room or a home business, ask Building Safety whether the certificate still matches how the property is used.

Splitting off part of a lot for sale triggers a platting requirement. Any tract inside the city limits needs a plat, and so does a tract of five acres or less in the extraterritorial jurisdiction that stretches five miles past the limits.

Does flood risk affect an Amarillo sale?

It can. Flooding in 1888 and 1889 pushed the original town to higher ground, and drainage on the High Plains remains a regular question from buyers. Randall County defines a 100-year flood as one with a 1% or greater chance of being equaled or exceeded in any year, which is different from a flood that comes once a century.

  • The county floodplain administrator will give you flood information if you provide the Randall appraisal ID, the address and the legal description.
  • On the Flood Insurance Rate Map, special flood hazard areas are shaded in. A Letter of Map Amendment takes out a property that was mapped in by mistake.
  • Work or repairs costing 50% or more of a building's market value count as substantial improvement or substantial damage under county rules.
  • Skipping a required county floodplain permit can mean fines up to $500 per day.

Whatever the map says, a buyer's lender may still insist on flood insurance.

Inherited, behind on payments or rented?

A few Texas deadlines apply here, and they are the same ones used across the state.

  • Inherited: an heir missing from the recorded deed can still claim the homestead exemption by handing the appraisal district an affidavit of ownership interest, the death certificate and a recent utility bill.
  • Behind on payments: a lender typically holds off until the loan is over 120 days late, then must mail the sale notice 21 or more days before the first-Tuesday auction.
  • Tenants: the lease can set its own notice period, and otherwise the written notice to vacate is three days or more. A justice court hears the eviction case, and the writ of possession can issue six days after judgment.

Each of these can end in a sale, and an early decision leaves more room to negotiate.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Amarillo houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What happens between contract and closing

Once a buyer signs, the title company orders a tax certificate from the Randall or Potter County office, gathers payoff letters and looks for open permits on the parcel. You then sign the deed before a notary, and the deed travels to the clerk in the county that holds the parcel.

Expect some back and forth over the tax figure, since the certificate has to cover every taxing unit. If the house is held through an estate, bring papers that show who has authority to sign.

Cash sale or agent listing in Amarillo

Begin with a list of what you owe: the mortgage payoff, any unpaid tax and the repairs a buyer is likely to demand. Set that beside what a listing might bring after weeks of showings and a lender's approval of the buyer. Cash offers tend to come in lower, yet they erase the repair list, the haggling after inspection and the chance that a loan collapses.

Before you agree to either, order a tax certificate so no unpaid year appears at closing, confirm which county records the deed, and ask Building Safety if the certificate of occupancy fits the house as it is today. Those three answers let you sign with confidence and choose a closing date that suits you. If a mortgage is involved, ask the lender for a written payoff figure at the same time.

Frequently asked questions

Is Amarillo in Potter County or Randall County?

Both. Most of the city is in Potter County and the rest reaches into Randall County, so your parcel decides which one applies.

When are Randall County property taxes due?

On receipt. Pay by January 31 to avoid penalty and interest. Statements are mailed each October 1, and unpaid taxes become delinquent on February 1.

How much is a tax certificate in Randall County?

The fee is $10 in certified funds, collected when you pick it up in Canyon or Amarillo. It shows any delinquent taxes unit by unit.

Does Amarillo require a Certificate of Occupancy?

Yes, city ordinance Sec. 4-10-21 requires it. New buildings get one automatically, while an older property may need one if none was ever issued or its use has changed.

What does an Amarillo owner-occupied home typically cost?

The middle value for owner-occupied homes in Amarillo is $196,900 in the 2020-2024 estimates.

Sell My House Fast in Brownsville, TX: Options, Costs and Cash Offers

Cash Home Buyers in Texas
Cash Offer in 24 Hours
  • Brownsville, TX: inherited, behind on payments, tenants or repairs, we buy the house as-is
  • No fees, commissions or closing costs on a Brownsville, TX sale
  • Turn the Brownsville, TX offer down and you owe us nothing

Sell Your Brownsville House for Cash

Tell us about your Brownsville house.

Call or Text  (424) 435-2326


Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Brownsville?
We buy Brownsville houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.
Get My Cash Offer →

Selling in Brownsville at a glance

Brownsville sits on the Rio Grande, facing Matamoros, and serves as the seat of Cameron County. Most sales involve three local offices: the appraisal district, the clerk and the tax office. Population was estimated at 192,957 in mid-2025, 3.6% above the 2020 base. Owner-occupants hold 61.7% of the homes, which carry a median value of $139,900. Median rent runs $923.

Because 83.6% of residents over age five speak another language at home, contracts here are often read in two languages. Everyone on the deed should understand the paper before signing it.

How Cameron CAD sets your value

The Cameron Appraisal District puts a number on your house, and every taxing unit then picks its own rate. Expect a fresh appraisal at least once in any three-year span, sooner where prices are jumping.

Raise a value by $1,000 or less and the district owes no notice, so some owners never see a mailing. Section 23.23 of the Tax Code has limited a homestead's assessed value to 10% yearly growth since January 1, 2008. New rooms, pools and similar improvements fall outside the limit.

Homestead exemptions

You prove Texas residency with something like a driver's license. Married owners each apply and show ID. A residence can carry the homestead, over-65, disabled person or 100% disabled veteran exemption. The disabled veteran exemption alternatively attaches to any one property that veteran owns.

  • You can claim over-65 or disabled in a given year, not both.
  • If some owners live elsewhere, the account splits, and the exemption shrinks to the qualifying owner's share.
  • Adding a pool, garage or room raises the school tax ceiling. A Tax Ceiling Transfer form carries it to a new Texas homestead.

A few exemption types need a new application by April 30 each year. Ask the district which ones apply to you.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Brownsville house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

How to contest your appraisal

Protests must be written. They are due on whichever date is later, May 15 or the thirtieth day after your notice arrived. You may mail, hand-deliver or email, though mail must be postmarked in time.

After the deadline, the district and the review board lose the power to change the value. Hospitalization can excuse a late filing. Forgetting cannot. File on time and you receive at least 15 days' notice of a hearing that tends to last about 15 minutes. If the ruling still seems wrong, you can sue in district court, request binding arbitration, or, in Cameron County, appeal to the State Office of Administrative Hearings.

  • Give your name and the address or account number of the property.
  • State the issue, such as market value.
  • Attach comparable sales, photos or repair estimates as support.

Tax calendar and penalties

January 1 fixes both value and the tax lien. The county tax office shares an East Levee Street address with the clerk. Call to find out which taxing units bill your house and what you owe.

Key dates for a Brownsville property tax bill
WhenEvent for the owner
January 1The year's value is fixed and the lien attaches
April 30Some exemption types need a new application
May 15, or day 30 after the noticeLast day to protest, whichever falls later
Around October 1Bills arrive
February 1Balances still owed become delinquent: six percent penalty, one percent interest
After July 1Twelve percent penalty; the taxing unit's lawyer may tack on up to 20 percent

Clear title is impossible with delinquent tax on the books, so pay any balance by closing.

What if the property is headed for a tax sale?

Tax sales are auctions conducted by a constable or a hired agent. No statewide list exists. Look for notices on county websites.

What an owner can recover depends on the property type. For homestead, farm or mineral land, the owner may redeem for two years after the buyer's deed is filed, paying 25% over in year one or 50% over in year two, plus costs. All other property gets 180 days and up to 25% over. Any surplus from the sale is yours to claim for two years after the sale.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Brownsville houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Selling an inherited house

Valley family land often remains titled to a relative who died decades ago. The quick fix is an affidavit of heirship, sworn and filed with the county clerk. Nobody in court reviews it, though, and a title insurer can turn it down.

Sturdier options: open probate within four years; use a muniment of title when the estate owes only liens on the real estate; or rely on a transfer on death deed recorded while the owner lived. An heir who is not on the recorded deed can still seek an exemption. The appraisal district wants an affidavit of ownership interest, the death certificate and a recent utility bill.

Where a Brownsville deed is recorded

Visit the Cameron County Clerk at 835 E. Levee Street for deeds, liens, plats and maps. After a deed is recorded, bring Cameron CAD the instrument, or its volume and page numbers, so the owner of record gets updated.

The state clerk manual lists $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for each additional page, plus other fees. Call the clerk for what your deed will cost.

Cash sale or listing?

Pick the route by looking at the house itself, not by what a neighbor did. A tidy home can draw several buyers who need mortgages, but you wait on appraisals and lender calendars. A home with an aging roof, a stubborn tenant or years of unpaid tax suits a buyer who pays cash, accepts the problems and closes once title work clears.

Compare offers on price, closing costs and closing date, side by side, and have the title company check that no tax or lien item changes the numbers. If two offers land close together, the faster and cleaner closing is usually worth more than a small difference in price, since each extra week means another month of taxes, insurance and upkeep on a house you are trying to leave.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Papers worth gathering first

Open a folder before you call anyone. Inside, keep the latest county tax bill, the appraisal notice if one came, and the Cameron CAD account number with its exemption list. Loan payoff letter, lease, probate papers or recorded affidavit go in too, whichever apply. Ask the clerk whether liens or old instruments are filed against the property, because a lien found late stalls a closing.

What happens at closing

Before any money moves, the title company gets the tax balance, runs a lien search and works out which signatures are needed. It settles any mortgage with the payoff figure. For an inherited house, the probate or affidavit route has to be sorted out first. The deed is then signed, acknowledged and recorded by the county clerk.

Your homestead exemption stays with you, so a buyer who intends to live there applies for a new one. Ask the clerk's office for copies of the recorded deed once it is filed, and keep them with your sale papers. If someone is still in the house, settle a move-out date with the buyer before you sign the contract.

Frequently asked questions

What does a typical Brownsville home cost?

Median value for an owner-occupied home is $139,900, but condition, lot and street move any single sale up or down.

Will Cameron CAD always mail a value notice?

No. A notice goes out only when the law calls for one, and an increase of $1,000 or less needs none.

When is a Brownsville appraisal protest due?

By the later of May 15 and 30 days after delivery of the notice. It must be written, and you may mail it, bring it in or email it.

Where can I get a copy of my Brownsville deed?

Go to the county clerk on East Levee Street. The appraisal district does not hand out deeds, surveys or plats.

Does a Brownsville homeowner over 65 get a tax ceiling?

Yes. School taxes on the home usually stay flat for as long as you own and live in it, and the ceiling can follow you to a new Texas homestead.

Sell Your Denton House for Cash

Selling in Denton?
We buy Denton houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

Your real choices for a fast Denton sale

You can sell a Denton house three ways: through an agent, to a buyer you locate, or to a cash buyer. How soon you need to close, and what shape the roof, kitchen and systems are in, will usually settle it.

The house is taxed and recorded through Denton County. Investors who want rentals compete here with families who want a place to live, and that mix can help if your house is dated or damaged: an investor builds the repair cost into the price rather than making you fix things first.

  • Agent listing: the biggest audience, in exchange for showings, repair requests after inspection and a wait for mortgage approval.
  • Owner sale: you keep the commission and also take on the contract, the disclosure form and the negotiating.
  • Cash purchase: a faster calendar and fewer contingencies, with the discount that comes from buying a house unrepaired.

Historic landmarks and older homes

Denton has an old core. The city counts 69 local historic landmarks across more than seven architectural styles, concentrated along West Oak Street, plus three local historic districts covering over 80 acres on the west and north sides.

If your house is a landmark, exterior changes go through a design review process and demolition needs approval from the Historic Landmark Commission. Designation does not change the zoned use of the property. A renovator will raise this early, so check whether your address carries a local designation before you sign anything. The city's development staff take those questions at development@cityofdenton.com.

Newer subdivisions have no such overlay, and buyers there focus on the roof, the foundation and the age of the mechanical systems. Wherever you live, get repair responsibility in writing.

Short-term rentals

Anyone who wants a vacation rental needs a city registration. Denton's definition of a short-term rental is renting a whole dwelling unit or a bedroom for at least 24 hours and no more than 29 consecutive days, and every operator must register.

Registration costs $150 and is valid for one calendar year, with applications and renewals filed through the city's STR permit system. Council approved amendments to the Denton Development Code on October 22, 2024, that changed these rules. For the packet and full requirements, call Development Services at (940) 349-8600 or write to building@cityofdenton.com. Violations can carry a maximum penalty of $2,000.

This touches a sale in two ways. If the house is on short stays today, expect the buyer to ask if your registration is current. If a buyer wants to use it that way, the offer depends on rules you cannot promise on their behalf, so send them to the city with the question.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Denton house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Permits before you sell

Unpermitted work is the most common surprise, so go through your records before the house goes under contract. Permitting runs through the Development Service Center. As of January 2, 2026 the center closes at noon on Fridays, and Friday afternoon occupied inspections are taken by phone at (940) 349-8195.

Ask for the permit history on your address if you added a room, a deck, a garage conversion or new electrical service. An inspector or lender may ask to see closed permits. If something was built without one, you can still sell, but you will either need to resolve it or accept a lower price from a buyer who takes that risk.

  • Gather receipts and permit numbers for any major work.
  • Call Development Services at (940) 349-8600 to ask about open permits.
  • Tell every buyer about known problems in writing.

Denton local rules at a glance

Ordinances change, so check each figure with the city before you rely on it.

Denton local rules
TopicCurrent rule

Short-term rental registration$150, valid one calendar year
Local historic landmarks69, with design review for exterior changes
Local historic districts3, covering over 80 acres
Conservation districtsNone at present

How a sale closes after you accept an offer

Expect a title company or an attorney to draft the deed, a notary to watch you sign, and the Denton County clerk to receive the filing, because Texas records a deed where the land is. An unacknowledged deed will be rejected. Ask the closing agent for the clerk's charges and the recording total.

Property tax creates a lien on January 1, and the person who owns the house that day is liable. Late charges begin in February. Most title companies pay the year's tax at closing, so ask the Denton County tax office for your balance in good time.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Denton houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Inherited, behind on payments or owing back taxes

Each of these has its own deadline. A will can be probated for four years after a death. An affidavit of heirship is a sworn statement placed on file with the county clerk, and no law forces a buyer to honor it. Because title companies set their own standards of proof, bring it up early.

With a mortgage in arrears, the lender starts with a default notice, and paying the arrears inside 20 days reinstates the loan. A notice of auction comes next, and the sale itself is held on a first Tuesday. Sometimes a cash buyer can close ahead of it.

For back property taxes, ask the Denton County tax office whether the account has gone to a suit. Penalty waivers exist in some cases if you pay promptly and ask in writing, so raise it with the tax office.

Preparing the paperwork

A slim folder can save days. Put in the deed, a payoff letter from your lender, the newest tax bill, permit numbers, and the lease if someone rents the house. When appliances are staying, name them in the contract so the final walk-through brings no argument. A few days before you list, ask your title company to look for open liens or permits. You will have time to fix a surprise without a contract deadline bearing down. It also helps to photograph the house in daylight, with the yard and street in frame, so buyers can compare it with newer listings.

Finally, decide ahead of time how you will handle questions about the historic or short-term rental rules. A one-line answer that points the buyer to Development Services keeps you from promising something the city controls. If the buyer plans to rent the house or change its exterior, say plainly that you cannot guarantee approval, and offer the city contact details instead.

Frequently asked questions

Is there a fee to register a short-term rental in Denton?

Yes. Registration costs $150 and is valid for one calendar year. Renewals go through the same STR permit system.

Does Denton require a permit for a house I plan to sell?

The sale itself needs none. Permits cover construction, so look into whether earlier work on your house was permitted, and phone Development Services at (940) 349-8600 if unsure.

Who bills property tax on a Denton house?

Local taxing units set the rates and the county tax office sends the bill, while the appraisal district assigns the value. There is no state property tax in Texas. The Denton County tax office can give you your current balance.

Can I sell a Denton house that has a historic landmark designation?

Yes. Designation does not affect the use of the property, which zoning controls. It does add design review for exterior changes and requires Historic Landmark Commission approval before demolition.

How soon can a cash sale close in Denton?

Whatever date the contract names. Get it in writing, and remember that title work, a probate or lien problem or an unpaid tax bill can push it back.

What drives the Killeen housing market

Killeen sits outside the East Gate of Fort Hood, and soldiers and their families create much of the demand for houses and rentals. Military moves, deployments and orders therefore set the timing for many sales.

Anyone holding a permanent change of station order cares most about a firm closing date, and an as-is sale can deliver one. The city's newcomer page for the installation links to local resources, transit and parks, which helps when you are pitching to buyers arriving from elsewhere.

Downtown Killeen and the vacant structure rule

Downtown Killeen runs from Rancier Avenue (FM 439) on the north to Business 190 on the south, and it is on the National Register.

If your property is empty and lies in the Historic Overlay District, you must register it and pay an annual fee. Phone Development Services before you list, because buyers will ask whether the registration is current.

Permits and city offices

Killeen uses a council-manager system, with a mayor and seven council members. Permits and code questions go through city Development Services, and the appraisal side sits with the county. Call before listing if you finished a remodel or a fence, so any open permit is closed out before a buyer's lender asks.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Killeen house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Bell Central Appraisal District

Bell Central Appraisal District sets values for Killeen in Bell County, while the city and other units set rates. You can pay at the district's offices with no fee by check, cash or money order. Its online and phone options go through a vendor that charges fees.

It offers a quarterly installment agreement, a homestead delinquent-tax installment agreement and a tax deferral option. A homestead's assessed value may rise up to 10 percent a year until it matches market value, and that increase is mandatory under the Property Tax Code.

Exemptions Bell CAD offers

Military households should look closely at the veteran items on this list.

  • Residence homestead
  • Disabled person and age 65 or older, including surviving spouses
  • 100 percent disabled veteran or surviving spouse
  • Surviving spouse of a service member killed in action or of a first responder killed on duty
  • Donated residence of a partially disabled veteran

Applicants need a current driver license or Texas ID, a Social Security letter for disability, and a recent VA award letter for a veteran. No annual renewal is needed, though the chief appraiser may request updated applications. The buyer applies for a fresh exemption after you sell.

Texas tax dates around a Killeen sale

A Killeen closing runs on four dates: the January 1 value and lien date, the October bills, the end-of-year split payments and the February 1 delinquency date.

  • Bell CAD lists a discount deadline of October 31 for entities that offer one.
  • A split bill has halves due at the end of November and in June.
  • The protest deadline is generally May 15.

Individual taxing units may offer discounts, so ask the county for the numbers on your parcel.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Killeen houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Options if you must sell fast in Killeen

Orders or a deployment push many owners to move quickly. Three routes are open.

  • An agent listing suits a house in showing shape and an owner without a deadline.
  • Skipping the agent keeps the commission and leaves buyer management to you.
  • A cash offer takes the house unrepaired and sets the closing date with you, which suits a PCS move, a rental with problem tenants or an inherited house.

If you rent the house out from another duty station, the tenant side has its own court process.

Squatters or an unwanted occupant

Texas Property Code chapter 24B lets an owner ask the sheriff or constable for removal without a court case. The occupant must have stayed after being told to go, the property must not have been open to the public when they entered, no suit may be pending between you, and the occupant cannot be family or a current or former tenant. A removal later found wrongful can bring a lawsuit against the person who asked for it.

A real tenant is different and needs an eviction suit. Adverse possession is another idea: an open, hostile claim to land, with a ten-year period in the usual case. A vacant Killeen rental invites trouble, so check on it often.

Selling a Killeen rental with a tenant

You can sell with the lease intact or end the tenancy as the lease allows. For unpaid rent Texas requires a written notice to vacate, and the suit is filed in justice court. The tenant is served several days before trial, and either side has only five days to appeal to county court.

Once judgment is final, the writ of possession waits a few days and is then followed by a 24-hour warning. Federal notice rules may add time on some covered properties. A cash buyer may take the house with renters still inside, so you skip the court calendar.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Late filing for a disabled veteran exemption

Texas lets a disabled veteran apply late in some cases. If you file after April 30, Bell CAD asks you to submit an application anyway so the office can apply any remedy the law provides once it approves. Gather a recent VA award letter before you call. The donated residence of a partially disabled veteran and the surviving-spouse items are named on the district's list.

Deeds, foreclosure and probate

The Bell County clerk records deeds for land in the county once a notary has acknowledged the signature, and the title company files at closing.

If the loan is behind, Texas runs the foreclosure outside court: a default letter, a short cure window, a courthouse notice and a first-Tuesday auction. If the owner has died, a will normally goes to probate within a few years of the death, and a small estate affidavit is only for modest estates without much real property. Get legal advice before relying on an affidavit.

Preparing a Killeen house for a deadline sale

Gather the deed, a lender payoff letter and your Bell County tax statement first, since the title company will ask for all three. If you are being reassigned, confirm what the buyer will do about your move-out date and tell them in writing when you can hand over the keys. Ask each buyer for a closing date in the offer. A cash buyer can often shape that date around your orders, while a loan buyer needs time for an appraisal. For a house with a tenant, the lease end is the date to build around. Leave a key contact, such as a relative or a property manager, who can sign papers or answer the title company if orders move you before closing day.

Frequently asked questions

Where is downtown Killeen?

Between Rancier Avenue (FM 439) and Business 190, just outside Fort Hood's East Gate.

Is there a vacant house registration in Killeen?

Yes, for vacant structures inside the Historic Overlay District. A 2020 ordinance requires registration with Planning and Development Services and an annual fee.

Which office handles permits in Killeen?

City Development Services, at 200 E Avenue D, 2nd Floor.

Does Bell CAD offer payment plans?

Yes. It lists a quarterly installment agreement, a homestead delinquent-tax installment agreement and a deferral option. Ask the office which applies.

Can a military household sell quickly in Killeen?

Yes. Cash buyers can set the closing date around orders. A traditional listing takes longer but can bring a higher price for a house in good condition.

Can a Mesquite house sell quickly?

Often, yes. Your options are a cash buyer, a listing with an agent or a landlord, and the right one depends on how much repair the house needs and how soon you must close.

Mesquite is about 15 minutes east of downtown Dallas. Commuters, investors and landlords all shop here, a mix that suits a house with work you would rather not do.

Mesquite at a glance

Mesquite is a large Dallas suburb with more than 155,000 residents, covering almost 50 square miles. It calls itself the official Rodeo Capital of Texas. The town began as a Texas and Pacific Railway depot in 1873 and became a city on December 3, 1887.

Buyers like the roads. The city sits where Interstates 20, 30 and 635, State Highway 352 and U.S. Highway 80 meet, and both DFW International and Dallas Love Field are about 35 minutes away. Thousands of new homes are under construction, so expect new-build competition if you list on the open market.

Which sale routes fit a Mesquite house?

Owners here usually weigh four routes. Every one gives up price, speed or effort somewhere.

  • Agent listing. Likely the top price, with showings, repairs and lender hiccups landing on you.
  • Cash buyer. Fastest route, often with no repairs, with an offer that factors in what the buyer must spend.
  • Landlord or investor. Natural for houses with tenants; that buyer then deals with Mesquite's license rules.
  • Owner financing. You are paid over time, and Texas applies special contract rules while you hold title. See an attorney before agreeing.

Put cash offers next to a net estimate for listing. The difference is the price of speed.

Rental license rules in Mesquite

Every rental in Mesquite must be registered, and a Single-Family Rental Property License is issued only after the home passes an inspection. A buyer who plans to rent the house will need to run this process.

Reviewers confirm that taxes are paid, no liens are outstanding, and a property manager or owner lives within 40 miles of Mesquite. A home that passes gets a green tag good for 90 days, during which the new tenant has to start water service. The license ends when the tenant changes or after three years with the same tenant, whichever comes first.

Review takes up to 48 business hours, and all utilities need to be running on inspection day. A separate short-term rental license costs $150 and expires each May 31.

Permits for past repairs

An open permit can hold up a sale. Ask the city about any past work on the property. All permits must be finalized before a rental inspection, and the city publishes a document on permit requirements for unpermitted work.

Did you finish a garage, enclose a patio or swap out mechanical systems years back? Confirm the permit was closed. Cash buyers often accept the house as it stands, but a financed buyer's inspector may flag open permits. Phone the city's rental program office or the permit counter, and save receipts and final inspection records to hand the buyer.

Selling with a tenant in the house

Selling is possible, but whoever lives there holds legal rights until a formal process runs its course. The opening move is a written notice to vacate, three days minimum unless the lease sets another period. Hand it over, tape it inside the door, mail it, or email it if the lease allows.

If the tenant refuses to leave, the case moves to justice court. Four days must pass between service and trial, and the hearing itself is set 10 to 21 days from filing. County court appeals have to be made within five days of judgment, and six days after a final judgment the court can issue a writ of possession. A 30-day federal notice can also apply to some covered properties.

  • Many cash buyers take occupied houses and keep the lease.
  • A tenant change ends the city license, so a buyer who brings in new tenants must pass a fresh inspection.
  • Ask the justice court that serves Mesquite for filing details.

Typical sale timeline

The sequence barely changes from one buyer type to the next. Once you know it, you can tell whether a promised closing date holds up.

  • Offer and contract: written terms are accepted and a title company opens the file.
  • Title search: liens, back taxes and recording defects get flagged.
  • Rental or permit review: a former rental or a house with remodeling needs its licenses and permits closed out.
  • Closing: everyone signs, the county clerk files the deed, and your net proceeds are released.

Buyers with a mortgage bring in an appraisal and underwriting. Cash buyers do without both, and that is mostly why their closings are faster. A few days before signing, ask your title contact for an estimated closing statement.

Property taxes when a Mesquite house sells

The lien attaches on January 1, which makes the owner on that date responsible for the year's bill. Statements arrive about October 1.

  • After January 31 penalty and interest begin to build.
  • Two payments are permitted, the first by November 30 and the second by June 30.
  • Owners aged 65 or older can split it into four.
  • A buyer who closes after January 1 can claim a homestead for the remaining months even if you never did.

Normally the title company divides the bill between you and the buyer and pays it from your funds. Ask to see the payoff and proration sheet before you sign.

Where the deed gets filed

Filing happens with the clerk of the county where the parcel is located. For reference, Dallas County received the first plat of the Mesquite townsite in 1873.

Before recording, a notary or similar officer has to acknowledge the signature. One 2023 clerk manual puts the charge at $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for each extra page, with capped records fees added. Call the clerk for the current schedule.

What if I am behind on payments or inherited the house?

Time matters in both cases. A foreclosure ends at a public auction on a first Tuesday, once notice has been posted for 21 days. Paying what is overdue within 20 days of the default notice can stop it, and selling before the auction date protects your equity.

Inheriting a house starts a four-year clock to probate any will. Heirs showing who may sign might need a muniment of title, a small estate affidavit or a full administration, and a bare affidavit of heirship is sometimes refused by title companies.

Where to begin

Start with the deed, newest tax bill, payoff letter and any rental license or permit papers. Gather cash offers and set them beside a listing estimate. Get closing costs and timing from every buyer in writing.

Frequently asked questions

How fast can a Mesquite house close on a cash offer?

Usually in a few weeks, because no lender underwriting or appraisal is involved. Liens and title work can add days, so put a target date in the contract.

Should I fix up the house first?

Not for a cash sale, where buyers usually accept the house as is. Repairs matter more if you list, since financed buyers bring appraisers who may require fixes.

Does the city regulate houses sold to landlords?

Every rental needs registration, an inspection and a local contact within 40 miles. The license lapses with a tenant change or after three years with the same tenant.

Who covers taxes at closing?

The title company prorates the year's bill and pays your portion from proceeds. Because the lien attaches January 1, review the split on the closing statement.

What happens to liens on the house?

Closing proceeds pay them off, as shown on a payoff statement from the title company. A rental review in Mesquite also wants taxes current and no open liens.

What to weigh before selling a McAllen house

Repair costs, any outside claim on the title and your cash deadline normally settle it. With McAllen prices modest beside the Dallas suburbs, a few thousand dollars of work or fees can swallow a large portion of what you net.

On July 1, 2025 the city was estimated at 150,640 residents, up 5.9 percent from 142,188 in 2020. It is a steady, unhurried rise.

  • Agent: the biggest pool of buyers and the longest wait.
  • On your own: you keep the fee and handle the forms.
  • Cash: no repairs or showings, but below-retail money.

McAllen home values and rents

Among large Texas cities, McAllen sits at the affordable end. Between 2020 and 2024 an owned home had a median value of $190,400, and a household had a median income of $61,579.
