Renters occupy four in ten homes, so tenant-occupied houses are part of what is for sale. Commutes average 21.9 minutes.

Hidalgo County and McAllen's land records

McAllen lies on U.S. Highway 83 in southern Hidalgo County, and that county's offices keep its deeds and tax accounts. The land goes back to Spanish grants of 1767 and the later McAllen Ranch, and the town incorporated in 1911.

Colonias of different sizes surround the city, so a buyer might ask about water, power and lot status. If your lot is out toward the edge of town, keep the survey and utility records close.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your McAllen house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Local factors that affect a McAllen sale

Get an inspector's view of the roof, cooling system and drainage ahead of listing. Written repair estimates let you judge offers fairly.

  • Make sure the deed names every current owner, especially when the house moved down a family without probate.
  • Ask the Hidalgo County tax office for the balance owed, earlier years included.
  • Verify homestead, over-65, disability or veteran exemptions with the Hidalgo appraisal district.

English and Spanish are both common in deals here, so a bilingual title officer and translated documents can keep a sale moving.

Short-term rental registration

McAllen wants every short-term rental unit registered annually. A rental is any residential dwelling or accessory building let for less than 30 consecutive days. Paperwork goes to the environmental health and code compliance department at the McAllen Development Center, North 15th Street.

If guests have stayed in your house, a buyer will want proof that the registration is current. The ordinance requires the following:

  • The fee is $100 per unit, and registration runs one year unless ownership changes.
  • A local contact must be on call day and night and arrive in person inside an hour when a complaint comes in.
  • Each sleeping space needs a working smoke detector, and an exit map has to be posted.
  • A monthly hotel occupancy tax report is due even in months with no bookings.

Breaking the rules is a Class C misdemeanor, with fines up to $500 and every day of violation counted on its own. The director can revoke a permit, and the property then waits twelve months to reapply. Since registration does not override private deed restrictions, check any HOA rules as well.

Eviction when a McAllen house has a tenant

Eviction opens with a written notice to vacate, typically three days unless a lease provides otherwise, and a justice court case comes next.

  • Hearings are set 10 to 21 days after the filing date.
  • The loser has just 5 days after judgment to take an appeal to county court.
  • The writ of possession is available from day six following final judgment.

Occupied houses do sell, often to investors. When you need it vacant for closing, schedule the notices before you sign a contract.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy McAllen houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Appraisal notices and protests

Each spring Hidalgo County Appraisal District sends out a Notice of Appraised Value, but only to owners whose market value rose $1,000 or more. Three numbers appear: market value on January 1, the assessed or net appraised value after limits such as the homestead cap, and taxable value after exemptions.

Think the number is too high? Protest by May 15 or 30 days after the notice goes out, whichever falls later. You can mail it or take it to the district's office on South Professional Drive in Edinburg. Afterward, an online account shows the district's evidence, and an informal meeting with an appraiser follows. Refuse the settlement offer and you go before the Appraisal Review Board, where a family member or friend may represent you with an Appointment of Agent form.

A successful protest lowers the tax bill but not the sale price, because buyers pay what the market bears. It can still reduce the tax split between you and the buyer at closing.

Behind on payments or inherited the house

If you close ahead of a foreclosure auction, the equity stays with you and a deficiency suit is avoided. Inherited houses go several ways. A transfer on death deed recorded in the owner's lifetime skips probate, and without it heirs can file a muniment of title or an affidavit of heirship, though buyers can say no to the latter.

Getting a McAllen house ready for buyers

Valley heat and heavy rain make three things count with shoppers: the cooling system, the roof, and where water goes when a storm passes. Switch the AC on before every showing, patch leaks you know of, and check that gutters and grading push runoff away from the slab. Each is a cheap job compared with what an inspector's report can cost you.

Long family ownership can leave messy records behind. Dig out deeds, tax receipts, utility bills and any survey, and keep them together in one folder. Where an owner has died and title is murky, begin the cleanup before an offer arrives, since nothing closes until someone with authority can sign.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Steps from offer to closing

Your yes to an offer starts a records review at the title company, covering liens, unpaid taxes and gaps in ownership. Houses passed down within families sometimes lack a recorded probate, so this step carries weight in McAllen. Cleared problems come first, then your signature on a deed that the county clerk records.

You will need the deed, the latest tax statement and a payoff letter if a loan remains. Financed buyers add an inspection and appraisal, and cash buyers do not, so the cash calendar is frequently far shorter. Get the price, closing date and cost split in writing, then hold the numbers up against a listing estimate that already subtracts commissions and repairs. A lease or odd lot situation deserves a mention to the title company right away. Keep every email and text from the buyer, since a written trail settles disputes about what was promised.

Frequently asked questions

Which county is McAllen in?

Hidalgo County. McAllen is in the southern part of the county, so Hidalgo County offices handle your deed and tax account.

What is a typical McAllen home value?

The 2020-2024 estimate is $190,400 for an owned home. Repairs, size and age move any single house away from that figure.

Can I sell an inherited McAllen house without probate?

Sometimes, if the owner recorded a transfer on death deed beforehand. Without one, heirs choose among probate, a muniment of title and an affidavit of heirship.

How fast can a landlord remove a tenant in Texas?

Expect a hearing 10 to 21 days after filing, then a writ of possession from day six after judgment. Appeals have a 5 day limit.

Does selling help if I am behind on my mortgage?

It can, when closing comes before the auction. Proceeds pay the lien first. Ask the servicer for a payoff statement.

Will a fast sale work for a Pasadena home?

Yes. Southeastern Harris County is home to Pasadena, where houses change hands through cash offers, investor purchases and agent listings alike. Closings go fastest for sellers who arrive with the deed, a mortgage payoff figure and a tax certificate in hand before signing the contract.

Rarely is the buyer the bottleneck. Delays come from title defects, an unpaid tax year, a tenant or heirs who cannot agree. Because the county is huge, give the title company your complete legal description and the account number printed on your tax statement from day one, so your lot is never confused with a similar address.

Pasadena in brief

Pasadena is an industrial suburb with a farming past. John H. Burnett of Galveston founded it in 1893, a rail line followed in 1894, and after the 1900 Galveston hurricane the area became a strawberry center. Ship channel industries then reshaped the economy, and today jobs are tied to refineries, the Bayport industrial district and the Johnson Space Center in nearby Clear Lake.

The city covers 58.6 square miles, and the school district has been independent since 1899. Buyers weigh commute, schools and employers, so mention which of those a house sits close to. San Jacinto College and Texas Chiropractic College are in town, and the Pasadena Rodeo and the San Jacinto Strawberry Festival are the big local events.

Who bills property tax

Values come from the Harris Central Appraisal District. Collection on a Pasadena home belongs to the Harris County Tax Office, which bills the other units on your statement too. January 1 is the valuation date, and each taxing unit picks its own rate.

A statement is due on receipt, and paying by January 31 of the following year avoids penalty and interest. Obtain a fresh statement from the tax office before accepting an offer, so the contract figure agrees with county records.

Penalties and payment rules

Confirm every date with the county office first.

Harris County property tax rules for late payers
TopicWhat applies

First late month6% penalty and 1% interest for February

Tax salesHeld by the eight county constables

Unpaid taxes can be settled from your closing proceeds, so being behind does not by itself stop a sale. It does enlarge the payoff, which is why you should request a figure dated for closing day.

Payment plans for late taxes

Once taxes go delinquent, an owner with a homestead can sign an installment agreement at any point. Current-year agreements open the first business day of February, and requests arrive after January 31 and before March 1, with the 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest assessed for February.

  • Homestead plans run from 12 months up to 36 months.
  • A deferral can protect the amount owed, but interest of 5 percent per year is added for each year taxes stay delinquent.
  • Online and phone payments count if completed by 11:59 p.m. on or before the due date.
  • Mail must be postmarked on or before the due date.

Someone about to move can lean on a plan for breathing room and clear the balance from closing proceeds.

Taxes at a Pasadena closing

A tax certificate from the title company shows what has been paid, and any gap is subtracted from your proceeds. Watch one timing trap: a closing between November 15 and January 31 when your mortgage escrows taxes. Phone the lender as soon as the date is fixed so the bill gets paid and the certificate comes back clean.

  • Tell the title company if the lender paid this year's bill from escrow.
  • Ask for any escrow balance back after the payoff.
  • If you claimed a homestead exemption and then sold, the county asks you to correct the account.

A lien stays on the property while taxes are unpaid, so the buyer cannot get clear title until they are.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Pasadena houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Exemptions and caps to check

Part of what the next owner pays is decided by exemptions. Each school district has to give a $140,000 homestead exemption, with another $60,000 for seniors and disabled owners.

  • A homestead's taxable value may climb no faster than 10 percent a year.
  • A disabled veteran may get $5,000 to $12,000 off by rating, and a 100 percent rating can mean a full exemption.
  • If you never claimed the exemption, a buyer late in the year may still claim it for what is left of that year.

Several taxing units can appear on one Pasadena bill, so go through every line.

Tenants and tax judgments

You can still sell in either case, though each follows its own Texas procedure.

  • Tenant. Eviction starts with written notice to vacate and a justice court case. A writ of possession is available six days after a final judgment. A buyer will ask for the lease and deposit details.
  • Tax judgment. The eight constables hold tax sales for property taken to judgment. Buyers take the property as is, and sales are final.
  • Collection firm. Accounts sent to a law firm face a further 15 to 20 percent penalty.

Paying the tax before judgment leaves more of your proceeds intact. Ask the county for a payoff figure.

Choosing between cash and a listing

Listing may bring a higher price, though commissions, showings and a buyer's lender come with it. Selling for cash gives up part of the price for certainty: the closing date is yours, repairs are not demanded and a loan cannot collapse.

Deferred maintenance or back taxes point toward a cash buyer. A move-in-ready house on a quiet street might do better on the open market. Obtain a written cash offer and a listing estimate, deduct repairs, commissions and carrying costs from the listing figure, then see which is bigger.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Questions to put to each buyer

Ask who covers the title policy, how many days closing takes and whether the price can shift after a walkthrough. Request proof of funds, and learn how much earnest money is deposited and when it comes back to you. Be cautious about anyone who asks for a fee before making an offer or will not commit terms to paper.

If the house is tied up with a tenant, a lien or heirs, say so at the start. Buyers who hear about a problem late tend to cut their offer.

Documents and steps before closing

Start a folder now: deed, latest tax bill, name and phone of whoever services your mortgage, any lease. Add court or estate papers if an owner has died, since a buyer must see who is allowed to sign.

When you say yes to an offer, the title company hunts for liens, requests the tax certificate and books the signing. Whatever you owe on the loan or in taxes is taken from the price, and the rest reaches you once the deed is recorded. Because cash skips the lender's appraisal and approval, fewer pieces can push the date back.

Rank offers by what lands in your account, and get the price, closing date and cost split written down by each buyer.

Frequently asked questions

Harris County, through its tax office, while the Harris Central Appraisal District handles values. Request a payoff and a certificate ahead of closing.

Must I clear delinquent taxes before selling?

No, the balance can come from your proceeds at closing. Penalty and interest keep growing, so ask for a total dated for closing day.

When is the county's tax deadline?

January 31 of the year following the tax year. Pay by then and nothing extra is added.

What happens to my escrow if I sell in winter?

The lender may already have paid the bill. Tell it the closing date quickly and ask for any leftover balance once the loan is paid off.

Can I sell with a tenant in place?

Yes. The buyer inherits the lease unless you first go through the Texas notice and court steps to empty the house.

When you describe a house to a buyer, tie it to a part of town: the older core, the Baylor area or a newer outer street. That helps a buyer place it quickly. Ask your title company how long a typical Waco closing takes so you can plan a move around it.

Waco housing numbers

A typical owned Waco home is valued at $221,700 in the 2020-2024 estimates, and only 49.4 percent of units are owner-occupied. That split explains why investors are a visible part of the market.

Waco housing snapshot
MeasureWaco

About 79.1 percent of residents were at the same address a year earlier, so roughly one in five had moved. The city covers 88.73 square miles of land with an average trip to work of 18.7 minutes, and a short commute is worth naming in a listing.

With rents near $1,165 a month, a rental-minded buyer will test an offer against that figure. Have the lease, deposit records and repair invoices ready.

An investor looking at a Waco rental will usually care about three things: the rent the house can command, the cost of getting it ready for the next tenant, and how soon the keys change hands. A house with a tenant already paying on time can be more attractive to that buyer, not less. A vacant house with deferred repairs can still sell, just at a price that reflects the work.

Tax sales in McLennan County

Unpaid property tax is secured by a lien, and paying back taxes on a property does not make someone its owner. Tax sales are the final remedy, and the City of Waco says they may occur on the first Tuesday of any month.

  • The McLennan County Tax Office conducts its tax sales online through GovEase, so confirm the current format with the office.
  • A property drawing no bid within city limits is struck off to the City of Waco, which resells it after a six-month or two-year redemption period.
  • Property without a homestead exemption can be bought back within six months by paying 25 percent of the auction price plus taxes, costs and fees.
  • Homestead or special-use property has two years, at 25 percent in the first year and 50 percent in the second.

Taxes are due on receipt of the bill and are delinquent if not paid before February 1. Online payments carry a 2.19 percent card fee or a $1.50 flat electronic check fee.

Deeds, heirs, tenants and exemptions

Deeds for Waco property are filed with the McLennan County Clerk after a notary acknowledgment. Ask that office for the full recording charge on your document.

For an inherited house, an affidavit of heirship has no court review behind it, and no law forces a title company to accept it. If a tenant will not leave, a justice court case follows written notice, and a writ of possession cannot issue until six days after judgment.

For homestead owners, school districts must give a $140,000 exemption, and a veteran rated 100 percent disabled can receive a total exemption on the homestead.

City offices for zoning and building questions

Calling the right desk first saves a week of phone tag. Fix-ups, additions and demolitions can all raise questions that only the city can answer, so a short call before you commit to work is time well spent.

  • Zoning and setback questions: Planning Services Division, (254) 750-5650.
  • What may be built on a lot: Inspection Services and Plan Review, (254) 750-5674.
  • Water and sewer access: Engineering Department, (254) 750-5440.
  • Affordable housing programs: Housing and Community Development Services, (254) 750-5656.

A buyer using housing assistance may have a timeline of their own, so ask early. The city sells tax-foreclosed properties by sealed bid, and most are sold at the courthouse auctions through a law firm. A seller whose house might otherwise end up there has far more control by selling before a tax sale takes place.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Waco houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

What to prepare before you sell

Collect the deed, your loan payoff, the latest tax bill and any lease. If repairs were done, add the invoices. A title company can then check for liens and tell you how quickly it can close.

If the house has a mortgage, request a written payoff that stays good through your target closing date. If it has none, ask the title company to confirm that no old lien remains on the record. Old liens from contractors or past owners are easy to miss, and they are far cheaper to clear before an offer than during the final week.

On the day itself, bring a photo ID, hand over all keys and openers, and schedule your utility shutoff. Expect the signing itself to take under an hour, with the notary confirming each signature before the deed goes to the McLennan County Clerk. A cash sale keeps this part simple: no appraisal visit, no loan underwriter, and a closing date set by the title work and your own plans. If a delay does come up, it is usually a missing signature from a co-owner or an unresolved lien, so find out early who else is on the deed and whether anyone must sign with you.

Frequently asked questions

When are Waco tax sales held?

The City of Waco says tax sales may occur on the first Tuesday of any month, while the McLennan County Tax Office conducts its sales online through GovEase. Confirm the format with the tax office.

Can a former owner reclaim a Waco house after a tax sale?

Sometimes. Property without a homestead exemption can be bought back within six months at 25 percent of the auction price plus costs, and homestead or special-use property has two years at 25 or 50 percent.

Does a tenant slow a Waco sale?

It can. A buyer needs the lease term and any deposit records. If the tenant must leave, the case runs through justice court after written notice.

Who do I ask about the tax balance on my Waco house?

The McLennan County Tax Office, which also sets out the due-date rules and payment options. The appraisal district sets value but does not collect.

How is ownership of an inherited Waco house documented?

Through probate or a court-backed route, or by a transfer on death deed filed before the owner died. A sworn heirship statement may not satisfy a buyer.

How quickly can a Midland house change hands?

Quickly, when the price reflects condition. Midland has an energy-driven economy, and investors, landlords and cash buyers all buy there. The usual trade applies: speed and certainty against top price.

Ask every buyer how long a written offer stays open, and compare the offers side by side.

Midland's market in brief

Midland calls itself the heart of the Permian Basin, and energy companies and Midland ISD are among its largest employers. The metro population is reported at 193,139 for 2026, up 8.1 percent from 2020, with a median age of 31.5.

A younger population tends to include renters and first-time buyers, so an investor or a buyer using financing may both compete for your house. Apartment rents are rising while occupancy has improved, which is relevant if your buyer is an investor. Rely on written offers and an agent's comparable sales for pricing, since citywide figures say little about one house.

Which selling routes make sense in Midland?

The usual choices are a listing, a direct cash sale or a local investor. Let the condition of the house guide you, not the biggest number.

  • Agent listing. Fits move-in-ready houses; you carry repairs and financing risk.
  • Cash buyer. Handles foundation, roof, plumbing or wiring problems and short-notice relocations.
  • Investor with a short close or leaseback. Gives you time to move out.
  • Keep and rent. Practical only if you can manage repairs and turnover from afar.

Work out what you would actually keep after fees, repairs and carrying costs under each.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Midland house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Midland permits that could trip up a sale

A residential permit is needed in Midland for new construction, additions, remodels, repairs and detached accessory buildings, and it is pulled by the owner or by a bonded contractor on the city's registry.

Work must begin within 180 days of issue, and a permit lapses if building halts for more than 180 days. You email the request to the permit clerk, paying 25 percent of the fee when you submit and 75 percent on approval. Plan on 5 to 7 business days for review. If earlier work went unpermitted, ask the city how to document it before an inspector raises it.

Anyone running a short-term rental also owes a seven percent hotel occupancy tax to the city on the price paid.

Midland property tax exemptions

Midland homeowners get school-district homestead relief plus local options. The Midland Central Appraisal District lists the amounts for each taxing unit, which matters to a buyer reading your tax history.

Midland Central Appraisal District homestead and senior exemptions
ExemptionTaxing unitAmount
HomesteadMidland ISD$140,000 plus a 10% local option (minimum $5,000)
HomesteadMidland County3% local option (minimum $5,000), $0 granted
Over 65Midland County$150,000
Over 65City of Midland$8,000
Over 65 or disabledMidland ISD$60,000

Disabled-veteran exemptions run from $5,000 up to $12,000 off assessed value by rating, with 100 percent homesteadable value for a full rating.

Tenants and unwelcome occupants

Tenants and trespassers are handled differently. A tenant must be eviction-processed: a written notice of at least three days, unless the lease differs, and then a justice court case that has its hearing 10 to 21 days after filing. Someone who moved in without permission may be removable faster.

Property Code chapter 24B covers a non-family occupant who was never a tenant. The owner can ask the sheriff or constable to remove that person without a court case, provided the occupant stayed after being told to go and no suit is pending. Removing the wrong person invites a lawsuit, so check each condition with the sheriff's office first.

  • After a judgment, a writ of possession must issue within 60 days, though a court can stretch that to 90 for good cause.
  • Many cash buyers will purchase an occupied home, so you do not have to wait.
Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Midland houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Paperwork to gather in Midland

Having these ready saves time with the title company.

  • Deed and mortgage payoff statement.
  • Latest tax bill, plus any exemption notice the appraisal district sent.
  • Permit records for remodels, repairs or outbuildings.
  • Lease and rent roll if someone lives there.
  • Roof, water or foundation reports.

Midland takes permit requests by email, so keep scans of old permits handy. If a permit is missing, call the permit clerk at 432-685-7390.

From accepted offer to closing

After the contract is signed, a title company handles the paperwork. It combs county records for liens, back taxes and anything clouding ownership, and asks you for a payoff letter and tax bill. A problem it finds, say a contractor's lien from old work or a co-owner who never signed, must be fixed before the deed can change hands.

At closing you sign the deed and the county clerk records it. The title company then pays off your loan and your share of taxes and sends you the balance. A buyer using a mortgage brings an appraisal and underwriting, and either can renegotiate the price. Cash buyers usually skip both, so their sales can wrap up sooner.

Selling a house that needs work

Shifting foundations, tired roofs and bad plumbing or wiring tend to turn away financed buyers, since lenders and appraisers insist on repairs first. A cash buyer builds the repair into the offer and takes the house as is. You avoid contractor bids, permits and months of carrying costs.

Get any offer in writing with the price, closing date and closing cost split spelled out, then compare it with what a fixed-up listing would net after fees. When the numbers land close together, the quicker sale usually makes more sense.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

City projects near your address

Midland's strategic plan includes capital projects, parks, downtown redevelopment and economic zones. Street, drainage or downtown work near your address can change how buyers see the block, so ask the city's planning office what is scheduled near you.

When Texas tax bills come due

Statements go out near October 1, and a bill still unpaid after January 31 is delinquent. February 1 brings a six percent penalty and one percent interest, with further charges each month after that.

The lien for the year belongs to whoever owned the house on January 1. Typically the title company splits the bill between buyer and seller and takes your part from the proceeds. To protest your value, file by mid-May or within 30 days of your notice, whichever comes later.

Conveying an inherited Midland house

The person who signs the deed has to show they have the authority. Depending on the case, that means an administrator's deed, a muniment of title order, a recorded affidavit of death paired with a transfer on death deed, or as a last resort an affidavit of heirship.

A small-estate affidavit works when everything apart from the homestead adds up to $75,000 or less and every heir agrees.

Questions to ask a cash buyer

Find out who the buyer is, whether the price covers the whole house as is, and who holds earnest money. Ask how many days to close and what happens if a lien surfaces. Read the contract before committing, and let the title company prepare the closing statement.

Frequently asked questions

Is selling as-is allowed in Midland?

Cash buyers regularly purchase houses with foundation, roof or plumbing problems. The offer will reflect the repair cost.

Which Midland repairs require permits?

Repairs, remodels, additions and detached accessory buildings. An owner or registered bonded contractor applies, and a permit lapses if work does not begin within 180 days.

What homestead relief does a Midland buyer get?

Midland ISD gives $140,000 plus a 10 percent local option. A purchaser may claim it right away if you never did.

Who settles the tax bill when the sale closes?

The title company, normally, with your share taken from proceeds. The lien attaches January 1, so read the split on the closing statement.

What paperwork proves I can sell an inherited house?

Court or recorded documents showing authority: a muniment of title, administration, a transfer on death deed, or an affidavit of heirship.

Why Round Rock's location draws buyers

Round Rock sits on Interstate 35 in south central Williamson County, roughly sixteen miles north of downtown Austin. Housing demand follows Austin's growth and Dell Technologies, which has its headquarters here. Expect buyers who commute toward Austin, work for technology employers, or want a house close to Old Settlers Park, the 570-acre park the city built with sales tax revenue.

Dell is the city's largest employer, and the city says the sales tax revenue from Dell sales has helped reduce property taxes for decades. A large employer base supports steady buyer interest, but your price still depends on your street, school zone and condition. Compare recent nearby sales rather than city-wide claims.

Historic overlay zoning

Old Town is a small cluster of restored limestone buildings now surrounded by the rest of the city. It matters if your house sits in a historic overlay area, because alterations to a structure or site with Historic Overlay Zoning need a Certificate of Appropriateness before a building permit. That includes fences and accessory structures.

Preservation staff can be reached through the Planning and Development Services desk at 512-218-5428. If you are selling an older home, ask whether the overlay applies before promising a buyer an addition or a new fence.

Building rules that can come up in a sale

Selling needs no permit, yet loose ends from past work can slow a contract. The city requires a permit to build, alter, repair or demolish, and for work on electrical, gas, mechanical or plumbing systems.

  • The city runs a one-permit system, so related electrical, plumbing and mechanical work goes on one permit, and all contractors must be named on it.
  • A permit becomes invalid if authorized work does not start within six months.
  • Contractors and subcontractors must register, with no registration or annual fee.
  • Sheds under 200 square feet and 15 feet tall still need a permit as accessory structures.

Carports, pergolas, pools and similar structures are allowed only in side or rear yards, cannot sit over easements or setbacks, and are capped at 15 feet tall. Call the Building Inspection Division at 512-218-5550 about older projects on your house. For fence permit questions, call Code Enforcement at 512-341-3329.

Do you need a certificate of occupancy?

For a house sale it usually means nothing. The city issues one only when a space is newly built, remodeled or renovated, and a new occupant who makes only cosmetic changes will not receive one.

  • The Fire Marshal's Office conducts annual fire safety inspections for commercial space, so this applies to a business, not a home sale.
  • If you converted a garage or finished an addition, ask the building office whether the permit was closed out.
  • For a move, contact Atmos for gas, Oncor for electricity and the city's utility billing office for water, and plan the transfers around your closing date.

The Williamson County and Cities Health District reviews food service plans, which would matter if you ran a home-based food business that you want to hand off with the house.

Renting instead of selling

You may be able to, but check the city's current short-term rental and hotel occupancy tax rules first. Ordinances change, so ask the city before you list a short-term rental.

A tenant in place also complicates showings, and many buyers want the house empty at closing.

Homeowner exemptions and tax caps in Williamson County

Williamson Central Appraisal District sets home values, and a homeowner's exemption takes part of that value off the taxable total. A late application can be filed up to two years after the tax becomes delinquent, under Tax Code Section 11.431(a).

Round Rock homeowner exemption rules at Williamson CAD
TopicRule
Regular filing periodJanuary 1 through April 30
Late filingUp to two years after the tax becomes delinquent
ReapplyingNot needed unless the chief appraiser asks or you move

The age 65 exemption starts the year you turn 65, and a disability exemption generally tracks Social Security disability benefits. A mobile home owner must furnish the title or a verified purchase contract. A surviving spouse who is 55 or older can inherit a school tax ceiling, but only when the late spouse received the over-65 exemption.

Property tax deadlines at a Round Rock closing

Round Rock follows the statewide tax calendar. At closing the title company settles whatever is owed for the year, along with any penalty. Request a current statement from the Williamson County tax office first. A bill still open on February 1 is delinquent and begins to build penalty and interest.

Inherited, in foreclosure or tied up with a tenant

Inheritance, foreclosure and tenancy each carry their own paperwork.

  • Inherited house: the deed route depends on whether a will exists, whether the owner recorded a beneficiary deed, or whether a court must appoint someone.
  • Foreclosure: a lender's sale is preceded by default and sale notices, so the calendar is fixed and a closing before the auction date matters.
  • Tenant: a written notice to vacate comes first, then a justice court case.

A title company can tell you what must be recorded before a buyer's lender will fund. The title company usually handles recording after closing, and the county clerk's fee schedule is in the Texas Courts clerk manual. Your settlement statement shows the final charge.

What happens between contract and closing

Once the contract is signed, the title company starts a file, runs the title search and requests your loan payoff. It also requests a tax statement from the Williamson County tax office. If an older permit was never closed out, the buyer's agent may raise it here, so call the Building Inspection Division early.

On closing day you sign the deed. Your loan and any tax due are paid out of the sale money, the deed is recorded, and the remainder is yours. A cash buyer needs no lender approval, so the closing date depends mostly on how quickly liens clear and the title work finishes.

Plan your move-out around the utilities. Atmos handles gas, Oncor handles electricity and the city's utility billing office handles water, and each needs a stop or transfer date that matches the day you hand over keys.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Weighing a cash offer against a listing

Cash buyers are busy in Round Rock, and what they offer reflects repairs and location. Take a listing estimate, remove commissions and carrying costs, and set the remainder beside the cash figure. Going cash avoids lender appraisal and repair haggling and lets you pick the date.

Before you decide, gather permit records, a tax statement and a payoff letter so each buyer sees the same facts and quotes you on the same basis.

Frequently asked questions

Do cash buyers operate in Round Rock?

Yes. Offers vary with the condition and location of the house, so weigh a cash bid against a listing estimate after commissions and carrying costs.

Does a Round Rock fence repair require approval?

Call Code Enforcement at 512-341-3329, the number listed for fence permit questions. Building permits and inspections questions go to 512-218-5550.

Can I claim a homestead exemption after buying mid-year?

Possibly. A buyer who moves in after January 1 may qualify for the remaining months of that tax year if the prior owner held no homestead exemption.

When do Round Rock area property taxes become late?

Once January 31 passes. From February 1 an unpaid bill is delinquent and accrues penalty and interest.

Who pays to record the deed?

Usually the title company records it after closing, and the settlement statement lists the final charge.

Selling in Lewisville?

How to sell a Lewisville house fast

You can sell a Lewisville house to a cash buyer or list it, and repairs plus your deadline usually settle the question. Located in Denton County in the north Dallas-Fort Worth area, the city has rental and tax rules that influence what investors and owner-occupants will pay.

If the house has been a rental, look at the city's rental inspection and short-term rental rules first. Buyers who plan to keep it as a rental will ask about both.

Lewisville's property tax rate

The city's fiscal 2026 rate is $0.419009 per $100. Because the county and school district add their own levies, your statement from the Denton County tax office shows the total you owe.

The median residential bill is $6,606, split 65 percent to Lewisville ISD, 24 percent to the city and 11 percent to Denton County. In dollars that is $4,294 for the school district, $1,585 for the city and $727 for the county. A penny on the city rate raises about $2.154 million. The school district drives most of what a buyer will pay each year, and the city's share is the smaller piece.

Rental inspections before a sale

Lewisville runs an inspection program for single-family rentals, with no fee or registration, that began July 1, 2008. Three things trigger an inspection: the owner or a future tenant telling the city, a tenant asking for a water transfer, or a complaint. Minor violations do not block move-in, but life-safety issues do. Apartments, mobile homes and houses outside city limits are not covered.

The Code Enforcement Division runs the program, and its number is 972.219.3470. The inspection list works as a handy checklist for any seller, rented or not.

  • House number visible from the street.
  • Roof, gutters, siding and exterior doors in repair.
  • Windows and screens intact, and fences or pool fences maintained.
  • Electrical service drop at least 10 feet above the ground and the meter secured.
  • Grass, weeds, hedges and trees along the right-of-way trimmed.
  • No inoperable vehicles, no cars parked on grass and no standing water.

Clearing these items before you list avoids a code complaint that could surface mid-sale, and it removes a common buyer objection.

Short-term rental limits

Lewisville issues short-term rental permits yearly and stops at 150 active ones.

Lewisville short-term rental rules
RuleRequirement
Permit termOne year, not transferable

Active permit cap150
Spacing, single-family or duplex1,000 feet between rentals
Multifamily limit3% of units or 2 units, whichever is greater

A permit stays with the owner and address, so a buyer who wants to host guests must apply fresh, with no promise of approval. Existing permitted rentals are treated as legal non-conforming until the use stops for six months. Hotel occupancy tax is reported monthly.

What a short-term rental buyer will ask

If your house was listed on a booking site, expect questions about the permit. The application closes when permits plus pending applications reach the cap of 150, and it reopens if permits are denied, revoked or expire. Current holders can reapply at least 30 days before expiry even when applications are closed.

  • A bedroom needs at least 70 square feet, and 50 square feet per person when more than one person shares it.
  • A 70 to 99 square foot bedroom counts as one occupant, and 100 to 149 as two.
  • Ads must show the permit number and say the unit cannot host paid events or parties.
  • More than two city code citations in a permit year can lead to revocation.

Because a permit cannot be transferred, the buyer starts in the application queue. The permitting office at permitting@cityoflewisville.com or 972.219.3470 can say whether space is open.

Denton County tax dates

Bills arrive in the fall and are usually due by January 31. The lien attaches on January 1, so the owner on that date is responsible for the year's tax.

  • An over-65 or disabled homeowner can ask the county about a four-payment plan.
  • A value protest is due by May 15 or 30 days after notice, whichever comes later.
  • After the appraisal board, appeals can go to district court or arbitration.

Get a current payoff and tax statement from the Denton County tax office before closing.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Lewisville houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

If a Lewisville house is in trouble

A lien for unpaid tax can end in a tax sale. A former owner can redeem land sold at a tax sale, paying a stated premium, within two years for a homestead or 180 days for other property. Any excess from a tax foreclosure can be claimed by the former owner for two years.

Should a tenant remain after the sale, the new owner may have to file an eviction case in justice court, where the tenant receives at least four days' notice of the trial. Selling before any of this starts keeps your options open.

Selling with tenants in the house

Many Lewisville houses are rented at some point. If yours is, decide before listing whether the buyer will take the lease or you will deliver the house empty. Tell the tenant early and in writing. A buyer who wants to keep the house as a rental will ask whether it passed the city's single-family rental inspection, and records of past inspections answer that fast.

An investor will often take a leased house as it stands. A buyer who wants to live in it needs possession, which means ending the lease on a schedule that fits the closing date. Put that schedule in the contract so nobody guesses.

Talking to the city before you list

A short call to the Code Enforcement Division can settle questions that would otherwise show up during the buyer's inspection. Ask whether any complaint or violation is open on the address, whether a rental inspection is on record and, for a house used for guests, whether a short-term rental permit is active. Ask the permitting office whether any permit for work on the house is still open.

Keep a note of who answered, and send the buyer or closing office whatever the city confirms.

What to have ready before accepting an offer

  • A copy of the deed and any survey.
  • The latest Denton County tax statement and exemption list.
  • Rental inspection or short-term rental permit records, if the house was rented.
  • A payoff letter from your lender.

With those four items in hand, a buyer or the closing office can move from contract to closing without waiting on you. If you are unsure what the city has on file for the address, call Code Enforcement at 972.219.3470 and ask about open violations or permits before you list.

Steps from listing to closing

  1. Fix or note any exterior items from the inspection checklist.
  2. Get offers from a cash buyer and, if you choose, a listing agent.
  3. Compare what each leaves you after the loan payoff and the year's tax share.
  4. Sign with a notary and let the closing office record the deed.

A cash buyer can skip the lender's appraisal and many repair requests, which is why the process can finish sooner. A listing may bring a higher price but adds showings and a buyer's loan timeline.

Frequently asked questions

Can I sell my Lewisville house if it was a rental?

Yes. Buyers may ask whether it passed the city's single-family rental inspection, so have any records ready.

Can a buyer take over my Lewisville short-term rental permit?

No. A permit cannot be transferred. The new owner applies on their own, under the 150-permit cap and the spacing rules.

What is the Lewisville property tax rate?

The city's rate is $0.419009 per $100 for fiscal 2026. Your full bill also includes Denton County and the school district, so check your statement.

When are Denton County property taxes due?

In most cases by January 31, with penalty and interest from February 1. Some owners can use a split or installment plan.

Do I need Lewisville city approval to sell my home?

No city approval is needed just to sell. Contact the city if you have open code violations or permits, since a buyer will want those resolved.

Choosing how to sell in Carrollton

Three options exist in Carrollton: an agent, a sale on your own, or a cash buyer. Choosing cash trades some price for speed and no repair work. Choosing a listing trades time for the chance at a higher figure. Weigh your repair list, any liens and your moving date, then decide.

The city lies in parts of Dallas, Denton and Collin counties, and that affects everything that follows. Your appraisal district, tax bill and recording office all depend on which county your lot is in. Check the tax statement before you start.

Carrollton neighborhoods and buyer questions

Carrollton sits in the middle of the Dallas-Fort Worth metroplex. It has three DART light rail stations, including Downtown Carrollton Station on the Silver Line, and IH-35E, SH 121 and the President George Bush Turnpike run through or beside it. Houses near stations tend to appeal to commuters.

The city incorporated on June 14, 1913, and the older core holds houses from several eras. A house near the Elm Fork or an old creek bed may carry flood history, and a nearby house on Belt Line Road is recorded as flooding in 1908, the 1920s and the 1940s. If your lot sits low, a buyer may ask for flood insurance quotes, so pull together any claims history. Be ready for questions about commute time and school zoning, too.

Buyers also respond to what is close by. Downtown Carrollton centers on the Town Square, and the city lists sports complexes, hike and bike trails and a nature preserve among its amenities. Name the nearest one in your listing or when you talk with a buyer, since it is often what a family asks about first.

New short-term rentals are off the table

Carrollton passed Zoning Ordinance 4297 and Code Ordinance 4291 on December 2, 2025. No new short-term rental or bed and breakfast will be allowed, and only certain existing properties can qualify for a lodging license under Chapter 97 of the city code.

Carrollton rules for existing short-term rental operators
RequirementRule
Lodging licenseNeeded every year for each location
Ownership changeA new license and hotel occupancy tax number must be sought
Hotel occupancy taxRequired of all short-term rentals
Other rulesChapter 97, the zoning ordinance and other city codes apply

A license belongs to a specific owner and location, so a house that runs as a rental today may not be able to keep that use for a buyer. Say so early. Call Environmental Services at (972) 466-3060 for the status of your address.

Property taxes for Carrollton homeowners

With a city split across Dallas, Denton and Collin, the appraisal district and tax assessor change from parcel to parcel. The state rules are the same everywhere: January 1 sets value and the lien, and bills are due by January 31.

  • School districts give a $140,000 homestead exemption, with $60,000 more for seniors and disabled owners.
  • A senior or disabled owner's school tax can be frozen.
  • Homestead appraisals are limited to a 10 percent annual increase, with exceptions for new additions.
  • Protests are due by the May deadline printed on your notice.

Ask the county that bills your parcel for a payoff figure, and whether an installment plan exists on any delinquent balance. Cities and counties may add local exemptions, so ask your county for the current list.

If property tax goes unpaid before a sale

An unpaid bill gets worse each month. Penalty and interest start after January 31, interest has no ceiling, and a lawyer retained by the taxing unit can add up to 20 percent.

  • Collectors may offer installment plans on delinquent tax, up to 36 months in some cases, and a plan is required for a residence homestead.
  • A tax lien lets the unit sue to foreclose even after the owner changes, so unpaid tax must be paid at or before closing.
  • Homestead land sold at a tax sale carries a two-year redemption right with a premium, so ask a lawyer what applies.
  • A former owner has two years to claim surplus from a tax sale.

Before you accept any offer, request a payoff from the tax office that bills your lot.

How a Carrollton deed is recorded

The county clerk where your lot sits takes the deed, which could be Dallas, Denton or Collin. Confirm the county before you send anything. A deed mailed to the wrong office costs you days at the end of a sale. Warranty, special warranty and quitclaim deeds all need a signature and acknowledgment, usually before a notary.

Recording fees add up by page, so let the title company quote the exact total. It usually pays them at closing and files for you. An old tax lien or a mechanic's lien that turns up must be cleared before a buyer can get clear title.

Inherited house or loan in default

For an inherited house, find out whether the estate used a muniment of title, a small estate affidavit or an administration, since each leaves different paperwork for the county clerk. An affidavit of heirship is only a sworn statement that no court checks, and buyers can refuse it.

With a loan in default, you have 20 days to reinstate. A notice of sale then goes out 21 or more days before a first Tuesday auction. Lenders have two years after the sale to sue for a deficiency. Selling before the auction date can keep equity that costs would otherwise eat.

Steps from agreement to closing

Once you and a buyer agree, the title company opens the file. It confirms which county holds your parcel, requests payoffs from the tax office and any lender, and searches for liens. If a rental license or flood question exists, it goes into the disclosures now, not at the table. The deed is then drawn up, signed and acknowledged, and recorded with the right county clerk. If heirs are selling, the probate or affidavit paperwork is reviewed before any of that begins, because a title company will not close without proof of who may sign.

What to hand a buyer

Collect the latest tax bill, any payoff letter, lease copies, and notes on flood history or rental licensing. A buyer can't see a house's past from the street, so a short written summary of repairs, claims and city licenses helps. Call City Hall at 972-466-3000 if you can't tell which office handles a permit or license question, and ask the clerk of your county how it wants a deed presented. A cash buyer who sees those documents on day one can make a firm offer and let the title company search the right county's records.

Frequently asked questions

Which county is my Carrollton house in?

It could be Dallas, Denton or Collin, since the city lies in parts of all three. Your tax bill or the county appraisal district map shows which, and that decides where taxes are paid and the deed is recorded.

Can I start a new short-term rental in Carrollton?

No. Ordinances passed December 2, 2025 allow no new short-term rental or bed and breakfast. Only certain existing properties can qualify for a lodging license, so call the city before assuming a rental use can continue.

Does a Carrollton lodging license pass to a buyer?

No. Licenses belong to a specific owner and location, and a change in ownership means a new license and hotel occupancy tax number must be sought.

How much homestead exemption do Carrollton schools give?

The school exemption is $140,000, and seniors or disabled owners get $60,000 more. Ask your county about local exemptions that may add to it.

Can Carrollton heirs sell without probate?

Sometimes. A small estate affidavit works for qualifying estates, and a muniment of title can follow a court order. Without one of those routes, title may be hard to clear, so speak with the county clerk or a probate attorney.

Selling in Abilene?

Ways to sell a house fast in Abilene

Three paths are open to an Abilene seller: hire an agent, go it alone, or take an as-is cash offer. Repairs and the remaining mortgage balance usually decide which.

  • Agent: the widest audience, paid for with showings, repair requests and a lender's schedule.
  • On your own: no commission, but the advertising and contracts are yours.
  • Cash: frequently as-is, with a closing date both sides choose.

Judge offers by what you net. Have each buyer put closing costs in writing, because a lower price with fewer charges can beat a higher one that arrives with repair credits.

Abilene prices and ownership costs

Abilene's mid-2025 population of 131,588 is about 5.3% higher than in 2020. A little over half of occupied homes (56.1%) are owned. The 2020-2024 home value benchmark is $183,700 and rent is $1,157. Owners spend a median $1,683 a month with a mortgage and $599 without, across 46,917 households of 2.47 people and a median income of $62,648.

Residents 65-plus are 13.9% of the population, and they can qualify for the school tax freeze on a homestead. A house that needs work you cannot pay for can be sold as-is, with the condition reflected in the price.

Permits in Abilene

Permits come from Building Inspections inside Planning and Development Services at 555 Walnut Street. A permit is required to alter, repair or tear down a structure, and to put in or swap out electrical, gas, mechanical or plumbing systems. Going without one is a code violation, and it can snag a sale.

Abilene permit answers from the city's inspections FAQ
ProjectPermit needed?
Re-roofing more than 5 squaresYes
Fence over 7 feet tallYes, and a variance from the Board of Adjustment
Fence 7 feet or lower that meets setbacksNo
Open deck 30 inches or lower with no roofNo
Deck over 30 inches or roofedYes
Small detached unit, up to 200 sq ft, no utilitiesNo
Detached unit over 200 sq ft, or any size with utilitiesYes

A permit expires when work stops for more than 180 days or never starts within 180 days. The city keeps house plans on file for a year after final approval. Use the city's MyGov portal to request permits and inspections, or call Building Inspections at 325-676-6273. Plumbing contractors must be registered locally. Anyone digging should call 811 beforehand, a free line-locating service.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Abilene house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Past work done without a permit

The city may post a stop work order and charge an investigation fee equal to the permit fee, plus a release fee for an owner. Work that was covered up before inspection may have to be opened at the owner's expense. A contractor's second violation within 12 months costs ten times the fee.

  • A homeowner may take out permits and do the work on a homestead, with proof of the exemption from the Taylor County appraisal district at 1534 S Treadaway Boulevard.
  • An owner doing electrical work must also pass the city's homeowner electrical test.
  • Renovation or demolition calls for an asbestos survey by an accredited surveyor, filed with the city's verification form.

Before listing, ask Building Inspections whether earlier remodel permits were finaled. An open permit is worth closing out before a buyer's inspector finds it.

Tax and recording steps in an Abilene sale

Property tax creates a lien every January 1, and it stays with the house. Whoever owned on that date is still personally on the hook, and a buyer cannot get clean title while delinquent tax is open. Closing staff get a payoff figure and take it from your sale funds.

Recording happens at the clerk's office in the county where the land lies. The manual sets $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for each page after, with extras of up to $10 each for records management and archive and $2.00 for technology. A deed also needs the owner's signature and a notary's or other officer's acknowledgment before it can be recorded. For your exemption status, ask the Taylor County appraisal district.

Selling in foreclosure, probate or with a tenant

Each of these can still be sold, but the clocks differ. Foreclosure sales are held on a first Tuesday after 21 days or more of notice. Probate of a will is usually filed within four years after the death. The small estate affidavit fits estates worth $75,000 or less, with the homestead set aside.

A landlord with a tenant in the house starts with a written notice to vacate and then, if needed, files in justice court. Before you list, ask a Texas attorney or the county clerk which route fits.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Abilene houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

From first call to closing

A quick sale still follows an order, and skipping a step usually costs more time than it saves. One: find out whose names are on the deed and whether an heir or lender must also sign. Two: learn what tax is owed. Three: ask Building Inspections about permit history so nothing open surprises the buyer. Four: write down the closing date and the cost split. Five: the title company drafts the deed, pays the old tax out of your proceeds and files with the county clerk.

Foreclosure, probate and tenants each add a step in front of this list, which is why a seller in one of those situations should start earlier. Keep copies of every notice, payoff statement and permit record in one folder, so each person who asks for a document gets it the same day. If a buyer's lender or inspector raises a question about work on the house, the permit record is the first thing they will want, and the Taylor County appraisal district can confirm the homestead exemption that the city requires before an owner pulls permits.

How a cash sale changes the steps

A cash buyer has no lender's appraisal or underwriting to wait for, and those are common sources of delay and repair demands. The title work does not go away. A payoff for any tax owed is still ordered, the deed is still checked for signature and acknowledgment, and the county clerk still records it.

Put a cash offer next to a listing and compare the money you would actually walk away with. Get the costs in writing, ask who pays for the title policy, and choose a closing date you can meet. Open permits, unfinished work or a foreclosure date should be disclosed early so the price reflects them.

What to gather before you sell

Prepared sellers close sooner. Gather your latest tax statement and have the Taylor County appraisal district confirm your exemption status. Get permit records from Building Inspections, particularly for roofs, decks and anything with utilities. When the deed owner has died, work out whether probate or a small estate affidavit applies. With a tenant living there, give the notice to vacate early, because it precedes any court filing.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Frequently asked questions

How quickly can an Abilene house sell?

That depends on who buys. With cash there is no lender approval to wait for. A listing needs showings, inspections and a loan to line up.

What is a typical Abilene home worth?

The 2020-2024 benchmark is $183,700. Individual houses vary widely, so a written offer or appraisal tells you more.

Is a permit needed to re-roof in Abilene?

Yes, when the job exceeds 5 squares, one square being 100 square feet of roofing. Most plumbing, electrical, gas and mechanical work also needs a permit.

What becomes of unpaid property tax in an Abilene sale?

It gets paid at closing. The title company wants the balance cleared before the deed is recorded, because the lien dates to January 1.

Where is the Taylor County appraisal district?

At 1534 S Treadaway Boulevard, phone 325-676-9381. It can verify the homestead exemption the city requires for owner-pulled permits.

Selling in Pearland?

How quickly can a Pearland house close?

If the title is clean and the paperwork is ready, a couple of weeks can be enough for a cash closing. Putting the house on the market takes more time, since showings, inspections and a buyer's mortgage all need to run their course.

There is one wrinkle here. Pearland reaches into three counties, and the county holding your lot determines both the recording office and the tax bill, so pin that down before anything else.

Which county records my deed?

Most likely Brazoria County, though not always. Pearland lies primarily in Brazoria County, with portions reaching into Fort Bend and Harris counties, roughly 20 miles south of downtown Houston. Population is about 132,900 across 47.5 square miles.

Your tax bill or the appraisal district record names the county. From that you learn which clerk receives the deed and which office sends the tax statement.

  • Brazoria County: the tax office publishes payment options for homeowners.
  • Fort Bend County: ask that county for the bill and exemption records.
  • Harris County: the tax office posts a detailed FAQ on penalties and closings.

Flood and drainage history

Clear Creek runs through the Pearland area and drains parts of Brazoria, Fort Bend, Galveston and Harris counties. Shoppers across the Houston region ask how close a house sits to the creek and whether water has ever come inside, and the coastal storm history makes those questions louder. The 1900 hurricane destroyed nearly all of the early town, and a second hurricane in 1915 did similar damage.

Know the facts before you list or accept an investor's offer. Collect insurance claims, repair invoices and any elevation certificate, and find out which FEMA flood map applies to your lot. The current map was issued December 30, 2020 for Brazoria County, January 6, 2017 for Fort Bend County and January 29, 2021 for Harris County, so which date applies depends on your parcel.

  • State any past water entry in the contract.
  • Check with the title company on drainage easements across the lot.
  • Keep records of repairs after any storm.
Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Pearland house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Brazoria County payment options

Brazoria County parcels can spread the bill out in several ways, all arranged through the county tax office.

Brazoria County tax payment options
OptionWho qualifiesDates
Two-part splitAny parcelNovember 30 for the first half, June 30 for the second
Quarterly planHomesteads of owners over 65, disabled owners or disabled-veteran ownersJanuary 31, March 31, May 31, July 31
Disaster planProperty hurt inside a declared disaster areaJanuary 31, March 31, May 31, July 31
DeferralOwners 65 or older, or disabledFile an affidavit; 5 percent interest per year
Partial paymentOwners who cannot pay all at onceAny amount is taken

Deferral only postpones the tax. Interest keeps running until the owner stops owning and living in the home, so a sale ends it and the balance is paid from your proceeds.

Settling taxes at closing

This year's share of the tax is prorated by the title company, which also pays off anything delinquent. Under the state calendar, a penalty of 6 percent plus 1 percent interest starts February 1.

  • Order a tax certificate from each county that touches your lot.
  • Tell the servicer your closing date if the lender escrows taxes.
  • Look at your homestead status. The state school exemption is $140,000, and a buyer late in the year may claim it if you never did.

Foreclosure and selling before the auction

Selling ahead of the auction is allowed, and the lender gets repaid from what the sale brings in. A home loan generally has to be more than 120 days behind before foreclosure can start.

  • The borrower gets 20 days to cure after a default notice.
  • The sale notice goes out at least 21 days ahead, posted at the courthouse and filed with the county clerk.
  • Auction day is a first Tuesday, so counting back from it shows how much time you have to find a buyer.
  • Any deficiency suit has to be filed within two years of the sale.

Get the payoff and the sale date from the servicer, then give both to the title company.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Pearland houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

City permits and annexation

Pearland runs as a home rule city, led by a council and a city manager. The council gathers the second and fourth Monday of each month at 6:30 p.m., and the city can extend its limits by voluntary annexation when a landowner and the council agree.

A lot near the city edge may have changed taxing units after an annexation, and the bill on your account lists the current ones. Planning and zoning, community development, water and sewer all sit with the city, so ask staff about any open permit before a title search turns it up. Any fee or inspection rule should be confirmed in writing before closing.

Buyers who like an older neighborhood may ask about the Old Townsite, the original 1894 plat. William Zychlinski bought 2,560 acres around the rail line in 1892, and the city later incorporated in 1959 and adopted its Home Rule Charter in February 1971.

Cash offer or listing?

Listing may fetch more from a buyer using a loan, yet you carry commissions, open houses and weeks of waiting for an appraisal. Cash trades part of that price for a closing date of your choosing and no repair requests. Flood history, deferred upkeep or back taxes make a house a natural fit for cash.

Get one written cash offer and one realistic listing estimate on the same property. Take repairs, commissions and carrying costs off the listing figure, and see which path leaves more in your hands.

Questions to ask every buyer

Find out which side pays for the title policy, how long closing will take and whether the price can change after the walkthrough. Request proof of funds and the earnest money figure, along with the conditions for getting the deposit back.

Skip anyone who wants an upfront fee simply to make an offer or refuses to write terms down. Mention a multi-county lot, a tenant or an unsettled estate in the first conversation, because surprises discovered late usually shrink the offer.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

What to bring and what to expect

Gather the deed, the latest tax statement for each county involved, the payoff contact at your lender and any insurance claim records. A cash buyer purchases the house as it stands, so no repair list is needed, but do mention any past water entry. If you are unsure about a document, the title company can tell you whether it is needed before the signing date, which saves a second trip.

After acceptance, the title company looks for liens, orders tax certificates and books the signing. Payoffs and taxes owed come off the price, and you collect the rest when the deed is recorded. Ask each buyer to commit price, closing date and cost split to paper, then compare the net each one leaves you.

Frequently asked questions

Is Pearland in Harris County?

Partly, though most of the city is in Brazoria County. Some areas fall in Fort Bend and Harris. The tax bill for your lot will say.

Do I need to repair storm damage first?

Not for a cash buyer, who takes the property as it is and prices in the work. Hold on to receipts and insurance claim records to describe its history truthfully.

Can I pay Pearland-area taxes in installments before selling?

For Brazoria County parcels, yes, using the plans in the table. If you sell, whatever remains is paid from proceeds, so request a payoff figure.

Who records the deed for a Pearland sale?

Whichever county clerk serves the lot. The title company usually files for you, and the fee is itemized at settlement.

When does the tax penalty begin?

February 1 brings a 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest. Check local dates with the tax office.

Your options for a quick sale

Cash money can arrive inside a month. A listing drags longer, though it may fetch more. Both work in College Station; pick by looking at what the house needs, who lives in it and how soon you need to be done.

Brazos County is home to this city, and Texas A&M University sits beside it. The school drives much of the buying and renting.

Does a College Station rental have to be registered?

Mostly yes. Any single-family house, townhome, duplex, tri-plex, four-plex, five-plex or six-plex that the owner does not live in must be registered with the city, rent charged or not. Condos and buildings of more than six units fall outside the rule.

Brazos County tax calendar

Values are set as of January 1 by the Brazos appraisal district. Appraisal notices arrive in several batches between April 15 and June 1. You can protest until May 15, or until the 30th day after your notice if that is later. Rates get set between July and September, and bills from the tax assessor-collector land in October and November.

Pay by January 31. From February 1 an unpaid account is delinquent, with a six percent penalty and one percent interest starting to build. The appraisal district office is at 4051 Pendleton Drive in Bryan, open weekdays, and exemption forms can go in by email to the address on its contact page.

Who owes the tax after a sale

A tax lien takes hold of the house every January 1, and the January owner stays on the hook for that year's bill after a sale. A buyer closing after January 1 can claim a homestead exemption at once if you never had one. Get a tax certificate before signing so the title company can split the year properly.

If a bill goes delinquent, the owner may ask the collector in writing to waive penalty and interest. Payment must come within 21 days of learning about the delinquency, and the written request within 181 days of the delinquency date.

A will can be probated for up to four years after the owner dies. An estate that needs no administration may use a muniment of title instead. Lenders sell foreclosed houses on a first Tuesday following a notice of sale, and a default notice leaves 20 days to reinstate. A sale closed ahead of that Tuesday lets you keep control of the price.

The county clerk records the deed, which must be acknowledged before a notary or two witnesses. Recording fees change, so ask the clerk for the current schedule.

A cash deal moves quickly. You send the buyer the address and deed details. One walkthrough later, an offer arrives in writing, priced for the house's condition. Say yes and the title company starts a file, searches for liens and asks each lender for a payoff figure. Closing happens on the day you pick, either in the office or by mail, and the wire reaches you once mortgages and any back taxes have been settled.

The deal skips the steps that stretch a listing: open houses, financing contingencies, appraisals that come in short and repair requests from inspectors. The tradeoff is price, because the buyer prices in repairs and risk. Request every offer in writing, then set it beside what a listing would leave you after commission, fixes and the months of carrying costs.

Selling near campus

Demand tracks the Texas A&M calendar. Houses close to campus attract investors and parents buying for a student, and houses farther out attract families and university staff. Tenants in place? Hand the buyer the lease, the rent ledger and the registration record early, and state when the lease ends.

A house left empty between school years prompts condition questions. Fresh photos, a cleanout and a list of work already done help, and the utilities should be on for the buyer's walkthrough.

Pricing against the local market

The median owned home is valued at $346,700, while renters pay a median of $1,194 a month. Mortgaged owners carry a median housing cost of $2,270. Those three numbers frame what a College Station buyer is weighing: buy and live in it, buy and rent it, or walk away.

If your house could rent well, an investor may pay for that income. If it suits a family, a listing may do better. Gather a few written offers and rank them by the net amount that would land in your account.

Documents to collect first

Start with the deed and the latest Brazos tax statement. Add the rental registration record if tenants have lived there, a mortgage payoff figure and a short list of known repairs. Buyers and title agents request all of it, and having it ready trims days off the path from accepted offer to closing.

Buyers here care about parks, the university and a short drive. Workers average 17.4 minutes getting to work, so put that near the top of your house description.

Do tenants have to register a College Station rental?

No. The duty falls on the owner. An owner who lives elsewhere must name a local contact who is not on the lease and lives within 30 miles of City Hall.

What does College Station charge to register a rental?

$90 per building, one time, as of October 24, 2022. Late registration adds daily penalties, so act before the first notice deadline runs out.

Where do I ask about a Brazos County exemption?

Contact the Brazos appraisal district by phone or email using its contact page. General exemption applications are due before May 1, and some special applications are due April 30.

When is the Brazos County protest deadline?

May 15, or the 30th day after notice if that is later. The notice itself prints your exact date.

Can I sell with a lien for back taxes?

Yes. The title company orders payoff figures and pays the balance from your sale funds.

Deed filing fees at the county clerk

Deeds are recorded by the Ector County clerk at charges set by state law: $5.00 for page one, $4.00 for every later page, and then records management, archive and technology fees added separately.

The signature must be witnessed by a notary or another authorized officer before filing. Ask the title company for the final total ahead of closing day.

Selling without a standard sale

Getting an Odessa house ready

Comparing offers fairly

Two offers with the same headline price can leave you with very different checks. Write each one down with the price, the repair credits, the closing cost split, the earnest money and the closing date. Then subtract what you still owe on the mortgage and any taxes due. The remainder is what you actually keep.

Ask whether the earnest money is refundable and under what conditions. A buyer who offers a large deposit and a short inspection window is usually serious, while a vague answer is a warning to slow down.

How the oil cycle affects timing

House demand tracks the oil patch, and swings have come at roughly ten-year intervals since the 1920s. When things are slow, cash with no loan condition takes one risk off the table. When things are hot, a listing may pull more bids.

Inherited, rented or behind on payments

Three situations can hold up a sale regardless of the house's condition. If the property was inherited, buyers need to see who can sign, so dig out the will or court papers early. A sitting tenant shifts the schedule: the buyer either inherits the lease or waits for the house to empty. A mortgage in arrears carries its own deadline, so phone the lender and the title company the same week.

In every one of these, disclose early. A problem found during the title search costs you leverage, and a buyer who hears late often cuts the offer or leaves.

The State Law Library publishes plain-language pages on foreclosure, probate and eviction, handy reading before you call anyone.

Step by step from offer to payout

Right after you say yes, the title company opens an order and searches the records for liens or unpaid tax. Whether the closing date holds depends on clearing those early.

Usually between one and a few weeks from the day you accept. No lender appraisal is involved, yet the title search and deed take real time, and inherited or older properties can run longer.

Not usually. Cash buyers price the repairs in. Share any known problems with each buyer so the contract matches what they find.

Who gets the tax bill when an Odessa house sells?

It is split by days of ownership, and the title company handles payment. Begin by asking the Ector County Appraisal District for your account statement.

Which office records my deed?

The Ector County clerk. The title company normally files it for you, and the fee appears on the settlement statement.

Does Odessa's oil economy change my timing?

It can. Boom and bust cycles repeat here, so a cash buyer with no loan condition looks especially good when the market is slow.

A permit does not pass to a buyer, so take active listings down by closing. Anyone buying to host guests needs a permit of their own, and an unresolved violation can slow the sale.

If a League City home is behind on its mortgage

Texas lenders usually foreclose under a power of sale rather than in court. A borrower who has fallen behind can cure the default with a payment within 20 days of the notice. The lender then sends a notice of sale at least 21 days ahead.

The auction takes place on a first Tuesday. A sale ahead of the auction can clear the loan and leave the equity with you. After an auction, any surplus goes first to junior lienholders and only then to the former owner.

Comparing offers

  • Get proof of funds and a written closing date from every buyer.
  • Confirm who pays title and escrow costs.
