  • Find out whether storm repairs stay with you or transfer to the buyer.

An offer with the highest price can lose to a slightly lower one that closes on a firm date with fewer conditions, so look at the whole sheet.

What to prepare before you call buyers

Pull your deed, the latest Galveston County tax statement and your mortgage payoff figure. If the neighborhood has an HOA, MUD or PID, request a statement of what remains owed on the property, because these charges stay with the house. If you ever rented the house short term, gather the permit and tax certificate records so you can show the account is in good standing.

Write down what you know about storm damage, past flooding and insurance claims, and keep the claim paperwork handy. Disclosing it up front keeps the price discussion honest and the contract from unraveling later.

Condition and disclosure

Buyers on the Clear Lake side of Galveston County expect straight answers about roofs, drainage, windows and any past water in the house. Make a short written list of every repair you know about, with dates and receipts where you have them. If an insurance claim was filed after a storm, keep the paperwork and the contractor's invoices together.

You do not have to fix everything. A cash sale lets you hand the remaining work to the buyer, and the price adjusts to match. A listing may bring more money, but a buyer's inspector will find the same issues and ask for credits or repairs, so decide early which path you can live with.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Who to call

The Galveston County Tax Office handles your bill and can confirm which installment plans apply. The Building Department, at 281-554-1429, covers short-term rental permits. Your lender or servicer provides the payoff, and your title company can request any MUD, PID or HOA statement. Making those four calls in the first week gives you most of what a buyer will ask for.

Steps to close

  1. Pick a buyer and sign the contract.
  2. Order the payoff letter and a tax certificate through the title company.
  3. Request any MUD, PID and HOA statements.
  4. Sign the deed in front of a notary.
  5. Review the closing figures and confirm the year's tax split.

Cash usually closes faster than a mortgage, yet the real clock is clear title and the payoff letter.

Frequently asked questions

How fast can I close on a League City house?

It depends on the buyer and on how quickly title work finishes. Paying cash usually shortens the wait compared with a mortgage buyer, though the date really hinges on clean title and a payoff letter.

Does a League City short-term rental need its own permit?

Yes. Along with a hotel occupancy tax certificate, a short-term rental permit is required, and its number has to appear in every listing.

Who collects League City property taxes?

The city, Clear Creek ISD and Galveston County each set rates, and the Galveston County Tax Office handles the bills. Confirm your balance with that office before closing.

Can I sell a League City house with a MUD or PID charge?

Yes. These charges stay with the property, so buyers will want a statement of what remains. Your title company can request it.

What if my League City house has storm damage?

You can still sell as-is. Investors price the damage in, and you should tell buyers what you know and keep your insurance claim paperwork.

Is a quick sale realistic in Conroe?

Yes. In Conroe the choice is usually a cash contract that funds within weeks or a conventional listing that trades speed for a stronger price.

The city holds the Montgomery County courthouse, with Interstate 45 running alongside. Reasons to sell range widely, from an inherited house to a tenant-occupied rental to a mortgage in trouble.

Conroe growth and housing figures

Conroe is growing quickly. By July 1, 2025 it had an estimated 119,564 residents, up 33.0% from 89,899 in April 2020. The city itself spread from 52.71 square miles in 2010 to 72.00 in 2020, and 82.8% of its people lived at one address all year.

Where your house sits matters

This is a big city. Shoppers drawn to the courthouse square, the interstate corridor or Lake Conroe, about seven miles northwest, are rarely the same people. The school district stretches across 330 square miles, so which campus serves a house follows its street address, not a Conroe mailing label. Ask the district about zoning with your exact address in hand.

Montgomery County tax bills and due dates

Statements go out in October and can be paid on receipt. Interest and penalty begin February 1, and a mailed payment is judged by its postmark.

Penalty opens at 6 percent, gains a point every month, and takes a last 2 points on July 1 to finish at 12 percent. Interest of 1 percent a month piles on besides. The office takes partial payments, yet whatever remains after January 31 keeps growing. Phone (936) 539-7897 or visit 400 N. San Jacinto Street.

Disputes over value, exemptions and protests belong to Montgomery Central Appraisal District. Its protest deadline is May 15, or 30 days after your notice arrives if that comes later.

Who pays the bill when a house sells?

The settlement statement tells the story. The tax office suggests that new owners read their closing papers or phone the title company, which may have taken your portion and credited the buyer.

A lien on the property appears every January 1, and whoever owned it then stays liable. Where a lender escrows your taxes, the county recommends writing the loan number on a statement you receive and forwarding it to the lender.

Homestead exemptions

Make sure your homestead status is recorded, since it shapes what the next owner pays. The school exemption is $140,000, and owners 65 and up or disabled get $60,000 more along with a school tax ceiling. Eligibility is the appraisal district's call, not the tax office's.

If the Conroe mortgage is behind

Lenders usually wait until a loan is over 120 days late before sending a default notice with a 20 day cure period. After an auction the lender may still pursue any shortfall for two years.

A tenant or an heir in the house

A tenant generally receives three days' written notice, unless the lease says otherwise, and a disputed case lands in justice court. An occupant who never rented falls under property code chapter 24B and is removed through the sheriff or constable. Heirs need probate, a muniment of title, a small estate affidavit or a recorded transfer on death deed before a buyer will close.

How a Conroe cash sale works

Few steps are involved. Tell the buyer the address and the condition. An offer follows in writing, often after one visit. Accept it and the title company searches records, asks lenders for payoffs and books closing on your date. With no bank underwriting, only title work sets the pace.

Price is the cost. Cash offers deduct repairs and risk, whereas a listing can bring more after a longer wait. When the house is an estate, a rental or a loan near auction, speed can outweigh the gap.

Older core, lake homes and new subdivisions

Streets around the courthouse square hold houses from many decades. The courthouse itself dates to 1936, and downtown survived fires in 1901 and 1911. Lakeside homes and brand-new subdivisions sit in other price bands, so a buyer will want to know where your house fits.

Population climbed from 27,610 in 1990 to 43,617 in 2000 and an estimated 119,564 today. With that much building, many houses are fairly new, though roofs and systems differ in age. Write down when each major system was last replaced and hold on to the receipts.

Selling a Conroe rental with a tenant

A rental with a lease running can still sell, and some investors like it because rent keeps arriving. Hand over the lease, the ledger and the deposit amount, and state when the term ends. An investor will measure your rent against the local median of $1,393.

If the tenant has fallen behind, send the written notice before listing so the timeline is clear. The buyer will price in any delay, and tidy payment records make the house easier to value.

Closing day in Conroe

On the day, you sign the deed and the settlement statement. The title company pays off your mortgage and any back taxes first, divides the current year's bill with the buyer, then wires what is left. Bring photo identification and every key and garage remote. Arrange the final utility readings in advance, and leave the house empty unless the contract says otherwise.

Afterward the deed is filed with the county clerk. Keep a copy of the settlement statement with your own tax records, because it shows what portion of the year's bill you covered.

What to bring to the table

Dig out the deed, your newest tax statement, each lender's payoff letter and any lease with its rent history. An inherited house adds probate papers to the pile. Ask every buyer who covers the title policy and how long the offer stays open. A brief list of known repairs heads off arguments.

Frequently asked questions

Which county covers Conroe?

Montgomery County. Its tax office is at 400 N. San Jacinto Street in Conroe and answers bill and payment questions.

What date do Conroe taxes turn delinquent?

February 1. The January 31 postmark deadline comes first, and after it a 6 percent penalty plus 1 percent interest begins.

Can I sell a Conroe house with taxes unpaid?

Yes. The balance is paid from your proceeds at closing, so ask for a tax certificate early to learn the amount.

Does Montgomery County take part payments?

Yes. Mark the check with the account number and the words partial payment. A balance still open after January 31 will draw penalty.

How soon before an auction must a lender send notice?

The notice must go out 21 or more days ahead of the first Tuesday sale, and only after the 20 day cure period on the default notice ends.

Selling options for a Richardson owner

In Richardson the realistic choices are an agent listing, a do-it-yourself sale, and a direct as-is purchase. A listing rewards a house in strong condition. The as-is route suits someone who wants no repairs, no showings and no long wait.

Richardson lies partly in Dallas County and partly in Collin County, and the line affects tax bills and school boundaries alike. Before choosing, find out three things: your county, your school district and your loan balance. Together they set your floor and your timeline.

  • Listing: wide exposure, then inspection requests and loan approval on someone else's schedule.
  • Private sale: you save the commission and do the contract and buyer screening yourself.

Where to pay the county tax bill

On the Dallas side, the appraisal district serves 61 local governing bodies. Collin CAD handles the other side and posts rates on a taxing-entities page. To contest a value, ask the appraiser for an informal review before the hearing date.

Home Improvement Incentive Program

Richardson will pay a homeowner who spends heavily on remodeling a single-family house. The payment equals ten times the increase in city taxes that results from the higher appraised value.

  • The project must cost at least $20,000 and finish within 24 months of approval.
  • Apply to Community Services before construction starts, and agree to inspections.
  • The appraisal district's certified value decides the tax increase.
  • Owners delinquent on taxes or fees are not eligible.

Payment comes on April 1 of the first full calendar year after the work is done, under an economic development agreement. Reach Community Services at the Temporary City Hall Annex on Campbell Creek Blvd, 972-744-4166. The payment may count as taxable income. A remodel will not pay you back before a sale, but an owner who stays can benefit.

School districts in Richardson

Richardson ISD covers 46 square miles in Dallas County, with more than 36,000 students on 50 campuses. Plano ISD serves the northern parts of Richardson on the Collin County side. Families often search by school zone, so put the district in your listing.

Commuting and amenities buyers ask about

Rail access is a selling point here. The city's pages describe DART rail and bus service, the Trinity Railway Express and NTTA tollways, and it lists hike and bike trails plus a transportation and mobility department. A commuter will want to know how far the house sits from a station, so measure the walk before you list.

Public amenities also give you something specific to name in an ad: the Eisemann Center, Sherrill Park Golf Course, a senior center, a tennis center, a gymnastics center and the recreation centers. The city sends a Richardson Today newsletter and runs a MyRichardson app for reporting issues, so buyers who follow city news will see a city that communicates often.

If a tenant still lives in the house, tell buyers about the lease up front and expect questions about showing times.

The city site lists code enforcement, residential building inspection with online permits, floodplain information, a 24/7 response center, trash and brush pickup, and permits for garage sales and alarms. A buyer's inspector may raise any of them.

Property taxes and exemptions at a Richardson closing

Since the lien took hold on January 1, the title company at closing divides that year's bill between you and the buyer. Bills go out around October 1, and January 31 is the usual cutoff.

From February 1, penalty and interest build, and by July the penalty reaches 12 percent. Homeowners who are over 65 or disabled can use installment plans. School districts must grant a $140,000 homestead exemption, and a homestead's appraised value may rise no more than 10 percent a year.

A buyer may have to apply for their own exemption, so find out from the appraisal district what is on your account.

Preparing a Richardson house for showings

Tour your own house the way a city inspector would. Look for unpermitted additions, floodplain questions and yard issues that code enforcement could flag. A short list of repairs finished before photos beats a long list of credits negotiated later.

Keep permit records, the water account number and your school district's name on hand for quick answers. Buyers in a two-county city often ask which county bills the taxes, so know the answer for your parcel.

Foreclosure and inherited houses

When a Texas loan goes into default, the lender may auction the house with no lawsuit. A borrower gets 20 days after the default letter to catch up, and the lender must mail the sale notice at least three weeks ahead of the auction, held on a first Tuesday.

An inherited house follows a route set by the estate. A will may go to probate any time in the four years after death. A modest estate, $75,000 or less excluding the homestead, can use a small estate affidavit with a judge's approval. A bare affidavit of heirship is merely a sworn statement, and buyers may refuse it. If the owner signed a beneficiary deed, the heir records proof of death before selling.

The clerk of whichever county covers the parcel handles recording. The state clerk manual sets the per-page charge and other records fees.

What a Richardson closing looks like

After you accept an offer, the title company starts a title search and requests a balance from the county tax office. It also requests a payoff from your lender. If your address is in Dallas County, call 214-653-7811. For Collin County, call 972-881-3014.

Closing is mostly signing. You sign the deed, the title company settles your loan and any tax due, and you keep the balance. A cash buyer needs no lender appraisal, so timing hinges mainly on clearing title. Before you hand over keys, close your water account through the city and take a last reading.

If you plan a remodel before selling, remember that the incentive program pays only after the work is finished and a full calendar year has begun, so it will not help a quick sale.

At least $20,000, completed within 24 months of approval, with an application filed before construction starts.

Which school districts serve Richardson?

Richardson ISD and Plano ISD. Richardson ISD spans 46 square miles in Dallas County, and Plano ISD covers northern parts of the city.

When do Texas property taxes become delinquent?

Unpaid bills turn delinquent on February 1, after the January 31 cutoff, and penalty and interest begin.

Closing quickly in Tyler

Speed in Tyler comes down to three items: a buyer with no lender to wait on, clean title, and a payoff number that holds. Cash offers usually deliver all three more reliably than retail listings.

Start a folder with the mortgage payoff, your newest Smith County tax statement and any letter about a lien, code complaint or missed payment. Together they show what closing must clear and whether a deadline is already ticking.

  • Retail listing: wide exposure, plus showings, repair requests and a lender's calendar.

Tyler's housing stock

Tyler is the Smith County seat, ninety-nine miles southeast of Dallas. Its townsite dates to 1846. Streets around the central square are old while subdivisions farther out are new, so houses range widely in age, and an inspector concentrates on whatever systems show a particular house's years.

Oil, roses, health care and education each shaped the city. Rose growing led to the Texas Rose Festival, held each October. Hospitals and four colleges, among them Tyler Junior College and the University of Texas at Tyler, tie housing demand to local jobs and campuses. A nurse relocating for a hospital post, a professor starting at a college, or a family moving from a smaller East Texas town all look at Tyler houses, and each weighs commute and school zone differently. Tyler housing numbers

Paying Smith County property tax

Two separate offices matter. The appraisal district sets values and processes exemptions. The county tax office mails bills and accepts payment, but it plays no part in valuations, and the district is not county government. Take value questions to the district at 903-510-8600.

Payment options: walk in, pay online, mail a check to P.O. Box 2011, Tyler, Texas 75710, or use the drop box. The tax office phone is 903-590-2920. A card adds a 2.30 percent fee with a $1.50 minimum, and electronic checks are free. Noonday and Lindale substations accept payments as well. Current-year tax still open after January picks up penalty and interest on this schedule:

  • 7 percent in February, 9 in March, 11 in April, 13 in May and 15 in June.
  • 18 percent in July with a 15 percent collection fee added, then 19 in August and 20 in September.
  • Interest adds one percent each month, and whatever remains on June 30 passes to the delinquent tax attorney.

Proposed tax rates and the yearly calendar

Smith County runs a Truth in Taxes site for property owners. It shows property values, proposed tax rates, an estimate of the taxes those rates would produce, and the dates and places of public hearings on rates. Budget, revenue and rate calculations for taxing units are posted there too.

A Tyler address can be taxed by several units. County and school district levies hit every property, and some owners also pay a city plus a hospital, junior college, water or fire district. Elected boards for each unit set rates in August or September.

From January 1 to April 30 the appraisal district works through exemption applications and agricultural appraisals, and the review board begins hearing protests around May 15. Sellers should remember that late-summer rates decide the October bill. Your title company can explain how the year gets prorated between you and the buyer.

How to protest your appraisal

Your written protest must reach the district within 30 days of the date printed on the notice of appraised value. With no notice generated, May 20 is the fallback date. A letter naming you, identifying the property and showing you disagree is sufficient, and the online system works with the ID on your notice.

The district's taxpayer liaison officer can explain the process at 903-510-8600. A review board of citizens hears the protest, and you and the district exchange evidence at or before the hearing. Bring photographs, repair estimates and recent sales of similar houses, since the board weighs evidence rather than opinion.

Losing at the board leaves appeal routes: state district court, binding arbitration or the State Office of Administrative Hearings. A deadline on a weekend or holiday moves to the next working day. Only good cause, such as a medical emergency, excuses a late filing.

Homestead exemptions and caps

Taxable value on a qualifying homestead cannot rise beyond 110 percent of the prior year's value. In the first year an owner qualifies there is no cap, so a buyer begins uncapped. Owners 65 or older get a school tax ceiling fixed at what they paid in the year they first qualified. The ceiling can rise when they add improvements such as a room, a pool or a garage, and it changes if they move.

School districts also apply a $140,000 homestead exemption under state law. Pick up an application at the district office, 245 SSE Loop 323 in Tyler, weekdays from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m., or call 903-510-8600.

What happens between offer and closing

Once you say yes, a title company in Tyler opens a file and searches the property history for liens, judgments, unpaid taxes and gaps in ownership. A problem found now can be cured or priced in. A problem found the week of closing usually cannot.

Your buyer may tour the house. A cash buyer rarely asks you to fix what shows up on that visit. Next come a signing appointment with a notary and the payoff of your loan and any tax balance from the proceeds, with the rest going to you. Keys change hands at funding, so empty the house and schedule your utility shutoff a few days ahead.

Selling with taxes owed or an open estate

A tax balance does not stop a sale. At closing the title company settles it from your proceeds, working from a payoff the tax office confirms through your closing date. An estate still in probate adds a step, because the signer needs authority: a personal representative after appointment, or a route through a muniment of title or recorded transfer on death deed.

On your first title company call, have the death certificate, any will and the latest tax statement in hand, and ask what else is required. Settling that early protects your closing date once a buyer signs. After closing the deed is recorded with the Smith County Clerk, and your title company normally files it for you. Keep the recorded copy with your papers.

Frequently asked questions

Which office handles a Tyler valuation complaint?

Phone the appraisal district at 903-510-8600. The county tax office has no role in valuations.

Where can I pay Tyler property tax?

Walk in at the county tax office, pay online or by mail, use the drop box, or stop at the Noonday or Lindale substation. Cards bring a convenience fee and electronic checks do not.

What happens if Tyler taxes go unpaid after January 31?

Penalty and interest begin at 7 percent in February and climb each month. Past June 30 the delinquent tax attorney takes over and a collection fee applies.

What is the deadline to protest a Tyler value?

Within 30 days of the date on your notice of appraised value, or May 20 if no notice went out. The notice itself prints your deadline.

Can I sell my Tyler house while a parent's estate is still open?

Only once someone holds authority to sign, such as an appointed personal representative or an heir using a muniment of title or recorded transfer on death deed. Ask a title company which papers it wants.

Three ways to sell in Allen

Owners in Allen can hire a broker, locate a buyer without one, or accept cash from an investor. Let the condition of the house and your own deadline decide. Allen is in the southwest corner of Collin County next to U.S. 75, with an estimated 113,447 residents in mid-2025.

Roughly seven in ten occupied homes here belong to the people living in them, which means a clean, updated house attracts many move-in buyers. A house that needs work, carries a lease, or sits in probate is easier to place with someone who takes it as it is and follows your calendar.

  • Brokered listing: the most buyers see it, but expect showings, loan approvals and inspection haggling.
  • Private sale: you set the number, show the house and handle the contract on your own.
  • Cash purchase: one buyer, no repair work for you, and a closing date you choose.

Allen housing numbers

Allen is an affluent suburb with a strong owner base. Its count rose from 84,246 in 2010 to 104,627 in 2020, roughly 20,000 new residents.

Rental registration in Allen

Landlords selling an Allen property should read this first. The council voted on October 13 to make single-family rentals (houses, townhomes and duplexes) register with the city and submit to inspection.

  • Yearly fee: $150, plus $50 if you register late.
  • A follow-up inspection for continuing problems costs $25.
  • Mailings to owners were scheduled to begin in November 2026, and registration is first due January 31, 2027.
  • Rentals of this type are about 14% of the city's housing yet caused 38% of property violations, hence the exterior inspections.

City staff are matching ownership data against utility accounts to find rentals. If a notice arrives for a home that was never leased, the notice tells you how to contact the city. If guests ever paid to stay overnight, ask permitting staff whether a permit was issued.

Remodel and repair permits run through the Building and Permitting Division. Request the permit history for your address, because a file a former owner left open can stall a closing.

Property tax in Collin County

Two Collin County bodies split the work. The appraisal district (Collin CAD) decides what your house is worth, and the county tax assessor-collector bills and collects. Bills arrive in October, and January 31 is the last day to pay without penalty. Tax certificates and similar special requests are handled only at the Property Tax Office, 2300 Bloomdale Road, Suite 2324, McKinney.

Exemption forms go to the appraisal district, not the tax office. The district accepts the standard homestead form from January 1 to April 30 only, and it charges nothing and will not take it by email. A late filing can still be made within two years of the bill going delinquent.

The district's 2023 table showed these entries for Allen city. The district posts a new table every year, so look up current figures first.

  • Homestead: 5.00% of value, but never under $5,000.
  • Owners 65 or older: $50,000.
  • Disabled owners: $25,000.

Sellers who are 65 or older and have a school tax ceiling can transfer it to a replacement Texas home as a percentage. Your buyer must file a new homestead application in their own name.

Filing the deed

The Collin County Clerk records every Allen deed. Bring the original, or a certified copy from the clerk, with signatures notarized. Some entries online are redacted under House Bill 4350, and that site is not the official repository, so rely on the clerk's office for the actual record.

Before recording, Texas needs the signer's acknowledgment in front of a notary or similar officer, or a witness. Charges vary by document and shift over the years, so ask the clerk what the current schedule is.

Normally the title company runs the process: it orders the tax certificate, pays the mortgage off and sends the deed in. Because each tax year's lien attaches on January 1, any earlier year still owing must be paid before the transfer is clean.

Inherited, behind on payments or rented?

Each of these has its own deadline under Texas law.

  • Inherited house: the window to probate a will runs four years from the death. If the estate needs no administration, heirs can convey with a muniment of title, supported by the court order and the will recorded in the county that holds the land.
  • Mortgage trouble: after a default letter you have 20 days to catch up, then the lender must post a sale notice at least 21 days before the auction.
  • Tenants in place: a lease may set its own terms, but the default is a written three-day notice to vacate, then a case in justice court.

Closing first, before the auction date or the eviction hearing, leaves the decisions with you instead of the lender or the court.

An investor paying cash needs no appraisal and no loan approval, so those waiting periods drop away. Staging, weekend open houses and post-inspection repair demands drop away too. Only the title work is left: the tax certificate, any mortgage payoff, and the deed.

If the house was a rental, say up front whether the tenants will remain and whether registration is current. Buyers factor that into the price, and a problem found at the last minute costs more than one disclosed early.

From signed contract to closing day

When a contract is signed, a title company starts the file. Its staff request the tax certificate in McKinney, ask each lender for a payoff letter, and comb the records for liens and permits that were never closed. At the table you sign the deed before a notary. Once funds move, the deed is sent to the county clerk, and the appraisal district later changes the owner of record to match.

Delays typically come from an overlooked tax balance or an old open permit. Ask for both the same week you accept an offer so the closing date holds.

Checklist before you sign

Collect these in writing.

  • A tax certificate showing nothing owed for earlier years.
  • Proof from Collin CAD that your homestead and any ceiling are on record.
  • If it was a rental, the city's registration record for the address.
  • A title search covering open permits and liens not yet released.
  • The closing date and who pays which closing costs, stated in the contract.

Have the title company quote a payoff for each lien, and keep a copy of every certificate. Paperwork on hand when the buyer's side asks means a faster close.

Does Allen require rental houses to be registered?

Single-family rentals must register, whether houses, townhomes or duplexes, and they are subject to inspection. The yearly fee is $150 with $50 added for late registration, and the first deadline is January 31, 2027.

Who collects property tax on an Allen home?

The county's tax assessor-collector, whose office is in McKinney. Values and exemptions come from Collin Central Appraisal District.

When can I apply for a homestead exemption on an Allen house?

January 1 through April 30, filed with Collin CAD, free of charge. Forms sent early or by email are turned away. A late filing is possible for two years after the account goes delinquent.

Can I sell an Allen house if property taxes are unpaid?

Yes. Whatever is owed gets paid from your proceeds at closing, because the lien dated January 1 stays with the house and blocks clear title until it is cleared.

How many people live in Allen?

An estimated 113,447 in mid-2025, compared with 104,627 at the 2020 count.

What sets a fast sale in Beaumont apart

On the Neches River, Beaumont is a port and refinery city whose housing market rises and falls with industry. Sellers commonly face older houses, mixed neighborhoods and a county tax system that works through its own appraisal district.

Beaumont's mid-2025 estimate is 112,967 residents, down 1.8% from the April 2020 base. With shoppers in no rush, the sellers who close soonest are those with a clear tax statement and a clean deed. Many houses go back to the oil booms of the early twentieth century and may predate modern code, which means questions about age and condition are routine.

Jefferson County's seat is Beaumont, roughly 85 miles east of Houston on Interstate 10 and one point of the Golden Triangle with Port Arthur and Orange. Your deed, tax account and any probate filing are handled at county level.

Beaumont housing numbers

Owner-occupied homes here are worth $166,400 at the middle of the range, and owners live in 55.3% of units. The median gross rent is $1,121.

Property tax: who bills you and when it is late

Three offices touch your bill. One appraisal district, Jefferson Central, assigns the value. Each taxing unit chooses its rate on its own. The Jefferson County Tax Assessor-Collector is who you pay, because the appraisal district never levies or collects anything.

Property is valued as of January 1, the same day that year's lien attaches. October brings the bill. You can pay through January 31 without extra cost, but after that the collector adds six percent penalty and one percent interest, starting February 1.

  • Ask the tax office for a payoff figure before signing anything.
  • Check the account for balances left over from earlier years.
  • Save your payment receipt so the title company can see it.

Homestead breaks for a seller or buyer

A buyer who moves in is entitled to a $140,000 school district exemption. If that buyer is 65 or disabled, the school tax exemption grows by $60,000. Cities and counties can adopt homestead exemptions of their own as well.

Tax freezes for older and disabled owners come from the school districts, Jefferson County and the City of Port Arthur. Nothing is charged to file, and if you missed the April 30 date you may still apply within two years after the bill went delinquent.

Apart from that, a homestead's taxable value can rise only 10% a year. For the 2024 through 2026 tax years, other real property worth $5,000,000 or less also has a 20% circuit breaker. New rooms and pools are outside both.

If a Beaumont appraisal looks too high

A written protest must be filed by May 15, or by the thirtieth day after the notice was mailed if that is later. Home notices typically arrive in mid-April, and an appraiser will offer an informal review ahead of any board hearing.

After an adverse ruling from the Appraisal Review Board, you may file suit in district court within 60 days of getting the written decision. The other choice is binding arbitration, available to every residential homestead whatever its value.

  • Recent sales of similar Beaumont houses, dated near January 1.
  • Photographs of any foundation, plumbing or roof trouble.
  • A survey if you think the district measured the lot or house wrong.

Foreclosure timing on a Beaumont home

Foreclosure in Texas seldom involves a judge. A power of sale in the loan documents lets the lender auction the house on the first Tuesday of a month, any time from 10 a.m. to 4 p.m., at a place the commissioners court picks.

  • The default notice opens a 20-day period in which you can catch up on the loan.
  • A notice of sale has to land at least 21 days ahead of the auction.
  • Afterward the lender may pursue any shortfall in court for two years.

A sale that closes before the auction lets you choose the buyer. Call the servicer for a payoff letter the moment you consider that route.

Selling an inherited Beaumont house

Start with a simple question: did the owner leave a will? If so, probate it inside four years of the death. A muniment of title can then pass the house when liens are the only debts. If there was no will, a small estate affidavit can handle an estate of $75,000 or less outside the homestead, but not other land.

Two shortcuts deserve a caution. An affidavit of heirship is sworn yet unverified by any court, so a title insurer may decline it. A transfer on death deed, by contrast, skips probate, provided it was recorded before the owner died.

Heirs who remain in the house can keep the homestead exemption in place. Bring the appraisal district the death certificate and an ownership affidavit.

Listing or cash: how to decide

Pick an agent if the house is in decent shape and you can endure showings and wait for a buyer's loan. Pick a cash buyer if the roof, plumbing or foundation is failing, a tenant is living there, taxes are behind, or a lender or court has given you a deadline. Expect a lower offer, but no repair bills and a closing date of your choosing.

Either way, begin with three documents: a tax payoff statement, a mortgage payoff letter and a copy of your deed. Together they show what you will net and reveal any problem before a buyer does.

From contract to closing

Once the contract is signed the title company takes charge. Its staff review the tax account, ask for each payoff and hunt for liens. Then you sign the deed in front of a notary and the county clerk records it when funds arrive. Skip the recording and your name stays on the tax roll, since the appraisal district follows recorded deeds.

Schedule your move-out and key handover for the funding date, and file copies of the settlement statement and recorded deed.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Short-term rental rules

A city permit is a must before offering nightly stays. Beaumont requires one for any rental of fewer than 30 consecutive days, issued through Planning and Community Development and renewed annually.

Online listings have to show the permit number, and a hotel occupancy tax certificate is part of the package. Fines are possible for advertising before you hold a permit, so a buyer with this plan should understand the steps before closing.

Filing the deed

The Jefferson County Clerk is the keeper of deed records for county land, and the clerk accepts a deed only with a signature and an acknowledgment.

In the 2023 clerk manual, page one costs $5.00 and each added page $4.00, with records fees running up to $10 each for management and archives. The tax roll changes owners only after the appraisal district sees a recorded deed, so a mismatch there often signals a missed recording.

Frequently asked questions

Does a Beaumont seller pay a state transfer tax?

No. Texas charges recording fees on a deed but no transfer tax, and the Jefferson County Clerk can quote the exact fees.

What date do Beaumont taxes become late?

Most bills turn delinquent on February 1. They are mailed in October with a general payment deadline of January 31.

Is a Beaumont homestead exemption still available if I forgot to file?

Most likely. A late homestead application is accepted by Jefferson Central Appraisal District for two years after the year's tax became delinquent.

Do Beaumont short-term rentals need permits?

Yes. Stays under 30 consecutive days call for a city permit and a hotel occupancy tax certificate, and each listing must display the permit number.

Who hears a protest of a Beaumont appraisal?

The Appraisal Review Board, once you file with Jefferson Central Appraisal District. The filing limit is whichever comes later, May 15 or 30 days after your notice was mailed.

Drainage questions after storms

The city has run sandbag distributions and a drainage pond project, which points to drainage as a topic buyers raise after heavy rain. Know how your lot drains before showings begin, and keep any repair receipts for grading, gutters or fencing at hand.

Code enforcement and city liens

The Code Enforcement Division checks that properties meet city codes on maintenance, zoning, sanitation and nuisances, and its officers answer complaints and inspect. The city bills water and utilities, runs solid waste collection and recycling, and keeps a floodplain management page within Engineering. Its utility billing office handles accounts, so plan to close your account or transfer service on the closing date and get a final reading.

Hidalgo County taxes at closing

What to have ready for a buyer

Collect permit, tax and utility records so a buyer's title officer finds no gaps. A house with a pool or a sewer tap should have matching paperwork.

  • Homestead and over-65 status from the Hidalgo County Appraisal District portal.
  • Utility account details, since the city bills for water and runs solid waste service.

If the house sits in a mapped flood area, ask the city for the information that applies, because buyers and insurers often ask. Write down the garbage and recycling pickup days and the brush and bulk collection schedule from the city site, since buyers like to know how routine services work on the street.

Filing the deed and heirs

The title company usually files the deed after a notary acknowledges the signature, and the clerk charges per page. Ask for the current schedule before closing.

Ask your title officer which city and county documents will be needed so you can request them in the first week, well ahead of any closing date.

A sale without a listing

Selling as is to a direct buyer skips the photos, the open houses and the repair negotiation that follow a buyer's inspection. What stays is the paperwork. The title company still searches the records, and any city lien, unpaid tax or unclosed permit has to be cleared or paid from the proceeds. That is why the first calls belong to Code Enforcement, the tax office and Building Safety, not to a buyer.

Write down what each office told you, with the date and the name of the department. If a buyer asks about a pool, a room addition or a utility tap, you can answer from your notes.

Your first week as a seller

Spend the first few days on records. Ask the lender for a payoff letter, ask the county tax office for the balance, and ask the city whether a complaint or lien is open on the address. Then request the permit history from Building Safety and confirm your homestead status through the appraisal district portal.

The City of Edinburg Building Safety Department at (956) 388-8203, with Planning and Zoning at (956) 388-8202 for site plan questions.

Use the Hidalgo County Appraisal District property search. The county tax office has the amount due.

Yes, if the lien is paid from the proceeds. Code Enforcement takes lien payoff requests by email, so ask for a figure before closing.

Three routes are open to a Sugar Land owner: list with a full-service agent, sell privately or accept an investor's cash purchase. Your closing deadline, the house's condition and any tenant, lien or heir on the title decide which suits you.

Sugar Land lies in eastern Fort Bend County, about 20 miles southwest of downtown Houston. A house ready to move into can go on the open market. One with a failing roof, or an owner against a deadline, is where a cash buyer usually appears.

  • Full-service listing: the biggest audience and frequently the top price, balanced against showings, inspection requests and the lender's approval of the buyer's loan.
  • Private sale: the commission budget stays with you, along with pricing, marketing and negotiation.
  • Cash purchase: the house sells as it stands, normally below what a polished listing could earn.

Start by collecting the payoff letter, the newest tax statement and any rental license paperwork. Once you have them, you can tell what an offer really leaves after those items are cleared.

Sugar Land housing figures

Sugar Land is an owner-heavy, high-value suburb whose headcount has slipped a little. The mid-2025 estimate is 107,726 people, down 3.0% from an April 2020 base of 111,018.

Sugar Land housing figures, 2020 to 2024
MeasureFigure
Homes occupied by their owners80.3%
Typical price of an owner's home$430,200
Midpoint monthly rent, all costs included$1,957
Average people per household2.85
Midpoint household income$136,217

Owners tend to stay put for years, and shoppers will hold your house up against that $430,200 midpoint. Listings that mention commute routes, home office space and low-maintenance yards speak to the households shopping here. If you are downsizing, you fit a sizable part of the market.

What it costs to carry a Sugar Land house

A buyer shoulders selected owner costs with a median of $2,883 with a mortgage and $1,165 without. Property tax makes up part of that outlay, and it differs by street and school district because each local unit sets its own rate. Ask the Fort Bend County offices for the rates on your parcel and give prospective buyers that figure early. Showing a mortgage buyer the monthly cost of carrying the house next to a cash buyer's position helps both sides compare.

Rental licensing

Rental properties in Sugar Land need a license and an inspection, and that includes owner-occupied houses that get rented out. The rule reached multifamily rentals in July 2009, and the city's Rental Licensing page dates the ordinance from November 2007.

You apply and pay through the city's online Citizen Self Service portal. A renewal filed late draws a $35.00 fee, and an unlicensed rental can be fined up to $500 for each day it is rented. Water service for a tenant cannot start until the owner has applied for the license.

  • Once you apply, the city checks the exterior and grounds against health, sanitation and maintenance codes.
  • Any violations come with a repair schedule, and the license is issued after the fixes.
  • Questions go to the rental program at rentalprogram@sugarlandtx.gov or 281-275-2170.

Renting out the house? Keep the license current until closing. An investor who keeps renting takes on the same duty.

Take a government-issued photo ID to the signing.

Selling a house that is rented

A rented Sugar Land house adds a few steps. Confirm first that the rental license is current, because an unlicensed rental can be fined for each day it is rented. If the city inspected the exterior and grounds and gave a repair schedule, finish those repairs so the license can follow. A new tenant cannot open a water account until the owner applies for the license, which matters if you replace a tenant before closing. Hand each buyer the lease and ask if they intend to keep it as a rental. An investor who continues the rental needs the license in their own name.

How tax dates affect a closing

Each January 1 a lien for that year's tax attaches to the property, which means whoever owns it at closing handles any unpaid balance. Appraisal is as of that date, and bills are mailed around October 1.

  • Anything still owed after January 31 is delinquent, and penalty plus monthly interest begin to build.
  • School districts exempt $140,000 of a principal residence's value.
  • Where the seller never held a homestead exemption, a buyer who closes after January 1 may claim one right away.

Account figures live with Fort Bend County's tax and appraisal offices, so ask for a current statement on your parcel ahead of signing. The title company then divides the current bill by closing date.

Documents to have ready

Gather a few papers before you accept a bid. You will want your payoff letter, the latest tax statement from the Fort Bend County offices, your deed and a government-issued photo ID. Add the rental license and lease if the house is rented, and the will and court papers if you inherited it. All owners on the deed must sign, and anyone who cannot attend should arrange a power of attorney well in advance. Keep it all in one folder so nobody waits on you.

Reading the market in Sugar Land

High home values raise the stakes on every repair and every month on the market. A buyer in this price range will have a home inspection, and a seller with receipts and permits holds an advantage. A cash investor will discount for visible work, so the difference between a listing and a cash offer is often the cost of repairs plus the time you would wait. Weigh it with real numbers from your own house, not an average. Sugar Land's slight population dip does not change that math for one house, but it does mean buyers have options.

Timing a Sugar Land sale around the calendar

Sellers who list in the fall will see tax bills mailed near October 1, and buyers will ask what the bill says. Listing in spring means the new value notice is about to arrive. Either way, a current statement for your parcel keeps the numbers honest. If you rent the house, avoid a lease that ends right at closing unless the buyer wants it empty. If a deadline is pressing, a cash buyer who can set the closing date removes most of this timing worry, though the price will reflect that convenience.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Recording the deed

The Fort Bend County clerk holds real property records for Sugar Land addresses, and a deed must carry a notary's acknowledgment or something similar before it is accepted. The fee is charged per page with additional records charges, so the total depends on how long the document is. Get the figure from your title company ahead of closing.

Inherited or mortgage-troubled houses

An heir has four years after a death to start probate of a will in Texas. The small estate affidavit works only if assets come to $75,000 or less, with the homestead and exempt property set aside.

A lender whose mortgage is in default may auction the house on a month's first Tuesday, once notice has been posted at least 21 days earlier. The borrower can reinstate by catching up within 20 days of the default notice. A sale ahead of the auction leaves the equity with you.

The steps in a cash sale

A cash sale moves in a short sequence. You accept a bid in writing, and a title company opens a file and searches for liens and tax balances. For a rental, the city license gets checked as well. Then comes a closing date and a signing before a notary. No buyer's lender means no appraisal or loan approval, so a clean title can close quickly. Liens, an heir who needs to sign or a license problem can add time.

Frequently asked questions

Can a Sugar Land house close in two weeks?

A cash sale can, if the title is clean and no one else has to sign. Financed purchases take longer while an appraisal and loan approval are pending.

Is a rental license needed before I sell a house I rent out?

Yes, for as long as the unit is rented. Sugar Land fines an unlicensed rental up to $500 for each day, and tenants cannot open a water account until the owner applies.

Who owes property tax when a Sugar Land sale closes?

The current year's bill is split by closing date, and an older balance comes out of the seller's proceeds. The settlement statement shows the split.

What is a typical Sugar Land home worth?

The federal survey for 2020 to 2024 lists $430,200 as the middle price of an owner's home. A specific house can land far from that midpoint depending on age, size and condition.

Can I sell during a foreclosure?

Yes, as long as the sale closes ahead of the auction date. Contact the lender or a title company right away to learn when the sale is set.

Georgetown seats Williamson County and ranks among the quickest-growing U.S. cities over 50,000 people. Residents numbered 47,400 in 2010 and 67,176 in 2020, and the mid-2025 estimate stands at 106,907. Demand is steady, yet a resale shares the market with plenty of new construction. Owing money on the house? Ask your servicer for a payoff quote before anything else, because no offer can sensibly fall under it. Plenty of longtime owners in town are older and thinking about a smaller place, a move nearer relatives or an estate to wrap up, and each of those tends to favor a simple, fast sale.

Historic downtown and older neighborhoods

If your house stands in or near the older blocks around the Square, expect some extra questions. The town counts four National Register historic districts and 52 individually listed properties.

Buyers who love character homes and walkable streets gravitate there. Landmarks close by include the Public Square, the 1911 Williamson County Courthouse, Southwestern University, Lake Georgetown and the San Gabriel River trails.

  • Call the planning office to learn whether your lot falls within a historic district or carries design standards.

Trails and landmarks buyers notice

People recognize the Square's shops and restaurants and the 1911 courthouse. Trails matter too: nearly nine miles of hike and bike paths along the San Gabriel River, nearly seven miles in Garey Park, and 28 miles around Lake Georgetown.

Living near one of these is worth stating directly, whether you list or talk to a cash buyer, since location feeds the price. Measure distances yourself. Make no promises about school zoning or future building, and send buyers to the school district and the planning office for current boundaries and plans.

Property tax breaks for older and disabled owners

Plenty of Georgetown owners are 65 or older, so these exemptions matter. A school district must exempt $140,000 of a homestead's value, plus another $60,000 for seniors and disabled owners.

Those owners also get a ceiling on school tax for the homestead, generally frozen at the amount from the first year they qualified. Part of that ceiling can travel to a new Texas homestead, scaled to the new house, though additions beyond ordinary repairs can raise it. A surviving spouse aged 55 or older sometimes keeps it. Cities, counties and junior college districts may set ceilings of their own.

Owners with a service-connected disability rating qualify for separate exemptions, from up to $5,000 at a 10 to 29 percent rating to up to $12,000 at 70 to 100 percent. A homestead owner rated 100 percent disabled gets a full exemption. Ask the Williamson County appraisal district which ones you hold and how moving would change your ceiling.

Tax bill and protest dates

You can carry a dispute beyond the review board into district court or binding arbitration, and to the State Office of Administrative Hearings when the value tops $1,000,000. Pay the undisputed share before the delinquency date while you appeal.

Paperwork to pull together first

Missing documents slow closings more often than repairs do. A tidy folder lets you weigh bids side by side and gives the title company less to chase after you say yes.

  • Permits and receipts for earlier work, especially near the older neighborhoods.
  • Signatures from co-owners or heirs.

Then ask a cash buyer for a written bid stating price and closing day, and ask an agent for a range based on nearby sales. Judge each by what lands in your pocket after payoffs and closing charges, not by the top-line number. The title company can draft a one-page net sheet that lines them up.

How a cash sale closes

A cash buyer needs no lender appraisal or loan approval, so those weeks vanish. Title work stays: the title company searches the record, gathers payoff letters, drafts the deed and a settlement statement, and holds funds until every signature is in.

Ask the buyer how long the search will take and whether you pick the date. Need a few extra days to move out? Get a short post-closing stay in writing. Read the settlement statement the day before, so any charge you do not recognize gets raised while it is still easy to fix. If a buyer asks for a repair credit late in the process, compare it with what an as-is price already reflects before you agree.

Inherited houses and unclear title

You can sell once ownership is on paper. An heir missing from the recorded deed who wants the homestead exemption has to hand the appraisal district an affidavit of interest, a death certificate and a utility bill.

Property covered by a recorded transfer on death deed bypasses probate. Probate filings, small estate affidavits and deed recordings all go through the county clerk. Before meeting buyers, round up the death certificate, any will and the lenders' payoff statements.

On closing day the title company confirms who is allowed to sign, pays off liens from the proceeds and files the deed. A buyer who takes the house as-is saves heirs the cleanout, the repairs and months of carrying costs.

Does Georgetown's growth help a quick sale?

Fast growth supports demand, with 106,907 residents estimated for 2025. Your own price and condition set the pace, so weigh offers by net proceeds.

What is the middle home value in Georgetown?

The survey puts it at $429,100 for owner-occupied homes in 2020 to 2024. Use it as background only.

Can seniors take their school tax ceiling to a new home?

Yes, in proportion, if you buy another Texas homestead. Check with the appraisal district first.

Which county records my Georgetown deed?

Williamson County, which has its seat at Georgetown. Deeds are filed with that county's clerk.

Do historic rules reach a newer Georgetown house?

Only if your address falls inside a district. Ask the city planning office, and keep permit records for any exterior work.

Your options in Wichita Falls

Three paths lead out of a Wichita Falls house: a broker listing, a private sale, or a cash purchase. Condition and schedule do most of the deciding. Hail or wind damage, a tired roof or long-delayed upkeep favor cash, and a house in good shape may earn more on the open market.

Wichita Falls is the Wichita County seat, on the Wichita River in North Texas near the Oklahoma line. Buyers come from across the county and from the Sheppard Air Force Base community. Much of the housing was built between the 1920s and the 1950s. Older wiring, plumbing and foundations are common, and buyers subtract those repairs from what they offer.

  • Start with the deed, any liens and your mortgage payoff.
  • Gather permit records for the roof, additions and similar work.
  • Set a listing timeline beside a cash closing date and compare.
  • Have the title company run a search for recorded liens.

Roof permits and the 1979 tornado

The April 10, 1979 tornado cut through the southern part of Wichita Falls, destroyed twenty percent of the dwellings in town and injured more than 3,200 people. Most of the damage was repaired within three years. The city still takes roofing and other major work seriously.

Any roof replacement, and any roof repair larger than 500 square feet, calls for a city permit. The contractor is the one who must obtain it, and before the first shingle comes off. Bonding is also required of contractors who work in town.

Keep the permit on file when you sell. Buyers down the road may hesitate over major improvements, a new roof for example, that went in without approval, and missing permits can complicate an insurance claim. If your roof was replaced after a hail storm, have the permit number and the roofer's invoice ready to hand over.

Building Inspections

Building Inspections, at 1300 Seventh Street, issues permits and does the inspections. Forms, checklists and the fee ordinance are on the city's site. Phone 940-761-7459 to reach the office.

The city gives four reasons to use a bonded contractor and pull a permit: code compliance, safety inspections, insurance coverage and the bond itself. An owner whose roof went on without a permit may find that insurance will not cover damage tied to that work. A closed permit in your paperwork answers that worry before the buyer raises it.

Check any additions, a pool or a roof replacement from your years of ownership against permit records. When a permit was left open, ask Building Inspections how to resolve it before you list. For utility questions about a specific address, the city's utility office can answer.

Wichita County property taxes

Eight taxing jurisdictions in the county rely on the Wichita County Tax Office to assess and collect, and the office distributes almost $120 million a year to them. Online payment, penalty and interest details, a tax estimator and a list of the units it serves are on the office website.

Texas property tax calendar for a Wichita Falls owner
DateWhat happens
January 1Appraised value is fixed and that year's tax lien takes hold
April 30Deadline for most exemption filings
May 15Final day to protest most appraisals
October 1Tax bills go in the mail
January 31Pay by this date to avoid penalty

Penalty and interest start February 1. At closing, the title company normally divides that year's tax between you and the buyer.

Homestead exemption, deeds and foreclosure

Homestead relief on the school tax is $140,000, plus $60,000 more for owners over 65 or disabled. It belongs to the person who qualifies and stops when you sell. A disabled veteran may qualify for larger amounts as the disability rating rises.

The Wichita County Clerk records deeds for property inside the city. Each deed must be signed and acknowledged. The first page costs $5.00 to record and each added page $4.00.

Lenders who foreclose hold the auction on a first Tuesday, after the notice has been posted and filed for three weeks. If your sale closes before that Tuesday, the lender is repaid from the proceeds and the foreclosure can stop.

Selling with unpermitted work or taxes owed

Unpermitted work does not make a sale impossible, but it changes the conversation. A cash investor will typically buy the house as it stands and lower the price to match. A buyer with a mortgage may hear questions from the lender or an inspector.

Back taxes are paid from your proceeds when the sale closes. Phone the county tax office for today's balance, then let the title company check it against its own search. The clerk's office can supply a copy of any recorded lien, so you know what has to be cleared.

Before you speak with any buyer, run through this list:

  1. Pull the recorded deed and check each owner name.
  2. Ask your lender for a payoff statement.
  3. Find permit numbers for the roof and any additions.
  4. Ask the tax office what is owed on the account.
  5. Decide how soon you must close, then judge offers by that date.

A cash sale skips the buyer's loan approval and appraisal, so the closing date depends mostly on title work. That can mean weeks rather than months.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Wichita Falls houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Visiting the offices and closing the sale

Two visits cover most of what a seller needs. At Building Inspections you can learn whether permits on your property were closed out. At the tax office you can get the balance due, see whether an exemption is on the account and hear how penalty and interest work on a late bill.

Take a photo ID, a copy of your deed, and the property address or account number. Selling on behalf of a relative or an estate? Add the recorded paperwork that shows you may sign. Also write down your questions, since staff can only answer what they are asked.

On closing day, the title company collects signatures, pays off the mortgage and any unpaid tax from the proceeds, and files the new deed with the county clerk. You hand over keys once funds are released. Ask for a final settlement statement a day ahead so you can read every line before you sign.

Ask each buyer how they plan to pay, who covers closing costs and how long they need to close. Two offers with the same headline price can leave you with very different amounts once repairs, fees and waiting time are counted.

If the house is vacant, remember that insurance and utilities are still yours until the sale is done. A shorter timeline means fewer months of carrying those costs, which is one reason sellers with storm-damaged or empty houses lean toward cash.

Frequently asked questions

Is a permit required for a roof replacement in Wichita Falls?

Yes, for a replacement or any repair over 500 square feet. The contractor must pull the permit before work begins and must be bonded. Call Building Inspections if you are unsure.

Who collects property taxes in Wichita County?

The Wichita County Tax Office collects for eight taxing jurisdictions in the county. Its website has pages on penalties and interest, online payment and a tax estimator.

Does the 1979 tornado still matter to Wichita Falls home sellers?

Mostly as building history. The tornado destroyed twenty percent of the city's dwellings, and the city now stresses permits on roofing and other major work. Keep permit records for any repairs.

What is the property tax deadline in Wichita County?

Taxes are due on or before January 31. Penalty and interest start February 1, and the lien for each year attaches on January 1.

Can I sell a Wichita Falls house with unpermitted work?

Yes, but a buyer or lender may ask about it. Missing permits can make future buyers cautious. Ask Building Inspections how to close an old permit before you list.

If the taxing unit brings in its lawyer, collection costs of up to 20 percent can be stacked onto the balance. If you pay within three weeks of learning the bill was late, a written waiver request may help in some cases. Every school district has to leave $140,000 of a homestead's value untaxed, and owners who are seniors or disabled get $60,000 more. Counties that charge farm-to-market or flood control taxes subtract $3,000. Older and disabled owners also get a frozen school tax amount, and the freeze can follow them, in proportion, to a later Texas homestead. If you sell mid-year to a buyer who lives there and you had no exemption, the buyer may claim it for whatever remains of that year. An owner with a service disability can take $5,000 to $12,000 off the value, and a 100 percent rating means the whole homestead is exempt.

Tenants in the house

Renters do not have to leave because you sold. A buyer who wants the place empty, though, depends on the landlord winning a Texas eviction first.

With no lease clause on the point, the landlord first hands over a written notice giving three days, then sues in justice court. A hearing date falls 10 to 21 days after filing, and the tenant gets served four days before it. Appealing to county court is allowed, within five days of the judgment. A writ cannot issue until six days after judgment, and the constable posts 24 hours' notice before carrying it out. Buyers who accept the tenant in place never face this process.

Selling an inherited house

Learn whether the previous owner left a will. The answer tells you which court document the buyer's closer will want to see.

Texas gives heirs until four years after the death to offer a will for probate, normally in the home county. If the only debts are liens on the real estate, a muniment of title can move the house to the heirs, with the court order and will filed in the county where the land sits. For estates with no will and no administration, a small estate affidavit works if the value outside the homestead is no more than $75,000. An heirship affidavit is just a sworn statement, and outsiders such as a title company can turn it down.

  • Pull together the death certificate and whatever deed is recorded.
  • Ask the appraisal district what heirs must file to keep a homestead exemption.
  • Talk to a probate lawyer before you sign a purchase contract.

Facing foreclosure

Texas power-of-sale foreclosure follows a set schedule. Selling ahead of it is how owners hold on to whatever equity they have.

Once the lender sends its default notice, you have 20 days to pay the arrears and reinstate. Then comes a sale notice, posted at least three weeks before an auction on the first Tuesday of a month, at a spot the commissioners court has designated. Any surplus after the lender is paid reaches junior lienholders first, with the remainder yours. If the sale falls short, the lender can chase the difference for two years. A cash buyer able to close inside that window may be your only way to sell in time.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

What changes with a cash buyer

A cash deal removes the buyer's mortgage, the appraisal and most repair credits. You still need clean title, a signed contract and an agreed closing day. Take your photo ID, the deed or inheritance papers and your latest tax summary to the title company. Settle who pays title and recording fees before you sign, and review the closing statement a day ahead so nothing catches you off guard.

What county is San Angelo in?

Tom Green County. San Angelo is the county seat, and the appraisal district there keeps the property records.

Can I pay San Angelo property tax online?

Yes. The district's Tax Summary page has a pay link for electronic check or card. Confirm current options with the tax office.

Must I clear old taxes before selling?

Closing proceeds cover any old tax, since the lien stays with the house. Get a tax certificate from the title company beforehand.

When does a protest hearing happen?

Hearings begin around mid May, and the review board approves the roll by July 20. Miss the filing deadline and you lose the hearing.

What does a cash buyer pay for in San Angelo?

It varies by buyer. Get the bid in writing and see who covers title, recording and repairs before you sign.

How fast a Temple sale can go

Say yes to a cash buyer in Temple and closing can land within a few weeks. Listing with an agent stretches the calendar: showings, an appraisal, then a lender's sign-off. What actually sets your pace is the payoff on your loan, the repairs the house needs and the date you must be out.

Hospital employment and big local employers keep newcomers flowing in, and many rent or buy while they get settled. Cash investors lean toward houses with deferred work. Owner-occupants want ones they can move into untouched.

  • Cash purchase: no lender in the middle, so your title work and your chosen move date control the schedule.
  • Agent listing: wider exposure, though more of the timeline sits in other people's hands.
  • Repair credit: a middle path when a financed buyer asks for a new roof or HVAC unit.

The town began when the Santa Fe railroad held a land auction on June 29, 1881, and the hospital tradition born in those railroad days still shapes who buys here. Homes near the medical campus and I-35 usually attract the widest crowd.

Temple housing market

Temple counted 98,412 residents in July 2025, a rise of 19.7 percent over the 2020 base. The decennial counts were 66,102 in 2010 and 82,073 in 2020. Growth that fast puts fresh subdivisions in direct competition with resale houses, so an older home tends to move best when priced for a buyer who would rather not do repairs.

Close to half of Temple households rent. Investors who intend to keep a house as a rental may take a tenant-worn property gladly, which helps an owner eager to leave without touching the paint or flooring. If a buyer finances with a VA loan, that lender's appraisal standards will influence which repairs get requested.

Property tax billing and payment

Value comes from Bell Central Appraisal District, while the Bell County tax office collects for most units. Walk-in payment at any location is fee-free by check, cash or money order. Card or check payment online runs through a vendor that adds a fee, and a drop box outside the Belton office takes payments once the doors are shut.

Three relief options are on offer: deferral, a quarterly installment agreement, and a separate installment agreement for delinquent homestead taxes. State law limits homestead value increases to 10 percent annually until assessed value catches up with market value. Phone the district to learn what terms would apply to your account.

  • February 1 is the delinquency date for anything still unpaid after January 31.
  • The tax lien attaches every January 1, so the closing agent clears that year's bill ahead of the deed transfer.
  • Homestead exemption applications generally close April 30.

Exemptions for Temple owners

Bell CAD recognizes residential homestead, disabled person, age 65 or older, 100 percent disabled veteran, several surviving-spouse categories, and a donated residence for a partially disabled veteran. Renewal is not required each year, but the chief appraiser can request a refreshed application.

  • A current Texas driver's license or ID showing the property address.
  • For disabled owners, a letter or card from the Social Security Administration.
  • For a veteran with a service-connected disability, a recent VA awards letter.

Filing after April 30 may still work: submit the application and the district applies the legislative remedies upon approval. Before you move out, ask Bell CAD how to remove your own exemption so the incoming owner can claim theirs.

Paperwork to pull together before offers arrive

Five documents do most of the work: a lender payoff statement, your newest tax bill, any HOA statement, repair invoices and the deed. A buyer with those can write a sturdier offer, and the title company can open the file the same day.

  • A written payoff from each lender holding a lien.
  • A tax statement that shows every unit billing you.
  • Receipts or notes on the roof, foundation, plumbing and air conditioning.
  • Lease and deposit details if a tenant lives there.

Offers deserve a side-by-side look at closing-cost responsibility, the length of any inspection period and the date earnest money turns nonrefundable. A big headline price loaded with open conditions may net you less than a smaller one that funds on schedule.

A cash sale moves in a plain order. You accept terms, the title company opens an order, the buyer may tour the house, and you choose a closing date that fits your move. Appraisal and loan underwriting never enter the picture, which removes two frequent causes of late collapses.

Inherited, behind on payments or tenant occupied

Each situation runs through its own Texas procedure, and the Texas State Law Library explains them. An heir might need to probate the will, seek a muniment of title, or rely on a transfer on death deed recorded in time. Until one of those is in place, nobody can sign a deed to a buyer.

When a lender has posted the house for foreclosure, the first-Tuesday auction is your cutoff. A borrower may reinstate by paying the past-due balance within 20 days of the default notice. Landlords serve written notice to vacate, three days unless the lease says otherwise, before turning to justice court.

Gather the death certificate, will, loan statement or lease before your first call. That small step gets you answers quicker than starting from scratch.

Cash buyers can often handle a tangled file but cannot get around absent authority. Closing waits until the signer holds the legal right to convey, so resolve that point first. A Bell County title company will say what it wants to see, and asking costs nothing.

Where the deed is filed

Once the sale funds, the deed is recorded with the Bell County Clerk, since the county that holds the land keeps its deed records. Recording demands the owner's signature and a notary's acknowledgment. A statute sets the recording fee, so you will see the amount on the closing statement, and the clerk can quote it early.

You rarely make this trip. The title company files the signed, notarized deed and passes along confirmation of recording, which finishes the sale on the public record. Keep that confirmation with your closing papers. If a tax bill or insurance notice for the old address shows up later, it helps you prove the date ownership changed hands.

On closing day, bring a government photo ID and any keys, garage remotes and gate codes. Utilities are usually transferred the same day, so call the providers a few days ahead to schedule a final read and stop service in your name.

Frequently asked questions

Must I renovate before accepting cash in Temple?

No. Cash buyers commonly purchase as is and build repair costs into the price. Repairs matter more when a buyer finances and the lender insists on them. If a buyer requests work after inspection, you can negotiate a credit rather than do it yourself.

Which office sends the tax bill for a Temple address?

Each taxing unit on your address has its own collector, all working from Bell CAD values. The district or the county tax office can tell you which units apply.

Can a house in probate be sold in Temple?

Often yes, as soon as someone holds legal authority to sign. The will and the estate decide which paperwork supplies it, so check with a Texas probate attorney.

Does my homestead exemption pass to the buyer?

No. It stays with you as owner. The buyer files for their own, and the state allows it for the rest of the year if the seller held none.

Which county records the deed on a Temple sale?

Bell County. Your title company usually handles the filing after closing.

Three ways to sell a Bryan house

A Bryan seller can use an agent, go solo, or take cash. Let the house's condition and the time you have drive the decision. An agent listing means cleanup, open houses and a closing that depends on the buyer's lender. Cash skips all of that, in exchange for a price that discounts repairs and risk.

The city has more than 93,000 people and shares Brazos County with College Station and Texas A&M. Long-time families, university staff, students and renters all shape who shows up to buy or lease a house here.

Rail service came in 1867 and Bryan incorporated November 29, 1871. The oldest houses stand near historic downtown, and an inspector will go straight to the wiring, plumbing and foundation. Electric service comes from the city's own Bryan Texas Utilities, so call the utility office about final readings and transferring service on closing day.

Brazos County property tax cycle

Brazos Central Appraisal District values each parcel, then each taxing unit serving it sets a rate. Use the calendar below to see who owes what at closing.

  • Send exemption applications to the district by email. Staff answer phones on weekdays from 8:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m.

A value dispute goes to the appraisal review board, which has an email address of its own. Certain properties, undivided-interest ownership among them, can't use the online appeals portal. If yours is one, phone the district well ahead of the deadline.

Selling a house that was a short-term rental

Rent a Bryan home, apartment or garage unit for 30 days or less and it counts as a short-term rental. Hotel occupancy tax of 7 percent applies to the gross rent, including cleaning and pet charges.

  • Returns are filed through the GovOS portal, due monthly by the 20th of the next month.

File your last returns before handing over the keys, so no tax balance follows you. The city's fiscal services office answers questions at 979-209-5080. Tell any buyer whether guests are already booked for future dates.

Inherited, behind on payments or rented?
