Old tax doesn't disappear when you sell. It clings to the land, so it has to be paid from your proceeds or the buyer inherits it. Phone the Brazos County tax office for the exact payoff before you weigh offers, and mentally subtract it from every number you hear. Delinquent balances keep growing after January 31, so ask early.

Recording a deed in Brazos County

Recording is done by the Brazos County clerk, so that is where the deed for a Bryan lot is filed. Before it records a conveyance, the clerk needs either a notary's acknowledgment or two witnesses.

The Texas courts' 2023 clerk manual sets one fee for the first page, a smaller one per added page, and several extras. The clerk can give you the current total. Your title company usually does the recording and sends you the copy.

What to line up before a cash closing

Pull together your latest tax bill, the mortgage payoff, any lease, and rental tax filings if guests stayed. Heirs bring probate or affidavit paperwork, and an heir who isn't on the deed must also show the appraisal district an ownership interest before claiming an exemption. With these papers in hand, a buyer can name a price and a closing date quickly. If students or other renters live in the house under a lease, a buyer will ask for that lease first, along with its end date.

Once an offer is signed, the title company looks for liens and open taxes, while you settle the closing date and request final meter readings from the utility office. At closing, tax proration and any loan payoff come out of your proceeds, a notary witnesses the deed signature, and the clerk files it. A cash sale with clean title can be done in a few weeks, because no lender has to sign off. Listing takes longer because the buyer's loan and appraisal set the clock. Either path slows down for an unprobated estate or an open lien.

Who pays the property tax when a Bryan house sells?

Buyer and seller normally share the sale year's tax, as shown on the settlement statement. Any earlier unpaid year gets paid at closing, since that lien stays on the land. Call the Brazos County tax office for your balance.

Can I sell a Bryan house that is listed on Airbnb?

Yes. File your hotel occupancy tax returns first, because the city requires monthly or quarterly reports on short-term rent. Tell buyers if future dates are already booked.

Usually, unless another recorded route shows who has authority. Choices include a muniment of title, a small estate affidavit or an administration.

What can I do if a Bryan foreclosure sale is scheduled?

Move before the first Tuesday sale. You can reinstate within 20 days of the default notice, sell the house, or talk to the servicer about alternatives. After an auction, leftover equity goes to junior lienholders before it reaches you.

Is Leander a good place to sell fast?

Leander is an Austin-area suburb on U.S. Highway 183 in southwestern Williamson County, and it keeps growing. You can sell to a cash buyer as-is or list in the usual way, and each trades speed against price.

The mix here runs from older houses near the original townsite to many newer builds, so age and condition vary a lot from street to street. New construction competes with resale listings. Exemptions and caps

A buyer's tax bill depends on the exemptions they can claim, so it helps to know the basics.

  • Starting the year after the exemption begins, a homestead's appraised value cannot climb more than 10 percent annually for school and other taxes.
  • School tax for an over-65 or disabled owner stays capped at what it was the year they qualified, and that ceiling can move to a new Texas homestead.

When Williamson County taxes are due

Statements go out around October 1. Balances left open on February 1 get a six percent penalty and monthly interest, and by July 1 the penalty hits 12 percent.

Eligible owners in Williamson County can pay in four installments, on January 31, March 31, May 31 and July 31. There is also a monthly prepayment option that pulls from a card or bank account. Ask the county tax office whether your account qualifies before counting on any plan.

Appraisal values and protests

Williamson County's appraisal district values property as of January 1 each year. Disputing the value? Mark May 15, or 30 days after a late notice arrives. If your value looks high compared with recent sales of similar homes, a protest changes what the next owner inherits, which can matter to a buyer weighing your house against a new build.

Closing steps in Leander

  2. Check for an HOA or utility district transfer fee.
  3. Sign the deed before a notary so the county clerk can record it.

Shoppers looking at Leander are usually also looking at other suburbs in the Austin area. They line up the total tax rate, the school zone and the age of the house, then ask what the monthly payment will be. A seller who can hand over the numbers for each taxing unit, a clear HOA statement and a short list of recent updates answers most of that before it is asked.

New builds nearby give buyers a benchmark for finish and warranty coverage. If your house is older, price it with that comparison in mind, and show what has been replaced and when.

Planning a second Texas purchase

Some sellers move within Texas. If you are over 65 or disabled and hold a school tax freeze, ask the appraisal district what proof the new county will want, and keep the paperwork from this house. The ceiling set in the year you qualified is the number that can carry over. Gather the closing statement from the sale as well, since it documents the date your ownership ended.

When a mortgage payoff is part of the sale

If you owe on the house, the lender provides a payoff letter showing the amount needed on a specific closing date. The title company uses it, with the tax statement and any HOA transfer fee, to build the settlement sheet. Because the payoff changes day by day, ask for an updated letter whenever the closing date moves. What remains after the loan, the year's tax share and closing costs is your net.

Preparing for an as-is sale

A prepared file speeds a quick sale and heads off price cuts late in the process. Collect these before you call buyers.

  • The HOA contact and any capital contribution or transfer fee.
  • Your most recent Williamson County tax statement showing each taxing unit.
  • A short written list of known defects.

Subdivisions started appearing in the late 1950s, and a house from that era may need electrical or plumbing work that buyers will factor into their offer. Cash buyers can leave that work undone; a mortgage lender may insist on it.

School zone and neighborhood details

Buyers with children often ask which school zone a house falls in. Confirm the zoning with Leander ISD before listing and put the answer in your marketing. Say what your street is like, how old the roof and air conditioning are, and what the HOA covers. Specific answers up front shorten the time between first showing and offer.

Cash offer or listing?

Not having to repair anything is why people take cash offers, and the price falls accordingly. A listing after repairs can bring more, but it adds commissions, showings and the wait for the buyer's loan. Put the two side by side with real numbers: the cash price on one side, and on the other the likely sale price minus repair costs, commission and the months you would carry the house.

Ask for a line-by-line list of closing costs, recording fees among them, ahead of signing day, so the net you compare is the net you receive.

Can I sell a Leander house without making repairs?

Yes. Avoiding repairs is the draw of a cash offer, and the price falls to reflect it. Then check that figure against a listing after repairs and commissions.

Which closing costs should I expect when selling in Leander?

Ask the title company for a full list of closing costs, with county recording fees, before you sign.

Who sets the appraised value of my Leander home?

Williamson County's appraisal district values property on January 1 of each year. Mark May 15 for a protest, or 30 days from delivery of a late notice.

What happens to my homestead exemption after I sell?

It ends with your ownership. A buyer living in the house as a main residence applies for a new one. If you are over 65, your freeze may move with you to another Texas homestead.

How soon can a Mission house be sold?

Selling for cash can take just weeks. Investors and buyers acting for out-of-town heirs are active here, and owners often choose cash after inheriting a house, moving away from the Valley or facing repairs. Keep your deed and tax bill handy.

About Mission, Texas

Mission is a Hidalgo County city on the Rio Grande, founded in 1908 when the Missouri Pacific Railroad set up a station near the center of a new development. It takes its name from La Lomita Chapel, and the population is approaching 70,000. The area is where citrus was first planted in the Rio Grande Valley, and the Texas Citrus Fiesta marks that heritage each year.

That history is the backdrop to the local housing stock, which mixes older parcels near the center with newer lots farther out.

Which sale routes does a Mission owner have?

You have three paths, and each runs on its own clock.

  • Cash buyer. A fit for as-is sales, clouded inherited title and storm or roof damage.
  • Agent listing. May bring more for a home in good shape, though showings and loan timelines come with it.
  • Seller financing. Slower and regulated. A contract for deed on a residence is governed by Property Code chapter 5, and the buyer keeps a right to cancel.

Insist on written offers and learn who pays for title, recording and survey.

Old land records and clear title

Land around Mission began as Spanish porciones, long strips running about two-thirds of a mile along the river and 11 to 16 miles inland. Porciones 55 and 57 held Rancho La Lomita, home of the chapel, and a land company later developed the area around the 1908 railroad station.

Because of that start, older Mission parcels may show long ownership chains in county records, and a title search follows every link. Land held by a family for generations calls for gathering old deeds, family agreements and probate papers, since a gap can hold up a sale. Ask a cash buyer's title company early what it needs.

Building permits and repairs in Mission

Mission's Inspections Division reviews permits for new buildings and checks compliance with minimum building codes. A permit is also required for any concrete or asphalt slab with a value of $100 or more, and mobile homes need permits.

Inspectors check foundation, plumbing, framing, mechanical, A/C, electrical, setbacks, sidewalks and buffering on new residences. Structures that existed before annexation are treated as grandfathered while they stay as they are, but expanding one requires a permit and brings zoning and setback rules into play. The division's phone is 956-580-8691. Prior to listing, find out whether any addition, slab or carport was permitted. Open work can hold up a buyer's lender.

Hidalgo appraisal district and tax dates

Hidalgo CAD sets values for Mission property. Homestead and over-65 applications go through its online portal, and you can reach customer service by phone at 956-381-8466.

Homestead notices land around April 1, with protests due by mid-May. State law holds a homestead's appraised value to a 10 percent rise per year. Ask the district which exemptions sit on your account so a buyer knows what happens after closing.

Homestead exemptions for a Mission buyer

A buyer who moves in can apply for the residence homestead exemption. School taxes drop by $140,000 of value, and an owner 65 or older or disabled gets $60,000 more.

  • Even when you never filed, a buyer who closes after January 1 can get it at once for that year.
  • For a disabled veteran the amount is $5,000 to $12,000 by rating, and a full 100 percent rating can exempt the whole homestead.
  • Heirs missing from the deed may still apply, using an ownership affidavit, a death certificate and a utility bill.

What if unpaid taxes lead to a tax sale?

Unpaid taxes are backed by a lien the county can foreclose. It attaches each January 1, and a court may take the property even after a sale. Expect court costs, plus up to 20 percent for contract attorneys.

Getting land back after a tax sale is hard. A homestead owner has two years from the filing of the purchaser's deed, and pays costs plus a 25 percent premium in year one or 50 percent in year two. Other property gets just 180 days. A former owner can claim excess proceeds for two years. Start by asking the tax office for a payoff and itemized statement.

  • Homeowners over 65 or disabled can use installments.
  • Some collectors offer plans running up to 36 months, and a homestead must be offered one.
  • Penalty and interest waivers must be requested in writing.

How a Mission seller compares offers

Reduce each bid to the same terms before you pick. The highest price with a slow inspection period can pay less than a smaller cash bid that closes fast.

  • Dollar amount and as-is status.
  • Closing date and title company.
  • Fees for title, recording and survey, and who pays.
  • Earnest money and its fate if the buyer leaves.
  • Loan or appraisal conditions.

Get final figures on a closing statement, and take questions about confusing lines to the title company.

Steps from contract to closing

Your accepted offer triggers a title search. The company reads county records for liens, tax balances and gaps in who owned the land, which matters most with older Mission parcels where a missing heir or an unreleased lien can turn up late. Each problem must be resolved before anyone signs the deed.

Bring the deed, your newest tax bill, a loan payoff letter and permit papers for additions. Closing takes one sitting. You sign, the county clerk records the deed, your loan and taxes are paid from the funds, and the remainder is yours. A buyer with a mortgage adds an appraisal that may reopen the price. Cash buyers generally skip that step.

Liens, probate and foreclosure

Proceeds at closing cover any liens and taxes. Inherited property brings a request from the title company for court orders or recorded papers showing who may sign, and probate of a will has a four-year limit from the death.

Foreclosure is usually a nonjudicial auction on a first Tuesday, preceded by 21 days' notice, and a deficiency suit has a two-year window. Selling beforehand leaves the equity in your hands.

Where a Mission deed is recorded

Once notarized, the deed is filed with the county clerk where the land sits. The 2023 manual lists $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for every later page, with records fees capped. Ask the clerk what is charged now.

Questions to ask a buyer before signing

Before you sign, learn the purchaser's identity, whether the offer is as-is and who holds the earnest money. Ask about the closing date and the plan if title trouble appears. Read every page of the contract, and have the title company, not the buyer, prepare your closing statement.

Frequently asked questions

Is a storm-damaged Mission house sellable?

Yes, to cash buyers who price in the repairs. Listing usually means fixing damage for lender approval.

When does Mission require a permit for concrete?

For any slab worth $100 or more. Expanding an older structure also needs a permit and brings zoning setbacks into play.

Who sets appraised values in Mission?

The Hidalgo County Appraisal District. Reach customer service at 956-381-8466 or use its portal for homestead and over-65 filings.

What proves I can sell an inherited house?

A muniment of title, administration or a transfer on death deed. A will must be probated within four years of death.

Can selling halt a foreclosure?

If closing happens before the auction, yes. Texas allows 20 days to reinstate after the default notice and at least 21 days' notice of sale.

Under Baytown's land development code, a nightly rental in a residential or mixed-use district needs a Special Use Permit approved by City Council. The first request was approved with conditions for an existing house in a Suburban Residential district.

Staff later drafted an amendment to swap that vote for a standard permit process in those districts. Council also weighed annual permits and inspections, along with occupancy and parking limits, so the rules may have changed by the time you list.

Has your house hosted paying guests? Planning staff can tell you which rule covers the address and whether an approval is on record. A buyer who is counting on rental income should confirm the status with the city before signing. The city's amendment notice describes the proposal.

Selling a house you inherited in Baytown

  • Small estate affidavit: limited to $75,000 in assets beyond the homestead. It rarely fits real property, with the exception of a homestead going to a spouse or minor children.
  • Affidavit of heirship: a sworn statement and nothing more; a title company is under no legal duty to take it.
  • Executor's or administrator's deed: signed once a court has appointed the person.

An heir left off the recorded deed can keep a homestead exemption by handing the appraisal district an affidavit of ownership interest, a death certificate and a recent utility bill. The State Law Library's informal probate guide explains each route, and a probate lawyer can tell you which one fits your estate.

Back taxes when a Baytown house sells

Taxes follow the house. Each year's lien takes hold on January 1, so any unpaid tax is deducted from your proceeds at closing. Bills come in October. Once February 1 arrives, an unpaid account is delinquent and adds a six percent penalty and one percent interest.

Behind on a homestead? Some collectors offer payment plans of up to 36 months, so ask. At the table you sign the deed in front of a notary, and the clerk of the county holding the land records it. Keys normally change hands at funding unless the contract says otherwise. Repairs, repair credits and a cash offer

Buyers of older Baytown houses ask about the roof, plumbing and foundation. In a regular listing the inspector notes each problem, and the buyer responds with a repair request or a lower price. A cash buyer inspects once and builds the cost into a single offer, which spares you the back and forth.

Whatever you choose, start by collecting the latest tax statement, any payment plan papers, mortgage payoff figures and permit records for past work, plus the lease if someone rents the house. A complete file helps a buyer decide faster and press for fewer concessions.

Both counties. Baytown is in southeastern Harris County and runs east into western Chambers County. The county on your tax bill decides where the deed is filed and which appraisal district values the lot.

Not until you have checked with the city. Council has had to approve a Special Use Permit for each one, and an amendment would swap that for a permit process. Planning staff will tell you which rule covers your address.

Is there a time limit to probate a will before I sell?

In general, file the will within four years of the death; a court may still accept it later for good cause. The muniment of title order and the will are then delivered to the clerk of the county where the property is located.

  • A disabled veteran gets a partial exemption in tiers, and a 100 percent rating can mean the homestead is fully exempt.

The title company divides the year's bill at the closing table. Any open lien is paid off from what you receive.

Foreclosure and unpaid taxes

Call the lender or the tax office before a deadline, since both processes move in fixed steps. Texas lenders holding a deed of trust can sell without going to court. Before they do, you get a default notice with twenty days to cure, and a sale notice must land three weeks ahead of an auction early in the month.

Afterward, a lender may sue for a shortfall within two years. If land is sold for taxes, the owner can redeem it within two years for homestead, farm or mineral property and within 180 days for other land.

Selling ahead of the auction usually beats whatever the auction would bring. Ask the title company to write down each payoff amount and lien balance.

Inherited and rented houses

Begin with the deed. If the owner has died, first work out whether probate is required. Four years after the death is the limit for probating a will. Real estate can pass by muniment of title if the estate owes only liens on the property.

A renter who will not leave is removed in stages: written notice three days ahead, a justice court filing, service four days before the trial, and a writ of possession six days after the judgment. Given that timetable, plenty of owners sell with the renter still inside.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Longview houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Preparing a mid-century house

Much of Longview's housing stock came from a long period of growth, so a lot of houses are older and show it. Walk the property as an inspector would: stand under the roof edge and look for lifting shingles, check the slab and exterior walls for cracks, run every faucet, and flip each switch. Write down what you find. Fixing a leaking faucet or a loose outlet cover costs little and takes a worry off the buyer's list; a failing foundation or old wiring is a bigger decision.

With a long repair list, an investor can take the house untouched and lower the price by the cost of the work. If the house is close to move-in condition, a listing can bring more. Get at least one written cash offer and one agent's opinion of the listing price before you choose.

Questions to ask the tax office

Ask what is owed today and what it will be on the closing date. Ask whether the house has an exemption and whose name it is under. Ask whether any installment plan or collection step is open. The tax office and the appraisal district are separate offices, and the title company needs paperwork from both.

Since the Gregg district is conducting a residential reappraisal, an appraiser may visit while your house is listed. That is routine. The visit does not change your sale, but a new photograph and an updated record may result.

Splitting the year with your buyer

Property tax in Texas is billed in the fall for the whole year, and the lien attaches on January 1. When a Longview house sells part-way through the year, the contract says how the bill is divided. Your title company usually handles that arithmetic, but you should read the line on the settlement sheet and ask how it was reached. If the bill has not been issued by the closing date, ask how the estimate was built and whether any adjustment is promised once the real bill arrives. Late January is the last safe payment date, so any amount still open after that begins collecting penalty and interest.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

A straddling city means two sets of offices

Because Longview sits in two counties, the usual advice to call the county tax office and appraisal district comes with an extra step: figure out which county first. Your tax bill names the right one. Do not assume that a neighbor two blocks over uses the same offices as you. When a buyer's agent or lender asks for county records, give them the name of the county and the account number from your bill so the request goes to the correct place the first time.

Recording the deed

Deeds are recorded by the Gregg or Harrison County clerk, whichever county holds the land. A notary must acknowledge your signature, and the clerk can quote what recording costs. Closing funds usually cover them. Check that the legal description matches the deed already of record.

Documents and calls to make first

Start with the deed, the newest bill and a loan payoff statement. Call the appraisal district named on that bill and ask which exemptions are active. Ask the tax office for the amount owed today and on your hoped-for closing date. If an old lien turns up in the county records, tell the title company at once; it is easier to clear one before a contract than after.

If you rent the house out, collect the lease and tell any buyer about it in writing.

From offer to closing

  1. Collect offers from a cash buyer and, if you want, a listing agent.
  2. Compare the amount each leaves you after payoffs, tax share and repair costs.
  3. Open title with a title company and give it your payoff figures.
  4. Sign the deed before a notary.
  5. The deed goes to the right county clerk once funds are released.

A cash purchase generally skips the lender's appraisal, so closing can come quickly once title is clear.

Frequently asked questions

Is a Longview house in Gregg or Harrison County?

Either, because the city crosses the county line. Look at your tax bill: the appraisal district named there is your contact, and the clerk in that same county records the deed.

Can a lien stop a Longview sale?

No, though it must be paid. Payoff figures come from the title company, which pays liens out of your proceeds. What a buyer cannot get is clear title while delinquent property taxes are still owed.

When are Longview property taxes late?

Most unpaid bills are delinquent from February 1, when a six percent penalty and one percent interest begin. The penalty keeps growing each month until July 1.

Must I repair a Longview house before a cash sale?

No. Cash buyers purchase in current condition and price in the work they expect. Before deciding, compare the offer with a repaired-and-listed price.

How quickly can foreclosure move in Texas?

Fast. Twenty days to cure after a default notice, three weeks between the sale notice and the auction, and a sale every month. Contact the lender early.

Your options for a quick Pharr sale

For most Pharr owners the choice is a cash buyer or an agent listing. What decides it is the house itself, any liens or tenants, and how fast you need the money.

Prices run modest, with a median home value of $121,900, so a repair bill of a few thousand dollars takes a big slice of the proceeds. Owners of older, damaged or inherited houses often set a direct sale against the cost of fixing up first.

  • Cash sale: deferred repairs, tenants, liens or an open estate.
  • Listing: a move-in ready house and a seller who can wait a few more weeks.
  • With either, insist on price, date and costs in writing.

The Pharr market and who buys

Pharr sits east of McAllen in south central Hidalgo County, with about 80,830 residents on 23.63 square miles. Households are large and incomes modest, which caps what buyers can pay. The Pharr-Reynosa International Bridge supports the job base through trucking, produce and warehousing, and jobs drive housing demand. Workers in those fields may want homes near freight routes, so say so if your house is close to major roads or the bridge approach.

Preparing and pricing the house

Set the price by what Pharr buyers can actually afford. With a $121,900 median value and a $52,814 median household income, price sensitivity is high, so a clean inspection matters more than extras. Fix visible leaks, broken windows and electrical hazards first, since an inspector will find them.

Owner costs explain the caution: $1,403 monthly with a loan, $499 without, and $1,037 for rent. A buyer deciding between renting and buying will compare those numbers, so a house with a low tax bill, a fenced yard and sound air conditioning stands out.

  • Photograph the house in daylight and list the bedroom count first, since households here average 3.36 people.
  • Write the listing in English and Spanish.
  • Mention nearby routes and the commute, which averages 21.1 minutes.

If the house needs more work than you can fund, a direct sale as is avoids repair costs and the wait for a buyer's loan.

Hidalgo County tax rules

Taxes you never paid ride along with the house, because each January 1 a lien attaches. Hidalgo County's tax office will quote a payoff for the closing table.

The bill arrives near October 1. Pay after January 31 and it is delinquent: six percent penalty and one percent interest start on February 1, the penalty keeps growing every month until July 1, and a collection attorney's fee of up to 20 percent may be added.

  • Your own home: $140,000 comes off school district value.
  • Owners who are seniors or disabled: an extra $60,000 and a ceiling on school tax.
  • A veteran with a disability rating gets $5,000 to $12,000 off, and at 100 percent the homestead can be fully exempt.
  • To protest value, file by May 15, or within 30 days of the notice when that is later.

Section 11.22 lets a veteran who missed April 30 apply anyway, for up to five years after the delinquency date.

A short look at how Pharr grew

Henry N. Pharr, a Louisiana sugarcane grower, and John Connally Kelley became co-owners of 16,000 acres in 1909, and the town was laid out in Pharr's name. The sugar plantation failed, yet the irrigation system kept vegetable and cotton farms supplied. Pharr incorporated in 1916, and counts rose from 4,784 in 1940 to 32,921 in 1990 and 70,400 in 2010. The bridge opened in 1994 and made the city a major port of entry.

For a seller the lesson is practical: much of the housing went up in different decades, so the age of your roof, wiring and air conditioning is a fair question from any buyer.

Questions to ask every buyer

Learn which side buys the title policy, how many days closing takes and whether the price can shift after a walkthrough. Request proof of funds, and ask when earnest money is returned.

Be careful with anyone asking for money up front or refusing to write terms down. Mention a tenant, lien or unsettled estate on the first call, since buyers who discover it later tend to drop the offer.

What the bridge means for demand

The international bridge is Hidalgo County's only full-service commercial crossing, with about 175,000 vehicle crossings a month and over 120,000 of them trucks. Pharr ranks third nationally for trade with Mexico after Laredo and El Paso, and first for produce, and more than $41 billion in global trade moves through the crossing.

That freight work supports steady jobs in trucking, storage and customs. It is background, not a promise of rising prices. If a buyer asks about traffic near your street or a planned second span, point them to the city for the current status.

Recording the deed

You sign the deed before a notary, then it is filed with the Hidalgo County Clerk.

The clerk charges $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for later pages, plus county records fees, and a missing grantee address can add $25. Your closing statement carries the final number.

When a family house never had a deed recorded, buyers want stronger proof of ownership. An affidavit of heirship is just a sworn statement that a title company may decline, so some buyers insist on a court order.

Foreclosure or an estate dispute

Count the days first. Receiving a default notice gives you 20 days to make up the arrears. The lender then owes 21 days' notice before it can hold a sale on a first Tuesday.

After a death, a will is normally probated within four years. When the assets come to $75,000 or less, leaving out the homestead, a small estate affidavit may be enough.

  • Obtain the reinstatement figure and sale date from the servicer on paper.
  • Ask the tax office about a payment plan; some collectors spread a homestead's back taxes across as many as 36 months.
  • Check with a Texas attorney or the court clerk about who can sign for the estate.
You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Selling with a lien or loan in default

Owing money against the house does not by itself end a sale. Provided the closing covers it, the title company settles the lien and the loan out of your proceeds. Your check will be smaller, so get a written payoff from the lienholder dated close to closing day.

If you would rather cure a default than sell, ask the servicer what reinstatement costs. Weigh that against what a direct sale would leave you, and decide before the notice period runs out.

From offer to closing

Right after you accept, the title company starts a file, hunts for liens and orders tax figures. Come to the signing with photo ID and every key. The statement shows price, payoffs, prorated taxes and fees, and after the deed is recorded you receive the balance.

Collect proof of funds, the earnest money amount and the closing date from each buyer in writing. A cash purchase skips the lender's appraisal and underwriting, so the date tends to hold. Do not pay anyone merely to receive an offer.

Frequently asked questions

Where is a Pharr house deed filed?

Filing happens at the Hidalgo County Clerk's office. You sign in front of a notary and the title company submits it.

How large are Pharr households?

They average 3.36 people, and there are 23,877 households, so buyers often want three or four bedrooms and room for family.

What happens if the Pharr tax bill is paid late?

Delinquency starts once January 31 passes. February 1 brings a six percent penalty plus one percent interest, and the penalty climbs every month through July 1.

Can I sell a Pharr house with a lien or a loan in default?

Yes, as long as closing covers the payoff. Liens and the loan are paid from your proceeds by the title company, and the servicer can quote a reinstatement figure if you would rather cure the default.

Why does the international bridge matter for Pharr homeowners?

It anchors local logistics jobs. Pharr ranks third nationally for trade with Mexico and sees over 120,000 trucks a month, which sustains work in trucking, produce and warehousing.

Short-term rental rules

The town requires short-term rentals to register through a platform run by GovOS and to collect a 7 percent hotel occupancy tax. Registration opened November 20, 2023, and tax collection began December 1, 2023.

Each month's filing is due on the 15th of the following month, including months when no tax came in. Miss the 25th and a 15 percent penalty applies. Interest of 10 percent per year starts accruing 30 days past the due date. A host who pays on time keeps a 1 percent collection fee.

  • Register on the town's GovOS portal.
  • Send questions to the town's short-term rental email address.
  • Keep receipts and exemption records in case of an audit.

For a house that hosted guests, shut down the account and pay the last month's tax before you sell.

Homestead exemptions and the tax cap

Under state rules every school district grants a $140,000 homestead exemption, with an added $60,000 for owners who are seniors or disabled. Other taxing units may adopt an exemption of their own, capped at a fifth of value and no smaller than $5,000. The appraisal district can tell you which ones your units chose.

A separate limit holds the yearly rise in a homestead's appraised value to 10 percent, beginning the year after the exemption is first granted. Seniors and disabled owners also have a school tax ceiling, and part of that benefit can move with them to a replacement homestead in Texas. If you never claimed it, a buyer who closes after January 1 can typically still receive it for the months left in the year.

Before you list, ask the appraisal district what it has on file for the house. A missing exemption may be worth claiming.

Selling with back taxes

Each January 1 a tax lien attaches to the house and stays with it, so delinquent amounts are paid at or before closing. Delay is expensive, since charges grow during the first half of the year. A balance open on February 1 draws 6 percent plus 1 percent interest per month, and the penalty rises to 12 percent on July 1.

A taxing unit's collection lawyer can add up to a fifth of the tax on top. Owners may request a waiver of penalty and interest in writing. In general that means paying within 21 days after learning of the delinquency and applying before the 181st day. Some collectors offer payment plans of up to 36 months for a residence homestead.

Should the house go to a tax sale, redemption rights vary by property type, and homestead land gets a two-year window. Get a payoff figure from the county tax office in writing before you accept an offer, and pass it to the buyer so it is built into the closing.

When a buyer needs a mortgage, the lender's appraisal, the inspection and the bank's own schedule can each reopen the price. Paying cash takes the bank out of the picture. If your house has deferred repairs, an unclosed rental registration or an open tax balance, that tends to mean fewer surprises between signing and payday.

Certainty costs something, and the price is a lower bid. Request a written net figure from each buyer. Then set it next to what a listing would leave after commission, repairs, and the extra months of mortgage, utilities and tax.

What to expect from buyers

Different buyers ask for different things.

  • Buyers with loans want an appraisal, an inspection and repair credits.
  • Cash buyers ask only for access and a clean title.
  • Any buyer will ask for school boundaries and the age of the roof.

With any offer, go through the settlement statement one line at a time. An amount you cannot place is worth a phone call to the closing office, because mistakes are cheapest to fix before money moves. Request the final figures a day or two early and hold them against the contract. When a buyer wants the appliances, curtains or a backyard shed left behind, put it in writing in the contract itself, and keep a signed copy.

Recording the sale

Your closing office can tell you which county clerk handles the parcel. That clerk keeps the liens and releases a title search turns up, and files the new deed once a notary has acknowledged the signature. Fees are set by the clerk, so ask for a quote before closing day.

Before you sign, confirm that the loan payoff, the current year's tax share and any short-term rental tax account are all settled on the closing statement. Keep a copy of every recorded document, and store them with your tax records in case a question comes up later, and store them somewhere you can find them easily.

  2. Close out any rental registration.
  3. Sign before a notary, with photo identification for every owner on the deed.
  4. Collect your copies after recording.

Buyers tend to be well informed. With a $166,219 median household income and 65.2 percent of homes valued at $500,000 or more, pricing and condition decide how quickly a house sells.

Yes. Short-term rentals register through the town's GovOS portal and remit a 7 percent hotel occupancy tax, with returns due on the 15th of the following month.

Lewisville ISD and Argyle ISD serve most of the town, with Denton, Grapevine-Colleyville and Northwest ISDs covering small areas.

Late charges begin on February 1 and step up on July 1. A collection attorney's fee can then be added.

Can I keep my homestead exemption when I sell?

It stays with you only while you live there. A buyer applies for their own after closing and may get it for the rest of that tax year if the prior owner did not receive it.

Ways to sell a Cedar Park house

Three Cedar Park items come up in nearly every sale: the permit record, any short-term rental registration, and the tax account.

Cedar Park in brief

Cedar Park is a Williamson County city that grew from a ranch settlement into an Austin suburb and incorporated in 1973. Its economic development group calls it the third largest city in the Austin metro. Most sale questions here concern current permits, registrations and tax accounts rather than old title tangles.

Which appraisal district and tax office apply?

Your latest tax statement names the county and the appraisal district that carry your parcel. Cedar Park is part of Williamson County, whose Central Appraisal District values property there.

Texas levies no state property tax, so each local unit sets its own rate. Value is set on January 1, the year's lien attaches that day, and bills follow in October. Tax unpaid after January 31 turns delinquent on February 1, and penalty and interest begin to build. For current rates, call the Williamson County tax office and ask for each unit's rate on your bill.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Cedar Park house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Homestead exemption and the 10 percent cap

Cedar Park homeowners get a brake on rising assessments, and it stays with the owner, not the house. Williamson CAD says a home qualifies in the second full year the exemption has been on the property for the same owner. After that, increases in existing assessed value are held to 10 percent a year even when market value climbs faster.

The cap doesn't transfer with ownership, so a buyer starts fresh and may see a bigger jump than you did. Tell a buyer to budget for that jump. Other points from the district:

  • You apply once, and the exemption stays unless you move or add another one.
  • A Texas driver license or ID showing your current address is required.
  • Processing can take up to 90 days.
  • The chief appraiser re-checks each homestead exemption within every five tax years.

Short-term rental registration

If your Cedar Park house is rented for stays of 30 consecutive days or fewer, the city's April 2026 ordinance applies. Registration is required, costs $100 a year, and ties into Hotel Occupancy Tax reporting under Chapter 10 of the City Code. The city estimates about 200 active short-term rentals.

A buyer who plans to keep renting will ask whether the registration exists and whether tax was remitted. Development Services at 512-401-5100 handles registration, and Utility Billing at 512-401-5300 handles hotel tax payments. Registered owners can watch remittance through an online portal. Gather the confirmation and remittance history before you list, since a rental buyer asks for them first.

Permits and repairs to check before you sell

Open permits are a common reason a Cedar Park closing pauses. The city runs permits through the MGO Connect portal, and Development Services is at the City Hall campus, 450 Cypress Creek Road, Building 1. Its zoning map tool, CPAtlas, lets you type in an address to see zoning.

  • Inheritance: a will can be probated for four years after death, and the small estate affidavit tops out at $75,000 excluding homestead and exempt property.
  • Tenant: a landlord normally gives 3 days of written notice to vacate before filing in justice court, unless the lease sets another period.

A buyer can take on these issues, but the title company still needs proof of who may sign. A Williamson County probate attorney can say which paper fits. If more than one of these applies, tell every buyer at the start, so nobody is surprised once the title search is under way.

The city says the registration lets it count and locate short-term rentals, support safety, and make sure hotel tax is collected. For you as a seller that translates into a paper trail. A buyer who reviews your account will see whether the house was registered, whether hotel tax was remitted and when. Missing months are easier to fix before a contract than during one, so check the portal now rather than after you have an offer.

How an open permit slows a closing

A title company or a buyer's inspector who finds an unfinished project, such as a deck, a water heater swap or a remodel, will ask whether it was permitted and closed. The permit record answers that. If the permit shows work that never started or that stopped, it may lapse after 180 days, and getting it reopened takes a request by email with the project status. Printing the inspection notes from the portal gives the buyer a clear picture, and the cash buyer can then decide what to do about anything left open.

An owner who pulled a permit without a contractor should be able to show the homeowner affidavit and proof of homestead that the city required. Keep those with the rest of the closing folder.

Five checks to run first

Do these in order and you will know which sale routes are open.

  • Pull the tax statement and confirm the district and any balance.
  • Ask Development Services whether any permit on the address is open.
  • Get your mortgage payoff figure.
  • If the house was a short-term rental, collect registration and hotel tax records.
  • Name your deadline, such as a sale date or a move, and tell every buyer about it.

Frequently asked questions

Can I sell my Cedar Park house with an open building permit?

Yes, though it complicates the sale. A permit lapses after 180 days without a start or with work stopped. Call Development Services at 512-401-5100 about the record, or sell to a buyer willing to take the open item.

Must my Cedar Park short-term rental be registered before a sale?

If guests stay 30 days or fewer, registration is required at $100 a year. A buyer planning to keep renting will want the registration and your hotel occupancy tax records.

Does my homestead tax cap pass to the buyer?

No. Williamson CAD says the cap does not transfer with ownership. The new owner applies for an exemption of their own, and the cap counts from their first full year.

When do Texas property taxes become delinquent?

Tax unpaid after January 31 is delinquent on February 1. Call the Williamson County tax office for the exact balance on your account.

What does the Texas foreclosure timeline look like?

A default notice starts a 20-day reinstatement window. The lender then gives notice of sale, and the auction happens at the courthouse on a first Tuesday.

Fastest way to sell in San Marcos

Selling for cash, with the house left as is, tends to wrap up first. No mortgage approval, no appraiser and no repair negotiation stand in the way. A listing might net more, though it demands prep work, showings and patience.

San Marcos is the Hays County seat, about 25 miles south of Austin on Interstate 35. Part of the city also falls in Guadalupe County, so check which appraisal district covers your lot before you read a tax statement.

Ask every buyer for a written offer, then set each one next to an agent's estimate of your take-home. The gap between the two is what speed costs you.

Housing market snapshot

San Marcos leans toward renting. Owner occupancy runs 30.8 percent, the median value of an owned home is $310,400, and median gross rent is $1,322. The population estimate is 77,830, up 14.9 percent from the 2020 base.

Monthly owner costs average $1,899 with a mortgage and $706 without one. Because so many households rent, investors make up a big share of buyers for older or rougher houses. If your roof is tired or the foundation is a worry, those buyers may price the work more calmly than a first time owner would. The housing stock is mixed, from older homes near downtown to newer construction on the edges, so describe your house's age, systems and lot clearly when you talk to buyers.

Demand rises and falls with the school calendar and with hiring in Austin. Houses near campus appeal to a different crowd than houses near the highway, and buyers watch monthly cost closely. A home with working systems and few surprises is easier to move than one that looks cheap but needs work.

Rental registration and city rules

The city regulates rentals closely. Code Compliance requires owners of short term and long term rentals to register under city ordinances, and its officers cover more than 30 square miles. Before you commit to a closing date, verify that your rental registration is current. Code questions go to 512-393-8479.

San Marcos ISD is among the school districts listed by the Guadalupe Appraisal District, so it applies to parcels on that side of the county line. Hays County parcels use the Hays Central Appraisal District. Your bill shows which units tax you.

Checking or contesting your Hays County value

Start with the Hays Central Appraisal District's property search and interactive map. Its online forms cover homestead filings, agricultural use applications, business personal property renditions and change of address requests. Its office, at 21001 North IH 35 in Kyle, has a drop box by the front door.

Staff answer (512) 268-2522 and see visitors 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. on weekdays. After August 7 of each year, Texas.gov/PropertyTaxes links to a local database showing the tax each unit would levy under its proposed rate, and owners can subscribe to alerts there.

The district also appraises through the year. Staff walk neighborhoods and commercial areas to measure new construction and update property details, so an addition you built without telling anyone can surface in your value. Make sure your records match the house a buyer will see.

Property taxes for a San Marcos seller

The Hays Central Appraisal District sets values and exemptions but sends no bills and takes no payments. Billing belongs to the Hays County Tax Office, which has no say over values. Texas collects no state property tax, so these dates apply to local units only.

Getting ready to list

Missing paperwork causes most delays. Find your deed and your latest tax bill, and look up your parcel on the district's search and interactive map to see what the district has on file. If you disagree with the appraised value

Protests go to the review board, and the usual window runs to mid May. File through the district's online forms or bring your paperwork to the office in Kyle. Gather what you have on condition: repair estimates, photos and any receipts. A worn roof or a settling foundation is the kind of detail a board member can actually act on. A lower value also gives a buyer a lower starting tax estimate.

Pricing for the San Marcos buyer pool

Think about who is likely to walk through your door. A household renting at $1,322 a month compares that figure with a mortgage payment, and the $1,899 average for owners with a loan is the number in their heads. An investor looks at the same house and sees rent potential near campus or along the Interstate 35 corridor. Describe the roof, foundation and systems plainly, and let buyers price the work themselves. Hays County and Guadalupe County parcels run on different appraisal districts, so confirm yours first and quote the right tax figure.

Your homestead exemption when you sell

The exemption ends the day you move out. Where you had none, whoever buys after January 1 can claim one for what remains of the year. Let Hays CAD know you left, and ask the title company how the year's tax gets divided with the buyer.

Deeds and inherited houses

Whichever county holds the land, its clerk records the deed. A notary or similar officer must witness the signature first. Recording runs $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for every page after it.

A house passed to an heir needs matching paperwork, such as an executor's deed, a will plus court order, or a death affidavit under a transfer on death deed. Your title company can tell you what a particular buyer will insist on.

Questions to ask before you sign

Before any San Marcos contract goes out, run through a short list with the buyer. Who orders the title search, and who pays for it? Does the offer assume the roof and foundation stay as they are? What happens if the title company finds a lien or an unpaid tax balance? When is the money wired? A buyer who answers each point in writing is easier to trust than one who promises a fast close and leaves the details open. If the house has tenants or a rental registration, add them to the list so nothing surprises you on closing day.

Lenders, tenants and repair problems

Texas foreclosures are mostly nonjudicial and end in a public auction, so a private sale before that date can protect equity. To remove a tenant, the landlord needs written notice and a justice court order, though some buyers will take the lease as is.

Repairs are the easiest problem to hand off. An as is purchase moves the roof, plumbing and cosmetic work, and the contractor bids, to the buyer.

What a cash closing looks like

After you accept, the title company starts a file and looks for liens, unpaid taxes and probate problems. Then you agree on a date and sign at its office. Bring photo ID, plus the deed or the estate papers. Any lien, tax balance or probate step can stretch the schedule, so ask the buyer to put the date in writing and decide who pays title and recording costs before signing.

Must I fix San Marcos repairs before selling?

No. An investor can buy the house in its current shape. You weigh that offer against a repaired listing.

Which office mails the tax bill for a San Marcos home?

It comes from the county tax office for the county that holds the parcel. For Hays County parcels that is the Hays County Tax Office, while the appraisal district only sets values and exemptions.

Does a San Marcos rental need registration?

Yes. Code Compliance requires short term and long term rental owners to register under city ordinances. Confirm yours before a closing.

How long will a cash sale take in San Marcos?

The timeline depends on title work and the buyer, so ask for a closing date on paper. Probate, liens or unpaid taxes can add time.

Does my homestead exemption move with me?

No. It ends at the move. If you had no exemption, whoever buys after January 1 may claim it for the rest of that year. Tell Hays CAD you left.

  • Foundation or roof problems serious enough to frighten off mortgage buyers.

Missouri City and the county line

Missouri City sits about twenty miles southwest of downtown Houston along U.S. Highway 90A and State Highway 6, in northeast Fort Bend County and southwest Harris County. Houston is where most residents work, and Fort Bend Independent School District runs the schools.

Two counties means two sets of offices, and the county line decides which appraisal district and tax office keep your records. Tax pictures differ between an older street, a newer subdivision and a lot inside a municipal utility district, so give buyers your exact address when asking for an offer.

Street reconstruction and drainage projects are underway in several neighborhoods. Should your street be on the list, ask the city for the schedule, since buyers notice torn-up roads.

For fiscal 2027 the City Council set the rate at $0.578363 per $100 of taxable value, compared with $0.570825 before. Debt service accounts for the rise, while maintenance and operations stayed flat.

It is only the city's slice. The county, school district and other districts set their own rates, which makes your total bill larger.

Who appraises and bills my property?

The answer follows the county. A Fort Bend parcel is handled by the Fort Bend Central Appraisal District, and a Harris County parcel by the Harris County Appraisal District.

January 1 sets values and starts the year's tax lien, so the tax stays with the property through a sale. A protest of value is usually due by mid-May.

Delinquent taxes and foreclosure

Waiting is expensive either way. A tax bill goes delinquent after January 31, February 1 adds a six percent penalty plus one percent interest, and interest of one percent accrues monthly from there.

After a default notice you get 20 days to get current. Failing that, the lender posts notice three weeks ahead of an auction on a first Tuesday. If a cash sale closes before then, the equity is yours and no foreclosure appears on your record.

Whatever you owe in taxes and loan principal is subtracted from your check, so get exact payoff amounts from the escrow officer before accepting a number.

Putting the house on the market means commissions, repairs, holding costs and waiting. A cash buyer mostly costs you a slice of the price. Condition and deadline decide which makes more sense for you.

Selling a rented or inherited house

Either one adds a hurdle before the keys change hands. A tenant is removed by notice to vacate and, when needed, justice court. A house left under a will may require probate, and the will must be offered within four years of the death.

  • Small estate: an affidavit covers estates up to $75,000 not counting the homestead, subject to court approval.
  • Nothing filed yet: an affidavit of heirship is just a sworn statement, and buyers may refuse it.

With no estate opened, consult a Texas attorney before signing.

Utility districts and your closing numbers

If your lot lies inside a municipal utility district or a public improvement district, the bill carries extra lines that the main city and county rates do not show. Those districts set their own charges, so two neighbors on different streets can pay noticeably different totals.

Buyers in this market tend to ask about the all-in figure, so open your statement before you list and write down each line. A clear answer about what the property owes, and to whom, takes a question off the table early. It also helps the title company, which has to confirm every taxing unit before it can promise a clean closing.

Steps from offer to closing

Once you accept, a title company starts a file and combs county records for liens, tax balances and holes in ownership. A buyer who borrows must also get an appraisal and loan approval, and either one can shift the price. Cash buyers dodge both hurdles, which explains the faster closings.

You will have homework too: proof of identity, the deed and a payoff letter. Before you sign, the title company should send a closing statement for you to read through.

What to have ready for the title company

Locate this year's tax statement before anything else, since it names the county and districts that bill you. Next come the deed, a loan payoff letter and, for a rental, the lease. If a county line or utility district complicates matters, flag it for the title company immediately so the search covers every office involved.

You sign in front of a notary, and the deed is sent to the clerk in the parcel's county. Taxes and loans owed are paid from the sale funds, and you keep the remainder. A cash sale follows the very same path minus the buyer's loan approval.

How fast can a Missouri City house close for cash?

Often within a few weeks, because there is no lender underwriting. The real pace depends on title work, a Fort Bend or Harris County lien search, and whether you need extra time to move. Ask for a closing date in writing.

Your address decides. Missouri City spans Fort Bend and Harris counties, so the appraisal district and tax office are Fort Bend's or Harris County's depending on the parcel. Look at your tax bill to see which one applies.

The council adopted $0.578363 per $100 of taxable value for fiscal 2027. That is the city's portion only and excludes county, school and district rates.

Do I owe taxes if I sell partway through the year?

The tax lien attaches on January 1, so the year's bill belongs to the property and gets settled at closing. The title company usually prorates it between buyer and seller. Check the settlement statement line by line.

Where can I find my Missouri City property's tax breakdown?

Look at the unit rates, then ask your county appraisal district for your parcel's value and exemptions. The Fort Bend tax office branch on Texas Parkway can answer billing questions by phone.

Ways to sell quickly in Harlingen

An agent, a do-it-yourself sale and a cash purchase are the three roads. Harlingen held nearly level between the 2020 count of 71,879 and the 2025 estimate of 72,467, up just 0.8%, so buyers are present but not scrambling.

When a market grows this slowly, a house priced far above its neighbors can linger for months. If time matters more than the last dollar, compare a written cash proposal with what a listing would clear once commission, upkeep and repairs are paid. Pick whichever matches your calendar.

  • Broker listing: suits a refreshed house and an owner with time.

Harlingen housing numbers

Over half of residents, 52.4%, speak another language at home. Request contract and closing documents in a form you read easily, and bring a trusted person to the signing if it helps.

How Harlingen grew

The town was founded in 1904 on the north bank of the Arroyo Colorado, and it incorporated on April 15, 1910, with 1,126 residents. It grew as a shipping and distribution hub where U.S. highways 77 and 83 meet in northwestern Cameron County. Wartime installations lifted the population from 23,000 in 1950 to 41,000 in 1960, and after Harlingen Air Force Base shut in 1962, local leaders bought and reused the base and its housing.

That mix of old neighborhoods and base-era housing means house ages vary widely. Say when yours was built and what you have updated, since buyers compare against nearby homes of the same era. A copy of any past repair invoices, a roof or air conditioning warranty, and a recent utility bill help a buyer judge the upkeep costs without guessing.

Who buys a Harlingen house

Local families and retirees fill most of the buyer pool. With children at 28.8% of residents and seniors at 16.4%, buyers often look for a one-story plan, a fenced yard and a quick route to the highways where U.S. 77 and 83 meet.

Some buyers are landlords, with median gross rent at $928 a month. For a rental, expect requests for the lease, the payment history and a list of deposits you hold. Health care and education jobs nearby bring tenants and buyers who want a short commute.

Who does what on property tax

Two separate Cameron County offices handle your taxes. Values and exemptions belong to the Cameron Appraisal District. Bills come from the Cameron County Tax Office, located across the highway in San Benito. People often confuse the two, but the appraisal district neither collects taxes nor holds tax amounts.

A school-district homestead exemption goes to anyone who lives in the house, with more for seniors and disabled owners. Those owners also receive a school tax cap that may travel to another Texas home. A disabled veteran's exemption rises with the VA rating, and at 100% the homestead's taxable value can drop to nothing.

  • Apply through the appraisal district, normally before May 1, though some veteran claims get longer windows.
  • Older and disabled owners may pay in installments, starting with a February 1 payment.
  • A buyer who takes the house after January 1 can still apply for the rest of that year, even if the seller never claimed the exemption.

Before closing, get a balance statement from the tax office and ask the appraisal district what recording the deed does to your exemptions.

When mortgage payments stop

Lenders in Texas seldom go to court, relying on the power of sale in the deed of trust. After a default notice, the borrower has 20 days to cure the arrears. The lender must then post and file a notice of sale at least 21 days before the auction.

Auctions run on a month's first Tuesday at a location the commissioners court designates, here in Cameron County. A sale before that day lets you pick your buyer and date. After the auction the lender has two years to sue for a shortfall, while the borrower may request credit at fair market value. Surplus cash goes to junior lienholders, then to the former owner.

A federal rule normally makes a lender wait until a loan is over 120 days behind. The window is short, so phone your servicer early and ask about loss mitigation.

Deed copies and inherited houses

Ask the Cameron County Clerk in Brownsville for deed copies and subdivision plats. The appraisal district keeps neither.

An heir who sells an inherited Harlingen house must prove ownership in a form a title company accepts. The usual proofs are an executor's deed after administration, a court order paired with the will (a muniment of title), and an affidavit of heirship placed in the public record. No judge reviews that affidavit, and a buyer or title insurer may refuse it, so learn early what the title company will take.

Collect papers right away, because these filings control how soon a sale can close.

  • The recorded deed, or the volume and page where it was filed.
  • The death certificate, after a death.
  • The latest tax statement from the Cameron County Tax Office.
  • The lease, where a tenant lives there.
  • Payoff letters from every lender with a lien.

Giving a buyer this folder up front tends to shorten the title search and head off late surprises.

From signed contract to funded closing

Once the contract is signed, a title company opens a file and orders the search. Payoff letters are requested from each lender, the tax account is checked, and a deed and settlement statement are drafted.

Read the statement before closing day and question anything unfamiliar. At closing you sign in front of a notary, the deed is recorded, and what remains after payoffs and charges comes to you. Without a loan approval or lender appraisal, a cash closing date holds more easily, although a slow title search or an extra lien can stretch it. Mention any tenant to the buyer and plan your move so the house is empty when the keys change hands. Cancel automatic payments tied to the property, such as lawn service, after closing and not before.

Frequently asked questions

How quickly could a Harlingen cash sale close?

In many cases within a couple of weeks, because no lender has to approve a loan or order an appraisal. A slow title search or an extra lien can stretch that, so get the target date written down.

Does the Cameron Appraisal District send my tax bill?

Housing stock and what buyers see

The city started in 1950 when a farm became a residential development, and voters incorporated it on April 25, 1953. Growth came fast: roughly 7,000 people in 1958, 38,959 in 1990, 55,635 in 2000. More than 70,000 live here today, so this is a dense, settled place.

Given that timeline, a large share of the houses date from the 1960s through the 1990s. Original roofs, plumbing and foundations come up in nearly every inspection. Selling to someone who accepts the house untouched means the repair list never has to be written.

A listing can lean on the parks, trails and water park, and an investor notices the same pull. Highway access and drive time often decide whether a commuting family looks twice at your street.

When those are in hand, buyers can commit to a firm figure in writing and you can test it against what a listing would realistically net.

Find out what each bidder plans to do with the place. Someone intending to renovate and resell, rent the place out, or move in takes on a different amount of repair risk, and that difference lands in the price.

After you accept, the title company hunts for liens, confirms the tax balance and books a signing. Payoffs are deducted from your proceeds and you collect what remains. If a lien or an unknown heir surfaces, expect the date to slide and get the revised timeline in writing.

Do not send money to anyone just to get an offer. Judge each one by what you would walk away with, not the headline price.

Come with photo ID, keys, garage openers and any gate or alarm codes. Read the settlement statement line by line before signing: it lists the buyer's price, your payoffs, the tax share and any fees. Anything unfamiliar is worth a question on the spot.

Several weeks is typical once title is clean. Liens, tenants and unsettled estates push it out, so name a target date in the offer.

Not for a cash buyer, who accepts the house in its present state and prices the work. Set the offer against a repaired-listing estimate before deciding.

How fast can a Kyle house sell?

Kyle sits in northeastern Hays County on Interstate 35, between Austin to the north and San Marcos to the south. Commuters along that corridor make up much of the buyer pool, and a fairly priced house with clear title tends to draw interest. Deferred maintenance, tenant trouble or an unpaid lien shrinks the pool.

Old blocks, new subdivisions

In 1880 two landowners deeded 200 acres to the railroad for a Kyle townsite, and the town incorporated in 1928. Blocks near the old depot sit beside newer subdivisions, so houses of very different ages are for sale at once.

Shoppers for older homes quiz you on foundations, drainage and electrical updates; shoppers for newer ones ask about HOA rules and school zones. Kyle belongs to Hays Consolidated Independent School District, so ask the district which campus your street feeds before you list. Survey, plat and deed restriction papers belong in a folder, since written answers cut the back and forth that stalls contracts.

How the Hays County tax cycle affects a sale

Kyle taxes come as one annual bill, and the lien attaches on January 1, which means you owe a share whenever the sale closes. The Hays County Tax Office gets the certified roll from the Hays Central Appraisal District and mails statements in October.

A balance still open the next February 1 starts accruing penalty and interest, and anything unpaid by July 1 can gain as much as 15 percent for collection costs. At closing the title company divides the current year, and it deducts any back taxes from what you receive. Request a payoff figure early.

Homestead exemptions and what a buyer pays

Because a homestead exemption cuts the taxable value of a main residence, the buyer's first bill depends on whether it stays. School districts take $140,000 off, and a city, county or other unit may add a percentage exemption of its own.

  • The owner lives in the house as a main residence and holds no second homestead.

An online Citizen Self-Service portal handles Kyle building permits, inspections and plan submittals, so you can apply and pay without a trip to City Hall. Pre-sale repairs often need a permit, and work done without one is a frequent snag when a buyer's inspector walks the property.

General questions go to the city's 3-1-1 line on weekdays in business hours, and the planning office answers at 512-262-1010. Filing the deed in Hays County

A Kyle deed is recorded at the Hays County Clerk's office, because Texas files deeds in the county where the land lies. Before the clerk accepts it, a notary must take the signer's acknowledgment, or two subscribing witnesses must swear to it.

The state's schedule is $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for later pages, with other clerk fees added. The title company files for you in most sales. For a direct family transfer, ask the clerk what the current fee list says.

Steps that move a Kyle sale forward

  • Choose between repairing, selling as is and pricing for a renovator.
  • Collect permits plus any HOA or deed restriction papers.

What to expect once you accept an offer

Once you accept, the title company opens a file, orders the tax certificate and a lien search, and sets the signing. A borrowing buyer faces an appraisal and lender conditions that can shift the date, while a cash buyer usually closes sooner. Either way, the settlement statement shows how the year's property tax was split, what was paid off and what you receive. Ask for it a day early and question anything unfamiliar. Choosing between a builder, an investor and a retail buyer

Each kind of buyer asks different questions. A family buying to live in the house wants the school zone, the HOA rules and a clean inspection. An investor wants a price that leaves room for repairs and will accept dated finishes. A builder looking at a larger tract starts with zoning and plat status, then the cost of getting utilities and roads in place.

Knowing which buyer fits your house saves months. A tidy house near a good school zone belongs on the market. A worn house with a tenant or an old roof may suit an investor, and a cash offer there can close without a single repair request. If you are unsure, take one cash offer and one listing opinion, then compare what each leaves you after costs.

What a cash sale lets you skip

A cash buyer in Kyle normally skips the lender appraisal, which removes a common cause of delay and a surprise price cut. The buyer also takes the house with its flaws, so there is no repair negotiation after inspection. Showings shrink to one or two visits instead of weekends of open houses. What you still do is sign before a notary, clear any lien and settle taxes through the title company. Do I owe property taxes at closing in Kyle?

Yes, for the part of the year you owned the house. Bills go out in October, and the title company usually prorates the year and pays any past-due balance from your proceeds.

When do Kyle property taxes become delinquent?

Once January 31 passes. Penalty and interest start on February 1, and unpaid taxes on July 1 can carry up to 15 percent more for collection costs.

Can I protest my Kyle appraisal before selling?

Yes. File with the appraisal review board by May 15, or by a month after your notice if that date falls later.

Where is a Kyle house deed filed?

At the Hays County Clerk. The signature needs a notary's acknowledgment, or two subscribing witnesses' oath, first.

Does a homestead exemption transfer to the buyer in Kyle?

Not automatically. If the seller never had one, a buyer closing after January 1 may request it for the rest of that year, then applies in person by April 30 for later years.

Rowlett requires annual registration of single-family houses and duplexes used as rentals, and an inspection applies when tenants change. A buyer may ask whether a former rental is registered and current.

  • Annual registration is $50.00 per property.
  • An inspection is required at each tenant change, and the new tenant cannot move in until it passes. The inspection fee is $75.00.
  • If a tenant moves in before approval, the owner is charged $200.00.
  • The water utility account must be current, and a floor plan is required with the application.

Short-term rentals face tighter rules. The city adopted a short-term rental ordinance in April 2025, with a $2,000 annual application fee and permits that expire January 31. A 1,000-foot separation requirement applies to short-term rentals, applications are first-come, and owners must file hotel occupancy tax quarterly, including zero filings. Platforms like Airbnb and VRBO do not collect or remit that tax for Rowlett.

An owner running a short-term rental should tell buyers about the permit status, because the permit is tied to the owner and the property.

Short-term rental permit conditions

Anyone planning to keep the house as a short-term rental should read the conditions before making an offer. Only online applications are accepted, and the city partners with an outside platform to administer permits and hotel tax.

  • A designated local contact who is reachable 24 hours a day.
  • Notice to all residential properties within 200 feet.
  • A site plan, floor plan, parking plan and emergency evacuation plan.
  • A guest safety sheet displayed inside, and signage on the exterior near the front door.
  • A city inspection approved before anyone occupies the property, with short-term rentals inspected quarterly through the MyGov portal.
  • Current hotel occupancy tax filings.

A separate 1,000-foot rule bars renting to a registered sex offender within 1,000 feet of places where children commonly gather, and it applies to both short and long-term rentals. Complaints about a short-term rental can be made by phone or online through the platform the city names.

Property taxes split between two counties

Because Rowlett lies in Dallas and Rockwall Counties, a house is appraised by Dallas Central Appraisal District or Rockwall Central Appraisal District, depending on location. Check your tax statement to see which district and which county tax office applies.

Dallas CAD lets a homeowner who moves away temporarily keep the exemption if no other principal residence is set up and a return is planned within two years, with longer allowed for military service abroad or a care facility stay.

Dallas CAD also explains a tax deferral for owners who qualify by age or disability. Payment of taxes is postponed while you own and live in the home, but the tax is not cancelled, and five percent interest accrues each year. When the property is sold or transferred to an estate or heirs, the taxes and interest become due. Raise this with the title company, since it will be paid from proceeds.

Texas uses one calendar for every city: appraisals are as of January 1, bills go out around October 1, and tax unpaid after January 31 is delinquent.

Applying for a Dallas CAD homestead exemption

The applicant has to own and occupy the home on January 1 of the application year, and Dallas CAD asks for a copy of a Texas driver's license or ID whose address matches the homestead address. A buyer should know that the ID address must be changed at a state driver license office after closing.

  • A single or married owner may be able to apply online.
  • Each individual owner who lives there, apart from married couples, completes a separate application, and the exemption is split by percent of ownership.
  • Any rented or non-homestead part of the property, such as a room over a garage, must be listed by square footage.
  • For a house inherited without a recorded deed in the heir's name, the heir supplies an affidavit, the owner's death certificate, a recent utility bill and any court record citation.

Filing a homestead application is free. False statements or claiming homestead on more than one property is a crime under the Penal Code.

Permits before listing in Rowlett

A permit is not needed for a sale, but past work should have been permitted. Rowlett runs an online permitting system for permit applications and contractor registrations. Ask the city's building safety staff if you are unsure about work done on your house.

Foreclosure or an inherited Rowlett house

In either case, call a title company early. A lender's foreclosure sale is set for a first Tuesday after a notice period. An estate needs the right deed or court order recorded with the clerk of the county that holds the land, either Dallas or Rockwall.

For a house you are selling after a death or while behind on payments, the buyer will want paper that shows who may sign the deed. Ask the title company what it will require, and have the water account, any rental registration and a tax statement ready before you list.

Frequently asked questions

Which county records my Rowlett deed?

Whichever county holds the land. Most of Rowlett is in Dallas County and a western part is in Rockwall County, with Dalrock Road as the dividing line, so check your tax statement.

Do I have to register a rental house before selling it?

Rowlett requires annual registration of rental single-family houses and duplexes, at $50.00 per property. If the house is currently rented, ask the city whether registration is current before you list.

Is a short-term rental permit transferable to a buyer?

Ask the city before you promise anything. The permit is tied to the owner and the property, with a January 31 expiration and a 1,000-foot separation rule.

Can I postpone property tax and still sell?

Yes, if you qualify for the deferral that Dallas CAD describes for older or disabled owners. The postponed tax plus five percent annual interest comes due when the home is sold.

How long does a Rowlett cash sale take?

Timing depends on how fast title is cleared and the deed recorded. Liens, an unpaid rental registration or an inherited title can lengthen it.
