Offices and phone numbers

Keep two addresses handy. For questions about the value on your parcel, the appraisal district is at 205 N Travis Street, phone 903-893-9673. For the bill itself, including what you owe and how to pay, the tax assessor-collector sits at 100 W Houston, phone 903-892-8297. Send an inquiry about a blighted structure to Neighborhood Services at the city. When a title company asks for a tax certificate or payoff, it will contact the second office, so a call from you ahead of time speeds things along.

Pricing against the Sherman market

Grayson County values and sold prices tell different stories. The appraisal district gives you a tax figure, and the district's database lets you compare nearby streets. What buyers pay depends on condition, timing and who is across the table. For a house that needs a roof or foundation work, a cash investor will subtract the cost and risk from the bid. For a house with updates and records, an agent listing may reach buyers who value the work. Both routes work. Pick the one that suits your timeline and the effort you can give it.

Selling a blighted house

Even a rundown house can sell, though you should call the city first. The Quality Neighborhoods Program in Sherman goes after blight and decay, taking down substandard structures with the owner's consent or under a court order.

Open city notices against the house should be cleared or disclosed before you list, since a lender may refuse a loan on a structure with violations. A cash buyer might accept the condition, with the bid reflecting repair or demolition costs. Questions about a particular property go to Neighborhood Services.

Deed paperwork

Grayson County's clerk keeps the record of every Sherman deed. Your signature must first be acknowledged in front of a notary or another officer with that authority.

Fees follow a statewide schedule with a flat charge for page one, a smaller one for later pages and some records charges. The title company will quote the total.

Selling with a tenant

Unless the lease or the law lets you end it, a lease keeps running, so a buyer may purchase with the tenant in place. Texas removal of a tenant opens with a written notice to vacate. Three days is the norm when the lease is silent. After that, the matter goes to justice court.

  • Service on the tenant must happen no later than four days before trial.
  • County court appeals have to be filed inside five days after judgment.
  • A writ of possession is available once six days have run from final judgment.

An investor can build those timelines into the plan. A buyer who intends to live in the house will usually expect the keys at closing.

Inheritance and foreclosure

Heirs have up to four years after a death to offer a Texas will for probate. If the estate owes nothing besides liens, a muniment of title may let them prove ownership without a full administration. Smaller estates, up to $75,000 excluding the homestead and exempt property, can use a small estate affidavit.

Auctions are held on a month's first Tuesday, following at least 21 days' notice. Within 20 days of the default notice, the borrower may reinstate by paying what is behind. A sale before auction day can keep your equity intact.

Frequently asked questions

Which county contains Sherman?

Grayson County, where Sherman is the seat. Valuation is the appraisal district's job, and the tax assessor-collector mails the bills.

What city tax rate did Sherman adopt in 2025?

The city lists $0.508000 per $100 of assessed value, adopted September 2, 2025. For your current bill, check with the Grayson County tax office.

Do unpaid taxes stop a sale?

No, though the lien stays with the house. The balance plus penalties and interest gets paid at or before closing, and you will see the amount on the settlement statement.

Could the city's blight program touch my house?

It can, if the structure is substandard. Removal happens by consent or court order, and Neighborhood Services can answer questions about a particular address.

How fast can a Sherman house close?

A cash deal skips loan underwriting, so it can finish sooner than a financed one. Title work, probate or lien payoffs can still set the schedule, so ask for proof of funds and a firm date on paper.

Put a written cash offer next to the net from a listing: agent fees, repair bills and several months of upkeep come off that side. A job move, an estate, a troublesome tenant or a growing tax balance all push the math toward a quick sale.

If you plan to keep living in the house for a few weeks after the sale, say so at the start and ask for it in the contract.

Location and local character

Grapevine sits along State Highways 114 and 121 at the northeastern edge of Tarrant County, with small sections reaching into Dallas and Denton counties. Grapevine Lake extends north into Denton County, and the airport next door has driven growth since the 1960s. The Grapevine-Colleyville Independent School District serves most of the city, so ask the school office which district your exact address belongs to.

Tourism adds to the town's profile. A convention center opened in 1988, Grapevine Mills in 1997, and TEXRail commuter service from Fort Worth reached the Grapevine station in January 2019. How close your house is to the runways, the lake and Main Street will color how buyers see it. Preservation rules apply in and around the historic downtown, and buyers may ask about them, so find out from the city whether your address is in a designated district.

What a buyer's inspector will look at

Houses near the downtown commercial district, where brick buildings date to the 1880s and 1890s, can need foundation, wiring and roof work before a lender will approve a financed buyer. Newer neighborhoods followed the 1960s airport decision.

A short trip to the TEXRail station is worth a mention in any listing. Population rose from 42,059 in 2000 to an estimated 56,753 in 2020, so current owners bought at many different points, and each one's loan balance and equity will differ.

  • Document recent roof, HVAC and plumbing work.

Short-term rental rules

Grapevine bans them in single-family homes. The city expressly forbids stays under 30 days in residential zoning districts, calls them never a permitted use, and applies the ban to an owner's own primary residence. Non-residential short-term rentals are forbidden too.

One opening exists for multifamily. A January 16, 2024 amendment lets multifamily developments in the R-MF and R-MF-2 districts apply to the City Council for a conditional use, then obtain a permit once the units pass inspection. Some operators that predate the September 4, 2018 ordinance run under a court restraining order while that ordinance is challenged.

Appraisal district and tax calendar

Most Grapevine parcels fall under the Tarrant Appraisal District, which handles appraisals and exemptions across seventy-three taxing units. The pieces of the city in Dallas and Denton counties answer to those counties instead, so read the header of your tax statement.

January 1 is the valuation date and October 1 the mailing date for bills, which are payable through the end of January. File a protest by May 15, or thirty days after the notice arrives. If the review board does not settle things, your next steps are district court, arbitration or an administrative hearing. Keep paying the undisputed amount in the meantime.

Exemptions that follow the homeowner

Filing an exemption with the Tarrant Appraisal District costs nothing. Homestead owners see appraised value capped at a ten percent annual increase, and older or disabled owners can choose an installment option.

An owner with a 100 percent disability rating can claim a total exemption on the residence homestead. Ask the district how any exemption or cap would carry to a new Texas home before you close, so you do not lose a benefit by timing.

A leased house can sell, though possession decides how fast. The process starts with a notice to vacate, at least three days unless the lease says otherwise. Next comes a justice court filing and a trial roughly ten to twenty-one days later. The tenant gets a brief window to appeal, and a writ of possession after judgment brings a day's notice before removal.

Because Grapevine bars nightly rentals in single-family homes, a tenant who sublets by the night is also a code issue. Settle that before you list. A cash buyer who accepts an occupied house can save you the waiting, but tell every buyer about the occupant in writing.

Selling when taxes are owed

Unpaid property tax stays with the house, so a balance owed does not block a sale. It does get paid first. The title company deducts every delinquent year from your proceeds at closing, which means you can sell without finding the cash beforehand.

Ask the Tarrant County tax office for a current payoff before you accept an offer, and compare offers by what remains after that payoff, any loan balance and closing charges. Taxes unpaid on February 1 start drawing penalty and interest, so the sooner you sell, the less the balance grows.

What to expect at closing

The title company checks who owns the house, requests payoff letters, reviews the tax status and drafts the deed. You sign in front of a notary, and money is released after the deed is recorded.

Take photo identification, keys, garage openers and any lease or HOA papers. Request the settlement statement early and check it against the offer you accepted. Cash deals skip the lender's appraisal and underwriting, the two steps that most often push a closing date back.

No. The city prohibits stays under 30 days in single-family homes, even in a primary residence. Longer leases are allowed.

Which appraisal district covers a Grapevine address?

Most parcels are in Tarrant County and use the Tarrant Appraisal District. Small parts of the city lie in Dallas and Denton counties, so check your tax bill.

When are Grapevine property taxes due?

Bills go out around October 1 and are due by January 31. Taxes unpaid on February 1 are delinquent and incur penalty and interest.

When must a Grapevine appraisal protest be filed?

Usually by May 15. If your notice arrived late, the cutoff is thirty days after delivery.

Can I sell a Grapevine house I inherited before probate is finished?

Not easily. Title companies want the heirs' authority on paper first, and routes include a muniment of title or an affidavit of heirship.

Routes for selling a Waxahachie house

Three practical paths exist for a Waxahachie owner: list with a broker, sell privately to someone you know, or accept an investor's cash offer. Your choice turns on the repair work the house needs and the day you need the funds.

Waxahachie is the seat of Ellis County, on Interstate 35E and U.S. Highway 287, about thirty miles south of Dallas. Shoppers often hold a house here up against homes nearer Dallas and weigh the drive, so mention highway access whenever you talk about the property.

  • Listing pays off for a sound home if you can live through showings and an appraisal.
  • A private sale skips marketing but still needs a signed deed and a closing agent.
  • Investors fit best with deferred repairs, tenants, probate questions or a hard deadline.

Old core, newer subdivisions

The town was laid out in August 1850 as the county seat and earned the nickname Gingerbread City for the Victorian carpentry on homes built before 1900. About 300 Waxahachie structures are on the federal historic register, including the red sandstone and granite courthouse on the square. A yearly Gingerbread Trail tour of Victorian homes keeps the old architecture in view.

A house in a historic pocket near the square can draw buyers who like period detail, and it can also carry older wiring, plumbing and foundations that an inspection will flag. Tour your own property the way a buyer would, and sort what you see into two columns. Charm goes in one: wood trim, porches, original windows. Trouble goes in the other: failing roofing, settling piers. Comparing the columns shows whether repairs before listing are worth it or whether selling as is is simpler. Photographs of both columns help when you explain the house to a buyer.

Newer subdivisions out toward the highways sit in a different market. The buyer pool there is mostly commuters and families, and the repair list is usually shorter. Ask a local agent or appraiser which category your street falls into before you set an asking price.

Student and rental housing near campuses

Waxahachie grew on cotton and rail, and education added another layer. Trinity University operated in town from 1902 to 1942, Southwestern Bible Institute took over the grounds in 1943, and Navarro College has a branch here. Those institutions explain the clusters of older rental and student housing near campus areas.

The town hosts the Scarborough Renaissance Faire and a Christmas parade and tour of homes, which bring visitors each year. Some sellers time a listing around those events so more people see the street. An investor looks at the house itself, so timing matters less for a cash sale.

Permits for work before a sale

Selling needs no permit, though repair work beforehand may need one from the Permitting Division of the city's Building and Community Services Department. The city runs an online Citizen Self-Service portal for applications, payments, inspection scheduling and plan review. Separate submittal guides cover fences, residential remodels, accessory structures, swimming pools, irrigation and certificates of occupancy. Construction fees are in Chapter 11 of the City Code of Ordinances.

Did an earlier owner add a room, deck or pool? Find out whether the permit was closed. Open or missing permits tend to surface once a buyer's financing is underway, and fixing them before you list costs less than fixing them under contract. Ask the Permitting Division what a closeout would involve, and budget time for an inspection visit.

Tax bills and dates at closing

Ellis County channels bill the taxes on a Waxahachie house, and at closing the year's bill is normally divided between buyer and seller.

Each year's tax lien attaches January 1, so the buyer's closing agent will want any unpaid bill cleared. The county tax office, at 302 N. Monroe Street in Waxahachie, can give a payoff figure for a specific account. Bring the account number from your latest statement and your photo ID to speed that along.

Homestead exemptions and deed recording

A seller who has claimed a homestead exemption loses it at the sale, and the buyer applies for their own. School districts must give a $140,000 homestead exemption, and an additional $60,000 applies to older or disabled owners. A buyer who closes after January 1 may be able to claim it for the rest of that year if the prior owner did not.

  • Ellis County Clerk staff record the deed, since that office keeps the land records for everything inside the county line.
  • A notary or other authorized officer must witness the signature.
  • The fee schedule charges $5.00 up front with $4.00 added per further page, plus smaller records fees.

The title company needs your government photo ID, the property's legal description and any loan payoff statement. With those in hand, the deed is drafted right the first time. After funding, the company sends the deed to the clerk, and you get a recorded copy for your files.

Selling before a foreclosure auction

If your Waxahachie loan is behind, the house is sold at auction on a first Tuesday after the notice has been out for three weeks. Selling before that date can avoid the auction. Check the loan paperwork and ask the county clerk where notices are filed.

Call the lender and a housing counselor right away. A cash buyer can often close within the time left, and a closing before auction day can pay off the loan and leave you any remaining equity. The sooner you start, the more choices you keep.

Gather the loan statement, the foreclosure notice if you have received one, and the deed. Share them with the title company on the first call so it can confirm the payoff figure and tell you how quickly a closing could happen. If equity remains after the payoff, it is paid to you at the closing table. Never let the notice sit unopened, because the auction date does not move to fit your schedule.

Frequently asked questions

Can I sell my Waxahachie house as-is?

Yes. State law sets no repair duty ahead of a sale, and a cash buyer can purchase a house without any repairs done. Open permits or code issues should still be settled or disclosed, and unpaid taxes or recorded liens will come up during title work.

Which office handles deeds for a Waxahachie property?

Ellis County Clerk staff record deeds, because Texas keeps deed records county by county. The clerk checks that the deed is signed and acknowledged before accepting it.

When are Ellis County property taxes due?

Statements arrive about October 1, with payment due by January 31. Late charges begin February 1, and on July 1 the county hands what remains to its tax attorneys.

Does the age of a Waxahachie house affect a sale?

It can. Many houses near the square date from before 1900, and buyers of those homes may ask for inspections of wiring, plumbing and the foundation. Newer subdivision homes usually raise fewer questions.

What if my Waxahachie house is facing foreclosure?

Contact the lender and a housing counselor right away. A Texas auction takes place on the month's first Tuesday after a sale notice has been posted at the courthouse and lodged with the clerk three weeks earlier. A closing before that day can pay off the loan.

Selling a Cedar Hill house for cash

Cedar Hill sellers can list with an agent, run their own sale, or take cash. A cash buyer needs no lender and can often close sooner, though the price already accounts for repairs and risk. Request every offer in writing, including title costs and what an inspection could change.

The condition of the house points toward an answer. A tidy home on a quiet street may bring more as a listing, while one carrying deferred repairs, tenants or tax trouble may fit a direct sale better. Weigh what you would take home each way once costs and waiting are subtracted, and ask every buyer how long closing will take and who pays for title work.

A sale by owner falls in the middle. You save the commission but take on the contract, the buyer screening and the paperwork, and the title company asks for the same documents in every case.

Cedar Hill's hills, lake and buyers

Cedar Hill sits about 18 miles southwest of downtown Dallas along US Highway 67, mostly in Dallas County with small parts in Ellis County. Joe Pool Lake lies along its western edge, with Cedar Hill State Park beside it. The Balcones Escarpment runs through town, so many lots slope, and Red Oak Creek and Bentle Branch Creek cross it. Drainage, foundation movement and flood questions come up often, so keep surveys and repair records ready.

Buyers tend to want hills, water and a short drive to the metroplex. Downtown Fort Worth is 30 miles away and DFW Airport 27 miles. Lead with the lake and park when you describe the house, and be ready to document any yard drainage or retaining work on a sloped lot.

Age of the housing stock

Growth came late to Cedar Hill. The population was 2,160 in 1970, 6,847 in 1980 and 20,267 in 1990, a jump tied to Joe Pool Dam, completed in 1985, and the lake behind it. Many houses therefore date from the 1980s or later. Roofs, HVAC systems and original windows from that period may be near the end of their life, and buyers will price that in. If you plan to list, a quick check of the roof, the air conditioning and the windows tells you what to expect before a buyer's inspector does. If you plan to sell as-is for cash, just tell the buyer what you know about each system and its age.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Cedar Hill house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Rental registration

Landlords have to register. The City Council passed a Single Family Rental Registration Ordinance on November 10, 2020, and enforcement began January 1, 2021. Single family rentals, duplexes and townhomes included, must be registered every year and again when ownership changes. A tenant-occupied sale should come with proof that the registration is current.

Cedar Hill single family rental fees
Registration typeFee
Initial annual registration or change in ownership$50.00
Renewal$25.00

Each tenant change calls for a new certificate of occupancy, and a code officer inspects the exterior within 30 days. Code Enforcement is at the Government Center, 285 Uptown Boulevard, and takes email at code@cedarhilltx.com.

Homestead exemptions and tax limits

For school taxes, $140,000 of a homestead is exempt, and an owner aged 65 or over or disabled gets $60,000 on top. Local governments can also offer an option of up to 20 percent of value. The county tax office can tell you whether Cedar Hill's units use it.

  • A senior or disabled homestead's school tax is frozen at the level of the first qualifying year.
  • If you buy again, the ceiling can move in proportion to a new Texas homestead.
  • A disabled veteran's exemption grows with the rating, and 100 percent means a full exemption on the homestead.
  • If the seller never held the exemption, a buyer after January 1 may claim it for that year.

Tell your agent if a freeze applies to your house. The buyer does not inherit it.

Contract for deed, Lady Bird deed and heirs

If a buyer lives in the home under a contract for deed, sometimes called a lease to own, Property Code chapter 5, subchapter D applies. The seller keeps title until payment is finished. State law gives the buyer a right to cancel, with notice periods spelled out in the code. Anyone holding one should ask a lawyer how it changes a sale.

A transfer on death deed filed before the owner dies sends the property to the beneficiary without probate. A Lady Bird deed lets the owner sell without asking the named beneficiary. Heirs with neither deed may need a muniment of title or a small estate affidavit to move the deed.

Removing an occupant before you sell

Start with the right notice. The written notice to vacate usually gives three days. Hand it to the tenant or to a household member aged 16 or older, post it inside the home where it can be seen, or mail it. Email works only when the written lease permits it.

  • The case is heard in justice court, and the tenant must be served at least four days before trial.
  • Expect the hearing 10 to 21 days after the filing date.
  • Appealing to county court has to happen within five days of judgment.
  • A writ can be requested six days after final judgment, and removal follows 24 hours' notice.

A person who stays after being told to leave, with no lease and no family tie, might be removed on a sheriff's or constable's request under Property Code chapter 24B, with no court case. A wrongful removal invites a lawsuit, so talk to the sheriff's or constable's office before acting.

Documents for a sloped or creek-side lot

Water shows up in buyer conversations here. If the lot slopes toward the house, backs onto a creek or has a retaining wall, write down what was done and when. Keep the survey, any engineer's letter and invoices for foundation or drainage work in one folder. If you have never had a problem, say that too, and note how long you have lived there. Buyers and their inspectors are far more comfortable with a seller who can show records than one who shrugs.

On the cash side, an investor will inspect the same things and subtract the cost of anything unresolved. Records can narrow that gap, because they replace guesses with facts.

What to prepare

Gather the tax statement, a payoff letter if a loan exists, the rental registration and certificate of occupancy if a tenant lives there, and any survey or drainage and foundation repair records. A buyer given those on day one can price faster, and the title company can see who needs to sign.

Frequently asked questions

Is Cedar Hill in Dallas County or Ellis County?

Most of it is in Dallas County, and a small part is in Ellis County. Check your tax bill for the county, which fixes your clerk and appraisal district.

How much does Cedar Hill charge to register a rental?

The city lists $50 for the first annual registration or a change of owner, $25 to renew and $75 for a late renewal. A Residential Rental Certificate of Occupancy costs $25 at each tenant change. Confirm current fees with Code Enforcement.

Can I sell a Cedar Hill house with a tenant?

Yes, and the buyer takes the house subject to the lease unless it ends first. Keep the rental registration current. A new certificate of occupancy will be required for the next tenant.

What is the school homestead exemption near Cedar Hill?

School districts exempt $140,000 by state rule, with $60,000 more for qualifying seniors and disabled owners. It follows the owner who lives in the house, so each buyer applies separately.

Can a Lady Bird deed help me sell?

It can. The owner stays free to sell or mortgage, and at death the home passes outside probate. No official form exists in Texas, so work with a lawyer or the county clerk's guidance.

Sell My House Fast in Huntsville, TX: Options, Costs and Cash Offers

Cash Home Buyers in Texas

Sell Your Huntsville House for Cash

Last updated November 14, 2026.

Selling in Huntsville?
We buy Huntsville houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

Three ways to sell a Huntsville house

Your route out of a Huntsville house depends on its repair needs, any debt against it and your deadline. An agent exposes it to the widest pool of buyers. A private sale saves the commission. A plain cash purchase asks the least effort of all.

Retail showings suit some houses poorly: a worn roof, an estate that is stuck or a tenant who quit paying. A tidy home on a good street, though, may fetch more on the open market.

  • List it if the house shows well and time is on your side.
  • Sell privately if a buyer is already in mind.
  • Take cash if the clock or the condition is what worries you.

Why Huntsville houses tend to be older

Huntsville is the Walker County seat, at the crossing of Interstate 45 and U.S. Highway 190. Growth came slowly: 11,999 residents in 1960, 23,936 in 1980, 35,078 in 2000. The housing stock spans every age as a result, from places near the courthouse square to newer homes toward the lake country.

Plaster walls, original wiring and settling are common in older houses, and an inspector will find them. Repair the obvious ones before listing or price around them, so the contract survives the option period.

Who buys in Huntsville

Public employers carry the local economy: Sam Houston State University and the prison system. Huntsville State Park, Sam Houston National Forest and Lake Livingston pull in weekend buyers as well. Expect three buyer types in practice: staff of the university and prisons, people wanting a base near water or woods, and investors buying student rentals.

With a student tenant in place, study the lease before naming a closing date, and line the sale up with the lease end.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Huntsville house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Walker County Appraisal District

Here a single office handles the whole chain. The Walker County Appraisal District works out the levy, mails statements, takes payment and passes the money to each taxing unit, where many counties divide those tasks between an appraiser and a separate tax collector.

The district is at 1060 Highway 190 East. Phone 936-295-0402 or 936-295-3061 for a bill question or a payoff figure.

If you dispute the value, you take it to the review board, whose members are local residents independent of the district. Budgets and rates come from city councils, school boards and the commissioners, so a protest can lower your value but never the rate.

Texas property tax dates that affect a Huntsville sale

Five calendar points explain most questions a Huntsville seller asks about the yearly bill.

Calendar for a Huntsville tax year
DateWhat happens
January 1Owner and value are fixed for the year, and the lien for that year attaches
April 1Appraisal notices go out for single-family homesteads
May 15Normal protest cutoff, or 30 days after the notice when that is later
October 1Bills are mailed and payable on receipt
January 31Final day for most owners to pay before delinquency charges

The person who owned the house on January 1 is answerable for that year's levy, and the lien stays attached to the property. If your Huntsville closing falls in spring or summer, write down who pays what share before anyone signs.

What falling behind on taxes costs

A bill unpaid by January 31 begins growing the next day: six percent penalty, one percent interest. Each following month tacks on another point of penalty until July, when it tops out at 12 percent. Interest never stops climbing.

  • A unit that hires a collection lawyer may pass along that lawyer's surcharge.
  • A homestead owner can request a payment plan that spans several years.
  • Penalty waivers exist, but you must move quickly and ask in writing.

Ask the Walker County Appraisal District what relief it offers. With heavy arrears, paying them out of the sale proceeds can beat a long plan.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Huntsville houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Homestead exemption

Your homestead exemption lowers the value used to figure school taxes. Districts must subtract $140,000 for a residence homestead, and an owner who is 65 or older, or disabled, gets $60,000 more off school taxes.

Texas also holds yearly appraisal growth on a homestead to ten percent. Older and disabled owners have a school tax ceiling too, and a share of it can follow them to a new Texas home. A disabled-veteran rating may qualify an owner under Tax Code section 11.22, and a total rating can earn a full homestead exemption under section 11.131.

Let the buyer's lender know if your exemption is active, since it shifts the monthly cost the lender models.

What happens if a Huntsville owner faces foreclosure or has died?

A Huntsville borrower facing foreclosure will usually see no courtroom. The lender sends a default letter, giving 20 days to cure. If nothing changes, a sale notice is posted and filed three weeks ahead of an auction on a first Tuesday at the Walker County location set for it. Federal rules generally keep the servicer from starting until payments are 120 days behind, so you have room to sell first.

After an owner's death, the path forks on one question: was there a will? Probate for a will generally begins within four years. Heirs not named on the recorded deed send the appraisal district an ownership affidavit and a death certificate to hold onto the homestead break. Before closing, the agent asks who has authority to sign, and a Walker County attorney can answer that quickly.

What to confirm before accepting a cash offer

  • Terms in writing, covering the closing date, the closing agent and which side pays each cost.
  • A lender payoff letter, when a mortgage is involved.
  • Where taxes, liens and any association dues stand.
  • Whether any tenant has to be out before closing.

Weigh the cash number against a listing's likely net, after repairs, agent fees and the months of carrying costs. Recording happens at the Walker County clerk. The Texas schedule is $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for each added page, plus a few small records fees, all rolled into one figure on your settlement statement.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

How a Huntsville sale moves from offer to closing

Accepting an offer sets the closing agent to work: open a title file, request the payoff, search for liens and open taxes. You sign the deed before a notary and the Walker County clerk files it. Find out who carries it to the clerk, and keep the recorded copy.

Paperwork to gather before you list or sell

Gather your recorded deed and newest tax statement before anything else, since a Huntsville closing agent wants both immediately. If a loan is outstanding, ask the lender for a payoff letter. A rental needs its lease handy, and any association needs to send a dues balance.

Prepared sellers negotiate less. Investors paying cash and families borrowing alike want clean title, a known tax status and a candid description of the house. Expect an inspection to find an old roof or original wiring? Say so in your first conversation and let the number reflect it.

Timing a sale around the tax year

A late-year closing meets a lien dated January 1 and a bill that arrived in October, so a large unpaid amount sits on the table. Expect the closing agent to split the year between you and the buyer, and ask for the exact split in writing. If you protested your value, phone the Walker County Appraisal District to see whether that case is still open.

Frequently asked questions

Can a Huntsville house sell without repairs?

Yes, at a price that reflects the work still needed. Cash buyers routinely take houses as they stand.

Where is the Walker County property tax office?

The Walker County Appraisal District, 1060 Highway 190 East, handles both appraisal and collection.

When does a Texas tax bill turn delinquent?

Generally on February 1, after the January 31 payment deadline.

Does the senior tax ceiling follow me to a new home?

It can transfer in proportion to a new Texas homestead.

Which office files a Huntsville deed?

The Walker County clerk, after the document is acknowledged before a notary.

What to weigh before a quick sale in Bedford

Bedford is a small suburb in northeast Tarrant County with almost no vacant land left, so a house here competes in a crowded metro market. Sellers handle paperwork with Tarrant Appraisal District, a city rental registry and buyers who commute across the Metroplex. SH-121 runs through town, about 14 miles from downtown Fort Worth and 22 from downtown Dallas, and DFW International Airport is within five miles.

An estimated 47,958 people lived in Bedford in mid-2025, a 4.0% decline from the April 2020 base. About half of homes are rented, so one seller may be juggling tenants, a registration file and a tax ceiling transfer at the same moment.

Bedford housing numbers

A midpoint owner-occupied home is worth $350,700, and owners occupy 50.6% of units. Renters pay $1,502 a month at the midpoint.

Bedford has 10.03 square miles of land and 4,977.9 residents per square mile as of 2020, and the typical trip to work is 24.5 minutes. Homes near Bedford Boys Ranch Park have an easy selling point to mention.

Exemptions through Tarrant Appraisal District

Homestead exemption applications go to Tarrant Appraisal District, free of charge. You can file online, send it by mail, or deliver it to the office on Handley-Ederville Road in Fort Worth.

  • Residential homestead, for owners who live in the house.
  • Over-65 and disabled exemptions, which add a ceiling on school taxes and on locally adopted city, county and special district taxes.
  • Disabled veteran and surviving spouse exemptions, tied to the service-connected rating.
  • Heir owners can claim the homestead on the whole property rather than a share.

Owners who are 65 or older, disabled or disabled veteran owners may also put off paying the homestead tax while it keeps accruing. Someone whose value rose more than 5% over the prior year can defer the extra portion too. The deferral charges 8% interest a year, and the deferred tax stays a lien on the property.

How much a Bedford tax bill can grow

School taxes on a Texas homestead start with a $140,000 exemption, and older or disabled owners get $60,000 more. A taxing unit can add its own percentage exemption beyond that.

Assessed homestead value can rise no more than 10% a year after the first full year of exemption is behind you. Bills are sent around October 1, and unpaid balances pick up a six percent penalty plus one percent interest on February 1. A delinquent homestead owner may be allowed to pay over as many as 36 months, depending on the collector.

Does Bedford regulate short-term rentals?

Yes. Before renting a home for fewer than 29 days at a time, an owner must register with the city, and no property is exempt.

Residential zoning is the only place for short-term rentals, never multi-family districts, and none may be within 1,000 feet of another registered one. Expect a fire inspection every year, a repeat visit if problems turn up, and a fresh inspection whenever ownership changes.

  • Liability insurance for the host, naming the city as an additional insured.
  • Proof that property taxes are current.
  • Written house rules on occupancy limits, off-street parking, quiet hours and a 24-hour local contact.
  • A floorplan with dimensions that shows the emergency exits.

Hotel occupancy tax is due by the 20th of each month for the month before, and a report is required even in a month with no stays. A buyer planning a rental should ask Neighborhood Services what a sale does to the registration.

Lender timeline on a Bedford foreclosure

A Tarrant County deed of trust usually gives the lender a power of sale, which means an auction with no lawsuit. Sales are held on a first Tuesday, and the posted start time may not be delayed by more than three hours.

The default notice comes first and gives you 20 days from receipt to pay what is past due. Next, the sale notice must arrive with 21 days or more to spare. A lender that wants the remaining balance after the sale must sue within two years.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Bedford houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Moving an inherited Bedford house to a buyer

The probate court in the decedent's home county hears the will, and you have four years from the death to start. When real estate liens are the only debts, a muniment of title allows the court order and the will to pass title.

The title company's requirements follow the route you took. Transfer on death deeds come with an affidavit of death and a certificate. Administered estates use a deed from the executor or administrator. A will with no contest and no administration is backed by the court order alone. Heirs will not be added to the old deed by the county on its own.

Where a Bedford deed is filed

A Bedford deed is filed by the Tarrant County clerk, since Texas records deeds in the county of the land. Before filing, the deed must be signed and either acknowledged by a notary or witnessed by two people.

Expect $5.00 for the first page and $4.00 for every page after it, plus other charges. Call the Tarrant County Clerk for the full amount before you mail in a deed.

From contract to closing

Accepting an offer sets the title company in motion: a tax statement is requested, each payoff is ordered and the records are searched for liens. At closing you sign the deed before a notary, and it goes to the Tarrant County clerk for recording. Give the buyer the lease and deposit information if someone rents the house. This is also the time to schedule a final walk-through and plan utility shut-offs for the closing date.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Cash buyer or listing for a Bedford house

Compare what you owe with what each route is likely to bring. A listing can pay more for an updated house, yet it comes with showings, repairs after inspection and a buyer's loan to approve. Cash buyers take the house in its current state and close on your timetable, a good fit for a tenant, an estate or a deadline.

Before deciding, gather the tax statement, any mortgage payoff, rental registration and inspection records, and a copy of the deed. Then you can set offers side by side and see what each would truly leave you.

Landlords should explain the registration to every buyer. It belongs to the owner, so someone who keeps the house as a rental must register under their own name and book a new inspection after the sale.

Frequently asked questions

What is a house in Bedford worth?

Owner-occupied homes sit at a $350,700 midpoint in the 2020-2024 figures. Your house may differ with its condition, lot and street, and a written offer or appraisal is the way to know.

Can I list my Bedford house on Airbnb or Vrbo?

You must register with the city first. Bedford asks for registration and a yearly inspection for stays shorter than 29 days, and no short-term rental can be within 1,000 feet of another.

Is there a fee to claim a homestead exemption in Bedford?

No fee applies. Tarrant Appraisal District charges nothing for exemptions, and most homestead applications are due by April 30.

Can a senior in Bedford postpone property tax?

Yes. Owners over 65, disabled owners and disabled veteran owners may defer homestead tax. Interest accrues at 8% per year while the tax remains a lien on the house.

What paperwork finishes a Bedford sale?

A signed and acknowledged deed, filed with the Tarrant County Clerk. For an inherited house, add whichever fits: an affidavit of death, a court order or an executor's deed.

How fast can a Midlothian house sell?

Fast enough for most deadlines if you prepare first. Midlothian sits southwest of Dallas in Ellis County, and houses there sell both to cash buyers and on the open market. Know your payoff, tax status and any open permits before you take offers.

The Midlothian housing market

Midlothian grew from a heavy-industry town into a Dallas-Fort Worth suburb, about 25 miles southwest of Dallas. It bills itself as the Cement Capital of Texas, and limestone from a chalk ridge beneath it is why cement plants set up here. A steel mini-mill, the RailPort business park and an auto-processing park along the U.S. 67 corridor add to the industrial base.

  • Growth from Dallas-Fort Worth gives you a broad pool of commuters.
  • Buyers sometimes ask what sits near a given street, so be ready with a plain answer about distance from plants and rail.
  • If your house is near U.S. 67 or the rail park, mention drive times in the listing and expect questions about traffic and noise.

Which routes could I take for a Midlothian house?

Your choices are listing, a cash sale or an investor purchase, and the house's condition plus your calendar should drive the pick.

  • Agent listing suits tidy homes with time to market.
  • Cash sale suits inherited, damaged, occupied or neglected homes.
  • Investor purchase can include a flexible move-out date.
  • Selling ahead of foreclosure matters if payments lapsed; auctions are held monthly after 21 days' notice.

With any choice, have the closing date, the title and recording cost split and repair assumptions put in writing. Press each buyer on how they arrived at their figure and test it against recent sales of similar houses close by.

Free, no-obligation offerTell us about your Midlothian house and get a written cash offer within 24 hours.Get My Cash Offer →

Building permits in Midlothian

Any improvement or alteration needs a permit first. A contractor has to register with the city to pull one, though registration costs nothing.

Projects that need a Midlothian building permit
Project typeExamples
Outdoor structuresDecks, fences, pools and spas, patio covers, carports, accessory buildings
Site workAll flatwork, irrigation systems
Exterior workRoofing
Building workNew or remodeled commercial buildings and residences, mobile home gas and electrical hookups

Permit costs are in the city's master fee schedule. Put in a fence, deck or roof without a permit? Ask the city how to fix that before a buyer's inspector spots it.

Property taxes and exemptions

No state property tax exists in Texas. Bills come from local units, and each January 1, when the lien attaches, appraisal districts set values.

  • A bill mailed in October becomes delinquent after January 31.
  • Pay in two installments if you like: November 30 and June 30.
  • Six percent penalty and one percent interest hit on February 1.
  • A homestead gets $140,000 off from school districts, plus $60,000 for owners 65 or older or disabled.

Amounts vary by taxing unit, so call the Ellis County tax office or the appraisal district about your address.

What happens on closing day?

At closing the title company verifies ownership, pays liens and taxes out of your funds and files the deed. For recording, the signature must be notarized or otherwise acknowledged.

A 2023 clerk manual shows $5.00 for the opening page and $4.00 for each one added, with capped records fees on top. The Ellis County clerk can tell you today's charges.

What if someone occupies the house?

Tenants receive a written notice to vacate, three days or longer unless the lease provides otherwise, before any justice court case. Someone who came in without permission and was never family or a tenant could fall under Property Code chapter 24B, which has the owner go to the sheriff or constable.

Adverse possession is a separate matter. Texas treats it as actual, visible use of land under a hostile claim of right, and the ten-year statute is the most familiar. If someone claims your land, consult a Texas attorney.

Probate and back taxes

A buyer needs proof that the person selling can legally sign. For an inherited house that could be a muniment of title, an executor's deed, or a transfer on death deed paired with a recorded death affidavit.

Delinquent taxes can end in a lawsuit, and an attorney the county contracts with may add up to 20 percent in fees. You can ask in writing for penalty and interest to be waived if you pay within 21 days of learning about the delinquency. Obtain a payoff figure from the tax office before you accept any offer.

Getting a Midlothian house ready

Start with what the city can see. Walk the lot and list any fence, deck, roof, pool, patio cover or slab added since you bought, then confirm each has a closed permit. The city runs MyGov for permit records and contractor registration, so past work can be looked up.

Next collect your deed, survey and mortgage statement. A tidy file speeds the title search. For a cash sale, write the closing date, title cost split and any repair credits into the contract.

  • Close open permits before listing.
  • Keep roofing and mechanical receipts.
  • Request a payoff letter early.
  • Check your deed and survey for easements.
  • Photograph the street and surroundings in daylight.
You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Weighing offers on a Midlothian house

Offers that look different on paper may not be. A big number tied to a long inspection window can leave you with less than a smaller cash bid that closes right away, so list the terms side by side.

  • Price, and whether repairs are the buyer's problem.
  • Proposed closing date and the choice of title company.
  • Split of title, recording and survey charges.
  • Earnest money held, and your claim to it if the buyer walks.
  • Any loan or appraisal the deal depends on.

Request the final numbers on a closing statement, and take any confusing line to the title company instead of the buyer.

Cash sale or listing for a worn house

Aging roofs, deferred maintenance and unpermitted additions do not stop a sale, but the route you choose sets your to-do list. Listing means repairing what an inspector or appraiser will flag, closing open permits and sitting through showings. A cash buyer accepts the property as it stands and discounts for the work, so no contractors for you and a lower figure.

Short on time, perhaps with an inherited house you cannot upkeep or a move you cannot postpone? Speed may justify the lower figure. With a few months to spare and a house in decent shape, a listing often pays more. In both cases tally what holding the house costs, including taxes, insurance and utilities.

What a title company asks for

The title company will ask for a government ID, the recorded deed (or its recording details), a mortgage payoff statement and your latest tax bill. A rented house also needs the lease, and records from any major contractor job help the buyer's side.

Closings drag when documents trickle in one by one. The county clerk can supply copies of anything recorded, and city permit staff can help reconstruct the work history.

Frequently asked questions

Which county is Midlothian in?

Ellis County. Deeds and liens for a Midlothian address are filed with the clerk of the county where the land lies.

Does a new roof or fence need a permit?

Yes. The city lists roofing, fences, decks, pools, irrigation and flatwork among permitted work, and contractors must be registered with the city.

Can back taxes block my sale?

They do not block it. The title company pays them from proceeds at closing, and a buyer will insist on that since the lien attaches each January 1.

How long does a Midlothian cash closing take?

Often a few weeks, depending on title, liens and your move-out date.

Could I stop a foreclosure by selling?

Possibly. Texas auctions occur on the first Tuesday of the month after at least 21 days' notice, and past-due amounts may be paid within 20 days of the default notice.

Developers planned this city along the eastern edge of Lake Lewisville. Families first arrived in October 1974, voters chose incorporation in 1977, and home rule status followed in 1979. Eastvale, a lakeside community begun in the early 1960s, folded into the city in 1987.

Age is what matters to a seller. Homes from that first building wave have decades on them, so buyers look at roofs, windows and plumbing before anything else. Sections closer to Grandscape and State Highway 121 attract another kind of buyer than the older lakeside blocks do.

Development that drives demand

Nebraska Furniture Mart of Texas opened in spring 2015 and anchors the 433-acre Grandscape project in the State Highway 121 corridor. Topgolf, Scheels and Galaxy Theatres are part of the mix, and the city estimates six to eight million visitors a year. Trails and green space, Tree City USA and Playful City USA designations, and a spot 35 minutes from downtown Dallas and 25 minutes from DFW International Airport complete the pitch.

  • Buyers near Grandscape and SH 121 weigh traffic and walkability.
  • Buyers near the lakeshore weigh trails and park access.

Who taxes and bills a Colony address

A Colony tax bill involves three offices. City council picks the city rate in September during budget season. Denton Central Appraisal District determines value and handles exemptions. The Denton County Tax Assessor/Collector sends the bill and takes payment. The levy date is October 1, applied to the value as of the previous January 1. For this year's rate, phone the city finance office or the county tax office.

  • Denton CAD: 3911 Morse St. in Denton, 940-349-3800, mailing address P.O. Box 2816, Denton, TX 76202.
  • County tax office: 940-349-3500 in Denton and 940-349-3510 at the Frisco Government Center, 5535 F.M. 423.
  • City finance office: 6053 Main Street, 972-624-3140.

A balance left after January 31 becomes delinquent on February 1, with a 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest. Since the lien starts January 1 and stays with the house, the title company clears any balance from your sale money.

Homestead exemptions

The city grants a homestead exemption equal to 5 percent of the property's market value, so the dollar figure shifts whenever market value does. If you receive a notice that an exemption was reduced or cancelled from the prior year, check the exemption code in the table it contains and review your status at the Denton CAD website. The notice alone does not mean a taxing unit changed its policy.

  • The statewide school exemption is $140,000, and seniors and disabled owners get extra relief.
  • Most applications are due by April 30.
  • If the seller never claimed it, a buyer moving in after January 1 may still claim the exemption for the remainder of that year.

The city exemption covers owner-occupied homes only, not rentals or investment property.

What a cash sale skips

A Colony cash sale removes the pieces that most often stall a financed one. No lender appraisal means no surprise valuation gap. No loan approval means no last-minute denial. No buyer repair demands means no second round of haggling after inspection. What remains is title work, a payoff and a signing appointment.

Timing is flexible too. Some owners want to close fast, and others need a few extra weeks to find a place or finish the school year. A cash buyer can usually build either schedule into the contract. Say so up front and put the date in writing.

Paperwork from contract to closing

Start with three documents: the lender payoff, the tax bill and any owners' association papers. After that you pick a route, sign a contract and open title.

  • Order the lender payoff and search for recorded liens.
  • Pay taxes through the closing date.
  • Sign the deed before a notary, which the clerk requires.
  • Record it in Denton County, home to most of The Colony.

A statutory fee schedule sets recording charges, and your closing statement lists the exact amount. When an HOA covers your street, request its payoff or transfer letter early. A missing HOA statement is a common reason closings slip by a few days. Bring photo ID and every key, remote and gate code to the signing, and schedule your utility shutoff for the same day.

Inherited, foreclosure and rental situations

Heirs get four years from the date of death to probate a will. Other estates run on a muniment of title, a small estate affidavit or a recorded transfer on death deed. Which one applies is a question for a Texas probate attorney.

Foreclosure auctions follow a first-Tuesday schedule with 21 days' notice, so selling beforehand can keep your equity. With a tenant in place, the landlord first serves written notice to vacate, three days at minimum unless the lease sets another period. A justice court filing follows, with trial set 10 to 21 days later, and a writ of possession can come six days after final judgment. Build your sale schedule around those steps.

Which county is The Colony in for tax and deed purposes?

Denton County covers most of the city. Denton CAD sets values, and the county tax office collects, with an extra office in Frisco. Your tax bill names the county for your parcel.

Does The Colony have its own homestead exemption?

Yes, at 5 percent of market value. School districts add the statewide $140,000 exemption on top. File with Denton CAD by April 30.

Should I update my house before selling in The Colony?

Not necessarily. Cash buyers purchase as is. If you list, weigh the cost of updates against the price difference, since buyers often compare your house with newer homes nearby.

How do I find The Colony's current tax rate?

Ask the city finance office at 972-624-3140 or the Denton County tax office at 940-349-3500. The city sets its rate each September.

Can I sell if I have not paid last year's property tax?

Yes. Closing pays off the balance plus penalty and interest from your proceeds. Get a payoff figure that stays valid through the closing date.

Keller covers 18.4 square miles of the Dallas-Fort Worth area and counted 47,516 residents on January 1, 2025. The city calls itself Texas's most family-friendly, and listings lean on that.

Old Town Keller and Keller Town Center are the two business districts. Buyers touring a house also ask about Big Bear Creek trails, The Keller Pointe recreation and aquatics center, the library and the senior activities center. Keller ISD is the school district, and the two main roads are U.S. Highway 377 (Main Street) and FM 1709 (Keller Parkway).

A house near either road gains convenience and loses some quiet. Describe that tradeoff honestly instead of letting a buyer discover it at the second showing.

Tarrant Appraisal District

Appraisals and exemptions for Keller come from Tarrant Appraisal District, while the city, the county and the school district each set a rate of their own. Seventy-three taxing units across Tarrant County rely on that one district, and there is no charge to file an exemption.

Hold on to your appraisal notice. If you sell after a protest was filed, tell the title company so the outcome is credited to the right person.

Homestead and senior breaks when you move

A $140,000 homestead exemption comes from school districts, and a senior or disabled owner gets $60,000 more along with a cap on school tax. Anyone qualifying who downsizes within Texas may take a proportionate share of that ceiling along.

Before you list, ask the appraisal district to confirm exactly what carries over. If the seller never had the exemption, a buyer closing after January 1 may claim it right away.

Disabled veteran exemptions

The size of the disabled veteran exemption follows the VA rating, and it covers a single property the veteran owns. At a 100 percent rating, including by individual unemployability, the residence homestead can be fully exempt, and an unmarried surviving spouse may keep that benefit.

Smaller ratings bring smaller dollar amounts: $5,000 for a 10 to 29 percent rating, rising to $12,000 for 70 to 100 percent. April 30 is the usual filing date, though Section 11.22 applicants can have up to five years after the delinquency date. How a Keller owner can sell on a short clock

An agent, a private sale or a cash buyer: each one costs you time or money in a different way.

  • Going without an agent keeps the commission in your pocket and puts showings and contracts in your hands.
  • A cash purchase hands repairs to the buyer and closes on your date, useful after a job move, a divorce, a tenant problem or an inheritance.

Closing and recording in Tarrant County

Keller deeds go into the official records at the Tarrant County Clerk after a notary or similar officer witnesses the signature. Fees are charged per page, with records fees on top. Inherited homestead exemptions

Heirs missing from the recorded deed must give the appraisal district a sworn statement of ownership, the death certificate and a utility bill, along with any court citation, before the exemption takes effect.

Depending on the facts, the new deed may be a transfer deed recorded before death, an executor's deed, a muniment of title order or an affidavit of heirship. Adding heirs to an old deed is not something a county clerk can do alone.

Tenants, a mortgage default or an open estate

All three add a step before closing. In a default, the lender's letter starts a short clock, and the auction falls on a first Tuesday at the courthouse. An open estate needs a court order or an affidavit before anyone can sign a deed. Renters need proper written notice, and a justice court handles the eviction suit.

Some cash buyers take a house with renters or an unsettled estate, though a Texas attorney should review the plan first.

Getting buyers past the first showing

Resale houses in Keller compete with new construction in nearby cities, so have answers ready on school zoning, park access and trail links. Rankings matter less than the roof, the furnace and the drains, which an inspector will examine. Walk your lot first and fix what you can. Keep permits for past work close, along with your tax statement and any payoff letter, and a serious buyer can go from interest to offer without waiting on you. Answer questions about the neighborhood honestly, since buyers verify what they hear, and keep your lot tidy for the second visit, when many Keller buyers bring a contractor or a relative to look at the house again.

A Keller timeline from listing to closing

Think of the sale as three phases. In phase one, before the sign goes up, assemble the deed, your newest Tarrant tax statement and any payoff letter, and settle how much repair is worth the money. Phase two is the listing, when inspectors tend to scrutinize roofs, furnaces and drains and buyers push back. In phase three the title company searches for liens, divides the year's taxes and books a signing before a notary.

A cash buyer folds the first two phases into a single conversation. You accept a lower price and in return pick the date and skip the repair list. To choose between slow and fast, take the listing price, subtract commission, repairs and the months of mortgage, insurance and upkeep, and compare what is left with the cash figure.

Questions to settle before you sign

Put identical questions to every buyer and the offers become easy to compare. Who covers the title policy? When is closing, and does the date slip if a loan drags? Will the buyer take the house with its flaws, or does an inspection reopen the price? Is financing needed or is the cash ready? Written answers head off the late surprises that stall contracts. With tenants or an estate involved, add one more: who clears the house before the keys change hands?

47,516 people as of January 1, 2025, living in 18.4 square miles.

Which county is Keller in?

Tarrant County. Appraisals and exemptions come from Tarrant Appraisal District, and deeds are recorded by the Tarrant County Clerk.

Does Tarrant charge to file an exemption?

No. Filing is free, and most exemption applications are due by April 30.

What date makes a Texas tax bill late?

Most bills become delinquent on February 1, after being mailed around October 1.

Is a no-repairs sale possible in Keller?

Yes, through a cash buyer; a loan-backed buyer may still ask for repairs. Disclose known problems either way, and check permits on past work.

Listing or cash: choosing a route in Hutto

Both paths work here. Putting the house on the market may bring a higher price, while a cash buyer trades some of that price for speed and for freedom from repairs and showings.

Hutto lies in south central Williamson County, about seven miles east of Round Rock, where State Highway 79 meets Farm Road 1660. Most housing is far newer than in older Texas towns, so a Hutto seller often competes with builders and neighbors offering similar floor plans. Condition, price and timing do the heavy lifting.

  • Go to market when the place looks sharp and your schedule bends.
  • Take cash when a move, a new job, an estate or a tenant dispute is pressing.
  • Sell to someone you know if you would rather skip fees and can handle the paperwork yourself.

From railroad stop to suburb: what it means for your house

Hutto began in 1876, when the railroad bought five acres from rancher James Emory Hutto and a depot, post office and general store followed. Cotton carried the early economy. The town peaked at 900 residents in 1928, slid to 538 by 1931 and incorporated in 1940. It fell as low as 400 in the 1960s before reviving, and the population was about 1,250 in 2000.

Since then Hutto has changed fast, and new construction surrounds the original core near the tracks and State Highway 79. Look up current counts with the City of Hutto before you quote any number in a listing.

  • Near the old core, expect larger lots and older systems.
  • In newer subdivisions, expect association rules and shared amenity fees.
  • Along the highway corridors, expect traffic noise to affect buyer interest.

Work out which of these describes your house, then price it against nearby sales of the same kind.

Williamson Central Appraisal District

The Williamson Central Appraisal District, known as WCAD, appraises Hutto property and keeps the parcel records. Its website has a parcel map, a taxpayer rights page, appeal information with prior-year results and a tool that breaks down what each local unit charges. You can also ask the chief appraiser for electronic notices.

Value is measured on January 1 and homestead notices go out around April 1. A protest to the review board generally has to be filed by mid-May. If you think the number is too high, consider protesting before you list, because a lower assessment trims carrying costs while the house waits for a buyer.

When Hutto tax bills arrive and when they are late

Statements show up around October 1 and are due by the end of January in most cases. Whatever remains unpaid turns delinquent on February 1.

If there is a will and the only debts are real estate liens, a muniment of title may avoid full administration. An affidavit of heirship is another option, though buyers and lenders need not accept it.

To keep the homestead exemption, heirs absent from the deed give the appraisal district proof of their interest along with a death certificate and a utility bill. A Williamson County probate attorney can tell you which path fits.

After a notary acknowledges the signature, the deed is filed with the Williamson County clerk. Texas sets a modest per-page charge, and a $25 add-on can apply when the buyer's mailing address is missing from the document.

Confirm who at the title company will file, and keep a recorded copy with your papers.

Behind on the mortgage in Hutto

Most Texas foreclosures never reach a courtroom. A default notice gives the borrower a short window to reinstate by paying what is owed. The sale notice follows about three weeks before an auction on a first Tuesday at the courthouse, which for a Hutto house means Williamson County.

Federal rules generally hold off foreclosure until a home loan is more than four months behind. Selling first, whether through a listing or to a cash buyer, can leave you with proceeds that an auction might not.

What to line up before you take an offer

Order matters here. Start with your latest Williamson County tax statement and, if a loan exists, a payoff figure, so you know what has to be cleared at closing. Next, find out whether your lot sits in an association and ask for the dues balance. Then decide whether the house is better priced against its newer neighbors or against the older homes near the railroad corridor.

When offers come in, compare closing dates, who pays title charges and whether the buyer needs financing. A cash buyer skips the lender appraisal, so the timeline is shorter and the paperwork lighter. Whichever you pick, the title company will check taxes and liens before the deed is signed, which is why a payoff and a tax statement in hand save days.

How the days run between offer and keys

A listing sale in Hutto usually unfolds in this order: showings, an offer, an inspection with a repair negotiation, an appraisal if the buyer borrows, then title work and signing. Each step can reopen the price. A cash sale compresses the list, since the buyer often waives the appraisal and may accept the house without repairs.

Whichever way you go, ask the buyer to name the closing date in the offer itself, and ask who covers title charges and recording. If the house has a tenant, tie that date to the lease end so nobody has to hunt for a gap. Sellers who skip this conversation tend to learn about it at the closing table, when a new cost appears and the schedule shifts by weeks.

Why protest before you list

A protest costs nothing but a little time. If the review board lowers your value, the bill that comes due while the house sits on the market drops with it, and buyers who see the lower assessment form a better first impression of the monthly cost. Gather recent sales of similar houses nearby, since WCAD publishes prior-year appeal results that give a feel for how others have fared. The Williamson Central Appraisal District, called WCAD. Its site has appeal information, a parcel map and a tax breakdown tool.

Mid-May for most protests, or a month after notice if that is later.

Yes, ten percent a year on a residence homestead, apart from new improvements.

How soon must an heir offer a will for probate?

Four years after death in general, though a court can accept a later filing for good reason.

The count was 18,694 in 2000 and 36,244 by 2015. A city that doubled in fifteen years has many newer subdivisions, and buyers often weigh a Schertz house against similar ones in neighboring suburbs. When you talk to buyers, name your subdivision and be straight about the roof, the mechanical systems and the lot.

Which county and school district serve you

Your tax statement answers that. Guadalupe County parcels go through the Guadalupe Appraisal District, whose member list includes the City of Schertz and Schertz-Cibolo-UC ISD. Parcels in Bexar or Comal County use those counties' districts.

Outdoor building work runs weekdays from 7 a.m. to 6 p.m. and Saturdays from 9 a.m. to 5 p.m. The city prohibits outdoor work on Sundays. The division's counter hours follow the same schedule.

Permits matter at sale time. If a room, deck or wall opening went in without one, a buyer's inspector may spot it. An as is cash buyer will likely price that risk, while the lender behind a conventional buyer may ask for a fix first. Ask the division what is on file before you list.

Working with the Guadalupe Appraisal District

You will find a parcel search portal on the district's site, along with online filing for homestead, disabled veteran and surviving spouse exemptions. Paper forms are still offered at the offices. Its Appraisal Review Board hears appeals at the main office in Seguin, and a taxpayer liaison officer attends on hearing days. Reach the liaison at 830.303.3313 extension 309.

One mail warning applies. Since late December 2025, USPS postmarks in Texas show the date of automated processing instead of the day you drop an item off. A paper form with a deadline should go to a post office counter, where you can request a hand-stamped postmark.

Bills arrive near October 1, with January 31 as the deadline. Any balance left at closing is paid from your proceeds, so request the county's payoff number early.

Behind on the mortgage or the taxes

Before a Texas lender can foreclose, a notice of sale has to go out, and the auction happens on a first Tuesday. A private sale ahead of that day can protect equity that an auction might send to junior lien holders first.

Overdue taxes add cost quickly. Penalties begin February 1 and reach 12 percent by July 1. A few collectors offer installment plans on a residence homestead, so phone the tax office sooner rather than later.

Comparing offers side by side

Offers rarely look alike on paper. One buyer pays title and recording costs, another expects you to. One closes in days, another needs weeks for financing. List each in a simple chart: price, repair credits, who covers closing costs, closing date and what happens if the title search turns up a lien. Add the county tax balance you will owe at closing, since it comes out of your proceeds no matter who buys. The highest number is not always the largest check.

Splitting the tax bill at closing

Most Schertz sales settle the year's tax by days of ownership, though your contract has the final say. Suppose you close in the spring: the new bill will not exist until October 1, so the title company works from the prior figure and adjusts later if the parties agreed to. Read that clause before you sign. If you sell after the bill arrives and have not paid it, expect the whole amount to be withheld from your check until the county confirms the payoff. Keep a copy of the receipt when you do pay, and give your buyer the account number so they can find the parcel on the district portal.

A note on parcels near the county line

If your lot is close to the line, call the Guadalupe Appraisal District or the other county's district and ask them to confirm the account number, then check that the legal description on your deed matches. A mismatch between the deed and the tax record is a common cause of closing delays. Neighbors who share a fence can still have different districts, and the title company will want the one that applies to you. Keep the confirmation email or a note of who you spoke to.

Selling with a tenant

A rented house can be sold. Some buyers will keep the lease running, and otherwise you can end the tenancy first. Ending it means written notice, a justice court case and, after final judgment, a writ of possession.

If the tenant pays on time and keeps the place clean, rent can continue right up to closing. If rent has stopped, ask whether the buyer will deal with the removal after closing.

Deeds and inherited houses

A deed reaches the public record through the county clerk, after a notary or other authorized officer witnesses the signature. Since Schertz crosses county lines, double check the clerk before you go.

An inherited house follows whatever route the estate allows.

  • If a will went through probate, an executor's deed or court order follows.
  • When real estate liens are the estate's only debts, a muniment of title can transfer the house.
  • An heirship affidavit is only a sworn statement filed with the clerk, and buyers or title companies may refuse to rely on it.

Before listing, ask a title company which route applies.

Offer to closing

Cash deals follow a short path. You accept in writing, and the title company opens a file, searches the parcel for liens and open tax, and, because Schertz touches three counties, confirms which clerk will record the deed. Next comes a closing date, a signing in front of a notary and your proceeds, minus any tax balance. Take photo ID and the deed or estate papers with you, and request the settlement statement a day before. With no lender on the buyer's side, nothing waits on an appraisal or loan approval, and that is where the time is saved.

Frequently asked questions

Which county is Schertz in?

Three, in practice: Bexar, Comal and Guadalupe. The city sits on the Bexar and Guadalupe line and spread into Comal County.

What if work on my Schertz house lacked a permit?

You can still sell, but expect questions. The Inspections Division issues permits and can be reached at (210) 619-1750.

Who pays the tax at a Schertz closing?

The contract sets the split, often by days of ownership. Get the amount owed from the county tax office before closing day.

What happens after the January 31 tax deadline?

The bill is delinquent from February 1, and penalty and interest begin. The penalty grows each month until it hits 12 percent on July 1.

Must a Schertz house be repaired before a cash sale?

Often not. Cash buyers frequently take houses in present condition, so weigh that offer against an agent's projection after repairs and commission.

Choosing a selling method in Prosper

A listing fits a clean, updated home. A private sale suits an owner with spare time and a buyer in mind. An as-is investor purchase makes sense for a house with deferred repairs or an owner up against a deadline. Prosper values run far above most Texas cities, so each option moves a lot of money.

What buyers at this price expect

Shoppers paying Prosper prices tend to want updated kitchens, strong internet and good schools. A buyer who closes as-is gives up some of that finish premium in exchange for certainty, which matters when you are selling on a deadline.

Appraisal districts and the tax calendar

Part of Prosper lies in Collin County and part in Denton County, so Collin Central Appraisal District or Denton Central Appraisal District handles your parcel. Both offer online property search and exemption information, and filing a homestead exemption costs nothing, so never pay a company that offers to do it for a fee.

  • Value date: January 1, the day the tax lien attaches.
  • Notices of value: April or later, with a protest window that ends May 15 or 30 days after delivery, whichever comes later.
  • Bills: from October 1, normally payable by January 31.
  • Homestead cap: once the exemption is in place, taxable value on the home cannot climb more than 10% a year.

Denton CAD's site carries a homestead value limitation page and a notice about canceled or reduced exemptions, a reminder that exemption records get reviewed. Check yours before you list, because a buyer's lender will look at the account.

Code compliance in Prosper

The Town of Prosper's Health and Code Compliance Division inspects properties and investigates complaints about nuisances and zoning violations. Fixing the usual problems before a buyer visits saves a delay.

  • High grass and unmanaged lawns

  • Junk in the yard

The division's office is at 250 W First Street, phone 972-569-1079. Development services also publishes a monthly report on permits, certificates of occupancy and new applications, and the Planning and Zoning calendar shows what is coming near you.

Peeling paint, a tired roof or stale carpet reads as a discount in a market where most homes are owner-occupied and well kept.

If you cannot spend on repairs, say so up front and price the house for an as-is buyer. If you can, fix the visible items first and keep receipts, because a buyer's inspector will ask about them.

Comparing offers on a Prosper house

Measure each offer by the cash you keep after every cost is paid. A higher retail price can leave you with less once repairs, concessions, carrying costs and months of waiting are subtracted.

  • Order a payoff letter from the lender to learn your minimum.

With owner costs of $4,000 a month or more on a mortgage, a few extra months on the market can cost real money. A direct sale stops those costs at closing. A listing may still win on price, so run both numbers before you decide, and read the title commitment before closing day.

Paperwork, estates and mortgage deadlines

Recording happens in Collin or Denton County, whichever holds the parcel, and the clerk charges per page. The state clerk manual sets the base figures and adds records fees.

After an owner's death, a will may be offered for probate within four years. When there is no will and the estate is $75,000 or less outside the homestead, an heir may ask a court to approve a small estate affidavit. Heirs need a recorded deed or affidavit before a title company will insure a sale.

On a loan in default, Texas lenders allow 20 days to cure after the default notice and must send a sale notice at least 21 days before a first-Tuesday auction. Starting your own sale before that date lets you choose the buyer and control the timing.

After you sign, the title company opens the file, searches the title and asks the lender for a payoff. A cash buyer shortens this because no lender appraisal or underwriting is needed. A financed buyer adds those steps, so ask each bidder how they plan to pay and how fast they can close.

Both. The town spans the two counties, so check which appraisal district lists your parcel before you look up taxes or file an exemption.

About $823,700 for 2020 to 2024. It is a median, so individual homes vary widely.

Yes. Texas appraisal districts charge nothing to file, so skip any company that asks for a fee.

The town's Health and Code Compliance Division at 250 W First Street, which inspects properties and investigates complaints.

How soon must I act on a mortgage default notice?

You have 20 days from the default notice to bring the loan current, and the lender's sale notice must come at least three weeks before the auction.
