A few Cibolo details shape any route: the city's place east of San Antonio, a county line nearby, and a permit office that works through one online portal.

Where Cibolo is

Cibolo lies in the far western corner of Guadalupe County, along FM 78 and FM 1103, with Interstate 10 to the south and Interstate 35 to the north. It is about 13 miles east of the San Antonio metropolitan area and sits in what the city calls the Metrocom, the northeast corner of Bexar County and the southwest corner of Guadalupe County. Schertz, Universal City, Selma, Live Oak, Garden Ridge, Converse and Kirby are neighbors.

Cibolo voted to become an independent township on October 9, 1965. It counted 440 people in 1970 and an estimated 37,061 in 2023, so many of the lots, surveys and permits you will deal with are recent.

Bexar County or Guadalupe County?

Cibolo is in Guadalupe County, but the surrounding Metrocom reaches into northeast Bexar County. Confirm the tax roll for your parcel on your statement before you set a price.

Valuation happens on January 1 everywhere in Texas, with notices mailed in spring and bills around October 1. A balance still open on February 1 picks up six percent plus one percent interest, then the penalty adds a point each month up to 12 percent in July.

School districts take $140,000 off a homestead, and the home's appraised value can climb no more than 10 percent a year. Your buyer files a fresh application once the sale closes. Call the county tax office for a balance and current rates instead of trusting an online estimator.

Permits and the Cibolo building office

Building codes and repair permits

Cibolo enforces the 2021 editions of the International Building, Residential, Energy Conservation, Plumbing, Fuel Gas, Mechanical, Swimming Pool and Spa, and Fire Codes, along with the 2023 National Electrical Code, under Ordinance 1475. Local amendments are listed on the city's Codes and Fees pages.

Before starting repairs, ask the office whether the work needs a permit. If you are selling as-is instead, put any unfinished work in writing for the buyer.

The city's FAQ adds detail for homeowners. Sheds need a permit when they rest on a permanent foundation, can't be moved after installation, or measure over 100 square feet. Water heaters, roof work, replacement HVAC, electrical, plumbing, irrigation and water softener permits can be issued at submittal without plan review. Residential plan reviews may take up to 10 business days, and the city has no process to expedite them.

Utilities and annexed land

City Utility Services at Cibolo City Hall, 200 South Main Street, handles water and wastewater accounts, and the city doesn't currently waive deposits or administration fees. Tell your buyer which utility account to open, and close your own as part of the move. Ask the department how much notice it needs for a final reading so you aren't billed after the sale.

If your land was recently annexed, the city's FAQ cites Texas Local Government Code Chapter 43 and lists what changes: voting rights and representation, public street maintenance, land use and density rules through zoning, and code enforcement. An agricultural exemption can continue while the property keeps qualifying, and the city doesn't expect address changes. A buyer of acreage on the edge of town should ask planning staff how zoning treats the parcel.

Probate, tenants and foreclosure

Texas puts different clocks on each.

  • Probate: a will can be probated for four years after death, and the court has discretion later. An affidavit of heirship may be filed with the clerk, yet a title company can decline it.
  • Tenant: the notice to vacate gives at least 3 days, a justice court case follows, and a writ of possession waits at least 6 days after judgment.
  • Foreclosure: a courthouse auction on a first Tuesday; if the lender later sues for a deficiency, it must do so within two years of the sale.

When two or more of these overlap, a cash buyer can often work around them. Even so, the title company needs documents that show who has authority to sign.

What a buyer will ask about

Expect three questions. Was every permit closed? Which county and appraisal district hold the parcel? Who has authority to sign? Put each answer on paper: the permit record printed from the portal, the tax statement, and the deed, with a payoff letter for any loan and probate papers if an owner has died.

If the property is acreage or was recently annexed, add a fourth: how the city's zoning treats the parcel. Planning staff can answer it before you list, and the buyer will want to hear it from you.

Before you list or take a cash offer

Start by looking up your permits and reading your county off the tax statement. Add a payoff figure for any loan. Then decide whether repairs are worth doing or whether to sell as-is and disclose what is unfinished. On closing day, loan and tax payoffs come out of your proceeds, you sign the deed before a notary, and it gets recorded. How do I check for an open permit on my Cibolo house?

Search the MGO Connect portal, or write permitting@cibolotx.gov, or call (210) 658-4175. Closing out an open permit before you list keeps the sale moving.

Which building codes does Cibolo enforce?

The 2021 International codes plus the 2023 National Electrical Code, by Ordinance 1475. Local amendments are on the Codes and Fees pages of the city website.

When do Texas property taxes become delinquent?

Anything unpaid at the end of January turns delinquent on February 1, and penalty and interest start building.

Can heirs sell a Cibolo house without a full probate case?

Ways to sell in Hurst, TX

An owner in Hurst can go with an agent, sell without one, or accept a direct cash purchase. Which fits depends on how much the house needs, what you still owe and when you need to be done.

Hurst is a compact suburb in the northeast corner of Tarrant County, north of Fort Worth near State Highways 121 and 10. The city has almost no raw land left, so almost every sale here is a resale of a house with some years on it. Owners who stage well do fine. Others face a roof, slab or kitchen that would cost more to fix than a listing would bring back, and a direct sale suits them.

  • Agent: the most eyes on the house, paid for with showings and a repair list after the buyer's inspector visits.
  • On your own: no listing commission, yet every contract and title form lands on your desk.

Why so many Hurst houses are from the postwar years

In the years after 1951, the town boomed. After Bell Aircraft announced a helicopter plant in 1951, residents voted 36 to 24 to incorporate. North East Mall opened in 1972, Dallas-Fort Worth International Airport in January 1974, and the population was above 27,200 by 1970.

That boom explains why many Hurst houses are fifty to seventy years old. Older houses can carry original wiring, plumbing and slab issues, and buyers will price those in. The city footprint has barely changed since, so you are selling in a mature neighborhood with established trees and close access to employers on both sides of the Trinity River.

Schools, permits and listing details

Hurst, Euless and Bedford share a school district. Put the district and the closest highways in your listing text. Shoppers filter on both.

Before you list, call the City of Hurst to confirm that any permits for completed work, such as a remodel or a fence, were closed out. An open permit is the kind of loose end that makes an underwriter hesitate.

Which office bills a Hurst homeowner?

Hurst sits in Tarrant County, so the county Tax Assessor-Collector handles collection. Its address is 100 E. Weatherford Street in Fort Worth, the number is 817-884-1100, and eight branch offices handle walk-in payments.

The county tax page offers a property tax estimator, a list of important tax dates and delinquent tax sale information. A truth-in-taxation database shows what each taxing unit has proposed for a given parcel. A bill is a stack of separate charges from the city, the county and the school district, so read each line on its own.

Late property tax charges

Anything unpaid after January 31 is delinquent from the next day. The charges stack up like this.

Late-payment charges on Texas property tax bills
TimingCharge
February 1A six percent penalty starts, with one percent interest
March through JuneEach month adds another percent of penalty and another percent of interest

Interest has no ceiling. The January lien can be enforced against the house even after it changes hands, which is why a buyer's title company cares about your unpaid tax as much as you do.

What if I am facing foreclosure on a Hurst house?

Texas lenders seldom go to court. They rely on the power of sale written into the deed of trust, and the timeline moves in fixed steps.

  • Then a sale notice goes up at the courthouse and into the clerk's files, three weeks before the auction.

Tenants and unwelcome occupants

The law separates tenants from squatters. A tenant is owed a written notice to vacate, and if the tenant stays, the landlord files in justice court. Someone who moved in with no right whatsoever falls under Property Code chapter 24B, so the owner can ask the sheriff or constable to remove them. That route is closed when the occupant is family or a past or present tenant, or when a suit is pending.

  • A hearing is set within a few weeks after the suit is filed.
  • Only a final judgment brings a writ of possession.
  • Removing someone wrongly can bring a lawsuit against the owner.

Before you file any removal request, talk it over with a Tarrant County attorney. Keeping an empty house locked, checked and insured is the simplest protection while it sits.

Preparing a Hurst house for a quick closing

A cash buyer in Hurst can often promise a closing within weeks. Someone financing with a mortgage needs an appraisal and underwriting first, and that stretches the calendar. Either way, decide before the first showing whether you will repair, sell as-is or price for someone who plans to renovate. Houses built in the postwar decades often draw buyers who expect to update the kitchen, wiring or plumbing, so a fair as-is price can find a taker quickly. Before signing with anyone, request proof of funds or a lender letter, and get in writing who pays for the title policy and recording.

A step-by-step path from decision to closing

Step one is choosing the route. Listing means showings, an inspection, repair requests and then a lender's schedule. Selling alone hands you the contract and title forms. Cash usually skips the repairs and moves faster. For most Hurst sellers the deciding question is how many weeks they can afford to wait.

Step two is paperwork: the deed, a payoff letter when a loan exists and the newest Tarrant County tax statement. Have the title company check for liens or unfinished permits. Step three is a side-by-side look at the written offers, comparing dates, closing costs and each buyer's reaction to inspection findings.

Step four is the signing. A notary must be present so the deed can go to the county clerk, and the recorded copy belongs in your files.

Taxes owed at closing

Back taxes do not require cash up front. At closing the agent can settle the balance out of your proceeds, because the title company wants that lien gone before it insures the new owner. Get a current statement from the Tarrant County tax office early. On a homestead, ask whether an installment arrangement fits before the penalty reaches 12 percent in July. Selling ahead of that step often costs less than waiting for it.

Tarrant County. Hurst is in the northeastern quadrant, just north of Fort Worth.

The Tarrant County Tax Assessor-Collector, reachable at 817-884-1100 or at the Fort Worth office on East Weatherford Street.

Does selling stop a foreclosure?

Yes, if the sale closes before the auction and pays off the loan. Auctions come monthly, so begin early.

When does a Texas tax bill go late?

Once January 31 passes in most cases, with penalty and interest running from February 1.

Must I hire a lawyer to sell in Hurst?

The state does not require it. A lien, a probate matter or a foreclosure notice is still worth a lawyer's time.

The city lies in southwestern Dallas County, with 40,706 residents, 14,272 housing units and a homeownership rate of 65.3 percent.   • On your own: the fee stays with you, and so do the contract and disclosure duties.

Rental certificate of occupancy

A single-family house, duplex or townhome with tenants must hold a Rental Certificate of Occupancy before anyone moves in. That is the city's residential rental registration program at work.

An owner registers the property, passes an interior and exterior inspection, and then applies for the certificate. Registration is renewed every year by December 31. The certificate is renewed after two years, when tenants change, or when ownership changes during the registration year. No certificate is issued until taxes, liens, utility charges and code issues are cleared.

That last rule matters if you have tenants. A buyer will ask whether the certificate is current, and open code issues can stall a closing. Call the Permitting Department at (972) 780-5000 to request an inspection.

Rental fees and penalties

Confirm amounts with the Permitting Department before you pay, because the city's master fee schedule controls.

Duncanville residential rental program charges
ChargeAmount

Schedule the inspection within 30 days of registration or of a failed inspection, or a $50 late fee applies. A failed property gets 30 days to correct violations, and the first reinspection is free. Inspectors look at the roof, walls and foundations, plumbing, electrical and mechanical systems, pests, and nuisance items such as high grass, junk and inoperable vehicles.

Showing a rented house

Start with the registration, then the inspection record, then the tenant. Owners must tell the city two days before an eviction and supply a clean-up plan for personal items within a day afterward, so a sale that involves removing a tenant adds city steps to the court steps.

The eviction process itself comes from state law. Where the lease sets no other period, the landlord serves a written notice to vacate with at least three days' warning, files in justice court, and may obtain a writ of possession six days after final judgment. A buyer who takes a rented house inherits those timelines unless you resolve them first. If the tenant is staying, give the buyer the lease, the deposit amount and the rent history. If the tenant is leaving, set a firm move-out date in writing and walk the unit together so the condition is documented before keys change hands. Take dated photos of each room for your own file.

  • Confirm the certificate is current and the last inspection passed.
  • Write down the lease end date and any deposit held.

Paperwork for selling a rental

Pull together your registration confirmation, the current certificate and the newest inspection result. A certificate is renewed after two years, on a change of tenant, or on a change of owner within the registration year, so your sale may mean a fresh one for the buyer.

The manager or agent for a registered rental must live or work inside the North Central Texas Council of Governments area, and the unit's maximum occupancy is fixed when it registers. A buyer who plans to hire a distant manager should know that before committing.

  • Copies of every lease and the dates tenants moved in.
  • Receipts for repairs made after a failed inspection.
  • Proof that taxes, liens and utility charges are paid.

Taxes and recording

Your deed is recorded in Dallas County, while the Dallas Central Appraisal District sets your value. Texas has no statewide property tax, and local units set rates.

A tax bill left unpaid after January 31 is delinquent from February 1. The lien lands on the January 1 owner, which is why the title company pays off the current year when you close. The county clerk records a deed only after the signature has been acknowledged, and the title company can quote the clerk's fees.

Back taxes can sometimes be spread out. Some collectors offer plans of up to 36 months, and a homestead owner may demand one. Check your balance with the Dallas County tax office.

Inherited house or mortgage behind

Both situations carry deadlines in Texas, and a sale can still work. Four years is the probate window for a will. Depending on the facts, a small estate affidavit, a muniment of title or an affidavit of heirship may do instead, and the buyer's title company has the last word.

Under a federal rule, a lender usually cannot begin foreclosure on a home loan until it is over 120 days delinquent, and a lender has a two-year window to sue for any shortfall. Those limits give a seller some room to act, though a written payoff request is the safest first step.

After a default notice, you may reinstate the loan by paying what is overdue within 20 days. An auction notice follows, and a closing ahead of the sale ends the foreclosure on that loan.

What a cash sale skips

A cash buyer has no lender appraisal to wait for, so loan approval drops out of the schedule. City rules do not disappear, though. If a rental inspection is pending or a reinspection is open, ask the buyer whether they will take the house that way.

If speed is the goal, clear open violations first and close out any failed inspection. A clean file widens the pool of buyers and shortens the questions at closing. Also gather the lease dates and deposit details so a buyer who wants the tenant to stay can decide quickly.

Before you sign anything, confirm in writing who is responsible for the certificate, the registration change and any late fee that may fall due near the closing date. Cash buyers who plan to keep the house as a rental will usually want that settled in the contract, and a clear answer helps them make an offer faster.

Frequently asked questions

Does Duncanville require rental registration?

Yes. A single-family house, duplex or townhome with tenants has to register and carry a Rental Certificate of Occupancy.

How often must a Duncanville rental be inspected?

At first registration, then every two years from the certificate, or sooner when tenants change.

What is the penalty for skipping Duncanville rental registration?

A Class C misdemeanor, with a fine of up to $2,000, separate from any other code violations.

Which school district serves Duncanville?

The city's schools belong to Duncanville Independent School District. Ask the district about the zone for a particular address.

Can a buyer rent out a Duncanville house by the night?

The rental registration program covers rentals of more than 30 days, so a stay-by-the-night plan is a separate question. Call the Permitting Department at (972) 780-5000 for the current rules before you promise anything.

Your choices for a quick Socorro sale

Three routes exist for Socorro owners: hire an agent, sell it yourself or take a cash bid. The right pick follows the house's age, its repairs and the state of the title. Socorro lies on State Highway 20 about ten miles southeast of downtown El Paso, so buyers compare it with the rest of the El Paso area.

  • Agent: reaches the most buyers, though you accept showings, repair requests after inspection and a lender's schedule.
  • Sale on your own: costs less, and you manage the contract and the title company.
  • Cash bid: fewer steps and an as-is sale, which suits repair needs, tenants and probate questions.

Before you ask for bids, collect the mortgage payoff, the newest tax bill and any utility balances. Then every buyer prices the same facts and you can compare offers fairly.

The Socorro housing market

Growth is quick in Socorro, and most homes are owner occupied. For July 1, 2025 the population estimate is 38,787, which is 13.1% above the 34,300 April 2020 base.

Owner households dominate and the population is young, so many buyers are families who watch monthly costs. Bilingual marketing, a clear explanation of the process and flexible showing times help reach them. Price realistically and document repairs so a buyer can see monthly costs clearly.

Streets, lots and utilities

Some subdivisions went up in the 1960s and 1970s with no paved streets, water or sewer lines. The Lower Valley Water District Authority brought water and sewage systems later. As a result, one street's history can differ sharply from the next. Ask the title company to review your legal description and any easements, and verify that your lot has water and sewer service.

Who appraises Socorro property

Every parcel of real and business personal property in El Paso County is valued by the El Paso Central Appraisal District. Its website carries a parcel search, exemption forms, a deadline calendar and a protest and appeals section. A Taxpayer Liaison Officer takes complaints about the Appraisal Review Board.

  • Texas fixes value and homestead eligibility as of January 1.
  • Homestead valuation notices go out about April 1.
  • The protest deadline is usually May 15, with a later cutoff when the notice reaches you after mid-April.
  • Bills are mailed near October 1 and turn delinquent after January 31.

For the rate on your own bill, ask the county tax office. If you buy a house, a first homestead claim should reach the appraisal district by the spring filing deadline.

Protesting your value

If the appraised value looks too high, use the protest and appeals section on the El Paso Central Appraisal District site. The deadline is usually May 15, so start by gathering what shows condition: repair estimates, photos and receipts. The Taxpayer Liaison Officer is there if you have a complaint about the review board. A lower value helps a buyer see lower monthly costs, which matters in a market where families watch every payment.

Questions to ask each buyer

Price is only one way Socorro bids differ. Find out who covers title and recording fees, how many days the buyer needs and whether the bid expects the house to stay as it is. Learn how an old lien or unpaid tax would be handled if the title search turns one up. With a tenant in place, ask if the buyer will honor the lease or wants the house vacant. Proof of funds and written answers should come before your signature.

What to bring to the title company

Having paperwork ready speeds closing. Take photo ID, the deed, your latest tax bill and, if a loan is open, the mortgage payoff statement. An inherited house calls for the will and any court papers, because probate or a small estate affidavit settles who may sign. For a rented house, add the lease. Before you sign, have the title company walk you through every line of the settlement statement.

Homestead breaks for sellers and buyers

Texas school districts knock $140,000 off the value of a principal residence. Owners who are over 65 or disabled get a further $60,000. Suppose you never claimed the exemption: whoever buys the house after January 1 can still apply for it for that same year.

The appraised value of a homestead may not rise more than 10 percent annually, and the cap starts on the January 1 following the first year the owner qualifies. An owner with a service-connected disability can take $5,000 to $12,000 off, based on the rating, and one rated fully disabled owes nothing on the home.

Late taxes

Overdue tax gets expensive fast. Once January 31 passes, the collector adds a six percent charge and one percent interest. Each month the penalty grows another percent until it hits 12 percent on July 1. Interest has no cap, and the taxing unit's attorney can tack on up to 20 percent.

A homestead owner may request an installment plan, which some collectors extend to 36 months, and can ask in writing for the penalty and interest to be waived. Because the lien follows the house, you cannot deliver clear title until the tax is settled. A sale can pay it off from your proceeds.

Floodplain rules

Floodplain rules can touch a sale. El Paso County's website cites Section 16.315 of the Texas Water Code, which tells local governments to adopt rules that limit flood losses, and Socorro sits near the Rio Grande. A lot near a channel or drain deserves a check with the county and the title company to learn if it lies in a regulated floodplain, ideally before you set an asking price. Flood insurance may be required there by lenders, and a buyer who finds out late could ask for a lower price.

Pricing a Socorro house

Socorro's middle owner-home price sits near $144,500, so a few thousand dollars of repair work is a large share of what a buyer pays. Show receipts for the roof, cooling and plumbing, and be candid about anything unfinished. A buyer paying cash may still lower a bid for visible work, but clear records keep the discount from growing. If you plan to list with an agent, ask for a written comparison of recent sales on your street so the asking price rests on facts.

Paperwork at closing

The El Paso County Clerk records Socorro deeds. An authorized officer must acknowledge your signature before it is filed, and the fee, charged per page, shows up on your closing statement.

Inheritance, foreclosure and tenants

A will can be opened for probate in Texas as late as four years after a death. For a smaller estate, the small estate affidavit fits only if assets come to $75,000 or less once the homestead and exempt property are set aside. Foreclosure auctions happen on the first Tuesday of the month after 21 days' notice, and a borrower can reinstate within 20 days of the default notice by paying the arrears. When a landlord wants a tenant out, the case starts with a written notice to vacate, three days by default.

Cash sale step by step

After you accept a bid, a title company starts a file, runs a lien search and requests a payoff figure from the tax office. Next you pick a closing date, sign in front of a notary and collect your proceeds. No buyer loan means no lender appraisal, so any delay usually traces to title work, probate or a lien.

Where is Socorro located?

Socorro is in El Paso County, around ten miles southeast of downtown El Paso on State Highway 20.

What does a typical Socorro owner's home cost?

The middle price of an owner's home is $144,500 for 2020 to 2024. Your house may be higher or lower depending on size, age and repairs.

Which office sets the value of my Socorro house for tax?

The El Paso Central Appraisal District. It runs a property search and posts exemption forms and a calendar of deadlines.

Is unpaid tax taken from my sale money?

Yes. Whatever is owed comes out at closing, and this year's bill is split by closing date. The January 1 lien stays attached until it is cleared.

Will anyone buy a Socorro house that needs work?

Cash buyers commonly buy as is, whereas a lender may demand repairs before it finances a purchase. Either way, expect the offer to account for the work.

City permits that touch a sale

Selling a rental or Airbnb

Renting the house out changes who needs notice and what a purchaser inherits. Under city rules, a short-term rental is a single-family home let for 30 days or less. To operate one you need an inspection and a permit, processed by an outside vendor called Host Compliance.

The application wants a driver's license copy, the inspection report showing a pass, a floor plan with room sizes and a signed Chapter 26 acknowledgement. Buildings with three or more units need a multi-family permit, which lapses every December 31 and costs $13 per dwelling unit. A violation brings a $150 inspection fee per unit or building.

Should the new owner want to keep renting, check with Code Enforcement on whether the permit carries over or has to be reissued. When a tenant lives there and the lease says nothing about it, the usual first step is a written notice to vacate of three days or more. Any eviction case goes to justice court.

Behind on the mortgage

Lenders on Texas mortgages generally skip the courtroom, so a missed-payment problem can turn into an auction faster than owners expect. Once the default letter lands, the borrower typically has 20 days to make up the arrears. The sale notice then has to be out three weeks or more before the auction date.

Auctions take place early in the month on a Tuesday, during the day. Notices go up at the courthouse and into the county clerk's records. If the house sells and the price falls short, the lender has two years to bring a deficiency suit. When there is money left over, junior liens are paid ahead of you.

Property tax and filing steps

Homestead owners get a notice near April 1. A protest is generally due by mid-May, or 30 days after the notice if that lands later.

Statements show up in October and go delinquent once January 31 passes. Since the January 1 lien rides with the land, closing normally divides that year's tax between the two parties. Call the county tax office for your parcel's balance and the city for its rate.

The new deed is filed with the clerk of the county where the house stands. That clerk's fee schedule sets what recording costs.

An organized folder helps every kind of buyer. Begin with the recorded deed, your latest tax statement, the loan payoff letter and the survey. Add receipts for roof, HVAC, plumbing and electrical jobs, and any city permit records for additions.

Hand copies to the escrow office early. A lien or a misspelled name is far easier to fix weeks out. Ask the city, too, what becomes of a rental license when the owner changes.

What a cash sale skips

An investor purchase usually removes the steps that eat weeks: no lender appraisal, no buyer financing contingency and no repair negotiation after the inspection. For a landlord with a tenant in place, that can mean the lease is simply assigned. For a house with an old roof or a code question, it means the buyer prices the problem instead of asking you to cure it.

The tradeoff is the number. Ask each investor for a written net figure, then set it next to what a listing would leave after repairs, commission and the extra weeks of carrying costs.

What to say in your listing

Stick to facts a buyer can check: year built, roof age, the last HVAC service and typical utility bills. If you are unsure about code history at your address, the city's Community Services department can tell you.

Disclosure forms should be plain and easy to translate, since many buyers here speak another language at home. After you accept an offer, keep a copy of every signed form. On closing day, compare the settlement statement with the contract, and confirm that any rental or short-term rental account has been closed out.

Yes, when the price fits. Buyers have plenty of nearby sales to compare, and your house is priced on its own condition rather than the $364,600 median.

Is a certificate of occupancy part of a Farmers Branch sale?

Ask Code Enforcement. The city lists a certificate of occupancy as a commercial requirement, so call before listing to learn what applies to a residential change of ownership.

Can I hold an estate sale before selling my Farmers Branch home?

Yes, with registration. City code allows two garage-type sales a year, each up to three consecutive days, and estate sales fall under that rule.

What does a short-term rental permit cost in Farmers Branch?

It costs $120 per year and requires a passed inspection first. Applications run through a vendor called Host Compliance.

How long does a Texas foreclosure take after a notice is sent?

Borrowers get a 20-day window to catch up after the default letter, and the auction cannot come sooner than 21 days after the sale notice. The sale itself is held on a Tuesday early in the month.

Selling a house in La Porte

In Harris County on the Gulf Coast, La Porte is an older, industry-linked city where flood risk and insurance arise in nearly every buyer conversation. Houses with a clear flood history, current permits and an organized paper file sell faster.

The city was incorporated on August 10, 1892, making it the oldest incorporated town in east Harris County. It grew into what it calls a bedroom community for industry after World War II, NASA and the Bayport Channel. The result is older bayside cottages, mid-century subdivisions and newer homes within a few miles of each other.

How flood risk affects a sale

Price, insurance and buyer questions all feel it. The city considers every property susceptible to flooding and lists Galveston Bay, Little Cedar Bayou, Clear Creek and Armand Bayou among the main water sources across roughly 20 square miles.

Buyers will recall Tropical Storm Allison in 2001, Hurricane Ike in 2008, two floods in 2015 and Hurricane Harvey in 2017. Lenders and buyers often ask which FEMA zone the house is in, so check before you list.

  • Call the city engineer or use the city's GIS map to see your parcel's flood zone.
  • Gather any elevation certificate, past claim records and repair receipts.
  • Know that a new flood policy has a 30-day waiting period.
  • Remember that new and substantially improved structures must sit at least 12 inches above base flood elevation.

Waterfront history and older homes

Sylvan Beach Park anchored the early economy, and the Sylvan Beach pier was badly damaged by Hurricane Ike in 2008 and has since been rebuilt. Waterfront buyers will ask about storm history and insurance, so be ready with dates and records.

If you own an older home near the ship channel or the bay, ask the city engineer which FEMA map applied when the house was built. That historical map can matter in a dispute with a lender or insurance agent. Collect repair receipts for the roof, windows and drainage, since inspectors check those first.

Permits for repairs before selling

A permit is required if you work in the floodplain or do substantial repairs. Development in the floodplain without a permit is illegal, and that includes new construction, filling, grading and paving.

A structure counts as new construction when repair or improvement cost equals or exceeds 50 percent of its market value. That rule can affect a buyer who plans a big renovation on a damaged house. Call the Planning and Development Department before you start work, and keep permit records for the buyer.

How taxes are split between buyer and seller

They are usually prorated at closing on estimated figures, and the real bill is worked out later in the year, so the final amount can differ from the estimate. The split does not change who is liable to the taxing unit.

If the house has only a general homestead exemption, it normally stays for the whole tax year, and the buyer files a new application for the next year. Timing an offer around flood questions

In La Porte the buyer's first call is often to an insurance agent. A strong quote helps the deal, and a surprising one can end it. Tell serious buyers early where the house sits on the FEMA map and share the elevation certificate if you have one, so they can get a quote before the option period runs out. Because a new flood policy has a 30-day waiting period, a buyer who delays that call may close without coverage in force. A cash buyer is less sensitive to this, which is one reason damaged or low-lying houses often sell for cash.

The step-by-step path to closing in La Porte

First, learn your flood zone and gather the elevation certificate, claim records and repair receipts. Second, choose a route: a listing with repairs finished, an as-is cash sale or a private deal. Third, once you accept an offer, the title company opens a file, orders a payoff from any lender and checks taxes and liens. Fourth, you sign before a notary and the deed goes to the Harris County records. Each step goes faster when the flood paperwork is done before the first showing.

Buyers using loans will also order an appraisal and an insurance quote, and either can change the price or the date. Cash buyers skip the appraisal and decide faster. Ask for the closing date in writing, and ask who is paying title charges, so nothing is settled at the closing table for the first time.

Is flood insurance needed to sell a house in La Porte?

It is not required to sell, but buyers and lenders often ask for it. Basic homeowner's insurance does not cover flood, and a new flood policy has a 30-day wait before it takes effect.

Who collects property tax on a La Porte house?

The Harris County Tax Office collects it, and the Harris Central Appraisal District sets value and handles exemptions. Taxes usually become delinquent on February 1 of the next year.

Can I sell a La Porte house that has flood damage?

Yes, as is or after repairs. If repair cost reaches 50 percent of the building's market value, the city treats it like new construction and requires permits and an elevation certificate.

When is the La Porte homestead filing window?

Regular applications are due between January 1 and April 30. Late applications are accepted for a general exemption up to two years after taxes became delinquent.

Do buyers pay La Porte taxes after closing?

Yes, the buyer owns the bill from closing forward, with the year's taxes prorated at closing on estimated figures. The tax office calculates the final bill later in the year.

Which districts cover your house

The Pharr-San Juan-Alamo Independent School District, established on March 24, 1919, took in all of the schools in San Juan. Check your tax bill for the district listed on your parcel.

On the Hidalgo County Appraisal District website you will find a property search, an online portal for filing exemptions and appeals, and a homestead portal for homestead and over 65 applications. You can reach the district's customer service line at 956-381-8466.

The city's interactive GIS map shows zoning and city limits. It also tells you whether a location falls under Hidalgo County Precinct 1 or 2 for services outside city jurisdiction, and it helps you work out whether you need city permits or utilities.

If your lot is near the edge of town, begin with a call to this office. Whether a parcel sits inside city limits changes who regulates a garage conversion, an addition or a fence. It is also the place to ask whether a permit is on file for earlier work, a question buyers raise.

The Virgen de San Juan del Valle Shrine, built in 1954, has drawn pilgrims and tourists for decades, and a new shrine was dedicated in April 1980. The city is also known as home of the Bougainvillea Trail of Texas. Visitor traffic gives the city a steady identity, though it does not set your price. When you describe the house, name your block, its distance to schools and the shrine, and any recent work.

Delinquent tax penalties

Tax bills come in the fall. A bill not paid by February 1 counts as delinquent.

How Texas delinquent tax penalties build up
WhenPenalty or interest
February 1Six percent penalty and one percent interest
Each month until July 1Penalty continues to rise one percent a month; interest is one percent a month
July 1Penalty becomes 12 percent
After attorney referralUp to 20 percent more if the unit has an attorney contract

A written request to waive penalty and interest has to be filed before the 181st day after the delinquency date. Installment plans of up to 36 months exist at some collectors and are required only for a residence homestead.

Selling with taxes owed

Each January 1 the tax lien attaches to the property. Any balance still open is normally paid out of what you receive at the closing table. An open bill can slow a sale but need not block it. The county tax office can give you a payoff figure, which your title company then builds into the settlement. If a payment plan is running, say so, so the right balance gets quoted.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy San Juan houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Getting your paperwork ready

A little preparation shortens any sale. Pull your parcel up in the Hidalgo County Appraisal District property search and note the value, owner name and tax history. If you filed an exemption or an appeal through the portal, keep the confirmation. If you hold a homestead or over 65 exemption, tell your buyer, because the new owner has to apply on their own. Gather receipts for roof, drainage and electrical work, and ask the city planning office whether permits were filed for any addition, garage conversion or fence. A buyer who sees permits and receipts up front has fewer reasons to lower the bid.

  • Photo ID and the recorded deed.
  • Newest tax bill, plus a payoff figure from the county tax office.
  • Repair receipts and permit records.
  • Names of any tenants and a copy of the lease.

Appealing your appraisal

If the appraised value looks too high, you can protest it. The appraisal district portal accepts appeals online, and the Comptroller's taxpayer pamphlet explains the protest process. The truth in taxation site shows the rates each taxing unit has proposed, so you can see how value and rate combine on your bill. A lower value helps a buyer, and it can help you if you still own the house when the bill arrives.

Deeds, probate and tenants

Deeds for San Juan land go to the Hidalgo County Clerk, and the signer must appear before a notary or other authorized officer.

Inherited houses start with the will, which can be probated up to four years after the death. If liens on the land are the estate's only debts, a muniment of title is one way to put the house in the heirs' names. A title company can tell the heirs which paper a buyer's lender will take.

A tenant complicates timing. Getting a tenant out takes a written notice and then a justice court case. Selling with the tenant in place skips that process and keeps rent coming until closing.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

Foreclosure and houses needing major work

Foreclosure in Texas is usually nonjudicial and ends in a public auction. A sale before that date can protect your equity, and excess proceeds after an auction go to junior liens before the former owner.

Houses that need a new roof, drainage work or electrical repairs fit an as is buyer, who absorbs the work. In return you accept a lower price and skip the contractors and the repair requests.

What to expect with a cash sale

A cash sale here goes in stages. Step one is a walk-through, after which the buyer names a price. Once you accept, the title company opens a file and searches for liens, including taxes. Next you choose a closing date, sign at the title company's office and collect the proceeds. With no buyer loan involved, nobody waits on a lender's appraisal. Take a photo ID and your deed along, and ask to see the settlement statement before the day itself.

Frequently asked questions

What school district is San Juan in?

The Pharr-San Juan-Alamo Independent School District, established in 1919, took in all of the schools in San Juan. Your tax bill confirms it for your parcel.

Who appraises property in San Juan?

Hidalgo County Appraisal District, which runs a property search plus an online portal for exemptions and appeals. Call 956-381-8466 for help.

Does San Juan have a planning office I can call about permits?

Yes. The Planning and Zoning department handles permits, zoning and rezoning at 956-223-2220. Its GIS map helps you check city limits and zoning.

When do unpaid taxes become delinquent?

February 1 for most bills, which is when the six percent penalty and one percent interest begin. The 12 percent penalty arrives July 1.

Can an unpaid tax bill stop a San Juan sale?

Usually not. Any balance is paid from your proceeds at closing, and the county tax office can quote the payoff.

Selling in Greenville?
We buy Greenville houses as-is, with no commission, no repairs and no closing costs to you.

Is a cash sale the fastest way out?

Frequently, yes. With cash, no lender appraisal sits between you and a closing date. A standard listing can still pay off for a home in good shape, but expect to prep the house and sit through showings.

Greenville is the Hunt County seat, roughly sixty miles northeast of Dallas along Interstate 30, so the buyer pool is smaller than in the inner suburbs. Every month a house sits unsold adds taxes, insurance, utilities and lawn care. Set that total against the lower number a cash buyer may offer.

  • Agent listing: fits an updated house and an easygoing timeline.
  • Private sale: fits owners comfortable handling contracts and disclosures.
  • Cash offer: fits an empty house, an estate property or one with postponed repairs.

Greenville at a glance

Greenville was established in 1846, the year the legislature created Hunt County, and incorporated in 1852. Blackland soil made it a cotton market, and railroads arrived between 1880 and 1896. Interstate 30, U.S. highways 380, 69 and 67, and State highways 224, 66 and 34 all pass through, which helps commuters who work toward Dallas.

The 2000 population was 23,960, after a peak near 27,750 in 1990. Local events such as the Hunt County Fair in August and the Cotton Pickin' Arts and Crafts Jubilee in November bring visitors, and a tidy yard during those weeks helps a showing.

Older housing in Greenville

Growth came in waves, and each wave left houses behind. Homes near the downtown square date from the cotton boom, and others went up for the workforce at the wartime airfield and the aircraft plants that followed. Plenty of those houses are decades old and may still have their original wiring, plumbing and roofs.

If your property dates from one of those periods, say so to buyers, and ask Hunt CAD for the year-built on its record so your description matches. Receipts for roof, plumbing and electrical work, kept in one folder, give a buyer something solid to read.

Property taxes for a Greenville owner

The Hunt County Appraisal District, known as Hunt CAD, values every parcel of real and business personal property in the county. The county tax assessor-collector mails the bill. On the district's website you can search properties, apply for a homestead exemption and use a truth-in-taxation tool. No one should charge you to file a homestead application, because the district itself charges nothing.

Texas collects no statewide property tax. Instead the county, the city and the school district each apply their own rate to your house, and the appraisal district supplies the January 1 value. Bills go out near October 1, and whatever is unpaid on February 1 turns delinquent and begins accruing penalty and interest.

Thinking of splitting a tract before selling? Ask Hunt CAD about its cutoff dates for splits and combines, because a late request can roll into the next tax year.

  • Protests are usually due May 15, unless your notice arrived late enough to extend the window.
  • If the review board rules against you, the dispute can go on to district court or arbitration.
  • The Hunt County tax office or the district can tell you the current rate for your address.

Exemptions that can lower a bill

More than one applies. School districts must give a homestead exemption, and any taxing unit may layer on a local one. Owners who are older or disabled receive extra relief, and a disabled veteran follows a sliding scale tied to the disability rating.

Texas homestead and disabled veteran exemption amounts
Exemption typeAmount
School district residence homestead$140,000
Age 65 or older, or disabled (school districts)Additional $60,000
Disabled veteran, 10 to 29 percent ratingUp to $5,000
Disabled veteran, 30 to 49 percent ratingUp to $7,500
Disabled veteran, 50 to 69 percent ratingUp to $10,000
Disabled veteran, 70 to 100 percent ratingUp to $12,000

At a 100 percent rating, the whole residence homestead can be exempt. Heirs whose names are not on the recorded deed must prove their interest to qualify, and Hunt CAD runs a page for people who inherited a home.

City permits and local rules

Greenville's Permits and Inspections Division reviews building permit applications and inspects construction on private property. Permit types include residential construction, pools and accessory buildings, along with electrical, mechanical, plumbing, concrete and energy work. The city takes applications through an online permitting portal.

Built a deck, garage or addition without a permit? Say so to the buyer and ask the city how to bring it into compliance. Open permits sometimes turn up during title work and hold up a closing. Before advertising a house for lodging, ask the planning office about short-term rentals and rental registration, and get an answer instead of guessing there is no rule.

Someone is living in a vacant house

Against some trespassers, Texas offers something faster than eviction court. Under Property Code chapter 24B you may ask the sheriff or constable for removal when all four of these are true:

  • The person stayed after being told to go.
  • The home was closed to the public.
  • No lawsuit is pending between you.
  • The person is neither family nor a current or former tenant.

Removing the wrong person can bring a lawsuit against whoever asked for it. Former tenants must go through justice court. Settle who is living there before you advertise.

When the lender threatens foreclosure

A sale is still possible if it closes before the auction. Foreclosure auctions here are held on the first Tuesday of a month, following a notice of sale sent at least 21 days earlier. Once that notice arrives, treat the auction date as a hard deadline.

Closing first pays the lender out of the proceeds and leaves any equity with you. Get a written payoff figure from the servicer, and hand the notice to a cash buyer immediately so the title company can build the schedule around it.

Selling a house with open taxes or liens

Debt on the property will not block a sale, but it gets repaid first. Taxes attach to the parcel as a lien, so any unpaid year is subtracted from your proceeds at the title company, as are a mortgage or equity loan.

Before meeting buyers, make a list with a figure beside each item: loan balances, back taxes, code or permit fees and HOA dues. Judge each offer by what remains once those are cleared, since the headline price says little about your bank balance. A charge that looks wrong deserves a question to the title company before you sign.

From offer to closing

Accepting an offer sends the file to a title company. It confirms who owns the house, asks each lender for a payoff letter, checks where your parcel stands on taxes, and drafts the deed and settlement statement.

Signing happens in front of a notary. After the deed is recorded, the title company settles your loans and any tax balance and sends you what is left. Ask what to bring, and agree on a move-out date so the keys change hands cleanly. Cash deals avoid the lender appraisal and underwriting, the usual sources of delay. Before you hand over the house, shut off or transfer utilities as of closing day and leave any manuals, remotes and spare keys for the buyer.

Frequently asked questions

Which office appraises property in Greenville, Texas?

The Hunt County Appraisal District appraises property in Hunt County, which includes Greenville. It also runs the homestead exemption portal and the protest process.

Is there a fee to file a homestead exemption in Hunt County?

No. Hunt CAD charges nothing for a residential homestead application, and owners should ignore any mailer asking for a fee.

When do Greenville protests have to be filed?

By May 15 in most cases, or later if your notice reached you after mid-April.

Will repairs on my Greenville house need city permits?

Most structural, electrical, plumbing and mechanical jobs do. Permits and Inspections reviews applications through the city's online portal.

May I sell a Greenville house the lender has threatened to foreclose on?

Yes, if the sale closes before the auction. The auction falls on a first Tuesday, at least 21 days after a notice of sale.

Texas side or Arkansas side

Start with the state line, because Texarkana is two cities. A house on the Texas side sits in Bowie County and follows Texas law. One across State Line Avenue in Arkansas follows Arkansas rules and is recorded in Miller County. This page covers the Texas side.

If you are unsure which side you are on, check the county printed on your tax bill or deed. Bowie means Texas. That one detail decides which laws, which appraisal district and which clerk apply to everything that follows.

For a Texas address, a quick sale usually takes one of three shapes, and each suits a different seller.

  • Cash purchase: no mortgage to approve, so closing waits only on clean title.
  • Agent listing: a bigger audience, paired with inspections and lender deadlines.
  • Sale with repair terms: after inspection the buyer asks for fixes or a credit toward them.

Who buys in Texarkana

The Texas city grew from a railroad junction founded on December 8, 1873, and it was chartered in 1876. The two halves keep separate mayors, councils and officials, yet share fire service, food and dairy inspection, sewage disposal and some recreation. The Federal Building straddles the line.

Interstate 30 meets four U.S. highways here, and the local economy rests on timber, farmland, minerals and rail. Texarkana College, three major hospitals and Wright Patman Lake round out the picture. Hospital and college staff, plus people commuting along I-30, are the natural buyers for a Texarkana listing.

A 2015 estimate put the Texas city at 37,280 people, within a metro area covering all of Bowie County and Miller County, Arkansas. Treat that as scale only. Your house competes across a small two-state market where employers on both sides pull workers toward either city. For a current pricing picture, a Bowie County title company or the appraisal district can help.

Selling points for a Texarkana house

Buyers respond to what the area offers day to day. Texarkana serves as a trading and industrial hub reaching into Oklahoma and Louisiana, with cotton, corn, rice, soybeans and pecans grown nearby and lumber, rail tank cars and paper products made here.

  • Education and medicine: Texarkana College, which includes a nursing department, and three major hospitals.
  • Recreation: Wright Patman Lake, Millwood Reservoir across the line, and the annual Four States Fair and Rodeo.
  • Transportation: Interstate 30 and four U.S. highways cross here, and the city is a major Southwest rail center.

Parts of town were built out by 1896, with waterworks, streetcars and brick schools, which hints that many houses here are old. If yours has decades behind it, expect buyers to ask when wiring, plumbing and the roof were last redone. Receipts and permits answer that quickly. Without them, an inspector will do the answering, and not always in your favor.

Tax calendar for a Texarkana seller

Annual tax calendar

The Bowie CAD website links to a payment portal, a property tax calendar, an exemption breakdown and a page on proposed rates. Need a payoff figure for your own account? Use the portal or phone the Bowie County tax office.

How to protest a Bowie CAD appraisal

Your window closes May 15, or 30 days after the notice is sent if that comes later. Each spring Bowie CAD mails a notice to owners whose market value climbed by at least $1,000, with market, assessed and taxable figures side by side.

  • By mail: P.O. Box 6527, Texarkana, TX 75505.
  • In person: 122A Plaza West in Texarkana or 710 James Bowie Drive in New Boston.
  • Online: through the portal, using the owner ID and PIN printed on the notice.

Once you file, request an informal sit-down with an appraiser. Those start April 16 and each property gets one. Refuse the settlement offer and the appraisal review board takes the case. Somebody else can speak for you if you sign an appointment of agent form.

Exemptions and caps

On a main residence, a homestead exemption lowers taxable value, and appraised value can rise no more than 10 percent a year. Someone buying to live in the house will ask what ownership costs after their own exemption kicks in.

State rules give school districts a $140,000 homestead exemption. Seniors and disabled owners receive extra relief and a school tax ceiling that can travel with them to a different Texas home. Disabled veteran exemptions scale by rating. File through Bowie CAD, and ask how to end your own exemption after you sell.

Back taxes, inheritance and foreclosure

Delinquent taxes get paid from your proceeds. Because the lien follows the property, the title company will ask for a payoff figure. Homestead owners may find collectors willing to set up plans of up to 36 months.

Heirs of an inherited house can probate the will, request a muniment of title, or use a deed naming a beneficiary that was recorded while the owner lived. Foreclosure sales fall on the first Tuesday of a month after 21 days' notice. Against squatters, Property Code chapter 24B lets you ask the sheriff or constable to act, but not against family members or current or former tenants.

Texas lets a seller close with taxes owed, so a balance does not block a sale. It simply gets settled at the closing table. Your own facts matter, so see a Texas attorney. Before that visit, collect the deed, your latest tax statement, any loan statement and a list of everyone living in the house. Most of these situations are workable for a cash buyer as long as title can be cleared by the day you pick. Sellers who start the paperwork early usually have the most choices about timing. Waiting until a notice arrives narrows those choices fast.

Closing and recording

After a Texas-side sale funds, the deed goes to the Bowie County Clerk, the office for the county where the land sits. Your title company handles that step in the normal course. Ahead of closing, request a written lender payoff that stays good through your closing date. Put every roof, plumbing and electrical receipt in one folder so a buyer sees the history at a glance. On closing day, bring photo ID, every key and any garage remotes, and sign the deed in front of a notary. Also arrange to stop utilities in your name that same day.

By the law of the state where it sits. A Texas-side house is in Bowie County and uses Texas rules. Your deed and tax bill show the county.

By May 15, or 30 days after the notice is mailed if that is later. Informal meetings come first, then the appraisal review board.

Can I sell a Texarkana house with unpaid taxes?

Yes. At closing, the balance plus any penalty and interest is paid from your proceeds. Request a payoff from the tax office that covers your closing date.

Do I have to repair a house before a cash sale?

No. Cash buyers often take a house as is, while a mortgage buyer is likelier to ask for repairs. Either way, collect receipts for major systems, since a clear paper trail speeds a decision.

Where do I record the deed for a Texas-side sale?

At the Bowie County Clerk's office, in the county where the land lies. Your title company ordinarily files it for you.

Selling in Anna?

Selling routes for an Anna homeowner

Three paths are open: an agent listing, a sale you run yourself, or a direct cash offer. The tradeoff is price against speed. Anna lies in north central Collin County, and its population roughly doubled in five years. Many sellers there own newer houses in subdivisions where builders are still active.

That shapes the sale. Anyone weighing your resale against a builder's model down the street will look hard at the price, the condition and any recurring assessment on the tax bill. Cash buyers skip that comparison and make an offer for the house in its present state.

  • List with an agent if the home is clean and newer and you have time to wait for a financed buyer.
  • Go without an agent only if drafting the contract and handling title paperwork feels manageable.
  • Take cash when the move is urgent, the house was inherited, a tenant is involved, or you do not want to fund repairs.

Anna's growth and housing figures

Few places in Collin County are growing faster than Anna. It counted 8,249 people in 2010 and 16,896 in 2020, then reached an estimated 35,245 by mid-2025, a gain of 105.7% measured from the 2020 starting estimate.

Anna city, Texas: housing and income, 2020-2024 estimates

Households here are big and young, and the average commute runs 30.7 minutes. The typical buyer is a family wanting space within reach of McKinney and the Dallas job market. Because so much of Anna was built recently, sale questions usually involve expired builder warranties, drainage on newly graded lots and neighborhood-level assessments.

Public improvement districts and special assessments

They can raise what a buyer pays every year. Anna's City Council forms public improvement districts by resolution. One example is Resolution 2023-02-1378, approved February 14, 2023, which created The Woods at Lindsey Place Public Improvement District. A district lets a city pay for streets, utilities and similar improvements through assessments on the lots that benefit.

Collin County also has many municipal utility districts and water districts, and each shows up as a separate taxing entity. A house inside one has an extra line on the property tax bill.

  • Have the title company check whether the lot lies inside a public improvement district or a utility district.
  • Ask the Collin County Tax Assessor-Collector which entities appear on your tax statement.
  • If the lot is in a district, ask the city for the assessment schedule.
  • Share those figures with the buyer early, so the price talk uses the true yearly cost.

Permits and inspections

Anna's Building Department handles both. It operates from the Municipal Complex at 120 W. 7th Street, Suite 142, on weekdays from eight to five, and its phone number is 972-924-2616. The city publishes requirements for fences, irrigation, remodels, roofing, solar panels, pools and spas, water heaters and patio covers.

Request an inspection by email before 4 p.m. the business day ahead; none take place on weekends or holidays. Certain jobs need extra forms such as a site drainage acknowledgement, a homeowner's affidavit or a pool affidavit.

Prior to listing, make sure each fence, pool, roof or remodel you added was permitted and passed its final inspection. Inspectors working for buyers ask about this, and a missing final can hold up the closing.

Property tax bills and exemptions

Billing comes from the Collin County Tax Assessor-Collector. October statements are due as soon as you receive them, and anything paid after January 31 draws penalties. The year's lien takes effect January 1, which is why a title company will deduct any unpaid balance from your proceeds.

The 2023 table from Collin CAD showed these exemptions for Anna city. A new table is posted each year, so confirm the current entries.

  • Homestead: 3.00% of value, with a $5,000 floor.
  • Age 65 or older: $30,000.
  • Disabled person: $30,000.

A buyer who moves in mid-year may be able to claim the homestead exemption for the remainder of that year when the previous owner never had one. School taxes are capped for owners with an age or disability exemption, and the cap can travel with them to another Texas home, stated as a percentage.

Appraisals on a homestead may climb no more than 10% a year, not counting new improvements. For that reason a long-time owner's bill can lag well behind market price.

Inherited or facing foreclosure?

The filings go through Collin County offices, and the Texas rules are short.

  • Heirs: if your name is not on the recorded deed, you can still get the homestead exemption by giving the district a sworn statement of ownership, a death certificate and a recent utility bill. An estate that holds real property beyond the homestead cannot use the small-estate route.
  • Lender action: the borrower has 20 days from the default letter to cure, and the lender must give notice of sale 21 days or more ahead of the first-Tuesday auction.
  • Deeds: bring the Collin County Clerk an original or a certified copy, signed and notarized.

If the clock is running, closing ahead of the auction keeps the timeline in your hands. With no loan to approve, a cash purchase can compress the schedule.

From contract to closing in Collin County

Accepting an offer sends the file to a title company. Staff there order a tax certificate, request payoff statements from every lender, and search for liens, open permits and assessments on the lot. If the buyer needs a mortgage, an appraisal and underwriting lengthen the calendar. Paying cash eliminates both.

You sign the deed in front of a notary at closing, and it is then sent to the county clerk. The appraisal district later updates the owner of record, and the new owner applies for a homestead exemption in their own name during the January through April window. File away the settlement statement, a copy of the deed, and any receipt proving the year's tax was paid.

Preparing an Anna house for a quick sale

Newer houses move fastest when the paperwork is ready to hand over. Pull together the settlement statement from your own purchase, any builder warranty papers still in force, and your latest tax statement. Note each special district that bills the lot and its annual cost. A buyer who sees those numbers on day one has less reason to reopen the price after an inspection.

Leaving for a new job or a family move? Share your deadline with the buyer. Cash buyers can often meet it, since no lender must sign off and title work begins the day the contract is signed.

Frequently asked questions

How fast is Anna growing?

The estimate for July 1, 2025 is 35,245 residents, more than double the 2020 estimates base of 17,137. The city has 16.45 square miles of land.

Is a PID assessment passed to the buyer when I sell an Anna house?

Yes, an assessment attached to the lot stays with the property. Ask the title company and the city for the schedule, and share it with buyers up front.

Which county office collects tax for Anna?

The Collin County Tax Assessor-Collector bills and collects. Collin Central Appraisal District, in McKinney, sets the value and processes exemptions.

Should I gather permit records before listing in Anna?

Can an heir claim the homestead exemption on an inherited Anna house?

Your choices for a fast exit

Your options are a broker, a private sale or a cash proposal. Cash is the only one that avoids a lender's approval, so it is fastest when a deadline is firm.

Harker Heights has 35,195 residents, and many work in Killeen or at Fort Cavazos. That ties numerous sales to job moves and orders, so closing dates carry extra weight. Get every interested buyer to commit to a funding date in writing, and treat a vague "a few weeks" as no answer. Moving on orders? Tell buyers, and ask who can close around your report date. Better a buyer who meets your date than one who offers extra and cannot.

  • Broker listing: for a tidy house and an owner patient with showings and financing.
  • Private sale: for owners with a buyer in mind and the time to handle contracts and title work.
  • Cash proposal: for houses needing work, empty houses and owners racing a move date.

Local housing and market background

Harker Heights began as a 1957 plat along U.S. Highway 190 east of Killeen. Today it is a bedroom community in the Killeen Independent School District. Population was 26,700 in 2010, 33,097 in 2020 and 35,195 for 2025. Most houses are newer subdivision stock, so buyers will hold yours up against others from the same years.

Nearby draws that families often ask about include the Killeen Municipal Golf Course and Stillhouse Hollow Lake. Say so in your description of the house if any of them is a short drive away.

The city covers 15.61 square miles of land. Voters approved incorporation on September 24, 1960, once a water system was finished, and a December 1988 annexation of the 2,200-acre Comanche Hills utility district grew the townsite from 4,400 acres to 6,600. Lots platted in different decades can carry different easements and setbacks, so a current survey helps a buyer feel sure about boundaries.

Values, owners and buyers

Owners occupy about 61.7% of homes and the midpoint value for 2020 to 2024 is $287,800. Those are citywide, so a quiet cul-de-sac house may price above or below that.

Households average 2.72 people, and 85.5% of residents had not moved in the past year, which suggests settled families who ask about bedrooms, yard size and school zones. Some buyers and sellers are military households who need a closing that fits an orders deadline.

Appraisal district and tax calendar

Your value comes from the Bell County appraisal district, and the resulting bill is tied to the property. Bills go out near October 1. A bill still unpaid after January 31 is delinquent, and the 6% penalty and 1% interest begin February 1. The penalty then climbs 1% a month and reaches 12% on July 1. If the unit hires a collection attorney, up to 20% more may be added.

  • Homeowners may pay half by November 30 and half by June 30.
  • The tax certificate comes from the Bell County tax office, since the appraisal district does not issue one.
  • Find out from the appraisal district which exemptions your account carries and whether the transfer ends them.

Funding waits until the title company sees this year's bill paid, so settle any back balance early. If a balance is left over, have the title officer show where it will be deducted from your proceeds before you sign.

Selling an inherited house

You can sell once the title names an owner. In Texas a will may be probated within four years of a death. When no administrator is needed, the will and a court order are recorded as a muniment of title with the clerk where the land lies.

A smaller estate can use the small estate affidavit, if there is no will, no petition for administration, no more than $75,000 in assets outside the homestead, every heir agrees and a judge approves. A transfer on death deed, if the owner recorded one before dying, hands the house to named beneficiaries with no probate.

Gather the death certificate, any will and the newest tax statement first. Probate staff at the Bell County clerk's office can name the right filing, and the buyer's title company will expect it recorded before closing.

Permits and rental history

The city's Planning and Development department can tell you whether a room, deck, carport or garage conversion was permitted. Unpermitted work gets noticed by inspectors and title companies, and it may delay a deal or cut an offer.

Did you ever host guests there? Phone the city and find out whether a rental registration exists that you should cancel before closing. Tell every buyer about open items. A cash buyer may take open items as they stand, while a buyer with a mortgage can require fixes before funding.

Papers to gather before you take offers

A thin folder now saves days later. Begin with the recorded deed and your newest Bell County tax statement, then add each lender's payoff letter, the tax certificate once ordered, and permit records for work done since you bought.

If the house sits in the former Comanche Hills utility district, which the city absorbed in December 1988, ask the title company whether older utility easements show on the plat. If someone is renting from you, add the lease and deposit record, and decide whether the buyer will inherit the tenant or receive the house vacant.

Ask each buyer for a written offer showing price, closing date, who pays closing charges and what happens to the earnest money if the deal collapses. Line the offers up and compare what you would keep after payoffs. A slightly lower figure with a firm date can beat a higher one that hangs on a loan.

What a cash sale skips

With cash there is no loan approval, no lender appraisal and no repair haggling after an inspection. Title work remains, though: the record gets searched, payoffs get requested and a deed and settlement statement get drafted.

Settle three points before signing: the closing date, who pays title and recording charges, and whether you may stay a few days after funding. Keep copies of the contract and every notice you received, and release the keys only once the title company confirms the money has arrived. Clear out belongings, remove trash and leave the yard tidy, since a cash buyer's final walkthrough often happens the day before closing.

Frequently asked questions

Must I fix the house before a cash buyer will make an offer?

No. A cash buyer prices the house in its present state. A broker listing typically needs more work, since a financed buyer orders an inspection and asks for fixes.

When does Bell County property tax become late?

Once January 31 passes with a balance open. Bills go out near October 1, and penalty and interest begin February 1. The Bell County tax office can quote your exact balance and any installment option.

Which office files my Harker Heights deed?

The Bell County clerk. A notary must witness your signature, and the title company normally carries the signed deed to the clerk after closing.

Can heirs list the house while probate is still open?

Usually only with legal authority, such as a court order or an executor's deed. A recorded transfer on death deed or a muniment of title order can also work. Check with a Texas attorney or the clerk's office first.

Is $287,800 what my house will sell for?

Not necessarily. It is a citywide midpoint for 2020 to 2024. Condition, size and street drive your price, so gather written offers and compare them with your Bell County appraisal account.

Selling a Del Rio house without a long wait

A broker's listing, a sale you manage yourself and a quick deal with a cash purchaser are the three choices. Listings take longer to turn up a buyer, whereas cash gives you the say over when you close.

Before you talk price, round up the deed, a payoff letter from your lender, your newest tax bill and whatever permit records you have. Every written offer needs to name the price and closing date, say who covers title and recording costs, and describe the condition the buyer wants at handover.

  • Check if the buyer plans an inspection before the offer becomes firm.
  • Decide whether furniture and appliances stay or go.
  • Have the closing date written down.

What buyers see in Del Rio housing

Del Rio lies on U.S. Highway 90 at the spot where the Rio Grande and San Felipe Creek meet, 154 miles west of San Antonio. It incorporated on November 15, 1911, and counted 33,867 people in 2000. The oldest homes sit near the creek. Housing later shifted north of the rail line, and the retail strip along Highway 90 and the reservoir built in the 1960s tugged growth north once more. Describe your block with that pattern in mind, and refer school zoning questions to the school district.

Permit steps for a home project

The Development Services Department reviews plans and issues building, electrical, plumbing, mechanical, sign and garage sale permits. Its inspectors also look at substandard buildings, and it grants certificates of occupancy.

Del Rio enforces the 2024 editions of the International Building, Residential, Mechanical, Plumbing, Fire, Energy Conservation and Fuel and Gas codes, together with the 2024 Property Maintenance Code and the 2020 National Electrical Code. A garage conversion or addition built with no permit should be disclosed to the buyer, and the city can explain how to close that file.

Val Verde County tax bills at closing

Values are set as of January 1, and the lien for the year attaches the same day. Bills go in the mail around October 1. Owners may split payment, with half due by November 30 and half by June 30, although most bills must be paid by January 31.

Property records sit with the Val Verde County appraisal district and tax office, and the city home page links to its tax department. A seller who never claimed a homestead exemption leaves that option open to a buyer closing later in the year. Your closing statement should show the year's bill divided between you and the buyer, so check that line.

Selling a rental that has a tenant

If a tenant refuses to go, Texas expects the landlord to follow a fixed order. First comes a written demand to vacate. Three days is the default unless the lease names a different period. Next the landlord files in justice court, the tenant is served at least four days before trial, and the hearing is set somewhere between 10 and 21 days after the filing date.

The losing side has five days from judgment to appeal to county court. When no appeal stops it, a writ of possession becomes available six days after the final judgment. An officer then has five days to serve it, and the tenant receives 24 hours of warning before being removed. People who buy occupied houses will want the lease, deposit records and rent history. Some owners sell with the lease still running, and a landlord going that way should talk with the tenant early about showings.

Inheritance and default

A will can be probated by heirs up to four years after the owner dies. Where no administration is needed, a muniment of title may be enough. With no will, a small estate affidavit works only if the assets come to $75,000 or less and every heir agrees. An owner who signed and filed a transfer on death deed during life leaves a house that skips probate.

Lenders on a defaulted loan usually wait out the first 120 days of missed payments. After that you get 20 days to catch up, and the lender has to post notice of the auction at least three weeks ahead of the first Tuesday on which it sells. Money left over after the lender is paid goes to junior liens and then to you. Begin by asking the servicer for an exact payoff.

City permits and licenses that can touch a sale

Development Services also hands out garage sale and sign permits, so an estate sale or moving sale may require one. The city has a business license service as well, and its business pages carry a hotel occupancy tax application for lodging operators. If guests ever stayed in the house by the night, ask whether those pages apply to you before closing.

Utilities run through the city, which handles billing and residential waste collection. Get a final bill and a stop-service date so the buyer begins with a clean account.

Cleaning out the house before closing is also on you. If a sale leaves furniture, a vehicle or yard debris behind, the buyer may hold back money or refuse to close. Decide early what stays, and take photos of the empty rooms once the work is finished.

Filing the deed and closing day

The Val Verde County Clerk records the deed after a notary has acknowledged it. Most title companies file it for you and pay the recording charge from the settlement funds. Closing day means signing the deed and a settlement statement, turning over keys and openers, and collecting what is left after the loan payoff and the tax share.

Questions to put to each buyer

Judge bids on more than price. Ask how each buyer is paying, how soon they can close and whether they expect repairs. Proof of funds and a written date are worth more than a bigger number resting on a loan nobody has checked.

Ask, too, who picks the title company and who pays for the owner's title policy, since those two answers change what you take home. If the house is rented, say so to every bidder at the start and hand over the lease in your first conversation, not after a contract exists.
