Frequently asked questions

Does Del Rio require a permit for home repairs?

Yes, when the work falls under the adopted codes: building, electrical, plumbing, mechanical and sign work. Development Services reviews plans, issues permits, inspects and signs off with a certificate of occupancy.

Who buys houses in Del Rio?

Local families, military households, landlords and cash purchasers all shop here. Offers from a financed buyer, an agent's advice and a cash quote will show you who is active at your price.

Which office files a Del Rio deed?

The Val Verde County Clerk, once the signature has been properly acknowledged. Your title company typically files it and pays the fee from closing funds.

How quickly can a Del Rio eviction finish?

Figure on several weeks. The hearing is set 10 to 21 days after filing, removal by an officer waits until at least six days after judgment, and notice, service and any appeal all take time.

Can Del Rio heirs sell without full probate?

In some cases. Heirs may be able to use a small estate affidavit, a muniment of title, or a transfer on death deed the owner filed in life. A title company can tell you which of these a buyer will accept.

Choosing how to sell in Lufkin

You can use an agent, sell by yourself, or find a cash buyer who is unbothered by the repair list. Listing may fetch the best price; cash trades some price for speed and certainty.

Lufkin is the Angelina County seat, at the crossing of U.S. highways 59 and 69 in the East Texas Piney Woods. The buyer pool is local and tied to timber, manufacturing and health care. A house needing work will find a buyer, though often after a longer stay on the market, so plan the asking price around that.

  • Listing: best for a move-in-ready house when you can handle showings and an appraisal.
  • Private sale: you keep the commission and run the contract yourself.

Older houses and what buyers check

The oldest blocks in Lufkin sit near the rail core, with later subdivisions spreading outward. Many older houses date to the decades when timber and manufacturing grew the town, and a buyer may ask when major systems were last replaced. Before a lender backs a conventional buyer, an older house may need work on its roof, wiring or foundation.

A mix of industry, services and recreation, from Sam Rayburn Reservoir to hunting land, means buyers arrive from several directions. Jobs in manufacturing and oilfield equipment rise and fall with the industry, so sell when you need to rather than waiting for a peak. Point school-minded buyers to the Lufkin Independent School District itself for its current campuses.

Who appraises and bills Lufkin property

The Angelina County Appraisal District values property throughout the county each January 1 and passes the values to the taxing units. It passes values to the City of Lufkin, Angelina County, Angelina College and Lufkin ISD, along with other school districts and two water districts.

The district keeps ownership records, assigns market value, administers exemptions and special appraisal, and explains disputes and appeals. Its outreach number is (936) 634-8456.

Values are fixed each January 1, which is also when the lien attaches. Mid-May is protest time, bills arrive near October 1, and the end of January is the payment deadline. On February 1 an unpaid balance gets a 6 percent penalty and starts collecting 1 percent monthly interest.

At closing the agent splits the year's tax between you and the buyer. A lender or buyer who asks for a tax certificate can get one from the Angelina County tax office.

Homestead exemptions and ceilings

  • Every school district takes $140,000 off a homestead, and seniors and disabled owners get $60,000 beyond that.
  • For a qualifying senior or disabled homeowner, a ceiling can freeze the school tax at the amount owed in the first year they qualified.
  • After the first exemption year, a homestead's value can climb by no more than 10 percent annually.
  • A disabled veteran gets tiered exemptions, with a total exemption for a 100 percent rating.

The exemptions belong to you, not the house, so the buyer files again after closing.

If a Lufkin mortgage payment slips

Move early. A borrower with a Texas deed of trust has twenty days from the default notice to reinstate, and three weeks must pass between the sale notice and the auction. Auctions are open to the public once a month, during the day.

Foreclosure usually cannot begin under federal rules until a home loan is over 120 days behind. Money left after a foreclosure sale pays junior lienholders before it reaches the former owner, and a suit over any shortfall must be brought within two years.

A sale beforehand lets you choose the buyer, skip the foreclosure record and keep your equity. Ask the servicer for a written payoff.

Inherited or rented homes

Title comes first. A will can be probated until four years after the death. A muniment of title lets heirs act on the will. If there is none, a small estate affidavit can cover assets below a set dollar ceiling, and the homestead does not count toward it.

A renter in the house means the landlord sends three days' written notice, files in justice court and may seek a writ of possession six days after judgment. Many owners avoid all that by selling with the renter in place. Before signing, confirm with the appraisal district who the owner of record is.

Where Lufkin deeds go

Land in the county is recorded by the Angelina County Clerk, once a notary or similar officer has acknowledged the signature. Page one of a recorded deed runs $5.00 and later pages $4.00, with capped records fees added, as the state clerk manual sets out. The closing agent usually files and deducts the cost.

Timing a Lufkin sale

Selling slowly in Lufkin is not unusual for a house that needs work. If you can wait, make the small fixes that buyers notice first: a clean exterior, working systems and a tidy yard. If you cannot wait, a cash offer gives you a date. Neither answer is wrong. What matters is that you know what each path leaves you after the mortgage, the tax share and recording costs.

Ask the appraisal district for the year's assessed value so you know what the house is carried at, and ask the tax office for the amount due. A buyer's lender will want both figures, and having them in hand keeps the contract from stalling in its first week.

Lufkin buyers and where they come from

Local employers in timber, manufacturing, paper and health care supply many of the buyers for Lufkin houses, and the area's lakes and hunting land bring in others. A seller who knows which group fits the house can aim the listing: a family house near the older core appeals to someone who wants an established neighborhood, while a worn house on a big lot may suit an investor. State the lot size, the age of the roof and the condition of the plumbing in plain terms, and say whether the house sits inside the city limits so buyers know which tax bill to expect.

A short checklist before you call buyers

Walk through the house once with a notepad. Write down the age of the roof, the last time the air conditioner was serviced, any leaks you have patched and any room that was added without paperwork. Take a few clear photos of each side of the house. Then write one paragraph describing the house as you would to a friend: what is good, what needs work and why you are selling. Share that paragraph and the photos with every buyer, so each offer is based on the same facts and you can compare them fairly.

What the closing agent handles

Right after an offer is accepted, the closing agent contacts your lender for a payoff figure, orders a tax certificate from the Angelina County tax office, prepares the deed and sets a signing time. Once the notary has witnessed your signature, the agent takes the deed to the county clerk and pays recording from your proceeds. You receive the balance. If the buyer needs a homestead exemption, they apply to the appraisal district themselves.

Keep every document the agent sends. If a question about the tax split comes up later, the closing statement is the record.

Getting ready to sell

Collect the deed, your latest Angelina County tax bill, a loan payoff statement and any repair receipts. Call the appraisal district and ask which exemptions are active and whose name they are under. Ask the tax office what is owed today. If you have a tenant, write down the lease terms.

Then ask two or three cash buyers and one listing agent for numbers. A written offer should show the price, the closing date and who pays title and recording costs. Subtract your payoff and tax share from each to see what you actually keep.

Which county holds Lufkin?

Angelina County, where Lufkin is the seat. Both the appraisal district and the clerk's office are in Angelina County.

Most unpaid Texas taxes are delinquent on February 1. Penalty (six percent) and interest (one percent) begin then, and by July 1 the penalty is 12 percent.

Is probate required before selling an inherited Lufkin house?

Usually some court or recorded step must show ownership. Proof of ownership for heirs can come from a probated will, a muniment of title, a small estate affidavit, or a transfer on death deed the owner recorded before dying.

How long does Texas foreclosure take after a default notice?

Twenty days to cure after the default notice, then a sale notice three weeks before the monthly auction. Selling earlier can protect equity.

Give the office at least a day of notice. Monday visits get called in on Friday. Morning appointments run about 8:30 to 11:30 a.m., and afternoon ones about 1 to 4 p.m. For foundation approval the city wants a form survey and an elevation certificate.

A permit with no final inspection

An unfinished permit file can stall a sale, and it can delay a utility hookup for whoever buys next. Think about the patio cover, the water heater swap or the sprinkler system someone added years ago. Irrigation appears among the city's plumbing inspections, which means an older sprinkler system may have left a paper trail at city hall.

If you find a permit that was never closed, say so to the buyer early and phone the inspection office to learn what it would take. It is cheaper in time to sort this out before you sign a contract than in the weeks between contract and closing.

Getting the house ready

Begin with permits, then turn to the lot. Pull the records for each remodel and look for work that never got a final.

  • Collect inspection stickers or approval records for recent projects.
  • Repair visible drainage, roof and fence trouble.
  • Report broken city property, such as potholes or damaged benches, through the online form on the city home page.
  • Ask neighbors or the city about street or utility work on the way, including the advanced metering project listed for residents.

Repairs you can document help every kind of buyer, and they let a cash buyer price your house with fewer guesses. A neat folder of receipts, permit numbers and final inspection dates also cuts down the questions from the title company and the lender in the last stretch. Send anyone asking about school attendance zones to the school district, because the city does not draw them.

Property tax timing

Deer Park's own fiscal year starts October 1 and ends September 30. For tax purposes your house is valued as it stood on January 1, with statements mailed near October 1. Pay by January 31 or the account turns delinquent, and penalty and interest begin piling on. Homestead owners can ask a collector about spreading payments over as long as 36 months.

The actual dollar amounts are on your Harris County bill, which combines separate rates from the city, the county and the school district. The year's lien took hold on January 1 and stays with the house, so any balance is settled at the closing table or cleared earlier. Expect the title company to confirm that number on the day you sign.

Homestead exemption

A homestead gets $140,000 knocked off its value for school taxes, and other taxing units are free to add exemptions of their own. Seniors and disabled owners gain another $60,000 on the school side plus a ceiling on what the school district can collect. Annual growth in a homestead's appraised value stops at 10 percent. File before May 1. To learn which local exemptions cover Deer Park, ask the Harris County appraisal district.

Inherited property or a loan in default

Heirs who hold a will get four years after the death to probate it. A house covered by a transfer on death deed that the owner recorded in life changes hands without probate. For a small estate with no will, an affidavit can sometimes stand in. Phone the Harris County Clerk to learn which papers a sale will require.

Mortgage lenders generally hold back until the loan runs more than 120 days behind, and then you have 20 days to cure. Foreclosure auctions take place on a first Tuesday, with posted notice at least three weeks earlier. Closing ahead of that date lets you pay the loan off on your own terms. Your servicer can give you the payoff figure and the auction date.

How closing works

Your deed is recorded by the Harris County Clerk, who will not accept it unless a notary or witness has verified the signature. In most sales the title company handles the filing and deducts the recording fee from the funds at closing.

Selling for cash removes the lender's appraisal and loan approval from the schedule. You still go through a title search, a payoff of any loan on the house, a tax settlement and a signing. Take a photo ID, the keys, garage openers and any warranty papers for work done on the house.

From accepted offer to payout

Once you accept an offer, the title company opens a file and orders a title search. It asks your lender for a payoff and looks for liens, including unpaid city charges, then reviews the year's tax account. With a cash buyer those are most of the steps. A financed buyer adds an appraisal and underwriting.

You will be given a signing date, usually at the title office. After you sign and the deed is recorded, the funds are released. Your proceeds are the price less your payoff, your share of the tax bill and any closing costs you agreed to pay. If a utility account is in your name, set the stop date for closing day and take a final meter reading.

Frequently asked questions

Does Deer Park inspect a house when it sells?

Inspections are tied to permits for building, electrical, mechanical and plumbing work, not to the sale itself. Confirm that earlier permits were closed out, and call the inspection office if you are unsure about your address.

Who records the deed for a Deer Park house?

The Harris County Clerk records it, but only after the signature is notarized or witnessed. Your title company usually files it and takes the fee from closing funds.

Can a Deer Park house be sold with unpaid taxes?

Yes. The lien dated January 1 stays with the property, so the balance is paid at closing or cleared before it. The title company lists the amount on a payoff statement.

Who sets the tax rate on a Deer Park house?

Each taxing unit sets its own, so a single house carries several rates. The county and the school district mail separate bills, and the city posts its own rate on its home page.

What if a Deer Park permit never got a final inspection?

Tell the buyer and ask the inspection office what it needs. An open permit can slow a sale or a hookup, since all four trade finals must pass before the gas meter inspection is released.

Sachse and the county line

Seventeen miles or so northeast of Dallas along State Highway 78, Sachse spills over both Dallas County and Collin County. Your lot's side of the boundary determines who appraises it and who mails the tax bill. The town took its name in 1886 from a railway station, and it grew from roughly 5,000 residents around 1990 to 9,751 in 2000. Housing here mostly arrived after the 1980s, once Sachse turned into a residential suburb of Garland, so many homes share a similar vintage.

  • Identify your parcel's county before requesting any tax paperwork.
  • A Sachse street address cannot tell you the county, because the city limits run across the line.

Choices for a quick Sachse sale

No exit from a Sachse house is free. A listing costs time, an investor sale gives up part of the price, and selling alone costs you labor. Listing reaches a wider crowd, though the sale then depends on loan timelines and inspection demands. Investor money arrives sooner, and the bid usually lands under what a staged, repaired listing could reach.

Cash fits best when something other than price has the house stuck: an inheritance, a tenant, a missed mortgage payment or a hard moving date. Get two bids on paper and read the closing-cost, repair-credit and closing-date terms closely.

  • Agent route: broad reach and a commission to pay.
  • Owner route: no commission, and you run the photos, showings and contract yourself.
  • Investor route: speed and as-is condition, at a discount.

Who sends the tax bill on a Sachse house?

Texas collects no property tax at the state level. Your school district, city and county each bill a share, working from the value the appraisal district sets every January 1.

So a Sachse parcel appears on the roll of Dallas Central Appraisal District or Collin Central Appraisal District, never both. Dallas CAD serves 61 governing bodies and keeps public office hours on weekdays. The Collin district publishes taxing entity information, the exemptions each entity offers and the adopted rates on its own site. Search the right database for your parcel, then read the entity list that applies to your lot.

Early October brings the statements. A balance still open in February is delinquent, and the January 1 lien means anything unpaid stays with the house.

Back taxes at a Sachse closing

The closer typically deducts an old balance from what you receive, because the lien stays on the house. Once an account is late, a 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest apply. The penalty hits 12 percent by July while interest continues. A collection lawyer retained by a unit may add up to 20 percent.

Before you list, ask the collecting office whether you can pay back taxes in installments. A plan can last up to 36 months at some offices, and a residence homestead is entitled to one. Penalty and interest may be waived on written request when you pay within three weeks of finding out the tax is late.

  • Get a payoff or certificate of taxes due from the office that bills your lot.
  • Find out how the closer plans to pay prior-year taxes.
  • Keep proof of your homestead exemption.

Homestead exemptions in a Sachse sale

Your own residence gets the exemption, which lowers its taxable value. Even if the seller never filed, a buyer who closes in spring can get it for what remains of the year.

School districts take $140,000 off a homestead's value, and seniors and disabled owners get another $60,000 off. Cities and counties may layer on a percentage exemption of their own. Seniors also get a school tax freeze. A homestead's appraisal also cannot grow more than 10 percent a year. You apply at the appraisal district, and Dallas CAD charges no fee.

Where a Sachse deed is filed

Either the Dallas County clerk or the Collin County clerk records your deed, based on the parcel's location.

Texas will not record a deed until a notary, another authorized officer or two witnesses has attested the signature. The manual sets the first page at $5.00 and each extra page $4.00, with records fees added. Filing normally falls to the title company after funding. If the sale is part of a probate or a foreclosure workout, tell the closer early so the right documents are in place.

An inherited house or a foreclosure in Sachse

Both situations come with fixed legal steps, and a buyer will want paper that proves who may sign the deed.

  • Inherited with a will: probate is possible for up to four years after death, and a muniment of title order may let heirs convey without full administration.
  • Inherited without a will: modest estates can use a small estate affidavit, which a court must approve.
  • Behind on the mortgage: a default notice gives 20 days to catch up, and a sale notice must come three weeks ahead of an auction on a first Tuesday.

Selling ahead of the auction lets you set the price and keep leftover equity. Request a written payoff from the servicer and talk over timing with an attorney or a HUD-approved counselor.

From signed contract to closing in Sachse

Following signature, the title company calls the correct county tax office for a balance, requests a lender payoff and searches the title for liens. You sign the deed at closing, the loan and old taxes come out of the sale money, and the title company forwards the deed to the proper clerk.

A cash buyer has no loan to clear, so title work sets the pace. Mention a tenant, back taxes or an estate issue to the buyer at the outset, since each can add days.

Preparing a Sachse house built in a growth period

Because so many Sachse homes were built during the same stretch of decades, buyers touring several houses in one weekend will see the same floor plans repeated. What separates yours is upkeep. Original roofs, tired windows, old water heaters and worn flooring all push an offer down, and a buyer's inspector writes each one into a repair request.

Choose before listing whether to fix, credit or sell as is. Fixing helps if you have time and cash. A credit keeps the sale moving without work on your part. Selling as is to a direct buyer ends the repair debate, and you pick the closing day. Whatever you choose, collect receipts for roof, plumbing, electrical and foundation work, since paperwork answers a skeptical buyer faster than assurances do.

Seventeen miles from Dallas along State Highway 78, Sachse draws commuters, so mention drive times in your listing and keep the yard and entry tidy for those quick weekend tours. Tell buyers which county your lot is in too, since it decides who sends the bill and where a new owner files for an exemption.

A Sachse seller's one-page plan

Begin with the county, because that answer shapes every other call. After that, get account details from the right appraisal district and a balance from the tax office. Then line up bids from at least two kinds of buyer so you can see the real spread between a listing and a cash purchase.

Choose the closing date at the end, leaving room for owed taxes, an unsettled inheritance or a tenant's notice. Buyers in Sachse generally respect a seller who arrives with the paperwork in order.

Protesting your appraisal before a sale

Think the appraised value is too high? Protest by the cutoff shown on your notice. Take comparable sales and photos of condition problems along, and consider an informal review with the district first. A lower value trims the bill that you and the buyer split for the year.

A pending protest will not slow a sale, but tell the title company so the closing tax figure accounts for it.

Frequently asked questions

Is Sachse in Dallas County or Collin County?

Both, because the city crosses the line. Confirm which county holds your parcel before you ask for tax records.

When are Sachse property taxes due?

October brings the bill and January 31 is the due date. You may pay in two halves instead, on November 30 and June 30.

Can I protest my appraisal if I plan to sell?

Yes. Your notice shows the cutoff for taking a protest to the appraisal review board, and a lower value reduces the year's bill that you and the buyer share.

Will a cash sale in Sachse skip the tax bill?

No. Old taxes are settled at closing for a cash buyer exactly as for a retail buyer, since the January 1 lien stays with the house.

Where do I record the deed for a Sachse house?

At the clerk's office for Dallas County or Collin County, whichever has the parcel. Expect an attested signature and a per-page fee.

Is a quick cash sale realistic in Nacogdoches?

Often, yes. With no loan approval or listing makeover in the way, closing can come within weeks. The offer will be lower than a fully fixed-up listing might bring, so measure it against repairs, holding costs and months of waiting.

Nacogdoches is a small East Texas city with a market of its own. Just 38.3 percent of homes are lived in by their owners, so rentals are common and investors shop alongside families. That works in favor of a seller whose house needs work.

Typical reasons for a fast sale:

  • A rental whose owner is done managing it.
  • Aging systems in an older home near downtown or the university.
  • Relocating for a job or family.

Prices are modest, and the market follows Stephen F. Austin State University closely. For 2020 to 2024 the median owner-occupied home is worth $186,000, median rent is $964 and median household income is $39,281.

Older homes and neighborhoods

The city bills itself as the oldest town in Texas. It is in the central part of the county, served by State highways 7, 21, 59 and 259. Mound Street has Victorian homes, and newer subdivisions surround the center.

One old house can offer period charm and a backlog of deferred repairs together. Investors can price both and take the renovation off your hands.

How the university shapes demand

The university is the backbone of the local economy and drives much of the rental demand. If your house is near campus, ask each buyer if the plan is to rent it out, since that shapes both the price and the repairs they will put up with.

Budgets are tight for many buyers, which keeps price points low. Your listing may sit beside several lookalike houses a few streets over, and condition and price settle which one goes first. Mature shade trees add curb appeal, but storm damage to limbs and leaves is a repair that cash buyers just factor into the offer.

Property taxes and the appraisal district

Nacogdoches Central Appraisal District does double duty, appraising property and collecting for the county, Nacogdoches ISD, the city and more. Its site offers a property lookup, online payment and a protest portal.

Values are fixed on January 1. Expect homestead notices near April 1, protest filings through mid-May and bills around October 1.

  • Anything unpaid after January 31 is delinquent from February 1.
  • School district homestead exemption: $140,000, with $60,000 added for seniors and disabled owners.
  • Because the lien attaches each January 1, clear title is impossible for a buyer until old taxes are paid.

First step: ask the appraisal district what exemptions and unpaid years show on your account.

Selling an inherited or probate house

A lot of Nacogdoches houses come to market through inheritance, and the paperwork sets your timeline. What the owner left behind decides your route.

  • Owner recorded a transfer on death deed: you record an affidavit of death plus the death certificate.
  • Estate under administration: the executor or administrator signs for the estate.
  • Will but no administrator: the will and a court order get recorded as a muniment of title.
  • Neither will nor court case: heirs may offer an affidavit of heirship, but some buyers and title companies say no.

Probate of a will is available for four years after death. Deeds are recorded in the county where the land lies, so ring the Nacogdoches County Clerk before you commit to a closing date.

What comes out of your proceeds

Costs come off the top before you are paid. In a cash sale they are chiefly title and escrow fees, unpaid taxes, loan payoffs and recording fees.

Recording starts at five dollars for the first page, with additional clerk fees on top. The clerk will not record a deed unless a notary or other authorized officer witnessed the signature.

Insist on seeing the price, closing date and cost split on paper. Then set that beside a listing estimate with commissions and repairs already taken out.

Pricing a Nacogdoches house for the market

With modest incomes and plenty of renters, shoppers look at price first, and a figure slightly too high can leave a house on the market. Find out how comparable houses on your own streets did lately instead of trusting a citywide median. Houses by campus, downtown or in newer subdivisions can end up far apart.

Be straight about condition. An inspection will find roof age, foundation, plumbing and storm damage to trees or fences, and a financed buyer will want a credit. A cash offer has that baked in. Decide whether the lower figure is worth the time you save.

Should you list, good-light photos, a neat yard and a note on how close campus and the highways are cost little and help. Unfinished work scares buyers off.

No matter which route you take, assemble a folder holding the deed, tax statements and receipts for repairs or improvements. A college town sees plenty of rental houses with spotty records, so one with tidy paperwork gets noticed. For a rented house, include the lease terms and the day the tenant's term ends.

Steps from offer to closing

With a written offer in hand, the title company pulls records and hunts for liens, tax balances and breaks in the chain of ownership. This is where older and inherited houses tend to hang up. After the issues are settled, you sign the deed before a notary and the county clerk records it.

Gather your deed, latest tax bill and a mortgage payoff letter before offers come in, along with the lease if someone rents the house. Some cash buyers will keep an existing tenant, which saves you from emptying the house. Go through the closing statement one line at a time and ask about anything unfamiliar. After the funds move, mistakes are much harder to fix.

What is a typical closing time here?

Usually within a few weeks if title is clean. Inherited or liened properties take longer because the title company has to clear them first. Ask for a target closing date in the written offer.

Must I repair the house first?

No. Cash buyers generally take the property in its current state, and the offer reflects that. You can still compare it with a repaired listing price to see which nets more.

Who bills Nacogdoches property taxes?

Nacogdoches Central Appraisal District values the property and collects taxes for the listed units, including the city, county and Nacogdoches ISD. Use its property search for your account and any balance.

Can a house still titled to a late relative be sold?

Only after the right paperwork is on record. Depending on the situation, that is an executor's deed, a muniment of title order, a recorded transfer on death deed or an affidavit of heirship. A Texas attorney can tell you which fits.

Are Nacogdoches homes mostly rented?

Renters make up a large share. Roughly six in ten homes are rented, so investors and landlords are active buyers.

When Bexar County property taxes are due

Statements arrive in October. Payment is due by January 31, and a postmark on or before that day counts as on time. An unpaid account is delinquent as of February 1.

On July 1, past-due accounts are handed to collectors and an extra 15 or 20 percent fee attaches. Business property accounts can be sent out as early as April 1.

  • Bexar Appraisal District sets values, grants exemptions and records changes of ownership or address.
  • The tax office mails bills and accepts payments, and will issue a duplicate if yours never shows up.
  • A lost bill excuses nothing, so the tax, penalty, interest and lien all stay in force.

Payment plans for Converse owners

Three plans exist, and your exemptions decide which you can join. A half-payment option splits the base tax between late November and the end of June. A four-payment plan is for homestead owners who are older or disabled. The ten-month plan runs October through July and is open to homestead owners with a disabled, over-65 or disabled veteran exemption, or a qualifying surviving spouse.

Bexar County is the only Texas county offering the ten-month plan, and it can still be joined in November with 20 percent down. Early-payment discounts ended under a 2003 commissioners court order, so there is no reward for paying ahead. A mailed payment is judged by its postmark, and a forgotten reminder does not extend a deadline.

Postponing taxes for older or military owners

Owners who are 65 or disabled may file a deferral affidavit with Bexar Appraisal District, and interest accrues at five percent a year. When the owner moves out or no longer owns the home, the back taxes and deferred interest come due on the 181st day.

Service members on active duty outside Texas during a declared war or emergency can defer under Property Tax Code section 31.02(b) by filing form 50-305 with their orders. If you hold a deferral, request a payoff figure before you list.

Finding out what is owed

Order a tax certificate. It costs $10.00, payment comes first, and it shows the status of taxes, including penalties and interest if they are delinquent.

If you owned the house on January 1, you remain personally liable for that year's tax even after selling in July, and the lien stays attached to the property. Title agents and buyers therefore insist on the certificate before closing. Order yours early.

Exemptions that help a buyer or seller

Local exemptions include the general residence homestead, a disabled exemption, a 100 percent disabled veteran exemption and an over-65 exemption. For school taxes, $140,000 comes off a homestead, with $60,000 more at age 65 or for a disability.

Someone buying after January 1 can begin the exemption immediately when the seller never had one. File applications with the appraisal district before May 1.

An inherited house or one with liens

First prove who may sign the deed. Texas gives heirs four years to probate a will, offers a small estate affidavit for modest estates, and lets an owner pass a house without probate through a deed recorded during life. Title agents want one of those papers before they close.

Tax foreclosures carry their own rules. A homestead owner has two years after the purchaser's deed is filed to redeem, and the former owner can claim surplus from a tax foreclosure for two years.

Papers to pull together

Before you talk to buyers, gather the deed, a Bexar tax statement or certificate, each lender's payoff figure and proof of any exemption or deferral on the account. For an inherited house, add the will or court order and a list of heirs. A buyer's title agent will request all of it, and having it ready keeps the closing date from slipping.

Photos of repairs you have already made, and a plain list of ones you have not, help a cash buyer quote faster. They also help a listing agent describe the house honestly.

Choosing between offers

Offers differ in more than price. Ask each buyer whether the figure stays firm after the walkthrough, who pays for the title policy, how long the inspection window lasts and whether you may stay a few days after closing. Write the answers down, then compare offers by the amount you would take home and the number of weeks to funding.

How a cash sale moves along

You provide the address and describe the condition. The buyer visits, then makes an offer on paper that reflects any repairs. When you accept, a title company opens the file, searches for liens and tax balances and collects payoff letters. You choose the closing date, and funds reach you after the lender and the county have been paid.

Skipping a listing means skipping buyer loans and repair negotiations, which is where weeks usually disappear. In exchange, expect a price below a retail sale. Weigh the offer by what you would net after commission, repairs and the carrying costs of waiting.

Frequently asked questions

Where is Converse, Texas?

In northeastern Bexar County, about thirteen miles northeast of downtown San Antonio, on Farm Road 1976.

Does Bexar County have a ten-month tax payment plan?

Yes, and it is the only Texas county with one. It is open to homesteads with an over-65, disabled or disabled veteran exemption, or a qualifying surviving spouse.

What is a Bexar County tax certificate?

It is a document showing the status of taxes on a property, with penalties and interest if delinquent. The fee is $10.00 and payment comes first.

Who sets property values for a Converse home?

Bexar Appraisal District values the property and decides exemptions. The tax office bills and collects. Call the district about exemptions and the tax office about statements.

Do I still owe taxes if I sold my Converse house during the year?

The owner on January 1 stays personally liable, and the lien follows the property, so the closing papers should settle that year's tax.

Ways to sell a Southlake house

Owners in Southlake choose among an agent, a private sale and a cash bid. What you hope to get, what shape the house is in and when you must close drive the decision. The city sits at State Highway 114 and Farm Road 1709, seventeen miles north of Fort Worth, next to Grapevine, Keller and Dallas-Fort Worth International Airport. Most houses here went up within the last four decades, so buyers will think hard about how old your HVAC, roof and finishes are.

  • Agent: the biggest audience, with staging, showings and a lender's timeline to endure.
  • Private sale: you keep the commission and take on the marketing and negotiation.
  • Cash bid: a quick as-is sale, priced to cover the buyer's repair costs and risk.

Compare offers by the check you would actually receive once the loan, taxes and closing costs are paid. The headline price can mislead.

Two counties, two appraisal districts

Southlake sits across the line between Tarrant and Denton counties. Its tax page links to both the Tarrant County Appraisal District and the Denton County Appraisal District, and the side your house sits on decides its appraisal district, tax collector and county clerk.

Your tax bill and your deed both name the county, and the bill also lists the taxing units. Read them before anyone orders a payoff or records a deed, then give copies to the title company at the outset so it contacts the right office and clerk.

Why the county line matters at closing

A Denton County parcel and a Tarrant County parcel can sit a few blocks apart yet use different offices for almost every step. The appraisal district, the tax office quoting your payoff and the clerk who records your deed all follow the county. A seller who calls the wrong one loses days. Write the county at the top of your checklist, and tell each buyer which one applies so their title company starts in the right place. Southlake's proximity to Keller, Grapevine and the airport draws buyers from several directions, and many will not know the split exists.

The city homestead exemption and tax pages

Southlake offers a 20 percent homestead exemption and describes it as the highest state law allows. Texas now requires every city to post a notice pointing to the appraisal district database where a parcel's estimated tax appears. Southlake complies with links to the Tarrant and Denton districts. The city also offers a form for property tax and budget questions. Search for your own parcel in the correct district's database instead of trusting a neighborhood average.

Texas property tax calendar

The statewide schedule shapes what a seller owes at closing. Values and homestead status freeze on January 1, and the tax lien attaches the same day.

DateWhat happens
January 1Value is set, exemptions are decided and the tax lien attaches

Separately from the city's exemption, a school district takes $140,000 off a principal residence, and $60,000 more off for older or disabled owners.

If you think the value is too high

If the appraised value on your April 1 notice looks high, you may protest. The usual cutoff is May 15, or 30 days after the notice when that falls later. Send it to the district for whichever county, Tarrant or Denton, holds your parcel, along with repair estimates, photos and any recent nearby sale prices. Permits and building inspections

If you finished a basement, added a room or replaced a roof or a major system, make sure each job was permitted and passed inspection. A buyer's inspector or lender may want proof, and a permit still open can delay closing. Southlake keeps its permit system online, so try your address there first. With these in hand a cash buyer can act quickly, and a listing agent will want most of them as well. You also avoid finding out about a lien or a missing permit in the final week.

Pricing and timing in Southlake

Buyers here compare houses closely. A listing that lingers draws lower offers, and a house needing work draws investors. Settle early on whether the top price or a firm date matters more. When a cash buyer names a date you can plan around, set it against what an agent expects after commission, repairs and carrying costs. Also ask each bidder, in writing, who pays and what happens if the title search turns up a problem. A clear answer now avoids a dispute at the closing table.

Selling a house you have remodeled

Southlake owners often update kitchens, baths and outdoor spaces before selling. Keep the permit number for each job, plus the final inspection date if you have it. A buyer who sees closed permits relaxes, and a lender has less to question. If the work was done by a contractor, find out whether that contractor was registered with the city, since the division expects registration. Photos before and after, and a short list of what was replaced and when, help a buyer's agent explain the value of the work.

Contacting City Hall

City Hall's phone is (817) 748-8400, and it answers weekdays between 8 a.m. and 5 p.m. A request portal called Southlake Serves handles questions that need follow-up. Residents use it to request a permit record, check a rule before listing or raise a concern about a neighbor's project that could affect a sale.

Deed filing

Depending on the parcel's location, either the Tarrant County Clerk or the Denton County Clerk records a Southlake deed. The signature needs an authorized officer's acknowledgment. Recording is priced by the page, with records charges on top, so longer documents cost more. Ask the title company for the exact total.

Inherited house or mortgage default

Probate of a will can begin up to four years after the date of death. If liens are the estate's only debts, a muniment of title can pass the property under the will. A small estate affidavit is out of reach once assets exceed $75,000, a total that leaves out the homestead and exempt property.

When a mortgage goes into default, the borrower has 20 days after the notice to catch up. An auction follows on the first Tuesday of a month, with 21 days' notice beforehand. Closing a sale first can preserve equity an auction might not.

What a cash closing involves

As soon as you accept a bid, the title company opens a file, looks for liens and asks the applicable county for tax figures. Then a closing date is chosen, and you sign before a notary, with your photo ID, the deed and the latest tax bill. Since the parcel may be in Tarrant or Denton County, ask which clerk will record the deed. Proof of funds and the date should be on paper before you commit.

Which county is Southlake in?

Both Tarrant and Denton counties. Your deed and tax bill show which one covers your parcel.

What homestead exemption does Southlake offer?

The city offers a 20 percent homestead exemption, which it calls the highest level state law allows. School districts add the state's $140,000 exemption.

Where do I find my Southlake property tax amount?

Look up your parcel in the Tarrant County or Denton County appraisal district database, which the city's tax page links to. Texas law requires that database to show estimated taxes.

Do I need permit proof to sell a Southlake house?

The law does not require it for every sale, yet buyers and lenders often ask on remodels and additions. Call Southlake Building Inspections at (817) 748-8236 to learn whether a permit was closed.

How soon can a Southlake house close for cash?

It is often quicker than a financed sale because nobody waits on loan approval. Title work, liens, probate or a tenant can still set the pace, so ask each bidder for proof of funds and a written closing date.

Getting a fast sale done in Alvin

Three things speed up an Alvin sale: clean tax and title records, candid answers about storms and flooding, and a buyer able to close when you need. The city is in the northeast part of Brazoria County, about twelve miles southeast of Houston, so taxes and deeds run through Brazoria County offices.

Alvin grew from 21,413 residents in 2000 to an estimated 30,115 in 2025. Sellers normally weigh an agent listing, a sale they manage themselves, and a cash offer. Cash is often quickest when the house needs repairs, has had water damage, came from an estate, or has a tenant, since the buyer accepts it as it stands.

  • Agent listing: suits a move-in ready house if you can wait on a buyer with a loan.
  • Self-managed sale: you deal with the buyer, the contract and the title steps.
  • Cash offer: a lone buyer, no lender, and a closing date built around your plans.

Alvin housing figures

Alvin is a mid-sized suburb south of Houston with lower prices than much of the metro. Population is estimated at 30,115 for 2025, up 11.7% from the 2020 base, when the count was 27,098.

About four in ten homes are rented, so an investor can be as likely a buyer as a family.

Storm and flood history

Alvin has long lived with severe weather. Floods, hurricanes and tornadoes threaten the area each year from July through November. The 1900 Galveston hurricane wrecked most of the city's businesses and homes, tropical storm Claudette dropped forty-three inches of rain near town in twenty-four hours in 1979, and Alicia hit four years later. That record is why buyers ask pointed questions about flooding and insurance.

Expect them to ask about elevation, any water that has entered the house, roof age and wind rating. For new construction the city's adopted codes use a wind load of 140 mph and require engineer-sealed drawings, a survey and a plot plan.

  • Ask the city's engineering and permit staff which flood zone your lot is in, and keep any elevation certificate.
  • Gather records of past repairs, including who did the work and whether a permit was pulled.
  • Know whether the house carries flood insurance and what the premium has been.
  • If you rebuilt after storm damage, keep the final inspection record.

Brazoria County also lets owners in a declared disaster area pay their tax bill in installments, described below. That can matter if the house was hit by a storm that year.

City permits and what they mean at closing

Alvin requires permits and inspections for new construction, remodeling and repairs. Before buying a remodel or repair permit, a homeowner must show proof of a homestead exemption, so a house worked on by a previous owner should have its history on file.

Inspections need 24 hours' notice and are scheduled in the city's online MyGov portal, the same place permits are handled. Driveways and driveway culverts need permits as well. Residential driveways can be 12 to 24 feet wide, and the front ditch may not be enclosed. When the lot fronts a state highway, TxDOT must issue a permit too.

If you replaced a driveway, added a room or finished a garage during your ownership, ask the permit office whether the permit was closed out. An open permit is a common reason a closing slips.

Brazoria County property taxes

The county tax assessor-collector mails the bills. The Brazoria Central Appraisal District, at 500 N Chenango Street in Angleton, values property and processes exemptions. It keeps weekday hours from eight until four-thirty, and the main number is 979-849-7792.

The county tax office offers several ways to pay:

  • Half pay: half by November 30 and the rest by June 30 of the following year.
  • Age and disability plan: four equal payments due January 31, March 31, May 31 and July 31, open to qualifying homesteads and unmarried surviving spouses.
  • Disaster plan: the same four payments for owners whose property was damaged in a declared disaster area.
  • Deferral: owners 65 or over, or disabled, can postpone payment with an affidavit filed at the appraisal district, and 5 percent interest accrues each year.
  • Partial payments: any amount is accepted, and only the unpaid remainder draws penalty and interest.

A deferral comes due when the owner no longer owns and lives in the home, so a sale triggers it. Tell the title company early about any deferral or installment plan so the payoff comes out right.

The person buying your house applies at the appraisal district and brings a driver's license or state ID showing the property address. If you hold a school tax ceiling, ask the district you are leaving for a certificate that carries the ceiling to a new county.

Probate, foreclosure and tax sales

Filings for an Alvin property go through Brazoria County.

  • Estates: offer a will for probate within four years of the death. If no administration is needed, heirs may use a muniment of title and file the court order and will with the county clerk.
  • Mortgage default: for most home loans the lender must wait until the loan is more than 120 days behind, allow 20 days to cure, then give at least 21 days' notice of sale.
  • Tax sales: a former homestead owner whose home was sold for taxes has two years from the filing of the purchaser's deed to redeem, under a Texas Supreme Court opinion.

Selling before an auction date keeps the choice of buyer in your hands.

Selling an Alvin house with a repair backlog

A house with storm damage, an old roof or unfinished permit work can still sell. The difference lies in who carries the repair cost. In a listing, the buyer's inspector writes up the problems and your price comes under pressure. A cash buyer looks at the house once and makes an offer that already allows for repairs, so nothing needs fixing before closing.

Whichever route you choose, gather the paperwork early: tax statements, any installment or deferral agreement, flood insurance details and permit records. Ask the title company to run the payoff figures, since taxes and liens are paid from your proceeds at closing. That sequence keeps surprises off the closing table.

If a tenant lives there, add the lease to the folder. Buyers want to know the term, the rent and whether the occupant is staying, and a clear answer lets them decide quickly instead of asking for time to investigate.

Frequently asked questions

Is Alvin, Texas in a flood-prone area?

Parts of it are, and storms have hit the city hard before. Floods, hurricanes and tornadoes threaten the area from July through November. Ask the city which flood zone your lot is in.

Can I pay my Alvin property taxes in installments?

In some cases. Brazoria County offers a half-and-half split, a four-payment plan for qualifying age, disability and disabled veteran homesteads, the same plan for owners in a declared disaster area, deferral for older or disabled owners, and partial payments.

Is a permit required for work on my Alvin house?

Yes for new construction, remodeling and repairs, and for driveways and culverts too. You must show proof of a homestead exemption before the city sells you a permit.

Who sets the value of my Alvin home for tax purposes?

The Brazoria Central Appraisal District, on N Chenango Street in Angleton. Owners apply there for homestead and age-based exemptions.

How many people live in Alvin?

An estimated 30,115 as of July 1, 2025.

Selling in a young, fast-growing Melissa

Melissa is small, young and almost entirely owner-occupied, so most competing listings are recent construction. An older or unrenovated house has to stand next to builder product with current finishes.

Where Melissa sits

You will find Melissa along U.S. Highway 75, roughly seven miles northeast of McKinney, in the north central part of Collin County. A railroad brought the 1872 townsite, and growth stayed slow for about a century.

Ask the county tax office for the amount due before the closing date.

Building rules and permits

A casita, garage apartment or similar extra building on your lot calls for a look at Melissa's rules on second dwellings. The city has allowed accessory dwelling units only in its larger single-family zones, on lots over 10,000 square feet, with review of parking, spacing and setbacks. State law can change what a city allows, so ask the planning staff what applies to your lot today.

  • Confirm with the city that every added structure on the lot was permitted.
  • Round up permits and final inspections for any addition. Lenders and inspectors both request them.
  • Check your HOA documents, because most newer Melissa subdivisions have them.

Unpermitted work often pushes back a closing date. Settling it before you list leaves the schedule under your control.

How Texas property tax dates affect a newer Melissa home

January 1 is when a year's tax lien attaches and when the appraisal district fixes your house's value. A sale in, say, June means the buyer inherits a bill that has been building for months.

Selling with a tenant, an heir or a default

Rentals are uncommon at a median rent of $2,532, and the typical buyer plans to move in. If a tenant lives there, expect to serve a three day written notice to vacate unless the lease sets something else. A tenant who refuses to leave ends up in justice court. Work your closing date backward from the lease end.

Inherited house? A will can be offered for probate within four years of the death, or heirs can file a muniment of title or affidavit of heirship with the county clerk. Behind on the loan? What Melissa buyers look for

Why Melissa has so many buyers

A lot of people have moved into a small area. Land grew from 10.11 square miles in 2010 to 11.45, yet density jumped from 464.3 to 1,213.8 people per square mile by 2020.

Just 81.6 percent of residents had the same address a year before, a sign of steady newcomers. Sellers get lively buyer traffic from that, though it also means neighbors on your street may have arrived recently. Newer subdivisions bring uniform lots, so condition, upgrades and the location of your lot within the neighborhood tend to set the price spread.

Can I sell a Melissa house with a tenant in it?

What exemption applies to a Melissa homestead?

The base is $140,000 from the school district, with $60,000 added at age 65 or on disability. Apply to the appraisal district by the end of April.

Do I need probate to sell my late parent's Melissa house?

Usually some court or recorded step comes first. A transfer on death deed recorded before the death skips probate.

Your fast-sale options in Fate

Fate owners can sell to a cash buyer, list with an agent, or sell without fixing anything. Demand comes from a city that grew from about 500 people in 2000 to an estimated 23,000 in 2022. Because growth was so fast, many nearby homes are recent builds, and an older or heavily worn house competes against newer neighbors.

That is the main reason owners here choose an as-is sale. It skips staging, repairs and the wait while a financed buyer's appraisal clears.

  • Cash offer: short closing, no repair list, usually at a discount.
  • Agent listing: more exposure and a higher possible price, with showings.

The city went from 497 residents in 2000 to 6,357 in 2010, 17,500 in 2019 and 23,000 in 2022. The comprehensive plan expects it to pass 50,000 people at build-out. New subdivisions keep arriving, so buyers have choices and price and condition count for more than location alone.

Schools and utilities

Rockwall ISD serves the west side of the city and Royse City ISD the east side. Confirm which one covers your address, because buyers ask early.

Water comes from the North Texas Municipal Water District. Electric service is split between a member-owned co-op, Farmers Electric Cooperative, and the Oncor grid, where residents pick a retail provider. Atmos Energy supplies natural gas. The city bills for trash and recycling, and Waste Connections does the pickup under contract. Pet registration costs $5.00 per pet.

Permits and building rules

The Building Safety department enforces the adopted codes: the 2021 International Building, Residential, Plumbing, Fire, Mechanical and Energy Conservation codes, the 2021 Fuel Gas Code and the 2023 National Electric Code. Contractors must register with the city, and the city posts a list of those who have.

If you added a deck, converted a garage or did other work, ask Building Safety whether permits were pulled. A missing permit can slow a buyer who needs a loan, and a cash buyer will lower the price to cover the risk. Fixing the paperwork before listing is cheaper than negotiating it afterward, and the city office can tell you what is on file for your address in a single call.

Storm and repair records

Buyers in North Texas ask about weather damage. If your house had burst pipes after the February 2021 freeze, a roof replacement or an insurance claim, keep every document, since an inspector or lender may ask for it.

  • Roof age and receipts for storm repairs.
  • Plumbing work done after hard freezes.
  • Insurance claim records and payouts.

Fate is a short drive from Dallas, and the closest DART station is Downtown Rowlett, about 17 miles west. STAR Transit buses serve parts of Rockwall and Kaufman counties, with a GoPass app for monthly and day passes. Commute options are worth a line in a listing.

  • Costs that reduce your proceeds: the loan payoff, unpaid taxes, recording fees and title charges.

From offer to closing

Selling to an investor follows a short chain. Gather bids, compare what each would leave you, choose one and sign the purchase contract. The buyer then opens an escrow file. A search of public records looks for liens, back taxes and name mismatches, and anything it finds must be cleared before funds move. You sign the deed with a notary present, your lender and the tax share get paid, and you receive the balance.

Delays usually trace to paperwork rather than the buyer. Bring the deed, the latest tax bill, a loan payoff letter, a list of utility accounts to close, and keys or garage remotes for every door. If the house sits empty, tell the buyer who has been checking on it. A relative who co-owns the property has to sign as well.

  • Ask how many days the buyer needs after signing.
  • Ask who pays for the title policy and recording.
  • Ask whether the price can change once the buyer walks through.

Put every promise in the contract itself, including who keeps the appliances, and read it twice before you sign. A seller who asks these questions early usually gets a cleaner closing than one who waits for the last week.

Probate and inherited property

When the owner has died, the county probate court can admit a will within four years. Clear title afterward depends on the estate. Heirs can avoid full administration through a muniment of title if the only debts are secured by the real estate.

A small estate affidavit is meant for estates worth $75,000 or less, not counting the homestead. It generally cannot move real property other than a homestead going to a spouse or minor children, and a judge has to sign off. Fate lies in Rockwall County, so the deed or probate order is recorded with that county's clerk.

  • Transfer on death deed: filed while the owner is alive.
  • Executor's deed: used when an estate is administered.
  • Affidavit of heirship: sworn, but a buyer need not accept it.

Have a probate attorney choose the route before you say yes to a buyer, and expect the buyer to want recorded proof of who may sign.

Tax dates and closing fees

Rates come from each taxing unit, while the appraisal district fixes values as of January 1. Statements are mailed around October 1, due when received, and January 31 is normally the last day to pay without delinquency.

If a balance is still open on February 1, a six percent penalty and one percent interest attach. The year's lien starts January 1. Vehicle registration for Fate runs through the Rockwall County tax office, and the county tax assessor-collector commonly bills property tax too, so call the county for your parcel's exact amount.

Once the sale closes, the deed becomes part of the public record at the clerk's office. Keep a copy of it and of the final settlement statement.

The population rose from 497 in 2000 to 23,000 in 2022. The comprehensive plan expects it to pass 50,000 at build-out.

Rockwall ISD serves the west side and Royse City ISD the east side. Confirm your address with the district before you list.

Does Fate require permits for home repairs?

Building Safety enforces adopted codes including the 2021 International Residential Code, so ask the city before structural, electrical or plumbing work.

Can I sell an inherited Fate house without probate?

Sometimes. A transfer on death deed recorded before the owner died or a muniment of title can avoid full administration, but an affidavit of heirship alone may not satisfy a title company.

When are Texas property taxes due on a Fate home?

Bills go out around October 1 and the tax is delinquent after January 31. A six percent penalty and one percent interest apply starting February 1.

Because 60.3% of households own, rentals are common, and some buyers are landlords who want a tenant in place. Say clearly whether you will deliver the house vacant. A vacant house is easier to show but costs utilities and insurance while you wait.

Older downtown Katy and newer subdivisions

The town site was platted in 1895 along the railroad and rebuilt after the 1900 hurricane. Katy became a city in 1945, and a local committee placed historical markers on more than a dozen older homes and buildings downtown in 1986. Much newer housing now surrounds that core.

Own one of the older downtown houses? Check with city planning staff on what rules apply before ordering exterior work. Period details deserve a line in your pitch, and the markers make a pleasant walking tour for out-of-town buyers.

For most structural, mechanical and outdoor jobs, yes. Katy's Permit and Building Services division wants a permit for new construction, remodeling, roofing, heating and cooling systems, electrical and plumbing, and anything that adds or removes walls.

Pools, hot tubs, storage buildings, carports, garages, driveways, sidewalks, patios, irrigation, water heaters, demolition and house moving are on the list too. An owner can still buy the property back in some cases. If you owe back taxes, a sale before any suit usually costs far less than letting it reach auction, since court costs and attorney fees are added along the way.

A mortgage in default or an inherited house

A Katy loan in default moves along the Texas out-of-court track: a default letter, a brief chance to catch up, then a posted and recorded sale notice and an auction on a first Tuesday. A housing counselor can show where your loan stands.

Inheriting from a relative? Find out whether a will exists and whether anyone opened probate. To keep the homestead tax break, heirs show the appraisal district proof of kinship and the death certificate. A lawyer in Harris, Fort Bend or Waller County can name the right deed route.

On any route, get a closing date in writing along with a plain division of title and recording charges. If renters live there, line the date up with the end of their lease. Since Katy parcels sit in three counties, find out early which clerk files your deed and which tax office issues the payoff statement.

Disclosing unpermitted work

Earlier additions cause more friction than almost anything else in a Katy sale. A garage, a patio or a replaced heating and cooling system may have gone in with no permit on file. Ask city staff whether any record exists. If none does, tell the buyer in writing before the inspector turns it up. Where Royse City sits

Royse City is on State Highway 66 about five miles northeast of Rockwall, in the northeastern corner of Rockwall County, and parts of it lie in Collin and Hunt Counties as well. That three-county layout is the first thing to understand before you sell.

Newer subdivisions now wrap around the older downtown blocks, and taxable value has climbed quickly. Shoppers here often tour brand-new construction before they see your place.

Three counties, three appraisal districts

The county your parcel falls in picks the appraisal district that values the house and the clerk who records the deed. The Rockwall, Collin and Hunt County appraisal districts each certify values for property inside the city, and Rockwall CAD compiles the three rolls.

These are taxable values from the city's fiscal year 2025 figures, not sale prices. Look at the top of your tax statement, or search each district's property search, to find the right one. An exemption must be filed with each appraisal district in which the property sits. Ask the tax office of your county for the current combined rate, because that office bills it.

Selling a Royse City house fast

Royse City owners can hire an agent, deal with an investor directly, or sell to a renovator. Condition and timing usually decide which.

  • Agent listing: suits a clean, repaired house and a longer timeline.
  • Direct investor sale: a shorter timeline and fewer contingencies, with the price adjusted for repairs.
  • Renovator sale: suits dated systems, damage or an awkward layout.

Many neighborhoods around town have homeowners association rules. Ask the HOA for a resale certificate or dues statement at the start, since the title company requires one.

How fast taxable values have grown

Growth is uneven across the three counties. Citywide taxable value rose 7.56 percent, with 5.30 percent in the Rockwall portion, 13.21 percent in the Collin portion and 10.49 percent in the Hunt portion. Existing properties alone rose 2.17 percent citywide, and new construction added $114,333,441 to the certified total.

Most of the jump comes from new building, not from older houses repricing. So look at recent sales on your own street, not citywide percentages, when you set a price. Taxable value also trails the market, so a tax bill is a poor guide to what buyers will pay. A buyer's agent will know this, and a seller who points to recent street sales looks better prepared than one who quotes a tax figure.

Permits and the MyGov system

Selling takes no permit. Improving or altering a property does, and the permit comes before the work. If you finished a project such as a pergola, flatwork or an electrical change, confirm it was permitted and inspected.

  • Permits, contractor registration, fee payment and project status run through the city's MyGov system.
  • Plan review may take as long as 10 business days, and feedback comes through MyGov or email.
  • Contractors must be registered before they can get a permit.
  • Inspection requests must be in by 4 pm for next-day inspection.

The Building Inspection department handles building, zoning and property maintenance ordinances, including fencing, yards and open space. Reach it at 972-524-4710 or permits@roysecity.com. Payment can be made through MyGov, by mail or at City Hall.

The city publishes permit guides for flatwork, arbors, pergolas and gazebos, and new single-family dwellings. Each says work cannot start until the permit is issued, and approved plans must be on site at inspection.

Before you list, gather permit numbers for any addition, fence, flatwork or electrical change, confirm each was inspected, and keep the approval email or MyGov record. A closed permit helps with a buyer's lender or inspector, and a past contractor's registered name makes the work easy to trace.

Property taxes and exemptions when you sell

Texas uses a single tax calendar, and a statewide homestead rule limits yearly rises in appraised value. The Comptroller publishes school district homestead exemptions and the age and disability add-ons, and your appraisal district can show which exemptions are on your house.

If the prior owner never filed, a buyer who moves in after January 1 can still claim the exemption for the remainder of that year. If a closing falls between the November 30 and June 30 halves of a split payment, the title company confirms what is paid.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Royse City houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Why the county matters on closing day

A title company in a three-county city checks one thing before anything else: which county holds the parcel. That answer tells it which tax office to ask for a balance, which appraisal district's exemptions apply and which clerk receives the deed. A wrong guess costs days.

If you are unsure, read the legal description on your deed and the header of your tax statement, then call the building inspection office or the appraisal district to confirm. Do this before you sign a contract so your closing date is realistic.

A lien, a tenant or an estate

Each has its own filing route.

  • Tax lien: unpaid tax follows the property and has to be paid before closing.
  • Tenant: a written notice to vacate comes first, then a justice court suit.
  • Estate: the route may be a beneficiary deed, a court-approved muniment, an affidavit of heirship or an administrator's deed.

The deed is recorded with the clerk of the county where the parcel sits, which here could be Rockwall, Collin or Hunt.

Papers to gather before you list

Buyers and title companies in Royse City keep asking for the same records, so having them ready saves a round of emails.

  • Your deed, plus the latest tax statement from whichever county bills your parcel.
  • A payoff statement from each lender with a lien.
  • The HOA resale certificate, dues statement and any pending assessment.
  • Permit numbers and inspection records for additions, fences, flatwork and electrical changes.
  • The utility account details, so service can move to the buyer on closing day.

For an inherited house, add the death certificate and the court order or affidavit that applies. With a tenant in place, bring the lease and schedule showings around the notice period.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

From offer to closing in Royse City

Once you accept an offer, the title company opens a file and requests a balance from your county's tax office. It also collects the HOA resale certificate and orders a payoff from your lender. Because three counties touch the city, the first thing the title company confirms is where your parcel sits.

You sign the deed at closing. The title company files it with your county clerk, settles the loan and any tax out of the proceeds, and pays you the remainder. A direct cash purchase has no lender appraisal or underwriting step, which leaves title work and any lien or estate paperwork as the pacing items.

Get each buyer's price, closing date and repair terms in writing, then compare what you would net.

Frequently asked questions

Which county do I pay taxes to for a Royse City house?

That follows the parcel. Royse City spans Rockwall, Collin and Hunt Counties, and each district certifies values for its own portion, so check the top of your tax statement or search all three districts.

Does Royse City require permits for fences or flatwork?

The city has guides for flatwork and for arbors, pergolas and gazebos, so call 972-524-4710 before assuming no permit applies.

How long does Royse City plan review take?

Up to 10 business days. Feedback goes through MyGov or by email to the contact on the application.

Can heirs sell a Royse City house without probate?

Sometimes. Whether a beneficiary deed, muniment of title or affidavit of heirship applies depends on the paperwork, and a title company can say which one a buyer's lender will accept.

When does tax become late?

After January 31, with penalty and interest starting February 1.

Selling in Lake Jackson?

Selling a house in Lake Jackson

Lake Jackson is a planned city, so many houses sit on curved streets under mature oaks. Buyers often care about the lot, the trees and the drainage as much as the floor plan. Population was 26,386 in 2000, and a seller who can explain the neighborhood and the Brazoria County tax picture tends to get fewer surprises late in the deal.

You have two basic routes. An agent can show the house to the most people, though you take on fix-up work, open houses and a buyer's loan approval. An investor offer is faster and asks nothing of you in the way of repairs. Work out your take-home on each after the mortgage, the tax bill and settlement charges, and let your calendar break the tie.

Lots, trees and drainage

Before a single lot was cleared, the planner drew the whole town on paper and asked crews to spare as many trees as they could. Streets are called drives, ways and streets. Drives circle the outskirts as through routes, streets end at drives or ways, and ways lead downtown. Street names come from flowers, fruits, shrubs and trees. Jackson Lake, Flagg Lake and two other lakes sit inside the town.

  • Curved streets give each lot its own shape, so check survey lines before listing.
  • Oak roots can reach slabs and sewer pipes, so have an inspector check both.
  • Older homes near downtown pre-date later codes, so gather any permit records you have.
  • A house near one of the lakes should come with drainage records and its flood zone designation from the city or county, since lenders ask for them.

Houses from the postwar boom and later

Lake Jackson began in 1941 and grew in stages: 2,897 residents in 1950, 11,090 in 1958, 19,102 in 1980 and 22,776 in 1990. Your house could be from the first postwar years or from a far later decade; the appraisal record shows the build year.

Older houses can carry foundation, plumbing and wiring questions. A pre-listing inspection costs less than a failed contract, and the report gives buyers a baseline they can trust. Shoppers also want to know which Brazosport Independent School District campus serves the address, and the zoning on the lot is worth confirming before you advertise.

Brazoria County tax payment options

Brazoria County gives owners several ways to spread a bill, and a buyer may use one of them after closing. If one is active on your house, tell the closing office so the payoff figure is right.

Payment options offered by the Brazoria County Tax Office
Payment optionRule
Split paymentHalf by November 30, remainder by June 30 of the next year, no penalty or interest
Over 65, disabled or disabled veteranFour equal installments due January 31, March 31, May 31 and July 31
Disaster area installmentSame four dates, for damaged property in a declared disaster area
DeferralElderly or disabled owners sign an affidavit, interest of 5 percent a year applies
