Details are on the Brazoria County Tax Office payment page.

Selling with deferred or unpaid taxes

A deferral ends the day the owner stops owning and living in the house, so closing a sale makes the whole deferred amount, interest included, payable. Debt that stays unpaid can draw penalties and legal action from the taxing units.

Each January 1 a lien for that year's taxes attaches to the property. Request a certificate from the Brazoria County Tax Office that lists every account tied to your parcel, and get it to the closing office ahead of time. Back taxes are paid from the sale proceeds, and the figure is much easier to live with when you saw it before signing day.

Texas tax dates for Lake Jackson owners

The calendar comes from state law, and Brazoria County does the collecting. Once January 31 passes with a balance, penalty and interest begin the following day, and by July 1 the penalty tops out at 12 percent.

  • File a homestead application by April 30; school districts take $140,000 off a homestead's value.
  • Value protests go to the appraisal review board by May 15, with extra time if your notice came late.
  • Statements arrive in October.
  • Older or disabled owners may request a school tax ceiling too.

The state publishes the full details on the Comptroller deadlines page and the exemptions page.

Sell as-isNo repairs, no cleaning and no showings. We buy Lake Jackson houses in any condition.See My Cash Offer →

Which repairs matter before listing?

On the coast, shoppers start with the roof, drainage, windows and foundation. Ask the city's permit office before any major job, and save invoices and permits for the inspector.

When repairs cost too much or time is short, an investor can purchase the house untouched and do the work later. Put that offer next to a repaired listing, subtracting commissions and the months you would keep paying the bills.

Deed recording costs

The Brazoria County clerk records deeds for Lake Jackson land. Three add-ons ride on top of the per-page recording charge: a records management fee of up to $10, a records archive fee of up to $10 and a $2.00 technology fee.

A notary or similar officer has to acknowledge your signature before the clerk will accept the deed. Filing is handled by the closing office; you only need to confirm the names and legal description match your own purchase deed.

Who to call about your Brazoria County account

Start with the Brazoria County Tax Office, which collects the bill, and the Brazoria County Appraisal District, which handles exemptions. Ask each for a written account summary that shows the exemption status, any installment plan or deferral on file, and any back taxes.

Pass both summaries along the day a contract is signed. With an installment plan open, settle early who clears the remaining balance, the buyer or your proceeds. Payoff figures change with the closing date, so request an updated figure for the closing day.

You pick the closing dateClose in as little as 7 days or on the date that works for you, with no fees or commissions.Get My Cash Offer →

What to bring when you visit the county offices

Offices in Brazoria County move faster when you arrive with your parcel number or street address, a photo ID and your latest bill. Ask the tax office whether a split plan, a four-installment plan or a deferral sits on the account, and ask the appraisal district whether a homestead, over-65 or disability exemption is on file. Write down the name of each clerk you speak with and the date, so any promise about a payoff figure can be traced later.

If a buyer plans to keep paying under an installment arrangement, the clerk can tell you what the account looks like today. That one answer often decides whether the closing office needs extra paperwork.

Steps from first offer to closing

  1. Gather your deed, newest tax statement, mortgage payoff statement, and whatever repair or permit records you hold.
  2. Ask for an investor offer and, if you want, a listing agent's price, and line up what each leaves you.
  3. Choose a title company and send it the county tax certificate.
  4. Sign the deed in front of a notary.
  5. Check the closing statement for how the year's tax and any plan balance were divided.

A sale to a cash buyer avoids the mortgage underwriting, the appraisal wait and most repair haggling, which shortens the calendar. You also skip prepping the house for showings.

Frequently asked questions

Who bills the tax on a Lake Jackson house?

The Brazoria County Tax Office sends the bill, using the certified roll from the Brazoria County Appraisal District. Mailing happens in October.

When are Lake Jackson taxes delinquent?

Anything still unpaid after January 31 is late, and penalty and interest start accruing February 1. The penalty reaches 12 percent on July 1.

Can I pay Brazoria County taxes in installments?

In several cases, yes. The split plan is half by November 30 and half by June 30; owners 65 or older, disabled owners and a disabled veteran get four installments.

Does selling end a Brazoria County tax deferral?

Yes. Yes, the deferred amount plus interest is due when you stop owning and living in the house.

Do I need to repair my Lake Jackson house before selling?

No. An investor buys the house in its current shape and lowers the offer to cover the work. Compare that figure with what a repaired listing would clear.

Selling in Balch Springs?

Quick ways for a Balch Springs owner to sell

You can sell a Balch Springs house three ways: list it, handle the sale yourself, or accept cash from an investor who buys it as it stands and closes on your date. What works best depends on the condition of the house, any liens or city notices on it, and how soon you need the funds.

This is mostly an owner city, with 64.7 percent of homes occupied by their owners and 3.29 people in the average household. Sales often involve family homes kept for decades, houses that came through an estate, or rentals whose landlords want out. Most of the housing stock went up in the postwar decades as Dallas commuters moved in, so repairs tied to age are common.

  • Market listing: a good match when the house shows well and the buyer's lender signs off.
  • Investor purchase: skips showings and loan approval, and normally the repair list as well.
  • Payoffs first: mortgage, tax and code-fine balances all come out of the proceeds. Get each figure in writing before you agree to anything.

Balch Springs housing numbers

In the 2020-2024 estimates the typical owned home was worth $224,400 and the typical renter paid $1,378 monthly. Population is estimated at 27,258 for mid-2025: 1.6 percent less than the April 2020 baseline of 27,705, yet far above the 23,728 counted in 2010.

The 9.02 square miles hold about 3,067.9 people each, and roughly 91.9 percent of residents lived at the same address a year earlier. Children here once attended Dallas or Mesquite schools, so find out from the county appraisal district which school district taxes your parcel.

Rental registration and certificate of occupancy

Both are required. Landlords selling, and investors buying, will meet each one.

  • Rental registration: bring a driver's license and proof of ownership, for example closing paperwork or a deed in your name. Renew the registration every two years.
  • Inspection timing: a rental inspection has to happen before a tenant moves in, or the owner owes a violation fee.
  • Certificate of occupancy: bring a driver's license, a lease or proof of ownership, a site map and a floor plan.

Because registration follows the owner's name and deed, an investor who keeps the tenant files a new one after the deed is recorded. To learn what is on file for your address, call Permits and Inspections at 972-286-4477. Inspection requests go by email to inspections@balchspringstx.gov, and the city's permits page has the forms.

Permits and sign-offs when a house changes hands

A seller or investor buyer may need several permits. Electrical, plumbing and air conditioning work each require a separate permit, and a registered master contractor must pull it. A roof job with no structural work can get a same-day permit. The codes in force are the 2021 IRC and IBC and the 2020 NEC.

Running an estate or moving sale at the house? Garage sales are limited to three a calendar year, with 90 days between them. Any contractor you hire for pre-sale repairs must be registered with the city, so check the list first. Permits and Inspections can be reached at 972-286-4477.

Can an open city notice get in the way of a sale?

An open notice will not stop a sale. It does stay with the property, so either clear it or talk it through with the buyer before closing. Code officers drive the neighborhoods every day and answer complaints as well.

Your first letter sets a 10-day deadline to fix the problem, or 7 days for tall grass and solid waste, and stays on record for 12 months. When a second visit shows no change, the officer issues a Notice to Appear naming the ordinance, the fine and the court contact. An owner can request extra time to finish a repair.

Prior to listing, walk your lot with the city's Top 10 violations list, available in English and Spanish on the Code Enforcement page. Disclose any citation or court date to the buyer so nothing delays closing.

Time left before a foreclosure auction

Most Texas deeds of trust let a lender auction the home without a court case. The steps follow a fixed calendar, so a sale ahead of it is often realistic. Under federal servicing rules a first filing normally waits until the loan is over 120 days delinquent.

  • Once the default notice arrives you get 20 days to reinstate by paying the past-due amount.
  • Next the servicer must send notice of sale 21 or more days ahead, then post it at the courthouse and file it with the county clerk.
  • Bidding happens on the first Tuesday of the month, from 10 a.m. until 4 p.m.
  • A shortfall after the sale gives the lender two years to sue, and the borrower can request credit for the home's fair market value.

The Dallas County commissioners court picks the auction site, and the county clerk can tell you where. A sale that closes before that Tuesday pays off the loan with the proceeds. The State Law Library's foreclosure guide covers every stage.

How a tenant changes the sale

Every buyer should see the lease, because it controls what a new owner may do about the occupant. If the tenant must be gone by closing, a written notice to vacate normally allows three days at minimum, unless the lease sets another period.

If the tenant will not leave, the matter goes to justice court. Service must come four days or more before trial, and the hearing is set 10 to 21 days after filing. Either side may appeal to county court within five days of a loss. A writ of possession cannot issue until six days after final judgment. Many owners avoid the whole process by choosing a buyer who will keep the tenant.

Filing the deed and finishing the sale

The Dallas County clerk records deeds for the city, which lies in Dallas County. Your signature has to be acknowledged before a notary or other authorized officer. After funding, the title company records the deed and pays each lien from your proceeds. Keep the settlement statement and payoff receipts.

Frequently asked questions

Must I keep my rental registered until the Balch Springs sale closes?

Yes, as long as the house is rented. A registration runs two years and needs an inspection before any tenant moves in. If the buyer keeps renting, they register under their own name with proof of ownership.

How soon must a Balch Springs code notice be fixed?

Within ten days for most notices, seven for tall grass or solid waste. A second inspection that still finds the problem leads to a citation with a fine and a court date, though you may ask for more time.

Where is the deed filed for a Balch Springs sale?

At the Dallas County clerk's office, because the city is in Dallas County. Sign the deed and have it acknowledged by a notary or other authorized officer.

Is it too late to sell once the lender posts a foreclosure notice?

No, provided the sale closes first. You have 20 days after the default notice to reinstate, and the lender owes 21 or more days' notice of sale. Count backward from the first Tuesday of the month.

How many people live in Balch Springs?

About 27,258 in July 2025, living in 8,247 households counted for 2020-2024. That sits 1.6 percent under the April 2020 baseline, on 9.02 square miles.

Choosing how to sell in Denison

A Denison's owner can hire an agent, hunt for a buyer alone, or phone someone who pays cash. Speed, repair spending and the final price all pull in different directions, so decide your priorities before you pick up any call.

Denison grew up around the railroad. The city was established on September 23, 1872, and incorporated on March 7, 1873. It sits in Grayson County and has roughly 28,000 residents. In a smaller city the pool of listing buyers is thinner, and a house with deferred maintenance can sit longer than it would in a big metro.

  • On the market: a stronger price is possible, but you face open houses, inspection requests and loan approval.
  • By owner: the commission is yours to keep, along with every contract and every round of haggling.
  • To a cash buyer: few contingencies and an early closing, with a price that has the buyer's repair costs built in.

Who bills Denison property tax, and the 2025 rates

Bills come from the Grayson County Tax Assessor-Collector. Value is the job of the Grayson County Appraisal District, found at 205 N Travis Street in Sherman. The county tax office has a main location at 100 W Houston in Sherman and a Denison office at the County Sub-Courthouse, 101 W Woodard.

Sales tax is 8.25 percent and the hotel and motel tax is 7 percent. Your own bill may differ from this table, so call the county tax office to confirm. For general city questions, the administration offices are at 300 W. Main St.

Due dates and penalties

Tax notices arrive in October and payment is normally due by January 31. A bill still open on February 1 is delinquent, and from then on the collector adds penalty and interest, with the penalty rising until July 1. The year's lien lands on January 1 on whoever owns the house, which is why buyers and title companies insist the current year be settled when you close.

  • Call the Grayson County tax office early for the balance on your account.
  • State law lets owners who are over 65 or disabled pay in four installments.
  • A delinquent account may qualify for a payment plan, which a homestead owner can insist on.

If you owe back taxes, the title company can pay them from your sale proceeds when it closes the file.

Permits to sort out before you hand over the house

Most structural work needs a city permit, and a few of the ones sellers forget are worth checking. A permit is required for any new fence, a replacement fence, or a fence repair covering 20 feet or more, and for every detached storage building or shed of any size.

A building permit stays valid while work goes on. It expires if work is suspended or abandoned for 180 days after issue or after the last approved inspection. An owner can take out a homeowner permit only for an owner-occupied single-family house that carries a homestead exemption, which the appraisal district verifies. A rental or a house without the exemption sends the applicant down the general contractor route, and any electrical, plumbing or mechanical work that needs a state license stays off limits.

The application usually asks for a scope of work with materials, owner and contractor contact details, a site plan or drawing, and a registered contractor. Request a final inspection through the online portal. The building office keeps weekday hours, 8 am to 5 pm. Cash or check works for in-person permit payments at the Building Inspections office, and the portal takes cards.

Historic downtown rules

One part of town has extra rules. In the area running from the 700 block of West Main to the 300 block of East Main, between Gandy Street and Crawford Street, exterior work, including painting, goes to the Historical Preservation Board. A buyer planning changes there should ask the city first. Certificates of occupancy apply to new buildings and tenant spaces, so the owner of a mixed-use building downtown should ask the department which rule fits.

Inherited house or mortgage behind?

Texas sets fixed steps for both situations, and a quick sale can work in either one if the paperwork is ready. If the owner left a will, there is a four-year window to probate it. If there is no will and the estate is small, a small estate affidavit can fit. It covers $75,000 in assets, leaves out homestead and exempt property, and needs a court's approval.

When a mortgage is in default, the lender mails a default notice, and paying the missed amount within 20 days reinstates the loan. A public sale follows an auction notice and happens on a first Tuesday, within a set window from morning to afternoon. Ask the Grayson County clerk where foreclosure notices are posted.

If you close before the sale date, the foreclosure on that loan stops. Have your servicer put the payoff in writing.

Filing the deed

A notary witnesses your signature, and the Grayson County clerk, who keeps the land records, files the deed. A conveyance without a proper acknowledgment cannot be recorded. Even though a branch tax office sits in town, a Denison house is filed in Grayson County, the county of the land. The title company will quote the clerk's recording charges and the final total.

Before you list, gather the last deed, your tax receipts and any lien releases. One missing paper can hold up a closing.

Getting from offer to closing

Accepting an offer starts a paper chase. Ask your lender for a payoff, get the current balance from the tax office, and confirm that every fence, shed or remodel permit has been closed out. If a tenant or a relative lives in the house, agree the move-out date in writing. Walk the property once more before closing, and take out anything the contract says you will remove.

Keep copies of what you send to the title company, and note the date. If a buyer asks for a repair credit or a later closing, answer in writing so the contract and your records match. A short written summary of the terms you agreed, sent to the buyer and the title company, heads off most late disputes.

A cash closing usually moves faster than a financed one, since no lender has to approve anything. On either route, try to see the settlement statement a day ahead, and have the title company explain any charge that looks unfamiliar.

Frequently asked questions

Which county handles taxes on a house in Denison?

Grayson County. The county Tax Assessor-Collector bills you, while the Grayson County Appraisal District decides the value.

Does Denison tell homeowners the total tax rate?

Yes. The combined rate for the 2025 tax year is 2.318114, made up of the city, school district, county and college rates. Your own bill may differ, so ask the county tax office.

Is a permit needed for a shed or fence in Denison?

Yes for a shed of any size, and for a new fence or a repair covering 20 feet or more. The city asks for a site plan with dimensions from the property lines.

When does a Texas tax bill go delinquent?

On February 1, for taxes not paid by January 31. Penalty and interest start to accrue at that point.

Is probate always required to sell an inherited Denison house?

Not always. Options include a small estate affidavit, a muniment of title or an affidavit of heirship, and the title company decides which it will accept. The Grayson County clerk can say what must be filed.

Saginaw in brief

Saginaw mixes homes and businesses along State Highway 496, roughly ten miles northwest of Fort Worth, and houses here are priced and advertised as part of Fort Worth's suburban ring. The 2020 population was 23,890. The area began as a farm settlement called Dido and took the name Saginaw in 1882. The city incorporated in 1949, and its population climbed from 561 in the late 1950s to 8,551 in 1990, 12,374 in 2000 and 23,890 in 2020, with 556 businesses on record by 2023. With the whole city inside Tarrant County, you deal with one set of tax offices.

Sellers in the Fort Worth ring often start by asking what a cash buyer would pay, then check that number against a listing. That two-number habit works well in Saginaw: write both down, subtract the commission and repair costs from the listing figure, and see how far apart the two really are. Often the gap is smaller than the months of waiting suggest.

Which way to sell in Saginaw

Saginaw sellers tend to compare a broker, a sale without one and an as-is investor purchase. How soon you need money and how much repair you can afford usually settle it.

A broker puts your house in front of the most bidders and often gets the best price when the property is in good shape. The tradeoff is weeks of open houses and waiting on bank approvals. Selling alone means no commission, and also means you handle the photos, the contract and the haggling. An investor can fund on a date you pick with no lender appraisal, but expect the bid to be marked down for repair and resale expenses. Whoever bids, get the price, closing costs and date on paper.

Who taxes and appraises a Saginaw home?

The value on your house comes from Tarrant Appraisal District. After that, each taxing unit chooses a rate, so what you owe is several levies stacked together.

Seventy-three taxing units rely on TAD, including the county, the cities and the school districts, and they pay for police, fire, schools, streets and water systems with the revenue. Exemption filings with TAD are free. January 1 is the value date. If you disagree with the number, protest before the deadline printed on your notice.

What late taxes cost on a Saginaw house

Late tax adds up fast: a 6 percent penalty and 1 percent interest arrive in February, and the penalty reaches 12 percent by July.

Interest is uncapped, and a collection lawyer hired by a unit may add as much as a fifth of the tax. If tax is still owed when you sell, the closer pays it from your check. Transferring and recording a deed in Saginaw

Deeds for Saginaw property go to the Tarrant County clerk, who also keeps the land records.

Before the clerk takes a deed, a notary or similar officer has to witness the signature. The clerk manual puts the first page at five dollars and each following page at four, with smaller add-ons. The title company usually files it, and a lender's lien release is recorded there too.

Mortgage payments behind in Saginaw

Texas home loans usually contain a power of sale clause. A lender with that clause can auction the property on a first Tuesday and never file suit.

The process opens with a default notice and a twenty-day window to cure. At least three weeks before any auction, a sale notice has to be posted at the courthouse and filed with the clerk. Under federal rules a lender cannot begin until the loan is over 120 days past due. A sale on your terms can protect equity, so phone the servicer and a counselor soon. If the auction price falls below the debt, the lender can sue for the shortfall for two years.

Selling an inherited Saginaw house

Start by asking whether a will exists. A buyer needs a deed or court order proving who may sign.

  • Will: take it to probate within four years of death.
  • Will and no debts to administer: a muniment of title order, recorded with the clerk of the county where the house stands.
  • No will, small estate: a judge-approved affidavit, for estates of $75,000 or less outside the homestead.
  • Recorded transfer on death deed: the house skips probate.

A probate lawyer, or the State Law Library's guides, can point you to the right route.

How a Saginaw closing works

With a contract in hand, the title company looks through Tarrant County records for liens and confirms the owner. It requests your loan payoff and a tax certificate from the office that bills your lot. Anything it finds has to be cleared first, so speak up early about a tenant, back taxes or an estate question.

The deed gets your signature at closing. Sale money pays the loan and any tax, the deed and lien release head to the clerk, and the rest becomes yours. An investor paying cash needs no lender appraisal, so how fast title is cleared sets the date.

Saginaw's spot ten miles from Fort Worth helps with timing, since the title company, county offices and most buyers are a short drive away and paperwork can move in person when it needs to. Ask the title company which documents it wants signed before closing day so nobody scrambles at the table.

Ahead of the key handoff, stop or transfer your utilities and give the title company a forwarding address. File your copy of the closing statement.

A quick checklist for a Saginaw seller

Keep a folder, paper or digital, with six things in it: the deed, the loan payoff letter, the tax certificate, the lease if a tenant lives there, receipts for major repairs and your bids. When a buyer or the title company asks a question, the answer is a minute away instead of a week.

Then rank the bids by what each one leaves in your account on closing day, and call the top two to ask about their schedule. A bid that looks lower on paper can win if it closes sooner and asks for no repairs.

Selling with a tenant in the house

A renter's presence does not block a sale. If the buyer insists on a vacant house, the landlord must use the justice court process.

Look at the lease for the notice period; without one, a written notice to vacate gives three days. A suit is filed in justice court, with trial ten to twenty-one days later. An appeal to county court must come within five days of judgment, and a writ to enforce possession cannot issue sooner than six days after it. Set the closing date with that timeline in mind, and see whether the buyer can tolerate a delay.

Which county is Saginaw in?

Tarrant County, where Tarrant Appraisal District sets values. Its property search will pull up your parcel.

How late can I protest a Saginaw appraisal?

The notice of appraised value carries your deadline, which for most owners falls in mid May.

What happens if I miss the January 31 tax deadline?

Penalty of six percent plus one percent interest starts in February, and the penalty reaches twelve percent by July.

Does a Saginaw homestead exemption cost anything to file?

No. Filing an exemption with TAD costs nothing.

Can a Saginaw house sell while taxes are unpaid?

Yes. The debt is paid from your proceeds at closing, and a tax certificate tells you the amount ahead of time.

Steady demand helps, but a seller still has a tax bill to square away, maybe a tenant to deal with, and a deed to sign. The sections below cover Belton details first and the Texas rules after them. Owners of older lots near Nolan Creek should check floodplain status before listing, since lenders ask.

Property tax bills and early-payment discounts

Bell CAD appraises property and also takes the payments. One statement for the whole year goes out each October. Payment is due when it arrives, and a balance left after January 31 starts drawing penalties on February 1. A full early payment earns a discount from certain taxing entities, as shown below.

Who values my house?

Bell CAD does, with offices in Belton, Killeen and Temple. Sales and properties get a fresh look each year, so a value can shift from one notice to the next. Tuck your newest notice into the closing folder, as buyers will want to see the figure the house carries.

Homestead exemption

Filing opens January 1 and closes April 30, at the district office or online. After approval the exemption carries forward by itself. Renewal comes up only if the chief appraiser sends a request or you change homes. Bell CAD will also accept a late filing for two years after the tax goes delinquent.

To qualify, you must have lived in the house as your residence on January 1, with no other homestead claimed. State law caps the land at 20 acres, but the district describes an acre or less as the usual case. A mobile home owner on rented land can still apply, using a title or a verified purchase contract.

Older and disabled owners get extra relief, and a surviving spouse aged 55 or over can keep the school tax ceiling. A disabled veteran submits a VA letter showing a rating of 10% or higher, and 100% may support a full exemption on the homestead.

Does the 10% homestead cap change what a buyer pays?

The cap touches assessed value only. Market value moves with sales and has no ceiling, but a homestead's assessment can grow only 10% per year. That protection begins after the owner has held the home through one full January 1.

A buyer paying far above the old assessment may see the bill rise for several years while the assessment works up to market value. A buyer who will live there should hear that from you.

Short-term rental permits

The ordinance on short-term rentals dates to March 13, 2023. Each rental carries a one-year city permit, and the owner has 30 days from expiration to apply for renewal. Unpaid local hotel and motel occupancy tax blocks the renewal.

A rental the owner doesn't occupy must stay at least 500 feet from another short-term rental. Every address needs a separate application in the online portal, where income is also reported each quarter, with zero entered for months without guests.

Tenants in the house before closing

Any Texas eviction begins with a written notice to vacate, and the default is three days unless the lease sets another period. A landlord may hand it over, leave it inside the unit, mail it, or email it if the lease allows.

A tenant who stays can be taken to justice court, where the hearing falls 10 to 21 days after filing. Appeals to county court must be made within five days of the judgment. A writ of possession can follow after six days, and removal comes with 24 hours of warning. Plan your closing date around that schedule, or sell with the tenant staying on.

Foreclosure and tax liens

Many Texas loans give the lender a power of sale, so the house goes to a courthouse auction held on a first Tuesday. You have 20 days after the default letter to reinstate the loan. Notice of the sale then has to reach you at least 21 days before the auction. An owner who can't catch up often does best by selling beforehand and keeping the equity.

Property tax works separately. Its lien attaches each January 1 and rides with the land through any sale. Because the January 1 owner stays liable, the title company should clear that year's bill at the closing table.

Where a Belton deed is filed

You record a deed for Bell County land with the county clerk, after it has been signed and acknowledged. Once it is on file, ask Bell CAD what it needs to update the owner name on the account.

The state clerk manual puts the recording fee at $5.00 for page one and $4.00 for every page after it, plus other statutory charges. Call the clerk for the exact total. Usually the title company files it and sends you a copy.

What a cash sale skips

Listing the house means showings, a buyer's mortgage, an appraisal and repair requests after the inspection. A cash sale cuts most of that out, so clear title mostly sets the pace. Ask for any offer in writing, then have the title company check the tax payoff, any liens and who must sign the deed.

Before you ask for offers, collect your latest tax statement and appraisal notice, a mortgage payoff figure if there is a loan, any lease or rental permit papers, and notes on floodplain or repair history. A buyer with that folder can price the house fast.

On closing day the title company settles the year's property tax, pays off the mortgage, and records the deed with the Bell County clerk. If a tenant is staying, say so in the contract. If the house ran as a short-term rental, show that the city tax filings are current. Both tend to draw last-minute questions from buyers.

Frequently asked questions

When must a Belton homestead application be filed?

The deadline is April 30 of the tax year. Bell CAD takes late filings for two years after the tax turns delinquent, and the exemption needs no yearly renewal.

Is there an early-pay discount on Belton property tax?

For certain taxing entities, yes: 3% off in October, 2% in November and 1% in December. January is the base amount.

Can I rent a Belton house on a nightly basis?

Only if the city issues a permit, renewed each year. A rental where the owner doesn't live must be 500 feet from any other short-term rental.

If I sell a Belton house mid-year, who owes that year's tax?

Whoever owned it on January 1 holds the lien and the liability. The title company normally splits the bill between seller and buyer at closing.

Which office values my Belton house?

Bell CAD, which keeps offices in Belton, Killeen and Temple and looks at sales and properties each year.

Tarrant County tax dates

Tarrant County mails bills near October 1. Pay by January 31 and nothing extra accrues. On February 1 a penalty of 6 percent begins and grows each month until it reaches 12 percent in July, and interest of 1 percent monthly runs alongside.

Come July 1, unpaid accounts pass to tax attorneys, whose fee can add as much as 20 percent. Anyone splitting the bill in two pays November 30 and June 30. Older and disabled owners may spread payments over a quarterly plan from January through July. Exemption filings at Tarrant Appraisal District close April 30, and protests close May 15.

Filing a homestead exemption with Tarrant Appraisal District

Filing costs nothing. Use the district's online form, or print form 50-114 and mail or email it. A Texas driver's license or ID card carrying the home address is required.

A buyer who moves in gets the exemption from that date, as long as the previous owner had not claimed one that year. It also holds yearly appraisal growth to 10 percent, except for improvements and added land.

Inherited property needs extra documents: an ownership affidavit, the earlier owner's death certificate, a current utility bill and the citation of any court record. Other heirs who live in the house must each sign an authorization.

Many Colleyville owners are old enough to hold a school tax ceiling, which freezes the school bill on their homestead. Those 65 or older also get an extra $60,000 school exemption. Can heirs sell a Colleyville house quickly?

Selling an inherited or downsized house

Next, ask the title company which documents it will insure on. One may close on a court order alone, another may insist on a recorded transfer on death deed or an executor's deed. Answering that question before buyers call keeps a deal from collapsing late.

Pricing a house worth $784,900

Colleyville's median owned home is valued at $784,900 and median rent is $3,263. At that level, small flaws shift the price a long way. A financed buyer will order an appraisal and an inspection, and either report can reopen the price talk.

Keep receipts for roof, HVAC, foundation and plumbing jobs, along with permits for any additions. A tidy maintenance file reassures buyers and gives you a firm reply to a low offer.

Questions worth asking every buyer

Before signing anything, get three answers in writing. Is the offer price firm after the walkthrough? Who pays for the title policy and recording? What is the target closing date, and may you stay a few days past it while the movers finish? A buyer who answers plainly is usually one who closes.

A cash buyer tours the house, typically once, then puts an offer on paper. If you agree, the title company searches records, requests lender payoffs and drafts the deed, and you sign on the date you picked. Because big, long-held houses often need updating, the buyer will discount for roofs, kitchens and mechanical systems, so the offer will sit under a fully staged listing price.

In return you get certainty: no loan can fall through, no appraisal can come in short and no showings disturb the household. For an owner relocating, settling an estate or dodging months of carrying costs on an expensive house, that can justify the discount. Line up written offers by what you would net.

Is selling without an agent common in Colleyville?

It can, for a sound house when you can manage showings and contracts yourself. The title company still drafts the deed and divides the tax year.

When does a Colleyville buyer get the homestead exemption?

From the move-in date, when the seller had not claimed one that year.

Where is a Colleyville protest filed?

At Tarrant Appraisal District, by May 15 for the current year.

What if taxes on a Colleyville house are late?

Penalty rises each month to 12 percent in July, with 1 percent interest monthly on top. Get the payoff from the county; closing normally clears it.

Can an heir sign a Colleyville deed before probate ends?

Seldom. A buyer's title company wants a court order, executor's authority or a recorded transfer on death deed first.

Kerrville sits on the Guadalupe River and bills itself as the capital of the Texas Hill Country. The parks, golf courses and arts venues pull buyers in, as do Schreiner University and the Kerrville Folk Festival.

Houses close to the river carry both the appeal and the flood exposure. After the July 2026 flood, that exposure shapes how buyers and insurers view the area, so expect questions about water history on any showing.

The July 2026 flood and your sale

The governor declared Kerr County a disaster area on July 17, 2026, and the city keeps a recovery page with debris collection, damage reporting through the state and a local disaster relief center. If your house was damaged, that history will come up in any sale.

Who appraises property in Kerr County

Kerr Central Appraisal District, at 212 Oak Hollow Drive in Kerrville, appraises all real and business personal property in the county. It has online search, interactive maps, a forms page and an online protest portal.

The entities it serves include Kerr County, the City of Kerrville, Kerrville ISD, Ingram ISD, Center Point ISD, the Upper Guadalupe River Authority and several emergency service districts. Your bill adds several of those together, so read each line. A Hill Country lot outside the city can carry more than one special district line, among them the Upper Guadalupe River Authority and Headwaters Groundwater Conservation District. Your school district appears on your tax statement, and buyers check it first.

Texas tax dates and a Kerrville closing

Value is set on January 1, the lien attaches that day, and bills go out in early October.

  • First half of a split bill: November 30. Second half: June 30.
  • Delinquent from February 1, with penalty and interest.
  • Homestead exemption filings are generally due April 30.
  • Protest deadline is generally May 15, or 30 days after the notice.

A seller closing mid-year normally credits the buyer for the unpaid part of the year at the closing table.

Ways to sell fast in Kerrville

A flood-affected or older house changes which of three routes fits: listing, selling privately or a cash sale.

  • A for-sale-by-owner sale cuts commission and puts disclosure on you.

The Kerr County Clerk records deeds for land in the county, and the instrument must be signed and acknowledged before an authorized officer. The title company handles filing, so ask for the final charges on your settlement statement.

Transfer on death deeds and land contracts

Texas lets an owner record a transfer on death deed so real property passes without probate, and a Lady Bird deed lets the owner keep selling or mortgaging the house without the beneficiary's consent. Either must be recorded in the county where the property sits, and the transfer on death deed has to be recorded before the owner dies.

A contract for deed is different. Under Property Code chapter 5 the seller keeps title until the buyer finishes paying, and for a residence the buyer has a statutory right to cancel. Seller financing on a Kerrville house is possible, but the rules are strict, so have a Texas attorney draft it.

Buyers ask about the river

The Guadalupe River gives Kerrville its parks and its trail, and buyers want to know which parts of town felt the July 2026 flood. The city's recovery page reported Louise Hays Park, Lehmann-Monroe Park, Tranquility Island, Guadalupe Park and the River Trail closed for flood damage, with Knapp Park and Cypress Park reopened.

If your house is on higher ground, say so and show the water history you know. If it took water, a cash buyer will price the repair and a listing buyer will want inspection reports. Accurate answers save time late in the deal. Mention festival weekends, parking and guest space where they apply, and be honest about flood history.

Inherited house or back taxes

For inherited property, Texas offers a will probate window of four years, a muniment of title when no administration is needed, and a small estate affidavit for estates of $75,000 or less excluding the homestead.

On back taxes, the collector can add up to 20 percent attorney fees under a contract and can pursue a suit. Homestead owners may ask about a delinquent installment plan of up to 36 months where a collector allows it. Call the Kerr County tax office for a payoff figure.

From offer to closing in Kerrville

A normal sale starts with an offer, then an inspection, then a title search and a signing before a notary. In Kerrville, add two flood-related steps: be ready with a clear account of any water history, and have your insurance and assistance claims documented so the title company and buyer see a consistent record.

If the buyer needs a loan, expect an appraisal and lender conditions, which stretch the timeline. A cash buyer can close on your date, and the date matters when you are moving to be near family. Ask for it in writing, along with who pays title charges and recording, so nothing is left to the closing table.

Papers worth gathering first

Pull the recorded deed and your latest tax statement from the Kerr County tax office. Add any payoff letter from a lender, photos and receipts for flood damage, permits for repairs, and the account of what insurance covered. If the house is a rental or an inherited property, add the lease or the probate paperwork. A buyer who sees these on day one will often offer faster and with fewer conditions, because there is less to discover later.

The city has thrived since its founding in 1889.

The filing window ran 105 days from the July 17 declaration. Call Kerr Central Appraisal District and ask whether a late option exists for your property.

What damage level qualified for the temporary exemption?

Kerr CAD said owners with at least 15 percent physical damage could apply, for property in an area the governor declared a disaster.

Where is the Kerr appraisal district office?

212 Oak Hollow Drive, Kerrville, Texas 78028.

Can I sell a flood-damaged house in Kerrville?

Yes, either as is or after you repair it. Gather damage documentation, disclose what you know, and ask the city about permits before any rebuilding.

The courthouse square anchors the older core. Mention it if you are close, and keep a folder with permits, receipts and any old survey, because a cash buyer cares more about condition and title than about local history.

Navarro County's seat and biggest city, Corsicana, lies about 58 miles southeast of Dallas, where Interstate 45 meets U.S. highways 75 and 287 and State highways 22 and 31. A commute to Dallas along I-45 is a normal selling point. Name the highway access a buyer would use for the daily drive, since small-town shoppers compare that early and it costs you nothing to include.

Which Corsicana projects need a city permit?

Structural work does. The city requires a permit to build, alter, enlarge or repair any home or commercial building within its limits, and the building inspector and Planning and Zoning Department review applications.

Code enforcement

The Community Support Department covers property maintenance, zoning, addressing, fencing and screening, and trash containment. Staff answer complaints, inspect and write citations. They also run the city cemeteries, which include Woodland, Oakwood and Modrell.

Heirs and borrowers in default

Probate of a will is open to heirs for four years after a death. Where there is no will and few assets, a small estate affidavit might do the job, and a recorded transfer on death deed sidesteps probate. The Navarro County Clerk can tell you which documents it requires.

Falling behind does not stop you from selling. A lender typically waits until the loan is over 120 days late, allows 20 days to cure, then posts a sale notice at least 21 days before a first-Tuesday auction. Your servicer can supply a payoff.

The buyer walks through, then sends an offer in writing. Once you agree, a title company examines Navarro County records, asks for payoffs and books closing on your chosen date. Since no loan is involved, nothing waits on an appraisal.

Compare your house with sales on its own block rather than citywide. A pre-1900 house near downtown, a mid-century ranch and a newer build answer different questions. The first draws questions about wiring and foundation, the second about plumbing and roofing, and the third about what the builder covered.

A written timeline of work done, with receipts, answers many of those questions before they are asked. Where work is still needed, say so. Buyers discount known problems far less than surprises found at inspection.

Closing day

Closing means signing the deed and the settlement papers. From the proceeds, the title company retires your mortgage, clears any tax balance and shares the year's bill with the buyer, then pays you the difference. Bring photo ID and all the keys. The Navarro County Clerk then records the deed, and your copy of the settlement statement belongs in your tax file.

Selling a Corsicana rental or vacant house

An empty house draws code notices faster than an occupied one, so check the yard and the exterior regularly while it sits. If a tenant lives there, hand the buyer the lease and the rent record, and say when the term ends. A buyer who understands the occupancy up front is less likely to renegotiate later.

If the house has stood vacant for a while, have the water and power on for the walkthrough and look for roof or plumbing leaks before a buyer's inspector does.

Getting the house ready

Handle anything code enforcement would flag, because an open notice can add days to a closing. Mow, haul off debris, mend broken fence sections and check that the house number can be read from the street. Close any open permit, and file receipts for roof, wiring and foundation work, so a buyer sees a house that has been cared for.

How soon can a Corsicana house close?

Anywhere from a couple of weeks for a cash purchase to a month or more for a financed sale. Payoff letters, title work and any probate step set the floor, so request those documents on day one. An open permit or a code notice on the lot can also add days.

Is a permit needed for a fence in Corsicana?

Yes. Fences are on the city's permit list, along with accessory buildings, demolition, drive approaches, irrigation systems, signs and moving a structure. Check with the inspection line.

Who files the deed after closing in Corsicana?

The title company usually records it with the Navarro County Clerk, after the deed has been signed and acknowledged before a notary or witnesses.

Will a Corsicana buyer inherit last year's tax bill?

The tax lien forms on January 1 and stays with the property, so closing settles it. Anything delinquent has to be paid for title to be clear.

  • Open-market listing: staging and showings, then a buyer's lender to wait on.
  • Private sale: the contract, the disclosures and the title paperwork are all on you.
  • Cash sale: nobody needs loan approval, and the price reflects the work the buyer inherits.

Whichever way you go, request a payoff letter and read how title is vested on your deed before talking price. A house held in a trust or estate must be signed by the person those papers name, so confirm who that is first.

A small city with no room to grow

Five miles north of downtown Dallas, University Park is bordered by Dallas on two sides and Highland Park on the south. Together the two towns are the Park Cities, and they split one school system, the Highland Park Independent School District, which is headquartered in University Park. Police and fire service are separate for each town.

The city covers only 3.69 square miles, and after the Park Cities turned down a merger with Dallas in 1945, Dallas annexed the land around it. Almost every sale is an existing house on an established lot, so the land can weigh as heavily in a buyer's mind as the structure. About 6,858 residents lived on each square mile in 2020.

Southern Methodist University opened in 1915, and houses grew up around it. Incorporation came in 1924, and construction surged after World War II. A public library opened at Preston Center in January 2013. Residents get close attention from city services, and that is part of what buyers pay for.

Permits and zoning rules

Building codes are enforced by the city's Community Development Department, and most new construction, remodeling and additions need permits. Every application has gone through a mandatory completeness meeting before plan review since January 1, 2025.

  • Demolishing more than 50 percent of a structure triggers a full rebuild to current codes, counted as 50 percent exterior walls, 25 percent foundation and 25 percent roof.
  • Nothing may be built over utility easements.
  • A permit is needed to replace a water heater or add a hardwired light, but not to paint or wallpaper.
  • A permit expires after 60 days if no inspection occurs, and unpermitted work can bring fines or an order to restore the site.

Contractor registrations expire on the same annual date as the state license, and contractor signs are not allowed in residential districts. Construction hours are 7 a.m. to 6 p.m., Monday through Saturday, with no work on Sundays or listed holidays.

Permits are issued at the Peek Service Center, 4420 Worcola in Dallas, from 8 a.m. to 4:30 p.m. on weekdays. Call 214-987-5411 to check what a given project needs. Expect a buyer's inspector to ask whether past work was permitted, so dig out those records before you list. Missing permits on an older addition can slow a sale or prompt a price request.

Property tax timing

January 1 fixes both value and exemption eligibility, and bills go out around October 1. Delay is costly on an expensive house: a six percent penalty and one percent interest land on February 1, and the penalty climbs to 12 percent by July 1.

At closing the agent pays the year's tax out of your proceeds. Ask for a payoff that runs through your closing date, and confirm which taxing units bill your address. On a house of this value, even a small proration error is a large number, so read the settlement statement line by line before you sign.

Inherited property and probate

After an owner's death, the will can generally be offered for probate for four years. Estates whose only debts are real-estate liens may use a muniment of title. A transfer on death deed works only if it was recorded before the owner died, and an affidavit of heirship involves no court review.

Each title company has its own comfort level, so ask what it will accept before you commit to a date. Bring the death certificate, any will, the deed and a list of liens. When heirs agree and one holds clear authority to sign, a cash buyer can close in a few weeks, because no lender is waiting. Disagreement among heirs is what drags these sales out, so settle it early.

Why cash can suit a house here

Large lots and older houses invite renovation plans, and a financed buyer who wants a rebuild may need months of design and permit work before committing. A cash buyer can decide faster. Sellers who value certainty and a clean exit over the last few dollars of price often choose that route. Sellers who prefer certainty over the last few dollars of price often choose that route, particularly when an estate must be wrapped up or a family is relocating on a fixed date.

What to prepare for closing

Pull together the payoff letter, the newest tax statement, permit records and any trust documents. At the signing you will need a notary, a photo ID and a plan for handing over keys, garage remotes and alarm codes. Move out any belongings you do not want to leave, since a cash buyer typically takes the house empty.

Cash buyers usually accept a house as is. That counts for a lot when updating a large older home would be expensive and take months. Before signing, get three things in writing: the closing date, who pays closing costs, and the length of any inspection period.

Frequently asked questions

Why is University Park so densely built?

The city covers only 3.69 square miles, and Dallas annexed the land around it after 1945, so it could never expand. Existing houses on established lots make up nearly all sales.

Is a permit needed to swap a water heater in University Park?

Yes. Replacing a water heater or adding a permanently wired light fixture requires a permit, while painting and wallpapering do not.

What happens if I demolish part of my University Park house?

Demolishing more than 50 percent of a structure requires a complete rebuild to current codes, measured by walls, foundation and roof.

When can contractors work in University Park?

Construction is permitted from 7 a.m. to 6 p.m., Monday through Saturday, except by special permission, and it is prohibited on Sundays and listed holidays.

Can an inherited University Park house be sold without probate?

Sometimes. A transfer on death deed recorded before the owner's death avoids probate, while other cases use a muniment of title or an executor's deed.

Which county records your deed

Denton County. The deed is recorded with the Denton County clerk, and the appraisal district for the county values the house each January 1. Local taxing units, not the state, issue the bills.

A lien for each year's tax attaches from January 1, so title work on a Corinth sale will check for unpaid balances. The clerk's office also holds liens and foreclosure sale notices for parcels in the county.

The school tax ceiling for older owners

Under the ceiling rule, a school district cannot raise the yearly tax on a qualifying older or disabled owner's homestead above what applied when the owner first qualified, except for new improvements. A surviving spouse aged 55 or more can keep it.

The ceiling can follow the owner, in proportion, to a new Texas homestead. Older Corinth owners thinking about downsizing should ask the appraisal district how that transfer works before committing to a purchase elsewhere. The extra $60,000 school exemption is a separate benefit.

Foreclosure steps

Most Texas home loans let the lender sell through a power of sale written into the deed of trust. A default notice starts a 20 day window to bring the loan current, and the sale notice follows at least 21 days before the auction.

  • The courthouse door and the clerk's files carry the sale notice.
  • Auctions take place on a set monthly day, within a daytime window.
  • Federal rules generally hold off a foreclosure start until the loan is well past 120 days late.
  • A lender seeking a shortfall has two years after the sale to sue.

You then sign the deed, the buyer funds, and the title company pays off your loans and sends you what remains.

A listing adds steps in front: photos, showings, an inspection and the buyer's loan approval. A cash sale starts at the offer. Either way, the work you can do early is gathering documents and learning what you owe, because surprises in the title search are the usual cause of delays.

Pricing a house in a compact city

Because Corinth covers only 8 square miles, nearby streets compete directly. Look up recent sales within a few blocks and compare square footage, age, lot and condition. A buyer coming from Dallas or Denton will likely compare you with houses in several suburbs along the interstate, so highlight what is distinctive: rail access, the lake area, a recent roof or a renovated kitchen.

If a cash offer comes in well under those nearby sales, ask the buyer to explain the repair costs behind the number. Sometimes the gap is fair. Sometimes it signals room to negotiate.

Selling with a lender lien

Most Corinth sellers still have a mortgage. The payoff comes out of the sale price at closing, so the question is whether the price covers it plus costs. Ask your servicer for a written payoff good through a specific date, and ask whether any other liens are recorded against the property.

If the price would fall short of the balance, the lender must agree in writing to accept less. Start that conversation before you list, not after you have an offer in hand.

Heirs and a Corinth house

Heirs begin by learning how title reads and whether a will exists. Corinth parcels are recorded in Denton County, and a title company decides which order or affidavit it will insure.

If the owner recorded a beneficiary deed before dying, the property can pass without probate. An heir who is not on the recorded deed and wants the homestead exemption gives the appraisal district an ownership affidavit and supporting papers. Collect the original will and a list of every heir first.

Paperwork to gather first

Begin with documents a buyer and title agent will ask for: the recorded deed, a recent mortgage statement, the latest property tax statement, any homeowners association papers and receipts for major repairs. Having them ready shortens the gap between acceptance and closing.

Neighbors a few streets apart share the same market, so recent sales on nearby streets are the best guide to pricing. A figure grounded in nearby sales also gives you a way to judge a cash offer.

Yes, north of Lake Lewisville. Your deed and tax records are with Denton County offices.

How far is Corinth from Dallas and the airport?

About 20 miles north of downtown Dallas. DFW International Airport is 15 miles southwest, roughly a 20 minute drive.

Does Corinth have commuter rail?

Yes. The Denton County Transportation Authority commuter rail passes through with two access points, linking to Denton and downtown Dallas.

Can I sell if I owe more than the house is worth?

Only if the lender agrees in writing to take less than the payoff. Call your servicer before listing.

Paris is the Lamar County seat in Northeast Texas, so the courthouse, the clerk and the appraisal district are all in town. Deed, tax certificate and ownership papers can all be sorted out within a few blocks, which helps if a deadline is closing in.

The housing stock is old by Texas standards. The town dates to 1844, rail arrived in 1876, and fires in 1877 and 1916 forced rebuilding. A tornado on April 2, 1982 destroyed more than 1,500 homes, and nearly $7 million went into downtown renovation afterward. Anyone buying an older house will ask how old the roof, wiring and foundation are, so hold on to repair receipts and insurance claims. Disclose any known damage plainly in the contract.

Who values and collects the tax

Property values for the whole county come from the Lamar Central Appraisal District, and separate taxing units choose the rates. Find the office at 521 Bonham Street or call (903) 785-7822. Employees there field questions on values and exemptions and will point you to the collecting office.

Put a protest in writing by May 31, or within 30 days of the notice being mailed if that falls later. The state calendar prints May 15 for most protests, so read the date at the bottom of your own notice. Hearings begin around June 1, and a letter arrives about 15 days before yours.

Ownership papers go to the Lamar County clerk. Whichever route you take, the buyer will want to see the paper that lets you sign.

Paperwork to gather first

Pull the deed and latest tax statement first, then the lender's payoff contact and any lease. Expect the title company to request exactly these.

The town is a regional medical and shopping center for Northeast Texas and southeast Oklahoma, and Paris Junior College has been here since 1924. This choice is time against dollars. Selling to a buyer with a mortgage may bring a higher price, yet you pay an agent, host showings, answer inspection requests and wait on the lender. If the roof is worn, the wiring is dated or the foundation is in question, a cash sale can net about the same once repairs and commissions are taken out. Find out who pays for the title policy, how many days closing will take, and whether the price can change after a walkthrough. Request proof of funds, and learn how much earnest money goes down and when it comes back.

Walk away from anyone who wants a fee before making an offer or refuses to write terms down. A solid offer spells out price, closing date, cost split and what happens to the deposit if the sale collapses.

Do not promise a move-out date you cannot control. If you need the tenant gone before the sale, start that process early and ask an attorney about the steps, because the timeline is fixed by the court, not by the buyer.

After you accept, the title company starts a file, orders the tax certificate and searches the Lamar County clerk's records for liens. When a lender is owed, they request that payoff on your behalf.

Bring photo ID on closing day and read the settlement statement, which lists the price, payoffs, prorated taxes and fees. When the deed is recorded, you are paid the balance. With no lender appraisal involved, the title search and your calendar mostly set the pace.

Call the Lamar Central Appraisal District at (903) 785-7822. It covers values and exemptions and can name the office that collects your bill.

May 31 or 30 days from mailing of the notice, whichever comes later. Your notice prints the date that applies.

Once ownership is on paper it is straightforward. That paper may be a probated will, a small estate affidavit or an affidavit of heirship, filed with the Lamar County clerk.

Recording your deed

Deeds are recorded by the El Paso County Clerk. Before a land deed is accepted for filing, the signer must acknowledge it to a notary or similar officer, or two witnesses must swear to it. Plan to sign with ID in hand.

Recording fees in the 2023 clerk manual run $5.00 for page one, $4.00 for each added page and $0.25 for every indexed name past five. Records fees add things like $2.00 for technology and up to $10 each for management and archive, and a missing grantee address can add $25. Fees change, so check the clerk's current schedule.

The title company usually files for you in the county where the land sits, El Paso County for a Horizon City house. The manual mentions no transfer tax. Each charge on your side appears on the settlement statement.

Owing taxes when you sell

A tax lien for each year attaches to the land on January 1 and rides along through any sale. Even after a transfer a court can order the property sold, so clear title waits until delinquent taxes are paid.

A bill still open once January 31 is behind you counts as late, and charges begin February 1. When a house is auctioned for taxes, the former owner may buy it back: two years from the filing of the purchaser's deed for homestead, farm and mineral land, at a 25 percent markup in year one and 50 percent in year two, or 180 days for other land. A tax sale surplus can be claimed for two years.

Selling before anyone sues over back taxes spares you court costs. Ask the tax office for a payoff figure, and ask whether an installment plan is available, which some collectors grant on a residence homestead.

Before you list or accept a bid

Set aside an afternoon for paperwork before the first buyer walks in, and keep every document in one folder. Pull the deed, find any survey, and note which taxing units and which school district appear on your tax bill. Ask the tax office for the current balance so you know the exact figure that must be paid at the closing table.

Then walk the house with a notepad. Write down what works, what is worn out and what you would rather leave alone. Any buyer or inspector will find the same items, and an owner who names them first earns trust and tends to face fewer late price cuts.

What happens after you accept an offer

Once under contract, the file moves to a title company that orders the search, requests payoffs and confirms taxes are current. You sign in front of a notary at closing, the deed is filed, and what is left after payoffs and charges is yours. No lender approval is needed with cash, which helps a firm date hold. Leave your utility district account open until closing day, then ask the buyer to move it into their name. Leave manuals, remotes and garage openers for the new owner, and take photos of the empty house for your own records.

Frequently asked questions

What is Horizon City's population?

The 2025 estimate is 25,118, which is 11.8% higher than the 2020 base.

Will I owe a transfer tax?

The clerk's fee schedule shows recording charges but no transfer tax. Your title company can give you the full settlement statement.

Does a tax balance stop my sale?

No. The balance gets paid out of your proceeds at closing, because the lien stays with the house. The county tax office issues the payoff statement.

Who decides the value of my property for tax?

The El Paso Central Appraisal District. Its calendar lists protest dates, and its taxpayer liaison handles complaints.

Is $170,200 the price my house will fetch?

That is a townwide midpoint for 2020 to 2024. For your own address, rely on written offers or an appraisal.
